News.title: Killer who murdered girlfriend’s children, 8 & 5, by tying them up & setting fire to house executed by lethal injection
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

JUSTICE SERVED Killer who murdered girlfriend’s children, 8 & 5, by tying them up & setting fire to house executed by lethal injection







Next

A KILLER who murdered his girlfriend’s children has been executed by lethal injection.

Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, set fire to his partner’s home in 2010 while siblings Alyssa Lynch, eight, and five-year-old Caleb were inside.

Alyssa’s body was found in a closet and Caleb’s body was tied to a mattress with duct tape.

Authorities found a railroad flare in the boy’s underwear and another was underneath his body.





The children’s mum, Lisa Lynch, was at work at the time of the horror in Evansville, Indiana.

She had left her two kids with Weisheit for him to look after them.

The depraved killer was executed by lethal injection at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City on Thursday.

The procedure started just after midnight, and he was pronounced dead at 12.45am local time, authorities said.

They confirmed his last meal request was barbecue ribs.

He had no final words.

Lisa described Alyssa as a creative girl who loved drawing sketches of her family.

The heartbroken mum said her boy Caleb loved hugs, cooking and playing with toys.



She said in court: “Everyday without them is a struggle.

“Every birthday, every holiday, every landmark moment is marked by their agonising absence.

“Time passes but the weight of losing them never fades. They will always be my children.”

It comes after a wave of scrutiny facing the death penalty following the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee.

Weisheit’s lawyers had tried to prevent the death sentence by claiming the suspect suffered from head injuries and mental health issues.



They argued he should have a brain scan and claimed this factor was not addressed properly during his 2013 trial.

On Thursday, Florida and Alabama were also set to carry out executions.

Jesse Guardado was sentenced to death after confessing to fatally stabbing a 75-year-old woman inside her Walton County home in 2004.

He stole her jewellery box, £50 and other valuables to support his drug habit.

And in Alabama, Michael Taylor, 54, also faces execution, 35 years after fatally beating an older couple with a metal bar during a robbery in their Gadsden home.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Taylor was arrested when he was 19 years old, driving the victims’ stolen Cadillac about an hour away from their home.

News.title: Football-loving former Labour MP Peter Snape left six-figure sum for his third wife after death aged 84
News.content:
LAST GIFT Football-loving former Labour MP Peter Snape left six-figure sum for his third wife after death aged 84







Next

FORMER Labour MP and football fan Peter Snape left his six-figure estate to his third wife after his death aged 84.

The backbencher died on August 13 after a short cancer battle, but not before leaving more than £180,000 to Lady Lynda Waltho-Snape.



The 84-year-old served as Member of Parliament for West Bromwich East for 27 years.

He stood down at the 2001 General Election and was succeeded by Tom Watson.



Football-loving Lord Snape was given a life peerage in 2004.

He was also the ex-chairman of his home town beloved Stockport County FC.

The three-times married, father-of-two left the £181,827 value of his estate to his wife Lady Waltho-Snape.

The gross value of the estate was £216,160, according to the Grant of Probate document revealed today by the High Court of Justice.

Lord Snape and Lady Waltho-Snape had been together for 20 years and she was the former Labour MP for Stourbridge and they wed in March.

He wrote his will on April 2, this year.



Lord Snape was married to first wife Winifred Grimshaw for 17 years and had two daughters together.

He wed his second wife Janet Manley, a school teacher, in 2004 and she later died in 2024.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in tribute at the time of his death three months ago: “Peter was a good friend to me and one of Parliament’s great characters.

“A proud son of Stockport, lifelong County fan and well-loved MP for West Bromwich.

“He always lifted others with a laugh and devoted his life to making his community and his country better.”



Stockport County Club President Steve Bellis paid tribute to Peter, said: “He was highly articulate, as you would expect given his position.

“But he was also extremely witty and never short of a good story.”

News.title: Neighbours LOSE 10-year planning row with millionaire developer after he built ‘monster’
News.content:
BITTER BLOW Neighbours LOSE 10-year planning row with millionaire developer after he built ‘monster’







Next

NEIGHBOURS of a “mega mansion” have been left fuming after losing a 10-year planning battle with a millionaire developer.

Thomas Worrall has been allowed to keep his seven-bedroom luxury home by Bath and North East Somerset Council despite residents claiming it’s a clear breach of planning permission.



It’s believed to be the largest new build in Bath in 100 years, which locals say has marred the beauty spot.

The monster-sized property on the edge of Bath has been constructed significantly higher and with a larger footprint than originally approved by the local council.



In 2021, Thomas was granted permission to build a five-bed home that blended into the hillside.

But locals have spotted that the building is facing a different direction than Thomas originally said with the property two metres taller and 130sqm bigger.



Two extra rooms have been added, including its own gym and cinema room which were not part of the original approved plans.

Tavis Hamilton, 48, who lives next door, is one of more than 100 locals that lodged formal objections against Thomas over the last 10 years.



Tavis said: “It is an absolute mega home – it will probably be worth more than £3million when it’s finished.

“It is enormous and dwarfs all the cottages. You could fit around 24 of the other cottages into the footprint.”

But following a meeting with local councillors, Thomas has had a retrospective planning application approved over fears that the building to remain derelict if they rejected it.



Thomas has nearly completed the grand property and insists he’s “not the bad guy”, adding: “I just want to finish the job and move in with my family.”

He explained that he bought the land with planning permissions but due to ground changes he had to make changes to the construction.

Locals are fuming and say the situation highlights how multi-millionaires are able to exploit loopholes during the planning process.

Tavis added: “It just shows how unfair the process is. It seems if you put the wrong guttering on your house or use the incorrect glazing, the council jump on you for enforcement.

“But you can build this enormous structure without the right planning permission and no enforcement is carried out until it is too late.”



Residents who attended the decision meeting with the council have accused them of authorising a “two- tier” system.

Speaking at the decision meeting, neighbour Paul Raithby told councillors: “The applicant, their surveyor and your own case officer all acknowledge that what has been built is an intentional breach of planning control.

“There is zero demonstrated local need for a seven-bedroom luxury mansion to justify overturning planning laws.”

Councillor Shaun Hughes said: “This isn’t a clerical error – a seven-bed luxury house with gyms and cinema room and stuff.

“This was not an error where they accidentally reoriented the building and added two bedrooms in.”



Cllr Wright stressed that the build has severely impacted neighbours along the narrow single-track road, with windows now positioned right beside adjacent properties.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meanwhile, Cllr Tim Warren said: “I don’t like it but I think we have no option but to go along with it.”

Following the verdict, Paul said: “It just continually goes to prove that the planners do not really have the teeth to fight a developer with deep pockets, and that is what it seems to come down to.”

News.title: ‘It’s a disgrace’, family of Henry Nowak blast early release of Vickrum Digwa’s mum – after she hid murder weapon
News.content:
FAMILY FURY ‘It’s a disgrace’, family of Henry Nowak blast early release of Vickrum Digwa’s mum – after she hid murder weapon







Next

THE family of murdered student Henry Nowak have blasted the early release of his killer’s mother after she hid the murder weapon.

Kiran Kaur, 53, was jailed for hiding the eight-inch blade used to murder Henry in Southampton, Hampshire, last December.



Vickrum Digwa, 23, knifed the 18-year-old five times with a ceremonial dagger before telling cops he was the victim of a racist attack.

Following the fatal stabbing, Kaur – who came to the UK 30 years ago – arrived at the scene and took the Sikh dagger home, hiding it in her son’s bedroom.



She was sentenced to three years behind bars for assisting an offender and could be freed this December as part of the government’s early release scheme.

Henry’s family have slammed the decision as a “disgrace” as Henry’s mother told ITV News: “She hid the knife, which had Henry’s blood on it.”





Lucy Ross said the release date felt “particularly cruel” as it falls around the date her son was murdered.

“She’s lucky enough that she could go and see her boy. I have to go to Henry’s grave to see Henry,” she said.

Henry’s father, Mark Nowak, added that it was an “absolute disgrace”.

“She’ll be out for Christmas, and I won’t have Christmas with Henry.”

Meanwhile, Vickrum Digwa has launched a shameless bid to appeal his conviction and reduce his sentence, another decision Henry’s family said was “ludicrous”.



Digwa, 23, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years on June 1 for Henry’s murder and is held at HMP Frankland in County Durham.

But the court will also hear the appeal of Attorney General, Ellie Reeves, who claims the 23-year-old’s sentence was unduly lenient with both appeals to be heard this Thursday.

Henry’s stepmother, Katie Nowak said “it doesn’t feel fair” and it was “another fight we have to have”

“It was a clear verdict. It’s not right that he’s allowed to do this,” she said.

And commenting on Kaur being freed early, she said the process around the early release scheme “doesn’t feel like anyone’s on your side”.



The Sun has contacted the Ministry of Justice for comment.

Henry’s heartbroken family previously told of the “dreaded knock” from police which changed their lives forever.

And earlier this week, they accused cops of “manipulating” them after Henry died in handcuffs begging for his life.



Vickrum Digwa murdered Henry in Southampton last December as the first-year student walked home.

He stabbed him with a large Sikh dagger he held in a sheath – before then claiming he was the victim of a racist attack as Henry lay dying.

Digwa and his brother Gurpreet, 27, lied that finance student Henry was drunk, had shouted slurs and attacked Digwa, knocking off his turban.

In the police body-worn camera footage shown in court after his death, Mr Nowak can be heard repeating, “I’ve been stabbed”, to which an officer replies: “Don’t think you have, mate.”

Later that night, Kaur was arrested after hiding the blade when police finally realised what had happened.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last week, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood announced an independent review into Henry’s murder.

An upcoming review led by former lord chancellor Alex Chalk will look at “any missed opportunities to intervene”, she told the House of Commons.

News.title: Three Brit women vanish in South Africa after missing flight back to UK sparking frantic search
News.content:
FIND THEM Three Brit women vanish in South Africa after missing flight back to UK sparking frantic search







Next

THREE Brits have mysteriously vanished after missing their flight from South Africa back to the UK.

Police have launched a major search operation to find the missing women.



Liz Osbourne, her niece Kimberlee Langley and friend Mel Wright were due to return home at the start of this week.

But fears are growing after the trio, from Market Harborough, failed to land and have been unreachable to family members.



Liz’s daughter Courtney officially reported all three women as missing on November 4.

The trio of friends made the 6,000 mile journey over to South Africa on October 22.



The three women were expected to arrive back in the UK between October 30 and November 1 – but no one has heard from them since then.

It is understood that their return flight may have been diverted to France, according to Market Harborough FM, but this has not been confirmed.

The three women’s whereabouts are currently unknown.

In a heartbreaking plea, Liz’s daughter Courtney has called on the public to help find her missing mum.



Writing online she said: “My Mum Liz Osborne has been officially declared as a missing person.

“Along with my cousin Kimberlee Langley and Kim’s friend Mel Wright.

“It is originally believed that they left the country on 22nd October and was due to return around the 30.10.26/ 01.11.26



“Please if anyone has any information at all please contact me or the police as soon as possible.”
