News.title: Is America on the brink of sparking a new flu pandemic?
News.content:
Of the 75 human cases in the US, at least 50 have been linked directly to cattle farming, meaning the outbreak in cows has become the main route by which the virus is reaching people.

Most human cases linked to cattle have been mild, and far less dangerous than historic cases linked to infections from wild or farmed birds. Of the roughly 1,000 human cases of H5N1 linked to birds since it first emerged in China in 1997, around half have died.

But on November 1, the first person to be infected with the cow variant of H5N1, known as genotype B.13, was confirmed to have died.

The individual, who worked on a farm in Washington where at least 40 herds have been infected with H5N1, had underlying health conditions, which may have exacerbated the disease, and died shortly after becoming sick – but the development is still of concern, say experts.

“This goes against the pattern of mild disease when infected from dairy cattle, versus severe disease when infected from birds, which is worrying given the circulation in cattle,” said Dr Sridhar.

Reassortment risks

One of the biggest fears among scientists is that bird flu could combine with ordinary seasonal influenza to create a new strain capable of spreading easily between people.

“This is a time of year when we can expect to see more circulation of [human] seasonal influenza,” said Dr Marion Koopmans, professor of public health virology at Erasmus MC Medical Centre in the Netherlands.

“A bad scenario would be that someone working with cattle brought the ‘regular’ human flu in, got [H5N1] on top of that, and that develops into a mix that can spread but to which people have less immunity.

“The chances of such an event are very low, but it is a concern shared among virologists.”

The process, known as reassortment, occurs when two flu viruses infect the same animal or person and exchange genetic material, potentially creating a new strain.

Scientists are particularly concerned as H5N1 spreads beyond cattle and into other mammals – chiefly mink.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged on a Utah farm housing thousands of mink, according to an investigation by US news outlet ProPublica.

Mink farms have previously been described as potential pandemic “time bombs”, because their respiratory systems are similar to those of humans, meaning viruses spread easily between them and people.

Despite calls for the animals to be culled, Utah officials have so far refused to mandate action, ProPublica reported.

The investigation also suggested that state officials were prioritising the financial interests of the fur industry, which exports much of its produce to China and Russia, while federal authorities had failed to intervene.

News.title: Attacks on water infrastructure intensify in conflict zones, warns Unicef
News.content:
Water infrastructure is coming increasingly under attack in conflict zones, leading to disease outbreaks and forcing civilians to make dangerous journeys to fill buckets, according to a new report.

Water Under Fire, published by United Nations children’s agency Unicef, found that attacks have become “more frequent, varied and geographically widespread”.

It said the number of attacks that damaged or destroyed water systems tripled between 2021 and 2025.

Recorded incidents, ranging from strikes on water plants to restrictions on access to water treatment chemicals, rose from less than 45 in eight countries in 2021 to more than 135 in 15 nations by 2025, according to data from Insecurity Insight, a Geneva-based humanitarian organisation that tracks threats facing people in conflict.

Maia Giorgio, humanitarian policy specialist at Unicef, stressed that the report only covers documented attacks, warning that it may be “just the tip of the iceberg”.

“It’s a global phenomenon, and unfortunately, it’s under-documented,” she said.

“Without water, you don’t have a functioning healthcare system. Without water, you can’t prevent infectious disease, and we know that children are particularly vulnerable,” she added.

News.title: Man City have a striker who will not be stopped and a defence that cannot be trusted
News.content:
“You can look at it that it’s difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it’s only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance – you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option,” Haaland added.

This was a victory to bounce back from losing in the Premier League at the weekend, but the question will be how can City mount a title challenge with such a brittle defence. Champions League winners do not leave themselves open at the back like this, and City have now gone seven games without a clean sheet.

Maresca insisted last week that his starting line-up is Donnarumma plus 10 others, but the reality is that Haaland is the guaranteed name on the team sheet. And his goalkeeper’s errors are becoming a problem.

This one added to the goals against Aston Villa and Paris St-Germain that were also on his watch. He could have claimed the cross that led to Brighton’s winner at the weekend too.

Here he went from hero to villain in the space of a few minutes at the start of the second half. Firstly, from kick-off Christoph Baumgartner got close with his angled drive heading towards the top corner until Donnarumma’s fingertips turned the ball around the post. It was a save that had the Italian celebrating like he had scored a goal.

But he had his head in his hands after Leipzig’s next move. Nico O’Reilly could have done better after losing the ball in midfield, then failing to track the overlapping run from Baku. With Red Bull Arena waiting for a cross, Baku had spotted Donnarumma slightly out of position and beat him at the near post. It was superb improvisation, but without doubt a goalkeeping error.

News.title: Gyokeres the creator and executioner to see nervous Arsenal past Slavia Prague
News.content:
“Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”

Those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

“We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” said Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

The goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

News.title: Liverpool calamity hands Iraola his most chastening night yet
News.content:
Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found issue had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

News.title: Oil prices plunge after Republicans suffer midterms defeat
News.content:
Oil prices fell sharply after JD Vance blamed the Republicans’ election rout on the Iran war.

The price of a barrel of Brent, the global benchmark, fell as much as 10pc to $93 a barrel by Wednesday evening, while WTI was down more than 8pc to $88.

It marks the first time since Oct 7 that Brent has fallen below $100 a barrel.

The decline came after the vice president said that voters had abandoned the party owing to dissatisfaction with Donald Trump’s war in the Middle East.

This has boosted traders’ hopes that the US President could seek to de-escalate his conflict in the Gulf, which would increase global oil supplies.

Posting on social media, Mr Vance said: “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”

Mr Trump later admitted Mr Vance’s comments were “largely true”.

He said he expected oil prices to “go up a lot more” than they did because of the war, reaffirming that “Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon.”

“If I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again, because long term, it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.

“I thought the oil would go up a lot more, and I did it on that basis.

“You have no choice. You have to do it. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon, or everything that you see here someday might not exist.”

Traders also responded to the prospect that the Democrats could restrict Mr Trump’s funding for the war.

Claudio Galimberti, chief economist at Rystad Energy, said the President is now likely to come under “greater institutional pressure” to strike a peace deal with Iran.

This will ease pressure on economies around the world after oil prices have risen by roughly 70pc since the war broke out in February.

The Republican rout also prompted Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX to lose nearly $159bn (£118bn) in market value when trading opened in New York amid fears the Democrats’ success will derail the AI boom.

The carmaker and rocket company both fell 5.8pc as Wall Street opened after the Democrats swept to victory although they pared losses later.

Mr Musk, the billionaire boss of both companies, was the leading donor to the Republicans during the election campaign as he hoped for light-touch regulation of his AI ambitions.

However, analysts said the Democrat victory would slow down the pace of the rapid build-out of data centres.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the race for Texas Governor and is expected to oppose the rapid build-out of AI.

A sharp decline in the value of data-centre developers Tesla and SpaceX, both based in Texas, would wipe billions off Mr Musk’s nearly $900bn fortune. He spent $446m on backing failed Republican candidates.

As the Democrat victory emerged, Mr Musk wrote on X: “Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now.”

He later wrote: “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time.”

News.title: Ebola risk to UK remains ‘low’ despite evacuation of infected Briton
News.content:
Authorities have insisted that the risk to the UK is low after it emerged that a UK humanitarian worker infected with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Britain for treatment.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said it would not disclose the identity of the worker but confirmed a British citizen currently in the DRC has tested positive for the viral haemorrhagic fever.

“The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated. Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low,” the FCDO said in a statement.

The patient is due to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday, according to Reuters, and will be transferred to one of the UK’s high-consequence infectious disease units based at the Royal Free Hospital in London and the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle.

The worker had been responding to the outbreak currently raging in the Ituri region of DRC. The first cases of the Bundibugyo strain of the disease were first reported in May and there have now been more than 10,000 cases and 5,000 deaths.

It is the second largest outbreak in history and is taking place in a region racked with conflict and where mistrust of authorities is widespread.

Several aid agencies are working in the area including Médecins Sans Frontières, Oxfam and Unicef.

There are no specific treatments or vaccines for the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus and the backbone of treatment is supportive care. In July the World Health Organization launched the Partners trial in DRC to test whether the monoclonal antibody MBP134, the antiviral remdesivir, or a combination of both can improve survival. Another monoclonal antibody will soon be added to the study.

Researchers are also testing multiple vaccines, two of which were developed specifically for Bundibugyo. These are ChAdOx1, developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469.

News.title: Budget cuts and ministerial churn has weakened aid spending transparency, report finds
News.content:
The UK has become less transparent in how it spends its aid budget, amid repeated cuts and ministerial turnover, according to a new report.

The 2026 Aid Transparency Index, the world’s only independent peer-reviewed assessment on aid transparency evaluates how well major donors, development banks, and UN agencies disclose their spending and activity data. In the latest ranking the UK’s transparency score fell 13.9 points from “very good” to “good”.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) lost points for its lack of “comprehensive forward-looking country and organisational budgets and strategies, and project objectives”.

Twenty of the 33 ranked international organisations, over 60 per cent, scored “good” or “very good”, with just three rated “poor” or “very poor”. Germany, the US and the UK gave over 40 per cent of all overseas development aid in 2025, yet all three saw their transparency scores fall, according to the index.

“It’s not like [the FCDO] made a conscious decision to do anything badly or to miss anything… Our gut feeling is they’ve just taken their eye off the ball,” said Gary Forster, CEO of Publish What You Fund, a global campaign for aid and development transparency, which published the index.

“The FCDO hasn’t had a meaningful strategy since 2023,” he told The Telegraph.

For over two decades, the Department for International Development (DFID) operated as its own cabinet level ministry after it was set up in 1997 by Tony Blair, then Labour prime minister. In 2020, Conservative prime minister Boris Johnson merged it with the Foreign Office to create the FCDO.

The responsibility for aid was downgraded from a secretary of state to a minister of state position. Even then, there has been rapid ministerial turnover, with four international development ministers in the past two years.

The UK’s development budget, which funds programmes to tackle poverty and is a lifeline to millions around the world, has been repeatedly cut in recent years.

The UK historically prided itself on committing to spend 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on Official Development Assistance (ODA). In 2020 that figure was cut to 0.5 per cent and last year, Sir Keir Starmer, former prime minister, cut the target to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo RETIRES from Portugal in emotional announcement weeks after walking out on team following bust-up
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO has announced his retirement from international football.

The 41-year-old steps away from the Portuguese national team having scored 146 goals in 234 appearances.

He shared the news with an emotional social media video – just weeks after clashing with head coach Jorge Jesus.



Ronaldo said: “The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team.



“I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision. Because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.

“When I look back at everything with the national team, I don’t just see the matches, goals, records or trophies.

“I see people. I see the Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home.

“I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life.

“Because at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.”



Ronaldo made his international debut at the age of 18 in 2003 against Kazakhstan.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner has appeared at six World Cups and five European Championships.

The highlight of his international career was Portugal’s historic Euro 2016 win.

He started the final against France but was forced off in the 25th minute after suffering a knee injury.

The forward left the pitch in tears but spent the latter stages of the game instructing his team-mates from the sidelines before lifting the trophy.



Ronaldo’s last appearance for the national team came on September 24 against Wales in Lisbon.

MORE TO FOLLOW

Sports.title: Jesus de Miguel’s friend opens up on girlfriend’s agony as it emerges dad burst into tears seeing horror collision on TV
Sports.content:
Next

TRAGIC Tenerife star Jesus De Miguel’s friend has spoken about how the striker’s girlfriend was left alone to cope with the ordeal.

The footballer died from “accidental chest trauma” aged 30 on Tuesday morning, hours after a brutal collision with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono.



His funeral will be held today and pal Fernando Roman sat down for an emotional interview with Vamos a Ver where he revealed they had been planning a trip to take their kids to Disneyland.

Roman, who plays for Talavera, was not watching Monday’s Tenerife match and was told about the incident by his girlfriend.





He then spoke to De Miguel‘s partner Maria, who had been at the match with the couple’s one-year-old daughter Carla.

She told him that she had been alone at the hospital and the unfolding events had hit her ‘very hard.’

De Miguel’s parents later joined her after flying to the island upon learning that he was in intensive care.

Roman said in his interview: “Yesterday, my girlfriend and I were talking all afternoon and all night with María, his girlfriend, who was alone in the hospital.



“I’ve spoken with his girlfriend, and you can imagine how she is. Now we have to be with the family.

“We have to send our love to his family, to María, to his daughter Carla, who is a year and a few months old.

“It was unbelievable because we were talking about travelling to Disney with the girls, with my daughter too, and look what’s happened.”



Roman also paid tribute to De Miguel on social media.

He wrote: “My friend… I can’t believe you’re gone… you have no idea how much I’m going to miss you. I didn’t just consider you a friend; I considered you a member of my own family.

“You were always there to help me when I was struggling—you were by my side during my worst moments.

“Many people didn’t truly know you, but having known you, I can say you were one of the best people I’ve ever had in my life: humble, hardworking, never one to look for trouble.

“You brought happiness to everyone around you, and above all, you were a truly good person.



“All the moments we shared keep coming to mind… that trip to Punta Cana with the four of us – a trip I will never forget… all the lunches and dinners we enjoyed together, the time we spent with our daughters, the escape rooms we both loved so much…

“Tamara and I are absolutely devastated right now, but we know that from up above, you’ll still be with us—and, most importantly, with your daughter, with María, and with your entire family.

“My friend, I’m going to miss you so much… I love you dearly! REST IN PEACE!!”



A neighbour of the grieving parents told Y ahora Sonsoles that the footballer’s father began to cry after seeing the impact while watching the game on TV at his bar.

Pathologists have submitted their preliminary conclusions about the reasons for the 30-year-old’s passing in a report to an investigating court in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The chest trauma has been described in the preliminary report as a “cause consistent with the player’s death.”

Owono used “excessive force” while contesting the ball near the halfway line, according to the match referee’s report.

Sports.title: Sydney Thomas dresses as Erling Haaland in busty Man City crop top but fans brand one pic ‘terrifying’
Sports.content:
Next

SYDNEY THOMAS caused an unexpected fright after dressing as Manchester City striker Erling Haaland for Halloween.

The American, 22, went viral when she stole the show as a ring girl for Jake Paul’s boxing dust-up with Mike Tyson two years ago.



And Thomas treated her fans to some revealing snaps after deciding to don a Haaland-inspired costume.

The model wore a tight-fitting crop top in the style of City’s sky blue home kit while holding a glitzy football handbag.



Thomas, who soaked up the sun with model Hannah Palmer during a holiday in Ibiza during the summer, also wore a pair of tiny shorts and knee-high socks.

But she sensationally scared her 919,000 Instagram followers by uploading another photo and a video where she replaced her face with Haaland’s after using AI.

Thomas, who tagged the City marksman in the post, had fans racing into the comments section when they noticed the cheeky twist.

One said: “These are beautiful. That is until I hit the fourth slide and then again in the last one. Terrifying.”



Another added: “Slide four got me.”

A third follower who was caught out by the Haaland face swap chimed in: “Fourth pic threw me for a loop.”



A fourth noted: “This is too good omg.”

And a fifth claimed: “This was my favourite costume to ever exist.”

Former University of Alabama student Thomas showed off her physique when she jetted out to St Tropez in July.

And she has been keeping tabs on Haaland since he made a huge impact when her homeland co-hosted the World Cup.



The Norwegian, 26, raked in millions of new fans while shining in the summer extravaganza.

But his hopes of World Cup glory were ended when Jude Bellingham inspired England to a quarter-final win.

Sports.title: Dirk Kuyt, 46, immediately steps down as Fenerbahce manager after masterminding astonishing victory over Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

DIRK KUYT led Fenerbahce to a stunning 3-2 win against Liverpool on Wednesday – moments before stepping aside as head coach.

The 46-year-old was appointed interim boss of the Turkish club last week following the departure of Ismail Kartal.



His final game in charge was against his former club in the Champions League – and he left a lasting impression before making way for new head coach Emre Belozoglu.

Emre – who made 227 appearances for Fenerbahce as a player – was appointed as the club’s permanent boss on Tuesday night.



However, interim Kuyt was given the responsibility of managing the team against Liverpool.

The ex-winger said: “He wished me all the best for this game and I said to him, ‘I will make sure the team will have a good performance so you can have a good start.'”

Kuyt also said he would love to remain a coach at Fenerbahce, adding: “If the club and Coach Emre want me to stay here, I will continue to stay.

“I love Fenerbahce so much and of course I want to stay.”

Fenerbahce found themselves behind in the match against Liverpool when Trey Nyoni broke the deadlock in the 25th minute.

But striker Mason Greenwood equalised just moments later.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Alexander Isak fired the Reds back ahead in the second half, but goals from Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi turned the game on its head.

Kuyt later hailed it as “another miracle in Istanbul” as Fenerbahce moved up to 19th in the Champions League league phase.

He said: “It was a very special night, I think not only for me, but everyone who loves Fenerbahce.

“We told each other to stick together, to be united. And also to keep believing in ourselves, and that is something [which] I learned from another club [that] means a lot to me, and that was Liverpool, the club we played against tonight.

“So I’m very happy with all the players, I’m very happy with all the people who were involved that we made a miracle tonight.”



The Dutchman added: “Although we are in a very difficult situation, we have a chance to bring another miracle in Istanbul.

“And if you get that miracle, things can change in a positive way.

“But the reaction needs to come from us first … If you create that atmosphere, even the best team in the world can get difficulties.

“And I think the win tonight was not an easy win, but it was not luck. I think at the end of the day, we deserved it. We create many chances.

“We keep pushing and we keep fighting against, in my opinion, one of the best teams in Europe.”



Kuyt joined Liverpool from Feyenoord in 2006 – one year after the original ‘Miracle of Istanbul’ where the Reds came back from 3-0 down to beat AC Milan on penalties in the 2005 Champions League final.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He made 285 appearances for the Premier League giants across six years, scoring 71 goals and providing 40 assists.

The Dutchman then joined Fenerbahce in a permanent deal.

Sports.title: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta gives Ezri Konsa injury update after worrying sign during Slavia Prague Champions League win
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL are sweating on the fitness of Ezri Konsa ahead of Saturday’s clash with Hull.

The defender was forced off during the second half of the Gunners’ win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday night.



Konsa appeared to be holding his knee early in the game, but played on before coming off just after the hour mark.

Mikel Arteta said: “Obviously he’s playing a lot. He’s played so many games in the last few weeks and he had some issues and we decided to take him off.”



Arsenal will hope the injury is not serious as they are hosting Hull in the Premier League on Saturday.

The Gunners do, at least, have William Saliba back to full fitness for the first time this season.



The France star has been out since the summer after aggravating a back issue at the World Cup.

Saliba was on the bench for the win at Prague, but he did not get on the pitch as Cristhian Mosquera replaced Konsa.

Speaking about the win, Arteta said: “Always we need to value winning away in the Champions League.

“It is extremely difficult. This was two very different halves. We should have had three or four goals in the first half but we didn’t do it.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Right at the start of the second half we were on the back foot, very sloppy and gave balls away. Then we had to suffer. A lot to learn.

“We should have scored more in the first half and if we didn’t do that we had to go and do that in the second half.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane becomes highest paid player in EUROPE as he signs new Bayern Munich contract days after winning Ballon d’Or

HARRY KANE has become the HIGHEST-PAID player in Europe – just over a week after winning the Ballon d’Or.

The 33-year-old pipped Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the most prestigious individual award in football last week.



He bagged the gong after an incredible season for club and country, in which he scored a whopping 73 GOALS.

And his 61-goal haul for Bayern Munich, which helped fire them to a domestic treble, has resulted in the Bundesliga big boys giving him a new bumper contract.



Kane has signed a new three-year deal with the German side, which will keep him at the Allianz Arena until June 2029.

And the England captain is delighted to have committed what could be the final years of his career to them.

He said: “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich.

“We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager.



“It makes me very proud to be part of this club.

“My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay.

Sports.title: Man Utd unlikely to appoint interim should they sack Carrick
Sports.content:
Manchester United are unlikely to appoint another interim head coach, Sky Sports News has been told, if they decide to replace Michael Carrick in the coming weeks.

There is still support for Carrick among the United hierarchy, and a lingering concern that changing the head coach won't necessarily change the team's fortunes.

The Champions League victory over Roma on Tuesday night has provided some respite, and boosted belief in the changing room and the boardroom. It was their first win in 10 matches in all competitions.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United's Michael Carrick hailed the second performance of his team after they came back from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League

However, there is a realisation that one win on its own isn't enough to turn a season around. United remain 17th in the Premier League, only outside the relegation places on goal difference. And the nature of the victory against Roma was chaotic.

Whilst the character of the team to come back from 2-0 down suggests the players are still behind Carrick, it took a re-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty to turn the tide, and United's bosses still have doubts about the team's direction and lack of consistency.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Dawson reflects on Manchester United's 3-2 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League

Carrick was given the top job on a two-year basis in May, after a brilliant record as interim United head coach that secured Champions League football. There was a clamour from United fans for their former midfielder to be given the role substantively.

Nevertheless, United's bosses were determined to carry out a period of due diligence when they did speak to other candidates before appointing Carrick. And it's thought United wouldn't want to repeat that process of having an interim head coach, as they try to take a longer-term strategy over their most important football role.

Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, who run United's football operations, are still considering other options, should they feel they need to make a change. And with the international break next week offering a chance to take a breath and reassess, there is a feeling that Super Sunday's game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford is a key one for Carrick's future.

Manchester United

Aston Villa Sunday 8th November 4:25pm Kick off 4:30pm

The fact that Sunday's opponents have now announced they are close to agreeing a new long-term contract with Unai Emery - and a new long-term strategy with the Spaniard and his staff at the heart of the club's planning - comes as a blow to Manchester United.

Emery was high up on United's list of potential future targets, with admiration for the way he has twice secured Champions League football and also the club's first European trophy in over four decades, with victory in the Europa League in May. However, there has always been a realisation that it would be difficult - and expensive - to try to get Emery out of Villa Park, especially mid-season, with Villa's owners adamant he is going nowhere.

As a result, United's bosses have remained open-minded about other potential candidates, with Julian Nagelsmann, Fabian Hurzeler and Eddie Howe prominent in their thinking.

So far, United have not spoken directly to any other coach, with the feeling that there is no current vacancy. The preferred option on all sides is that results improve, and Carrick remains in charge of the team.

Sports.title: From forgettable EFL loans to Ballon d'Or winner - Kane's 'Cinderella story'
Sports.content:
From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale.

"This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports.

"He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking: 'Are we talking about the same kid?'

"There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further.

"I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest."

The Bayern Munich striker has become the first English Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years and just the fifth in its history.

The last English winner, Michael Owen, had a simpler route to the top, winning it aged 22 in 2001, just four years after his senior debut at Liverpool.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane said winning this year's Ballon d'Or was 'beyond his wildest dreams' and was happy to put England 'back on the map' by being the first Englishman to win the trophy in 25 years

Kane's win has come at the age of 33, some 15 years after his senior debut on loan at Leyton Orient in League One.

"We have to highlight his journey," says Sherwood, who Kane thanked on stage when collecting the Ballon d'Or.

Image: Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or at a ceremony in London

"Even when we go back to Michael [Owen], he was a superstar as a kid, and he got the opportunities at a very young age at Liverpool, which is a giant football club.

"Kane came through the hard way, really. He was a player who wasn't universally loved.

"He's not like a Max Dowman, for instance, who is a superstar at 16 years of age.

"He [Kane] struggled to get some game time and to get a manager to really buy into what he had."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kane spoke exclusively to Sky Sports the morning after being voted as the best footballer in the world

Kane even mentioned his tough path to the top in his Ballon d'Or acceptance speech.

He said: "My journey wasn't straightforward; I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now."

For Sherwood, it was those low-key loan spells at Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester that have turned Kane into the world's top player.

"I hear a lot of people talking about failed loans," he says, "but we never felt like that because we felt that him playing in U21 football was a waste of time.

"They were really good loans, and those loans were the reason why we've got a player like that."

Kane's 'sliding doors' moment

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at all of Kane's Bundesliga goals for Bayern Munich last season

Kane was out in the cold at Spurs until Andre Villas-Boas' sacking, when Sherwood's subsequent arrival opened the door.

He handed Kane his first Premier League start - and the then-20-year-old took his chance as he scored the opener in a 5-1 home win over Sunderland in April 2014.

"He wasn't getting anywhere unfortunately," Sherwood says. "He wasn't around the first-team squad, so I suppose it's a sliding doors moment that I managed to take over until the end of the season and I managed to give him a stage where he could perform."

And perform he has.

Kane has hit nearly 550 goals for club and country to become Tottenham's record scorer, England's all-time scorer, England's leading World Cup scorer and the top English scorer in Champions League history.

His incredible goalscoring feats hit new heights last season as he plundered 73 goals in all competitions.

Sixty-one of those came for Bayern in all competitions, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues last season. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.

For Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher, Kane's £100m move from Spurs to Bayern in the summer of 2023 has allowed him global recognition and respect.

"It's a move he needed to make," Carragher tells Sky Sports.

"I thought he might be obsessed with the Premier League goalscoring record, but he's obsessed with goalscoring records, not just that one.

"But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections.

"There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham."

'Kane is an example to all young kids'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Kane's best 'clutch' moments for Tottenham and Bayern

The Bayern move has delivered the trophies Kane so desperately craved.

Despite winning three Premier League Golden Boots at Spurs and becoming their all-time top scorer, personal honours were never the aim of the game for Kane, according to Sherwood.

His trophyless career at N17 is what drove Kane to join Bayern, where he has won back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a German Cup.

"The boy loves Tottenham," Sherwood says. "He wanted to win there, but he was winning individual accolades at Spurs, and it wasn't enough for him.

"When we all grow up, we all want to be footballers, and we don't want to be footballers because we want to be rich. There are possibly some players like that now, but that certainly wasn't his motivation.

"He wanted to go to a team that could win, and he picked Bayern, and we have to say it's been a good choice."

Sherwood adds: "He's a 100 per cent team man. If I told you he would rather win the Champions League and the Bundesliga title than the Ballon d'Or for himself, that would be the truth.

"Not every player would say that, but I genuinely believe that that is the measure of the man and that's what you're talking about, and that's why he's such a dream to manage.

"The work rate and the example he shows to any young kids coming through, and to genuinely go around the houses to try and make it, and he certainly made it."

Is Kane England's greatest-ever player?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett debates whether or not Kane is the greatest England player of all time

Kane continues to break record after record in Germany.

He is the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, has the most goals in his first 100 Bundesliga appearances and is the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goal contributions.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Kane score his 150th Bundesliga goal for Bayern Munich

It is that last stat where Kane has proven he is more than just a goal scorer. His excellent vision, awareness and superb passing range make him an exquisite playmaker.

This was on show recently in Bayern's 2-2 Champions League home draw against Arsenal as Kane, who spent much of the game dropping deep, sumptuously set up Alphonso Davies for an equaliser with a pinpoint ball from inside the centre circle.

His assist ability has been on display for years, where at Spurs he claimed the Premier League Playmaker of the Season award in the 2020/21 campaign.

So, does his all-round game combined with his records and this Ballon d'Or prize make him England's greatest player? Not for Carragher, who puts a fellow English Ballon d'Or winner ahead of him.

"I would still always put Bobby Charlton as the greatest England player ever," he says.

"He's won the World Cup. He's won the Champions League with Manchester United. As a midfield player, he was the leading goalscorer for a very long time for both United and England.

"I'd still always say Bobby Charlton, because right now this England team, even though it's been a golden period for us, Harry Kane and the others still haven't got their hands on a trophy, and that's what Bobby Charlton did."

Could Kane return to Spurs?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kane has previously revealed he no longer feels the need to return to the Premier League

Kane, who needs just one cap to become England's most-capped player, signed a new Bayern deal 10 days after winning his Ballon d'Or.

But despite committing to the German champions for another three years until the summer of 2029, Sherwood believes there is a longer-term goal in Kane's thinking.

"I believe he will come back for that individual accolade to be the Premier League top scorer in the future, maybe in a couple of years' time," the ex-Premier League-winning captain says.

Kane is 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's all-time Premier League record of 260 goals.

"He will only come back to a team he believes can win," says Sherwood. "At the moment you're looking at Manchester City with the troubles they've got, so Liverpool possibly, that could be a chance for him.

"Tottenham could be in the frame if they start progressing. Manchester United could be in the frame, but they've got a long way to go to prove that they can win anything as well.

"I'm not sure it's ever going to be Chelsea or Arsenal because of the Tottenham connection.

"It's on a positive note for Tottenham fans if they can start progressing and you can prove to him that he can come back and he can possibly have a good chance of winning at your club as he will have at Liverpool, Manchester United and Manchester City - but we don't know what's going to happen with them - then there's an opportunity he might come back and see out his career where he started it."

It seems a fitting final chapter in Kane's Cinderella story.

Sports.title: Carra: Young guns starring shows Liverpool haven't spent money well enough
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher called Liverpool's recruitment into question after their 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

The Reds were 2-1 up with 20 minutes to play in Istanbul but went on to lose 3-2 in a game where teenagers Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha again starred.

Nyoni scored the opener and Alexander Isak hit the second, but Bradley Barcola extended his run of scoring in just one of his 13 appearances for the club so far.

Image: Liverpool twice gave up the lead to lose at Fenerbahce in the Champions League

"It [defeat to Fenerbahce] reinforces to supporters that the squad Liverpool have got is very expensive, but not as good as it should be and not as balanced as it should be," said Carragher, speaking on CBS Sports.

"When you think of some of those players that have come in, what's a little worry for not so much the manager, but the people who run the club... Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha were the best players for Liverpool, and they were a week or so ago against Chelsea.

"But they also play in the position of players where Liverpool have spent big money.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bradley Barcola discusses his £123m move to Liverpool, PSG exit and more!

"Bradley Barcola has come in for £120m. He played up front tonight, didn't play well, but the younger players are playing better than him.

"And in Nyoni in midfield; Liverpool haven't spent expensively on a player as such, but they've given big contracts this summer to Ryan Gravenberch - who was left out at the weekend for Nyoni - and Szoboszlai who played tonight and didn't play particularly well.

"You can imagine the type of figures they would be on and when a young player in midfield is playing ahead of them that causes a problem about where you've spent your money - and you basically haven't spent your money well enough."

Liverpool's spending over the last three seasons

2024/25: Federico Chiesa (£12.5m)

2025/26: Alexander Isak (£125m), Florian Wirtz (£116m), Hugo Ekitike (£79m), Milos Kerkez (£40m), Jeremie Frimpong (£29.5m), Giorgi Mamardashvili (£29m), Giovanni Leoni (£26m), Armin Pesci (£1.5m), Freddie Woodman (Free)

2026/27: Bradley Barcola (£123m), Jeremy Jacquet (£60m), Victor Munoz (£34.5m), Ifeanyi Ndukwe (Undisclosed)

Youthful attack let down by experienced defence

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was left frustrated after his side conceded some 'messy goal's' during their 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce, although he admitted the atmosphere made it difficult for his players to communicate

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

The average age of Liverpool's starting front three was less than 22. The average age of their defence was just shy of 30.

On a European night and in a hostile environment, you'd expect it would be the experienced heads who stepped up. But the opposite was the case in Istanbul.

Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni stole the show on the night where he became the club's second-youngest Champions League goalscorer. Meanwhile, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz had their moments threatening the Fenerbahce backline.

Yet, at the back, Liverpool looked stuck in the mud. The state of the wall for Fenerbahce's first was well below par and Jacquet paid the price with the deflection. The marking and miscommunication that led to the second was also shocking to see.

But the third was the biggest failure. With the ball high in the sky, Muriqi drifted away from Virgil van Dijk, beat three static red shirts and headed past Alisson.

If Iraola was looking for a response after the defeat at Anfield, he would have been banking on that back five to be the leading lights within one. Instead, they are the reason he has suffered back-to-back defeats for the first time since taking the Anfield hot seat.

Sports.title: Former F1 world champion Jones dies aged 80
Sports.content:
Alan Jones remains the last Australian to win the F1 drivers' championship; he triumphed in 1980 while racing for Williams; Jones won 12 grands prix across his F1 career

Former Formula 1 world champion Alan Jones has died at the age of 80 following a brief illness.

A statement from Jones' family, issued through Motorsport Australia, announced the death of the 1980 championship winner - who remains the last Australian to win the F1 title.

Jones was only the second Australian to win the championship after Sir Jack Brabham, and topped the podium at 12 grands prix during a career that took in spells with Hesketh, Williams - with whom he won his title - and Arrows.

Sports.title: Fifa wants to restrict women’s Olympic football to under-23s in controversial move
Sports.content:
Fifa wants the International Olympic Committee to restrict the women’s Olympic football tournament to under 23s owing to concerns over fixture congestion and the workload of senior players.

The eligibility criteria for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles has been set, with qualification tournaments having begun in some regions, so no change can be made until Brisbane 2032 at the earliest, but sources at both organisations have told the Guardian that they are open to dialogue.

Although no formal proposal has been made, Fifa is understood to be interested in examining the matter in talks with the IOC and other key stakeholders, such as the players and leading member associations whose national sides routinely qualify for the Games.

A move to bring in age restrictions would dramatically alter the nature of the event and require careful analysis, consultation and consideration through Fifa and IOC processes.

Such a change would be controversial and could provoke a backlash from leading international players because the Olympics has long been regarded as one of the highlights of the women’s calendar, with Emma Hayes’s United States team securing gold in Paris two years ago. The Olympic title has been contested eight times and the US have won five.

Women’s football also has a major commercial appeal for the IOC, particularly in markets such as the US, Europe and Australia, so it may resist Fifa’s overtures.

Women’s football was introduced to the Olympics at Atlanta in 1996, and as an amateur sport at that time never had eligibility requirements, in contrast to the men’s game.

After admitting football to the Olympic programme in 1908 the IOC did not permit professionals to take part until 1984 owing to Fifa’s insistence on maintaining the primacy of the World Cup, as well as the demands on players from a congested calendar. Under pressure from Fifa the IOC introduced an under-23 age restriction in 1992, although three overage players have also been allowed in each squad since 1996.

The huge growth and professionalisation of the women’s game over the past decade has created increased fixture congestion, with the 2028 calendar the most bloated yet.

Fifa is to a large extent culpable for this because the world governing body has chosen to launch the Women’s Club World Cup in an Olympic year, with the US to stage the 16-team competition between 5 and 30 January, six months before the Games.

The Women’s Club World Cup will cause major disruption to the European club season, with Arsenal and Chelsea or Manchester City likely to be absent from domestic competition for up to a month if they reach the latter stages, missing four Women’s Super League matches and the FA Cup fourth round.

The importance of the sport to the IOC is shown by the fact that the women’s football tournament will be bigger than the men’s for the first time in LA, featuring 16 teams to 12 in a reversal of the numbers at Paris 2024.

Fifa and the IOC declined to comment.

Sports.title: Japan FA head Kozo Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency
Sports.content:
The Japan Football Association president, Kozo Tashima, ⁠has said he will run for the ⁠Fifa ​presidency in March.

Gianni Infantino, ⁠who is seeking re-election, has faced opposition since his failed ⁠move in July to bring ​private investors into ‌a new ‌Fifa commercial entity holding rights linked ‌to competitions including the World Cup.

Tashima told Sports Nippon: “I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the JFA. It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying ​to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What Fifa ⁠needs now are these values that ​we ​have protected. I ​have decided to run in ​order ‌to make ​this ​appeal to the world.”

Quick Guide How do I 

The 68-year-old Tashima is a former Japan player who has been on Fifa’s ruling committee since 2015, when Sepp Blatter was president. He has a reputation as a respected, diplomatic and low-profile official in the often murky world of football politics.

Candidates need formal support from five of Fifa’s 211 member federations, who will vote on 18 March in Rabat, Morocco. They must also pass an eligibility check by a three-member panel appointed by Fifa.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls time on Portugal career after 234 caps and 146 goals
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his intention to retire ⁠from the Portugal national team in a social media post, ⁠bringing to ⁠an ​end one of the most illustrious international careers in ⁠football.

The 41-year-old said he would “hand back the No 7 shirt” after the November ⁠international break. Ronaldo captained the team to their first ​major trophy at Euro ‌2016 and ‌helped them win the 2019 and 2025 Nations ‌Leagues.

“It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. They are also made with the heart,” he said. “If I ever made you ‌happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a ​worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.”

Ronaldo thanked his family, the Portuguese people and the teammates, coaches and ⁠staff he worked with over his 23-year ​career with ​national team. “Portugal will always ​be a part of me,” he ​captioned the ‌announcement video.

Ronaldo ​has made ​234 appearances for Portugal and scored 146 goals. He holds the all-time record for men’s international appearances and for international goals.

Sports.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
Sports.content:
Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier.

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments.

“Of course, we plan to submit documents,” the Sevastopol CEO Valery Chaly told local media last month. “According to the regulations we should advance to the next stage.” The RFU remains a member of Uefa and Fifa but there would be fresh calls for it to be ejected if Sevastopol’s ascent is not blocked. It is understood no decision about their potential admission has been made.

Football’s governing bodies were given a similar dilemma in 2023 when Sevastopol and another Crimean club, Rubin Yalta, were accepted into FNL 2B even though sides from the occupied territory have not been allowed to compete in Russia since its annexation in 2014.

The Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) asked Uefa and Fifa to consider ejecting Russia, alleging a “gross violation” of their statutes and Uefa’s ruling, made in 2014, that Crimean clubs must not compete in RFU-run events. Uefa claimed it would assess the situation but the authorities appeared to turn a blind eye, the RFU saying it had created a workaround by making FNL 2B an amateur competition that it did not operate. At the time, several clubs at that level contacted by the Guardian confirmed informally that they were fully professional. No such blurring of the lines exists for FNL 2A, which has never denied its clubs are professional.

That unwillingness to act led to escalation when, in April 2024, an imitation of the Ukrainian club Zorya Luhansk – whose home city in Donbas is illegally occupied by Russia – was admitted to FNL 2B. This year they were joined by a fake Shakhtar Donetsk, mimicking the current Champions League side who have been forced to play elsewhere since 2014. Five of the 15 teams who completed the recent FNL 2B group one season played in or claimed to represent occupied areas, the Simferopol-based club Kyzyltash Bakhchisaray completing the quintet.

View image in fullscreen FC Sevastopol’s logo at their home in Crimea. Photograph: Vasiliy Batanov/AFP/Getty Images

Should the RFS decide, of its own accord or under pressure from international bodies, to bar Sevastopol from promotion an even bigger flashpoint may await. The imitation Shakhtar finished runners-up in group 1, securing that spot by winning 2-0 at Sevastopol on the season’s final day last Saturday, and are next in line to go up. Unlike Sevastopol their home matches are played on Russian territory, in Taganrog, rather than an occupied area. The club is, however, registered to an address in Donetsk.

In October 2025 the UAF asked Uefa to review and explain the imitation clubs’ legal positions but, as with any assessment of the Crimean clubs’ participation, the results are still awaited. It warned of a“coordinated political attempt to legitimise the occupation and erase the identity of Ukrainian football”.
