Last month Russia competed in a Fifa-run event for the first time since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, finishing 19th in the new under-15 World Cup. Teams at under-15 and under-16 levels have continued to play in smaller Uefa development tournaments, largely against invited opponents on home soil, during the war in Ukraine.

None of Uefa, Fifa, the RFU, the FNL, Sevastopol or the imitation Shakhtar Donetsk offered comment when contacted by the Guardian.

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane signs new contract with Bayern through to 2029
Sports.content:
England captain and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane has signed a new deal with Bayern Munich through to 2029, the German club have announced.

Kane moved to Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 for a record €100m fee and has proved a huge success, scoring 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances and leading the German club to two Bundesliga titles and a DFB Cup.

The 33-year-old was named as the world’s best male player last week after scoring a remarkable 89 goals for club and country since the start of August 2025, becoming the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years and the first Bayern player since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981 to win the award.

“I feel right at home at FC Bayern,” said Kane. “I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

In September, Kane became the fastest player in German history to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, doing so in 98 games to shatter the previous record set by Dieter Mueller in 1977 by 31 games.

1:27 Harry Kane ends England's 25-year wait for a Ballon d'Or winner – video

Bayern did not disclose ⁠financial details of the agreement. However, German media reported that the extension is ​the most lucrative contract ​in the club’s history and part ​of a long-term commitment to the England captain.

“We’re absolutely delighted, because with Harry Kane we have the Ballon d’Or winner on the pitch – a team player, a leader, the best all-round striker in the world,” said Christoph Freund, Bayern’s sporting director. “We all benefit from his qualities as a player and as a person, day in, day out. FC Bayern thrives on players who never stop giving their all, even when they have already achieved the greatest of goals.”

This month Kane equalled England’s all-time men’s caps record, while nudging his international goal tally to 91 in 125 appearances.

Sports.title: ‘In our veins’: Arsenal pushed by pain of Champions League final defeat, says Raya
Sports.content:
David Raya has said Arsenal are using the pain of losing on penalties against Paris Saint-Germain in last year’s Champions League final to “make it better this year”.

The Spain goalkeeper produced an outstanding save to help Arsenal hold off Slavia Prague on Wednesday as Mikel Arteta’s side moved up to third in the league standings with 10 points from four matches.

Arsenal will face Borussia Dortmund next at home this month before hosting Real Madrid on 9 December in a showdown that could be vital to their chances of finishing in the top two and ensuring the second leg of their first knockout tie and any that follow would be at the Emirates.

That was the case last season when Arsenal became the first team to win all eight league stage matches and made it to the final in Budapest. Raya has admitted he is haunted by that experience as PSG won back-to-back titles.

“I think it is never going to be out of the system,” he said. “It is something that is going to live with us and hopefully we can win the Champions League to get that out of us. But it has to be in our veins. It has to be on us to make it better this year.”

Raya came to Arsenal’s rescue as Slavia valiantly attempted to fight back from 2-0 down at the break. His diving stop to keep out Oskar Kubiak’s header helped to make it 10 away games in Europe without defeat. Raya, who missed out on the Yashin award for best goalkeeper at the Ballon d’Or to his Spain teammate Unai Simón, credited his self-belief as key to making extraordinary saves on a regular basis.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Belief is really important but hard work [is, too],” he said. “I work very hard during the week to try and help the team as much as possible on these types of nights. It is just the belief that I have in myself, and the belief the staff, the goalie coach, has in me and the team. That gives you that extra edge and motivation to keep doing it every single week, and the consistency I have been playing with throughout the years is a key factor for us.”

Sports.title: Bournemouth’s decision not to panic after their tough start is paying off
Sports.content:
It would have been easy, understandable even, for Bournemouth fans to feel down and worried. Their revered head coach, Andoni Iraola, had left in the summer and his replacement, Marco Rose, had not got off to a great start. Three defeats and three draws was all they had to show from their first six league matches, and whispers about Rose’s future had begun in the media.

But Bournemouth fans know it can take a while for new ideas and methods to yield positive results. Iraola didn’t win any of his first nine Premier League games in charge of the club and he ended up having a remarkable impact.

Still, the outlook wasn’t great after Bournemouth were hammered 5-1 by Chelsea. But Rose maintained his level-headedness. He had been adamant until that point that Bournemouth’s performances had been better than results suggested. “It’s about results at this level. But performance-wise, I see a lot of good things,” he said.

Rose was much less understanding after the hammering at Stamford Bridge, but again there were still reasons to think the result was harsh. Chelsea’s five goals came from only 1.1 expected goals (xG). The standard of their finishing was incredibly high at times, with Jordan Henderson scoring twice from outside the box (one a free-kick) and João Pedro rifling emphatically into the roof of the net from a Pedro Neto cut-back. And Morgan Rogers’ effort was helped by a deflection. Bournemouth created opportunities, with a greater xG total (1.38) than their hosts, but ended up on the end of a hiding.

The one-sided result was something of a novelty, but the overriding sense that Bournemouth had been unlucky was familiar. Not much had gone their way in the five matches before that. In their defeat at Manchester City on the opening weekend, Bournemouth led 1-0 until the 84th minute, before losing 2-1.

In their second match of the season, they were denied by a 90th-minute equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Everton. “As a coach, you evaluate the performance as well as the result, and in most phases of the game it was really good,” Rose said. “I don’t want to blame anyone because I saw so many positive things.” Next up, an 88th-minute leveller rescued Newcastle a 2-2 draw from 2-0 down at St James’ Park. And in their fourth match of the season, Bournemouth led twice against Brentford but had to settle for a 2-2 draw after individual errors from Adrien Truffert and Djordje Petrovic.

Rose continued to focus on the positives. There was an acceptance that results needed to catch up eventually, though he liked a lot of what he was watching. “I’m really happy with the confidence the lads came here today to take the three points,” he said after the Newcastle draw. Even after the loss to Liverpool left them with only three points from a possible 15, Rose cut an optimistic figure, saying: “We played a good game against Liverpool. They had some days more to recover, and I think we looked fit, even at the end. We were the team that went for a goal.”

Bournemouth won the “xG battle” four times in their first six matches. That obviously doesn’t count for much in real terms, but it shows that they were creating more high-value opportunities than their opponents. Their position of 18th in the table was not a clear reflection of their performances. “We can see the table. Now it’s up to us to prove we can handle the situation,” Rose challenged his players after the Chelsea loss.

We can use expected points (xPts) to support the idea that Bournemouth’s position was false. Our xPts model uses xG data from each match to calculate how games “deserved” to finish based on the quality and quantity of chances at each end. Although Bournemouth were in the relegation zone with three points, their 8.4 xPts put them comfortably in mid-table.

Rose’s optimistic appraisals should not be overlooked as standard post-match managerial guff either. There’s an argument his positivity and clarity played a big role in helping the Bournemouth players appreciate they were on the right track even when results were underwhelming. The worry was the team could lose confidence and sink, but hindsight suggests the coach did well to mitigate such a threat.

Since the defeat to Chelsea, Bournemouth have played six and won six in all competitions. They have scored 16 goals from 16.4 xG and allowed their opponents chances worth only 0.81 xG on average – and, crucially, Henderson’s free-kick at Stamford Bridge was the last goal they conceded. They have beaten Sturm Graz and Milan in the Europa League, Aston Villa in the League Cup, and Sunderland, Manchester United and Leeds in the Premier League.

Their recent fixtures have been slightly kinder given they played City, Newcastle, Liverpool and Chelsea – three of which were away – during their first six Premier League outings. But Milan and Leeds both made decent starts to the season, Villa have been resurgent of late, and wins at Old Trafford can never be taken for granted.

The outlook for Bournemouth is now considerably different in the Premier League. Those three wins have lifted them to eighth in the table, and because their recent victories have been so comprehensive, they’ve absolutely shot up the xPts table as well. Only Arsenal (18.2), Man City (17.1) and Nottingham Forest (15.5) can better Bournemouth’s 15.4 xPts over the full season to date.

It’s been an impressive transformation but Rose isn’t trying to take the credit. “I would love to say I’m a magician and I changed some good stuff, but sometimes it’s just about getting this kind of experience, and then if you react well that’s always the most important thing,” he mused before the Leeds win. “You can make mistakes – you can lose, you can have a bad day – but the reaction is the most important thing, and I think we showed a good reaction. We didn’t lack much, and now we just have the last ​5​% in everything.”

Evanilson finding some form in front of goal has helped, with the Brazilian scoring in each of his past four league outings, his four goals coming from 2.8 xG. Bournemouth have also limited their opposition’s flow of high-quality chances. And their upcoming fixture list looks kind.

Over the next five matches, only Coventry and Aston Villa have more straightforward schedules than Bournemouth according to our rankings. Their climb could yet continue.

Bournemouth’s surge up the table shows how quickly a club’s fortunes can change, and it’s evidence of how patience can be rewarded when it might be easier to panic. Rose may not feel as though he has changed much, but ensuring his team retained belief when heads might have dropped is as valuable as any tactical alteration.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Goalkeeper Jesús Owono experiencing ‘hardest days of my life’ after De Miguel’s death
Sports.content:
The FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after he was involved in the collision that led to the death of the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel.

Owono had raced out of his goal and crashed into De Miguel in added time at the end of the Spanish second division match on Monday afternoon, causing the striker to experience a cardiorespiratory arrest. De Miguel was taken to hospital in Santa Cruz de Tenerife but never regained consciousness and died on Tuesday morning.

“These are being the hardest days of my life,” Owono said in a statement published by Andorra. “I find it hard to find the words and very difficult to assimilate what has happened. I feel a huge pain, the loss of Jesús. I am thinking about him, his family and all the people who loved him.

“I know that there will be many questions to address and I will face up to whatever comes with respect. But right now, sincerely, I cannot think about anything other than Jesús and the pain that we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesús.”

Andorra’s statement said that the club remained “deeply affected” by De Miguel’s death and demanded “the greatest respect and sensibility”. The homicide division of the Spanish national police opened an investigation, which is standard procedure in Spain whenever there is a death not by natural causes. Santa Cruz de Tenerife’s chief prosecutor, José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui, told the Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings against the goalkeeper were “very unlikely”.

The investigation will focus on the events that preceded De Miguel’s death, including the attention he received after medics sprinted on to the pitch. De Miguel was treated on the field for five minutes before being taken off on a stretcher and to an ambulance that waited in the corner. Tenerife had reported that medics were able to recover a pulse in the ambulance before he was admitted to intensive care.

View image in fullscreen Jesús Owono ‘would never intentionally hurt anyone’ one of his Andorra teammates said. Photograph: Walter Cunha/NurPhoto/Getty Images

“We can’t say if they acted correctly or incorrectly, but we can demand that all the emergency procedures follow international standards of correct practice,” Elvira González, the president of Spain’s Association of Nurses, Emergency Medics and Caregivers, told the Associated Press. “There is contradictory information. The first thing we need to know is where and when he supposedly recovered a pulse. The first minutes are critical. You can only move a person once a pulse is restored.”

Tenerife’s majority shareholder, Rayco García, told Cadena Ser radio: “There are those who say that the impact caused his death, and that later they were able to stabilise him artificially even though it was very difficult to bring him back. I prefer to wait for the autopsy and then we can take steps. I would like to see [the results of] the investigation to know if there is something to ensure this doesn’t happen again, something that could have prevented this tragedy.”

Owono had earlier been defended by his teammate Lautaro Spatz, who wrote on social media: “I also ‌want to say a few words about my teammate, goalkeeper ‌and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he ‌would never intentionally hurt anyone. In football, unfortunate incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Equatoguinean Football Federation expressed its support, saying that Owono, who has 47 caps for the country, was going through a situation of profound sorrow and grief. He was subsequently left out of Equatorial Guinea’s squad ⁠for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers this month against Zimbabwe.

Owono was sent off for the challenge and immediately walked towards the touchline, only to turn back as staff began running in the other direction. The goalkeeper deactivated his Instagram account on Tuesday after receiving abuse online, with some users commenting “murderer” on his posts. Andorra said they were offering psychological support to anyone at the club who needed it after De Miguel’s death. The Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, had said they would need “professional help”.

De Miguel, 30, was married and had an 18-month-old child, both of whom were in the stadium when the incident happened. Flowers have been left at the stadium by gate nine, his shirt number, and a minute’s silence was held at the Canarian government building.

De Miguel’s body laid at the Tanatorio Santa Lastenia funeral parlour in Santa Cruz before being flown to the Spanish mainland on Wednesday afternoon. Tenerife’s players and staff will fly to Madrid on a charter on Thursday morning and go from there to the village of Navahermosa in Toledo province, where De Miguel’s parents are from, for the funeral. A final homage will be held at Tenerife’s Heliodoro Rodriguez López stadium on Saturday evening.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty with emotional five-minute statement
Sports.content:
The Portugal hero posted a five-minute clip on social media, which is translated from Portuguese below.

To the Portuguese, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of the national team to all of us.

I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility to wear it, to defend it and to take it with me to the stadiums all over the world. Today the time has come to give it to the future.

It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not taken only with the head, they are also taken with the heart.

I finish a journey that started in August 2003 and changed my life forever. When I look back and think about everything I lived in the national team, I do not see only games, goals, records or trophies. I see people.

I see immigrants who for 90 minutes felt Portugal a little closer. I see millions of Portuguese that I never met personally, but who were part of my life. Because after all, football is much bigger than a game. Football is people.

Throughout my career in the national team I tried to overcome my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be the best, I wanted to make history. I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed that we could go further.

And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories that I will never forget. There were defeats that I still have a hard time remembering today.

I also failed, I also suffered, there were also times when I was not able to give the Portuguese what they so desired.

But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal. Over the years I learned very simple things. The goals pass, the cups are in museums, the records are beaten.

But there is something that time can never erase. The place that we occupy in people's hearts. If I ever made you happy, if a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel pride in our country, then everything was worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that.

We suffer together, we get up together. We believe again. Portugal will always need young people who dream, players who never give up, new generations who believe that it is possible to get where no one has reached. Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never ceases to believe in itself.

To my teammates, I want to leave a special word. Thank you for every race, for every hug, for every discussion, for every silence before entering the field. For every victory we celebrated together and for every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain.

A captain doesn’t walk alone. You are part of my story. To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, dressers, employees and to so many people who worked with me over the years, my thanks. Many of you never appeared in the photographs.

But without you, none of these photographs would have been possible. To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, sacrifices and the moments when the national team had to occupy a space that also belonged to you. If I got so far, it was because we were always at hand.

And to the Portuguese, to all the Portuguese around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image that I will always carry with me. The moment when the national anthem begins. I look around me, I see my teammates, I see the benches, I see children, mothers, parents and grandmothers.

I see the Portuguese who came from so far just to be there. And during those minutes, we stopped being different. There are no clubs, no colors, no classes, no professions, no opinions. There is only one passion. Portugal.

It is this feeling that I will carry with me for the rest of my life. Today I finish my journey on the pitch with the national team. I leave my head held high, with pride in the path I took and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

But I will never stop being one of you. I will continue to suffer, to vibrate and to celebrate every victory of Portugal with myself. I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realised that the greatest victory was to have the merit of representing the best country in the world.

Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for having believed in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that started when I was just a boy on Madeira, running after a ball, in Lisbon, wearing the jersey number 7, the pride of having worn it will be mine forever.

Portugal will always be in me. Forever.

Sports.title: Glazer family told they’re ‘tone deaf’ over £317m claim as Man United owner gives rare interview
Sports.content:
Glazer family told they’re ‘tone deaf’ over £317m claim as Man United owner gives rare interview

Avram Glazer has been slammed for claiming that Manchester United are not reliant on sporting success for their commercial power.

Speaking in September, in quotes which have only just emerged, the Red Devils' co-owner argued that his club’s value is insulated from on-field losses, like the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys.

4 Man United won the last of their 20 league titles in 2013 under Alex Ferguson (right) Credit: Getty

The Yankees remain the biggest name in baseball, winning the World Series 27 times (16 more than their nearest rivals), but their last triumph came in 2009.

Meanwhile, the Cowboys, whose five Super Bowl rings are only behind the New England Patriots and Pittsburgh Steelers (both six) across the NFL, haven't lifted the trophy since 1995.

Despite their drought, the Cowboys have ranked as the most valuable sports team in the world by Forbes for the past decade.

Jerry Jones' side reached a record $17 billion valuation in 2026, 25 per cent more than the NFL's second-most-valuable franchise.

Meanwhile, the Yankees are still regarded as the most valuable franchise in major league baseball at $8.5bn.

Avram Glazer says Man United are not reliant on sporting success

According to The Athletic, Glazer told an audience of financiers at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London that Man United's value is protected from on-field results as a major global brand in the same way.

The report adds that the American's remarks are to show the Red Devils as the most appealing investment prospect possible, as he keeps an open mind on market opportunities.

However, the truth has shown that Man United, who last claimed the Premier League title in 2013, have seen income plateau recently.

The Old Trafford outfit reported commercial revenue of £317m for the 2025/26 financial year (down £16m from the previous 12 months).

4 United fans have passionately protested against the Glazers and their ownership as United continue to underwhelm on the pitch Credit: Getty

Man United, which ranked top of Forbes list of most-valuable football clubs in 2017 and 2018, have now slipped to third in 2026.

The English giants are said to be worth $7.2bn (up from $6.6bn) but have been leapfrogged by Barcelona ($5.65bn in 2025 to $7.5bn).

Real Madrid were also previously just ahead of Man United at $6.75bn 12 months ago, but have now skyrocketed to $9.5bn this year.

In January, Michael Carrick's side also dropped out of the top five in the Deloitte Money League for the first time in their history.

But Man United were able to flex their status as a sponsorship superpower by signing a record-breaking deal exceeding £10 million with Amazon Prime to feature in an All or Nothing series.

Glazer's comments came in September, ahead of the club's latest crisis that saw manager Carrick on the brink of the sack.

4 Man United fans threw tennis balls onto the pitch when the team were two goals down against Roma Credit: Getty

'The comments are tone deaf'

On Tuesday, Man United fans interrupted the dramatic 3-2 comeback win over Roma with a protest against the club's ownership.

It was their first win in ten matches, but United remain 17th in the table - only outside of the relegation zone on goal difference.

Chief football correspondent Alex Crook told talkSPORT: "The comments are absolutely tone deaf at a time when United have made their worst start to a season in more than 40 years.

"Sadly, it is not a surprise coming from this treacherous ownership group.

"Their greed has turned United from an all-conquering team renowned and feared the world over to also-rans.

"Nothing will change all the time Old Trafford is full, and the cash machines at the megastore are still ringing."

4 United supporters are desperate to see the Glazers depart Old Trafford Credit: Getty

Gabby Agbonlahor added while speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast: "If you're not winning trophies, you're going to lose fans, aren't you?

"You're not going to gain extra fans...If I'm a Manchester United fan, I'm saying, 'No, I want to win, I want to win games.'

"'I want to win games of football, I want to see success, I want to get back to winning Champions Leagues, Premier Leagues.'

"So to hear that from one of your owners just sums them up, doesn't it?"

Sports.title: Panic Index: Newcastle boss can relax but Michael Carrick given 9/10 sack alert despite Man United comeback
Sports.content:
Panic Index: Newcastle boss can relax but Michael Carrick given 9/10 sack alert despite Man United comeback

Welcome to the Panic Index.

Every week, talkSPORT.com will measure a number of crises in the Premier League and assess the level of urgency required.

6 Should Carrick still be concerned about his future at Old Trafford? Probably Credit: Getty



Who is blowing everything out of proportion? And who has every right to feel worried?

Each situation will be assigned a score out of ten. 1/10 = storm in a teacup. 10/10 = emergency board meeting.

Got it? Great. Let's see who's in trouble and who's not...

Michael Carrick - 9/10

9/10 is ironically the number of matches Manchester United have not managed to win in recent months.

Red Devils boss Carrick is not out of the woods just yet despite his side coming from two-goals down against Roma to secure their first win in 10 matches.



While it might have bought him more time, ex-England midfielder Danny Murphy told talkSPORT: "I think we're just waiting for the inevitable."

Meanwhile, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said: "I think he's probably still on thin ice, but those headlines describing the victory as a lifeline are accurate.



"At half-time, I thought it was over for Michael Carrick. Honestly, I was in the stands with my nephew. If it wasn't for him, I'd have left at half-time.

"I was so disgusted with that first-half performance. It was abysmal from Manchester United. So I'm not sure what Michael Carrick did at half-time to inspire that comeback.



"Was it the players who just finally decided, actually, we need to turn up and give something back to these fans who, by and large, have been very good this season?

6 Man United's epic comeback against Roma eased the pressure on Carrick Credit: Getty

"But either way, it was a brilliant second half. And you say it's turned into one of the great nights at Old Trafford. And if you're a Michael Carrick supporter now, you've got to hope it is a corner that's been genuinely turned."

Matthias Jaissle - 2/10

Matthias Jaissle's job as Newcastle manager is not under immediate threat, talkSPORT understands.



The Magpies have lost five of their last seven games in all competitions, but the Newcastle hierarchy are aware Jaissle took on a big rebuild after replacing Eddie Howe in the summer.

Some Newcastle fans have turned on the German boss after two consecutive defeats at home without scoring.

But Jaissle did make a bright start, and after an underwhelming summer transfer window, ex-Premier League striker Darren Bent believes he deserves more time.

Bent said: "They're not going to go down. But they are sliding in that direction.



"And to be fair, they have lost four, but they have won three. So there's a few victories in there.

"I just think at this present time, it's about stability for Newcastle. And if he's the right man for the job then stick with him.

"There are going to be these type of problems. It's very rare you get a manager coming like Eddie Howe and everything is just unbelievable.

"He gets you into the Champions League. He wins you your first trophy in forever. Then there's another trip to the Champions League.



"It just doesn't happen. And the strength of the Premier League every single season is getting harder and harder."

6 The tide is starting to turn against Jaissle Credit: Getty

Regis Le Bris - 8/10

Is this what second-season syndrome looks like?

Despite their success in Europe and the EFL Cup, Sunderland find themselves rock bottom of the Premier League.

Ex-Arsenal winger Perry Groves points towards a challenging run of November fixtures which could put Le Bris in danger.



Groves: "I think November is a massive month for Le Bris because they've got four out of the next five games at home. They play Chelsea at home and Spurs at home in the Premier League. Worst case, you're going to need four points from that. They play Aston Villa away.

"But their form in Europa League and in the EFL Cup has been outstanding.

"It's not that the players don't believe in him. It's not that they're not trying to implement his philosophy. It's just individual mistakes.

"Last season, Sunderland were very difficult to play against. They made it physical. They made it difficult for you.



"This season, they're not. So they've collectively just dropped off. The reason I think Le Bris can turn it around is because he's proved last season that he can manage in the Premier League and get a tune out of the players."

6 Sunderland manager Le Bris could be in trouble as his side are sat bottom of the Premier League following a woeful start to the campaign Credit: Getty

Oliver Glasner - 7/10

The Nottingham Forest manager has just one win from his opening nine Premier League matches and talkSPORT's Adrian Durham thinks he will be gone by Christmas.

Reds owner Evangelos Marinakis is not known for his patience with underperforming managers - and Glasner risked his wrath by challenging the club to sack him last weekend.



Nevertheless, ex-Republic of Ireland striker Tony Cascarino believes Forest are playing a lot better than their points tally suggests.

Cascarino said: "It's going to be hard because it's going against the grain of what this owner thinks like... but I'd like to think he's going to go, we need time.

"And there is evidence by watching Forrest that they are on the right road.



"I think they're gradually going to pick themselves up and the table and get points. Because I think they've been a little bit unfortunate not to have more."

6 Glasner believes he is safe at Forest and says that a change of manager would not bring improvement to the club Credit: Getty



Pierre Sage - 7/10

Rounding off the relegation zone are 18th-place Crystal Palace.

Replacing Glasner was never going to be an easy task, especially after a difficult summer transfer window.

And ex-Palace owner Simon Jordan, who once made these decisions himself at Selhurst Park, suggests Sage should get more time.

Jordan said: "I don't know if he's good enough, but I think he's got to be given more time, because you're just selling the best players all the time.

"Last year, you sold Marc Guehi from underneath Oliver Glasner, but you had to because it was going to be a free transfer.



"Maxence Lacroix went in the summer. You keep on losing players.

"Jean-Philippe Mateta, does he want to be there? Does he not want to be there?

"He's got £50million Jorgen Strand Larsen, you know what I think of him...

6 Sage was appointed on a three-year deal less than five months ago Credit: Getty

"The bottom line is that I think it's a difficult transition for him.

"And I don't think it's a Frank de Boer situation, where the players simply were not having him after four games and there were problems and Steve Parish had to step in."

Sports.title: £21m West Ham star axed from squad due to little known rule
Sports.content:
£21m West Ham star axed from squad due to little known rule

Scott Parker’s decision to axe striker Pablo paid off as he masterminded a stunning comeback in his first match as West Ham manager.

Just hours after being unveiled as the Hammers' new boss, Parker enjoyed a thrilling return to the dugout as his side fought back from 3-0 down at half-time to draw 3-3 with Cardiff City.



4 Parker enjoyed a dramatic return to management on Tuesday night Credit: Getty

4 Max Kilman's 82nd-minute goal saw West Ham fight back from 3-0 down to get a point Credit: Getty

Replacing Nuno Espirito Santo following his sacking 24 hours earlier, Parker's tenure got off to a quite unbelievable start in Wales.

Things could hardly have begun worse when West Ham found themselves three goals down at the break after Jack Moylan's hat-trick.



But few could have expected the response Parker would get from his side after the interval, as they then mounted a stunning comeback.

Divine Mukasa pulled a goal back on 58 minutes, and Arne Engels struck shortly after to make it 3-2 with 25 minutes remaining.



As the game entered its final ten minutes, Max Kilman grabbed a thrilling equaliser to spark pandemonium in the away end.

The late fightback saw Parker make an instant statement as Hammers boss, as his side avoided falling to a third straight defeat by snatching a point.



Pablo axed due to EFL matchday rule

The result came after some bold team selections, as Parker made five changes to the side that lost 3-1 to West Brom on Saturday.

Most brutal of all was the decision to drop striker £21million man Pablo from the squad entirely after starting at the weekend.

However, it was born out of necessity due to the EFL rules that require seven home-grown players in the matchday squad.

4 Pablo was the victim of a little-known rule around Championship matchday squads Credit: Getty



An injury to Kyle Walker-Peters and Konstantinos Mavropanos' return left Max Kilman, Divine Mukasa, Jarrod Bowen, Oliver Scarles, Lewis Orford, Airidas Golambekis and Ezra Mayers as the seven.

It meant that Pablo and Maxwell Cornet were both left out of the matchday squad, despite both travelling to the Cardiff City Stadium.

Portuguese Pablo has struggled since his arrival from Primeira Liga side Gil Vicente in January, finding the net just twice in 28 games.

He failed to get off the mark in 14 Premier League appearances last season, as the Irons were relegated to the Championship.



His absence meant Taty Castellanos took his place in the starting XI.

This didn't initially seem to have the desired effect, as West Ham found themselves up against it after going 3-0 down at Cardiff.

4 Parker is targeting promotion with a fourth different team with West Ham Credit: Getty

But after pulling off a stunning second-half fightback, Parker was vindicated in his decision which helped snatch a point.

West Ham remain eighth in the Championship - now the final Championship play-off place following the decision to expand.



With six months of the season still left to play, Parker will now be looking to use his past experience to inspire his side to an automatic promotion push.

The former Hammers midfielder was available as a free agent after leaving Burnley in April.

Parker has won promotion out of the Championship three times in his managerial career with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley.

As a player, the former England international spent four years with West Ham between 2007 and 2011.



During that time, he made 129 appearances for the club, scoring 12 goals from midfield.

Sports.title: Football news LIVE: Ronaldo retires from Portugal, Glazer makes bizarre Man United statement, Jaissle’s job not under threat
Sports.content:
In full

Well, that has certainly livened up a quiet Thursday morning hasn't it?

Cristiano Ronaldo after 234 appearances for Portugal spanning 23 years has announced his retirement from international football.

He did so with a five minute video on social media, and here is the statement in full.

"To the Portuguese, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of the national team to all of us.

"I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility to wear it, to defend it and to take it with me to the stadiums all over the world. Today the time has come to give it to the future.

"It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not taken only with the head, they are also taken with the heart.

"I finish a journey that started in August 2003 and changed my life forever. When I look back and think about everything I lived in the national team, I do not see only games, goals, records or trophies. I see people.

"I see immigrants who for 90 minutes felt Portugal a little closer. I see millions of Portuguese that I never met personally, but who were part of my life. Because after all, football is much bigger than a game. Football is people.

"Throughout my career in the national team I tried to overcome my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be the best, I wanted to make history. I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed that we could go further.

"And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories that I will never forget. There were defeats that I still have a hard time remembering today.

"I also failed, I also suffered, there were also times when I was not able to give the Portuguese what they so desired.

"But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal. Over the years I learned very simple things. The goals pass, the cups are in museums, the records are beaten.

"But there is something that time can never erase. The place that we occupy in people's hearts. If I ever made you happy, if a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel pride in our country, then everything was worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that.

"We suffer together, we get up together. We believe again. Portugal will always need young people who dream, players who never give up, new generations who believe that it is possible to get where no one has reached. Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never ceases to believe in itself.

"To my teammates, I want to leave a special word. Thank you for every race, for every hug, for every discussion, for every silence before entering the field. For every victory we celebrated together and for every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain.

"A captain doesn’t walk alone. You are part of my story. To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, dressers, employees and to so many people who work with me over the years, my thanks. Many of you never appeared in the photographs.

"But without you, none of these photographs would have been possible. To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, sacrifices and the moments when the national team had to occupy a space that also belonged to you. If I got so far, it was because we were always at hand.

"And to the Portuguese, to all the Portuguese around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image that I will always carry with me. The moment when the national anthem begins. I look around me, I see my teammates, I see the benches, I see children, mothers, parents and grandmothers.

"I see the Portuguese who came from so far just to be there. And during those minutes, we stopped being different. There are no clubs, no colors, no classes, no professions, no opinions. There is only one passion. Portugal.

"It is this feeling that I will carry with me for the rest of my life. Today I finish my journey on the pitch with the national team. I leave my head held high, with pride in the path I took and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

"But I will never stop being one of you. I will continue to suffer, to vibrate and to celebrate every victory of Portugal with myself. I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realised that the greatest victory was to have the merit of representing the best country in the world.

"Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for having believed in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that started when I was just a boy on Madeira, running after a ball, in Lisbon, wearing the jersey number 7, the pride of having worn it will be mine forever.

"Portugal will always be in me. Forever."

Sports.title: Harry Kane lands highest salary in Europe as Ballon d’Or winner announces decision on future
Sports.content:
Harry Kane lands highest salary in Europe as Ballon d’Or winner announces decision on future

England captain Harry Kane has signed a three-year contract extension with Bayern Munich.

The Ballon d'Or winner lands what is thought to be the most lucrative deal in Bayern Munich history, making him the highest paid player in Europe by salary.



2 Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 games since joining Bayern three years ago Credit: AFP

Kane's contract extension ties him down until 2029 and ends any speculation around his future.

The 33-year-old was set to enter the final six months of his pre-existing deal with Spanish giants Barcelona eyeing him up.

According to The Sun, Kane's new deal is worth £401,115-a-week and £20,858,000 each year.



Erling Haaland became the highest-paid player in Premier League history when he agreed a £250million nine-year deal with Manchester City in January 2025, working out at around £525,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, Kylian Mbappe is thought to earn around £518,000-a-week at Real Madrid.



However, both of these deals include bonuses and Kane's new basic salary is thought to be higher.

He said: “I feel right at home at FC Bayern.

“I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager.



“It makes me very proud to be part of this club.

“My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay.

2 Kane has scored 89 goals for club and country since the start of August 2025 Credit: Getty

“I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

World's best player

Bayern Munich also expressed their delight at securing the services of Kane for the foreseeable future.

“We’re absolutely delighted, because with Harry Kane we have the Ballon d’Or winner on the pitch – a team player, a leader, the best all-round striker in the world,” said Christoph Freund, Bayern’s sporting director.



“We all benefit from his qualities as a player and as a person, day in, day out.

"FC Bayern thrives on players who never stop giving their all, even when they have already achieved the greatest of goals.”

Sports.title: Como make Champions League era history with incredible nine-goal mauling
Sports.content:
Como enjoyed an historic night as they thumped Lens 9-1 to equal the biggest win of the Champions League era.

Cesc Fabregas' side continued their stunning debut campaign in Europe's premier competition by producing their most impressive display yet with a record-breaking away victory.



4 Como have been the Champions League surprise package this term, especially after thumping Lens Credit: Getty

After thrashing Manchester United 4-1 last time out, Como reached a new level against Lens as seven different players found the net.

Anastasios Douvikas led the way with a hat-trick for the Italian side, grabbing a brace in the first half before Nico Paz struck to put the visitors 3-0 up at the interval.

And the best was yet to come in the second half, with Como grabbing six more goals to write their name into the record books.



Douvikos completed his treble, while Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli all struck for Fabregas' side.

Ruben Aguilar found the net on 65 minutes to score the smallest of consolation goals for Lens, as the game finished 9-1.



Records galore for superb Como

The result saw Como climb to fourth in the Champions League league phase table with their third win in four games, and record multiple records in the process.

The eight-goal margin equalled the biggest victory in Champions League history since it rebranded under this name in 1992.



Liverpool and Real Madrid have both previously won by this scoreline - doing so against Besiktas and Malmo respectively in 2007 and 2015.

Meanwhile, Como also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a game.

The German giants famously thrashed Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the 2024/25 season - with Harry Kane netting four goals on the night.

4 Fabregas' reputation continues to grow after Lens' historic 9-1 win in the Champions League Credit: Getty



4 Douvikas was the star of the show as he grabbed a hat-trick in the rout Credit: Getty

And there was further history for Como by recording their eye-watering scoreline away from home.

They are now the first team of the Champions League era to score nine goals in an away match, and the first to do so in 45 years in the European Cup altogether.

Feyenoord were the last side to do so, when they won 9-0 at Olympiakos Nicosia in September 1971.



And while Como found themselves in the record books for the right reasons, Lens instead made unwanted history.

Their crushing defeat was a record Champions League loss for a French club, and their third consecutive loss in this season's competition.

Lens now sit a lowly 33rd out of 36 in the overall Champions League standings after four games with three points.

4 Highly-rated Argentine youngster Paz impressed against Lens Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Como are flying high in fourth on nine points, three points behind Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and one point behind Arsenal.

The Serie A side, who finished fourth in Serie A last season to qualify for the Champions League for the first time, had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Man United 4-1 at home in this campaign.

His retirement comes just weeks after his explosive falling-out with new manager Jorge Jesus, which ended with Ronaldo abandoning Portugal's camp during the most recent international break in September and October.

It appeared as if he could return for the upcoming break this month for clashes with Denmark and Wales, but he has decided to step away after 23 years.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

He is hoping to pass the baton to his son, 16-year-old Cristiano Junior, who this week has been called up for Portugal's Under-17s.

Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 aged 18 and went on to play in six World Cups, a record he shares with Lionel Messi, as well as six European Championships, two Nations League finals, and a Confederations Cup.

Cristiano Ronaldo has called time on his illustrious international career with Portugal

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

He never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Sports.title: Harry Kane signs £400,000-a-week contract to become the highest-paid footballer in Europe as England's captain commits to Bayern Munich and stays in Germany for three more years
Sports.content:
Harry Kane signs £400,000-a-week contract to become the highest-paid footballer in Europe as England's captain commits to Bayern Munich and stays in Germany for three more years

Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has extended his contract at Bayern Munich until 2029 in a move that will make him Europe's highest-paid player.

According to reports in Germany, his bumper new deal takes his weekly wages to a staggering £400,000 - believed to be the highest base salary in the continent.

Kane scored 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country last season, earning him the award for the world's best player ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal at last week's ceremony in London.

Tthe England captain has scored 156 goals in 161 games since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023.

Kane was entering the final six months of his deal at Bayern but any hope of returning to the Premier League to break Alan Shearer's goalscoring record has been dashed, as he commits another three years to the German champions.

The 33-year-old has settled into life in Bavaria with ease, moving to Germany with his wife and childhood sweetheart, Kate, and their four children to embark on a new life together three years ago.

Signing his new deal, Kane said: 'I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich.

Harry Kane's new deal will extend his stay in Germany to at least 2029

Kane has scored 156 goals at almost one a game since joining from Tottenham in 2023

'We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club.

'My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.'

Kane had never lifted silverware before joining Bayern but has made up for it in the last two years, claiming two Bundesliga titles, the DFB Cup and two German Super Cups.

He has earned plenty of individual honours, too. Alongside the Ballon d'Or, Kane has been Bundesliga top goalscorer in both seasons and has twice won the Golden Shoe, which recognises Europe's best striker. He was also crowned Germany's best player last season.

For country, Kane led England to their best World Cup finish since 1966 this summer, as the Three Lions won bronze. Kane scored six goals in seven outings for Thomas Tuchel's side.

Later this month, Kane is poised to become England's record appearance holder when the Three Lions face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League. He currently shares the record with Peter Shilton, with the pair capped 125 times.

Kane and his family have settled into life in Germany with ease. Pictured with wife, Kate

Kane is already England's all-time leading goalscorer, having netted 91 times - 38 more than second-placed Wayne Rooney.

He told The Guardian in 2024: '[The children are] in school now and have been skiing the last couple of weekends. Just having that has been great for them. We've met a few of the parents at school and made friends with teammates' wives and kids.

'Slowly but surely it starts to feel like home. People ask what are the big differences, but a lot of the routine is pretty much the same.

'You miss friends you have at home or a golf course, but you soon learn about those things here and it becomes part of your home.

'They’re loving it. They’ll be speaking the language before me too.'

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador

Casino firm BC Game has been Leicester's primary shirt sponsor since the 2024-25 season

Welcome to BC Game @EvaElfie! Let the fun begin 😏 pic.twitter.com/xzLJ4uBOx7 — BC Game (@bcgame) November 3, 2026

'From the moment the Club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values. Our first article in July 2024 said that "It doesn't feel like who LCFC are to have a gambling website on our shirts and seems to be another step away from our well run family club reputation".

'The Club has not only partnered with a gambling company, but chosen one that is unlicensed to operate in the UK, has unanswered questions about the legitimacy of its funding and its origins, and allows clients to "game" using cryptocurrencies.

'Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content.

'Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?

'Our end of season survey showed 73% of fans felt negative about the relationship, and only 5% were content with it.

'As always our message is, if you're purchasing an LCFC replica shirt, opt for one that doesn't have the BC Game logo on it.'

BC Game, which The Foxes Trust claim has failed to respond to questions about its funding and legitimacy, lost its UK operating licence in December 2024 and has since shifted its focus to overseas markets.

Focusing on Elfie's esports portfolio in his announcement, BC Game chief executive Ali 'Ako' Muhanned said: 'Eva has built an incredible relationship with the gaming and esports community through genuine passion and consistent content creation.

'At BC.GAME, we want to work with creators who understand how to entertain, connect with audiences in real time, and bring positive energy to our players. Her live streams are dynamic and engaging, making her a natural fit as we expand our footprint across esports and interactive entertainment.'

Elfie, who has 4.8million followers on Instagram, also released her debut single 'Fairyland' last month.

Since partnering with BC Game, the Foxes have plummeted down the football league, suffering back-to-back relegations from the Premier League to League One.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too

BC Game lost its licence to operate in the UK in 2024 and now targets overseas markets

Leicester, who famously won the Premier League against all odds in 2016 and lifted the FA Cup in 2021, were docked six points for breaching spending rules during last season's dismal Championship campaign and failed to survive the drop.

Today, the East Midlands club sit 10th in League One after 13 matches, winning five, losing four and drawing four.

When the partnership was first announced in 2024, Leicester City chief executive Susan Whelan said: 'We welcome BC Game to Leicester City – an opportunity to work with an innovative partner in a new category for the Club.

'As a leading global operator in a rapidly evolving environment, BC Game already have a history of successful relationships in sport and we look forward to the development of a mutually beneficial partnership.

'The ability to attract high-value partners upon our return to the Premier League is vital to our determination to re-establish Leicester City among the game’s elite, to continue to invest in a competitive squad and to ensure the best possible experience for our supporters.'

Sports.title: Tennis billionaire heiress Jessica Pegula is caught on hot mic saying 19-year-old rival Mirra Andreeva is a 'diva who needs to be humbled'
Sports.content:
Billionaire tennis heiress Jessica Pegula has been caught red-handed gossiping about her 19-year-old rival Mirra Andreeva.

The American star, 32, was caught calling Andreeva a 'diva' who 'needs to be humbled' by a microphone that she was unaware of during training.

She also said she had 'lost respect' for legendary Spanish player Conchita Martínez, who now coaches Andreeva, this year's French Open champion.

Andreeva has gained a reputation for her fiery temperament – at Wimbledon this year she smashed her rackets, snapped at the umpire and her team, said 'I quit,' and left the court in tears after losing to Barbora Krejcikova in the second round.

Pegula, daughter of £8.9billion oil and gas tycoon Terry Pegula, was recorded by a hot mic while training for WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

'Conchita has always been very nice to me, but I've lost a little bit of respect for her,' she began.

Jessica Pegula (left) was caught on a hot mic saying Mirra Andreeva is a 'diva' who 'needs to be humbled'

Andreeva, 19, is known for her explosive outbursts on court, including smashing her rackets

Pegula is the heiress in a billionaire family but has worked hard to reach her position (Instagram: @jpegula)

'I think she's a nice girl, she's just a diva. She needs to be humbled. You have to put her in her place.

'Do it, stand up to her. If I was a coach, and my girl just played four great games, and you're up 4-0, and you're mad at me throwing balls at me, first of all, that's so disrespectful. You're up 4-0, like shut the f*** up.

'But she can't. Conchita pokes her and eggs on her behaviour. She has a perfect serve, she's smart, she anticipates well.

'If she had Coco's mentality, she's better, serve, everything, all around. Mentally she's just...'

Pegula also swirled her finger close to her temple, appearing to indicate that she thought Andreeva was crazy.

The pair are yet to face each other in competitive action, but they could in this tournament. While Andreeva won the French Open this year, Pegula is still waiting to win a Grand Slam – she reached the final of the US Open in 2024.

Pegula has come under fire for her 'diva' comments, particularly because of her high-ranking background.

Her father grew rich through oil and gas – he founded East Resources to explore those markets in 1983 with a loan of $7,500 (£5,565) before selling most of its assets in 2010 for nearly $5billion (£3.710billion).

Pegula, left, with her family after her parents Terry and Kim bought the Buffalo Bills in 2014

Andreeva regularly lets the umpire, her team, and the crowd know about her frustrations

Together with his wife, Kim, Pegula now invests in sports teams. They own the NHL's Buffalo Sabres and in 2014 they beat groups spearheaded by Donald Trump and Bon Jovi to buy the NFL's Buffalo Bills for $1.4bn (£1.038bn).

But Pegula told Daily Mail Sport a couple of summers ago: 'It's funny when people assume that I fly private everywhere, or that I have had a chauffeur driving me around since I was five… I grew up pretty normal, and a lot of that [her family's wealth] didn't happen to me until I was already older and playing.

'My goal since I was six or seven was to be No 1 in the world… I was just a normal kid growing up in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, taking lessons after school.'

That hasn't shielded Pegula, 32, from allegations that, to win a Grand Slam, she 'needs [a] dynamic that family billions can't buy'.

It is fair for her to indicate that Andreeva has an explosive character on court. The Wimbledon incident was far from the first.

At the French Open last year, she imploded on her way to defeat against world No361 Lois Boisson and hit a ball into the crowd, which brought on boos and a warning.

At Indian Wells in March this year, she threw and smashed her racket after losing against Katerina Siniakova, before exchanging heated words with members of the crowd.

'I feel like it’s not the best way to handle yourself, but once in a while it really helps to get mad at yourself and get it done,' she has said.

She also says she should try and learn from Serena Williams: 'I think the one person that was handling losses very well was Serena Williams, like I've never heard or seen her upset.

'Even I remember, she was losing finals on the Slams, and she would always smile and be happy for her opponent that she won the match and she got the trophy. So maybe it's something that I can also try to learn, and we'll see how that's gonna go. Yeah, we'll see.'

Sports.title: Furious Martin O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting
Sports.content:
Furious Martin O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has hit out at individuals wearing balaclavas who turned up at a meeting between directors and supporters.

Staged at the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening, the event afforded around 120 fans a rare chance to grill the hierarchy on the direction the club is taking.

Chief executive Michael Nicholson, finance director Chris McKay and interim chairman Brian Wilson attended — with O’Neill also venturing along after learning that it was scheduled to take place.

And while the manager was pleased to have participated in a ‘robust’ discussion, he was horrified that those executives who’d agreed to front up were abused by certain fans — believed to be ultras — who hid their faces as they congregated outside.

It’s understood that they weren’t permitted access to the meeting room itself but it was still a worrying sight amid the ongoing unrest surrounding the club, with the threat of more protests ahead of Thursday night's Europa League clash with Besiktas at Celtic Park.

The flashpoint came weeks after Dermot Desmond, the club’s largest shareholder, had tennis balls thrown at him by protesters as he participated in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews.

‘There was a bit of a debacle beforehand,’ said the Northern Irishman. ‘But the meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

O'Neill admitted he was disappointed to see individuals wearing balaclavas outside meeting

‘(We were) trying to give the answers that (were) not necessarily what people are looking for, because I’m not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway.

‘But, yeah, it was really interesting and an experience.

‘Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? Well, you’d have to ask the people there at the time.

‘There was no shouting. It wasn’t like (last year’s) AGM. The shouting had taken place before the meeting, you know? I mean, you are aware that people with balaclavas came up to the thing? To me, I think that was the saddest thing.

‘Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening, I think that’s really disappointing.

‘I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.’

The meeting came amid speculation that the club’s forthcoming annual general meeting would be held remotely.

Last year’s AGM was cut short by then chairman, Peter Lawwell, after it was disrupted by individuals shouting and brandishing red cards.

O'Neill attended meeting with Celtic fans in Greenock where he said questioning was robust

It’s understood, though, that the meeting will go ahead as normal in a suite at Celtic Park — with O’Neill expecting to attend.

‘That’s early December, isn’t it?’ he asked. ‘So, I would expect to be at it as a manager. I assume that Brendan (Rodgers) was (present previously), so you’d be at it.

‘If given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

‘I hope it’s similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year.’

While no minutes were taken at the meeting in Greenock, there’s been speculation that O’Neill confirmed he’d be leaving the club in the summer — despite a one-year option remaining.

Although he didn’t confirm this on Wednesday, he said: ‘I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

‘Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute.’

Sports.title: Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table

Manchester United's 4-1 battering by Como two weeks ago now looks a lucky escape – after the Italian side romped to a 9-1 victory at Lens in the Champions League.

Cesc Fabregas' side put in a stunning performance in a record-equalling win which well and truly announced them as contenders on the biggest stage.

Como now sit fourth in the Champions League standings after also thrashing RB Leipzig and Man United, who are likely relieved that Lens took such a pounding.

It means only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, and Arsenal have got off to better starts, despite this being their maiden season in European competition.

The lakeside outfit were 3-0 up at half-time – with the scorer of the third goal, Nico Paz, paying his respects to late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel – before a rout after the break.

It is the latest statement win for Como, whose transformation began in 2019 when a pair of Indonesian billionaire brothers, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group.

Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a record-equalling victory in the Champions League on Wednesday

Cesc Fabregas is quickly building his name as one of the most talented coaches in Europe

With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football.

Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como have built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment, and a clear footballing identity – and it is paying off big-time.

They have now won six games on the bounce, though they still sit fourth in Serie A five points behind leaders Lazio, who have had an almost perfect start.

Their crushing of Lens was the first time an Italian side had scored seven or more goals away from home in European Cup/Champions League history.

And their hat-trick hero on the night, Anastasios Douvikas, is now the top scorer in the Champions League ahead of Erling Haaland.

All of this comes for a side who were playing in the third tier just six seasons ago and on the back of a relatively modest summer spend of £58million on nine permanent arrivals and loanees.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

There was a poignant moment when Paz paid homage to Miguel and his hometown club, holding aloft a shirt with the picture of the late star alongside the caption: 'Rest in peace.' Though he plays for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also spent time in the club's youth system from 2014-16.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 – Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline – as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Fabregas's side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.
