Sports.title: Alan Jones, 1980 Formula 1 world champion, dies aged 80 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world champion Alan Jones has passed away at the age of 80.

Jones was the first driver to win a world championship for Williams, clinching the title in the penultimate round of the 1980 season driving a Ford Cosworth-powered FW07B.

He scored his 11th and final grand prix victory the following year but announced his retirement from F1. He later returned with the original Haas team but left for good at the end of 1986.

Williams paid tribute to Jones, whose 80th birthday was on Monday.

“Everyone at Williams is deeply saddened to learn of Alan Jones’ passing,” said the team in a statement. “Alan was instrumental in making Williams what it is today, forming an extraordinary bond with Frank Williams and Patrick Head to become our first drivers’ world champion in just our fourth season in Formula 1.

“He set the standard for Williams champions: a fast, uncompromising racer with a challenger mentality who loved motor racing and dedicated his life to it. He is a true Australian icon and a Williams legend, and he will be dearly missed.

“We send our love and thoughts to the Jones family and all his friends.”

The Australian Grand Prix promoters issued a statement saying they received the news of Jones’ death “with great sadness.” Jones won the race in 1980 when it was held as a non-championship event at Calder Park and was chiefly contested by Formula 5000 machinery plus two Formula 1 cars, one of which Jones drove.

“As a Formula 1 world champion and one of Australia’s greatest racing drivers, Alan holds a special place in the history of our sport,” the statement continued. “His 1980 world championship inspired a generation of Australian motorsport fans, while his victory at the Australian Grand Prix that same year remains the last time an Australian driver has won their home grand prix.

“He leaves an extraordinary legacy in Australian motorsport and will be deeply missed by the motorsport community around the world.”

Sports.title: A home debutant and another Mercedes title? Six Brazilian GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Brazilian fans unexpectedly have two home drivers on the grid this weekend. Here are the talking points for Formula 1’s trip to South America.

Brazil’s new generation

For the first time in 10 years, two Brazilian drivers will line up on the grid at Interlagos this weekend.

Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will make his grand prix debut earlier than expected. Haas will put the Ferrari junior driver into the seat formerly occupied by Esteban Ocon, which he was not due to take over until next year.

He will join Gabriel Bortoleto, who impressed in his debut season last year and is on course to end the season ahead of experienced team mate Nico Hulkenberg in the standings.

It’s an exciting time for Brazilian motor racing talent. But spare a thought for the sadly overlooked Felipe Drugovich, who spent years testing for Aston Martin after winning the F2 title, came close to making his F1 debut at the beginning of 2023, but now appears unlikely to get another chance.

All over for Ocon?

Also at this race 10 years ago, Ocon put in an under-rewarded performance for Manor, finishing just one-and-a-half seconds outside the points in streaming wet conditions.

His sensational and as-yet unexplained ousting by Haas in the middle of the last race weekend looks like being the end of his time in F1. It was not a career he came by easily, and one he almost lost at the end of 2018, when Lawrence Stroll bought Racing Point and dropped Ocon to create a vacancy for his son to fill.

With few opportunities elsewhere on the grid remaining, it’s hard to see how the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix winner can come back from this.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ferrari fall-out

There were testy moments between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc before last weekend. But the Mexican Grand Prix was by far the clearest example of them costing each other a win.

In 2024 Leclerc claimed victory at Monza by capitalising on the feuding McLarens at the start. Two years on, will Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur react the way his rivals did, by imposing stricter conditions on how his drivers race each other?

The other championship

How well Ferrari perform this weekend will have a strong bearing on whether Mercedes clinch the constructors’ championship or have to wait until Las Vegas.

Mercedes arrive in Brazil 126 points ahead of Ferrari, the only team that can still beat them to the title. If their lead is at least 129 points when the chequered flag falls on Sunday, Mercedes will regain the crown they last won in 2021.

McLaren respond to Red Bull

Mexico was the sixth consecutive weekend in which Red Bull out-scored McLaren. The two teams are separated by 17 points in their scrap for third place, but McLaren intend to respond this weekend.

McLaren will introduce changes to their front and rear wings this weekend, plus a modification to their floor. Will that improve the performance of the car – or at least make it easier for Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to extract the best from it?

The final act?

While Formula 1 races in Brazil, at least some of Moto GP’s teams are due to race in Qatar. Only some, because Yamaha has already confirmed it won’t send its teams due to concerns over the threat to the event from the war in Iran.

America resumed strikes on Iran on Wednesday and it remains to be seen what steps it will take following yesterday’s midterm election results. Many in F1 will be anxiously monitoring the situation and whether Moto GP presses ahead with its plan to race in Losail.

Sports.title: Cracked sump almost put Antonelli out of Mexican Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes has revealed Andrea Kimi Antonelli came close to retiring from the Mexican Grand Prix.

The team discovered the new world champion’s car had developed a fault in its power unit in the final laps.

Mercedes’ deputy team principal Bradley Lord described it as “a sign of the fact that this is Kimi’s year and things are rolling with him.”

“We got the car back after the race, took the floor off the bottom, [and found it was] covered in oil,” he told High Performance Racing. “Sump cracked.”

Antonelli was already detecting signs of trouble from his Mercedes power unit. “Kimi said he thinks about four laps from the end he could start to feel the engine just starting to struggle. So [he was] right on the edge of retirement [from] that race and yet it held together.”

The Mercedes driver lost almost two seconds on the final lap of the race, though he said that was because he was crying. He would still have clinched the title had his engine failed, but a retirement would have robbed him of the iconic photograph with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton he wants to put on his wall.

Lord also shed more light on the loss of power George Russell suffered on the run to turn one at the start of the race, which allowed several of his rivals to overtake. “He’s taken the lion’s share of these technical problems and quirks and we had another one on Sunday,” said Lord.

“He was in prime position for going for the lead into turn one and then [has] a de-rate out of nowhere because of one of the complex bits of the energy rules mean he’s back in P5, P6 and caught up in the [mess] with Hadjar.

“It was a little bit like Spa, the start of the race there where he was so well positioned and then it just became that collision at turn four.”

Sports.title: Stats: Hirakawa is sixth one-off starter to score a world championship point | 2026 Mexican Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen won the race and the new world champion finished third: this year’s championship-deciding race resembled last year’s, though the similarity was superficial.

There may have been three drivers still in contention but this wasn’t a down-to-the-wire nail-biter: Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s coronation was virtually assured before he even set foot in Mexico.

Third place ensured Antonelli succeeds Lando Norris as F1’s second new world champion in as many years. That hasn’t happened since 2010 when Sebastian Vettel became the fourth new world champion in a row, following Kimi Raikkonen, Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button.

Norris’s reign as world champion therefore lasted less than a calendar year. At 329 days, this is the sixth-shortest individual duration as champion. However others who had short spells as champion won the title more than once, giving them longer reigns:

Shortest reigns as world champion (days)

*Died before winning the championship

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli’s championship success produced several notable statistics which were previously covered here:

Lewis Hamilton became the oldest driver to claim pole position for a grand prix in his lifetime. At 41 years and 297 days old he is the most senior pole-winner since another Ferrari driver, Mario Andretti, took pole position for the 1982 Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton is the fifth-oldest driver ever to claim a pole position in F1.

Oldest F1 pole-winners

Driver Race Track Age Giuseppe Farina 1954 Argentinian Grand Prix Buenos Aires 47y, 78d Juan Manuel Fangio 1958 Argentinian Grand Prix Buenos Aires 46y, 208d Jack Brabham 1970 Spanish Grand Prix Jarama 44y, 16d Mario Andretti 1982 Italian Grand Prix Monza 42y, 195d Lewis Hamilton 2026 Mexican Grand Prix Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 41y, 297d

Hamilton’s pole position was his first for over three years. That’s well short of the longest spell between consecutive pole positions: Raikkonen went 3,262 days (over eight years) between his pole positions in the 2008 French Grand Prix and 2017 Monaco Grand Prix.

That record-extending 105th pole position for Hamilton was a close thing: he beat George Russell by just nine-thousandths of a second. But that was three times the scale of his last pole-winning margin. Hamilton beat Verstappen to pole by just three thousandths of a second in Hungary three years ago.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Unexpectedly, 17 places behind Hamilton on the grid was Ryo Hirakawa, who arrived in Mexico only expecting to take part in the first practice session. However Haas’s shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon after Friday’s running handed Hirakawa his grand prix debut at the age of 32 years and 239 days. That made him the oldest debutant since Andre Lotterer made his one-off appearance for Caterham in the 2014 Belgian Grand Prix – he was older by 39 days.

It’s not uncommon for a driver to take part in practice and then be replaced due to illness or injury. Occasionally, teams swap drivers between garages if damage leaves them with only one car available, as happened with Logan Sargeant and Alexander at the 2024 Australian Grand Prix.

But it is very unusual to see a healthy driver begin a race weekend with a team and then be replaced someone else. The last time something akin to Ocon’s substitution happened was when Ensign attempted to run Ricardo Londono-Bridge in the 1981 Brazilian Grand Prix.

The race moved to Jacarepagua that year and the Colombian driver took part in the then-customary pre-event acclimatisation session for the new circuit on Wednesday. However the FIA refused to grant him a superlicence, so Ensign replaced him with Marc Surer.

Hirakawa’s surprising weekend continued as he scored a point despite originally taking the chequered flag in 13th place. Penalties for Oscar Piastri and both Alpine drivers meant Hirakawa, like Arvid Lindblad earlier this year, finished his first grand prix inside the points.

As it stands, Hirakawa will not take part in any more races – Rafael Camara will take over in Brazil. F1’s rules only allow Haas to use a total of four drivers all season, unless they get a dispensation, and the team has an obvious reason to keep Camara in the season as he will drive for them next year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hirakawa therefore stands to join the tiny group of drivers who scored a point in their only start. Just six drivers can claim this unusual feat, and only one – Neville Lederle – did it driving solo in a race run to Formula 1 regulations:

Single-start points-scorers

Driver Race Position Points Notes Joie (George) Chitwood 1950 Indianapolis 500 5th 1 Shared car with Tony Bettenhausen Dorino Serafini 1950 Italian Grand Prix 2nd 3 Shared car with Alberto Ascari Eric Thompson 1952 British Grand Prix 5th 2 Formula 2 regulations Oscar Galvez 1953 Argentinian Grand Prix 5th 2 Formula 2 regulations George Amick 1958 Indianapolis 500 2nd 6 Neville Lederle 1962 South African Grand Prix 6th 1

It remains to be seen whether Ocon will return to start another race. At the beginning of the season the Mexican Grand Prix was due to be his 200th career start. Without him, the number of race-winning drivers on the grid has fallen to 12.

Finally, Verstappen’s sixth win at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez makes it the venue he’s scored the most wins at. He could equal that with a sixth win at Yas Marina next month – if the race takes place.

Sports.title: Zuffa Boxing Promised A Revolution And Delivered The Copper Box
Sports.content:
Zuffa talked a massive game about revolutionizing boxing, but the actual product inside the ring tells a different story. Fans are already questioning whether these initial shows are making any real splash.

The choice of the Copper Box sparked plenty of talk during a talkSPORT preview covering Chris Billam Smith against Cheavon Clarke alongside Denzel Bentley against Shane Mosley Jr. Hardcore boxing followers might appreciate those matchups, yet they hardly signal the massive shakeup Zuffa promised.

During the broadcast, the host questioned whether Zuffa would eventually book an arena bigger than the Copper Box. One panelist pointed out that the promotional powerhouse talked up massive announcements without delivering anything groundbreaking. That prompted the host to recall Dana White asking critics to grade the venture after a full twelve months.

The venue itself isn’t the real issue. A cozy arena creates electric energy when the action heats up. Booking a cavernous stadium means nothing if the seats end up empty or the bouts fall flat.

The real test is whether Zuffa can stage matchups people crave. Billam Smith taking on Clarke brings local intrigue alongside their amateur history, yet Clarke losing to Viddal Riley softened fan enthusiasm. A victory keeps Billam Smith active, though it won’t ignite massive demand for his next appearance.

Bentley versus Mosley offers solid matchmaking, too. Bentley openly praised the financial incentives of signing with Zuffa, which makes total sense for his career. Spectators tune in for compelling drama, not fighter paychecks. Handing out better contracts won’t instantly transform an ordinary bout into appointment viewing.

Zuffa created this problem through its own bold marketing. Staging decent regional fight cards works fine if the goal is modest roster growth. Because White guaranteed a complete overhaul of the business, viewers naturally expect something groundbreaking.

Collecting recognizable athletes gives the banner talent to book. The brand still has to generate genuine excitement around those athletes, ignite heated rivalries, then secure opponents that get fans genuinely invested. The company logo won’t carry the load by itself.

There is definitely runway left for things to click. One modest night at the Copper Box doesn’t seal the outfit’s fate, nor does skeptical radio banter mean the experiment is doomed. What it proves is that early hype won’t cut it anymore. People want hard proof.

White asked for twelve months before everyone delivers a final grade. When evaluation day arrives, the only thing that counts will be a lineup of matchups fans begged to see. Fresh sales pitches simply won’t fool anyone a second time.

Sports.title: Did Callum Smith Take Something Out of Joshua Buatsi for Good?
Sports.content:
Joshua Buatsi insists his loss to Callum Smith prepared him for deep water. His rematch with Willy Hutchinson will test whether that ring education took something out of him physically.

Buatsi showed real grit against Smith, yet his flat showing against Zach Parker raised doubts about what that night took out of him. Hutchinson now steps in with the knowledge that he can push Buatsi into an uncomfortable place.

That question surfaced during talkSPORT’s preview, where pundits questioned whether the Smith war aged the Londoner. The flat outing against Parker gave the debate real traction, even if a single night cannot settle what remains in his gas tank.

Buatsi counters that the Smith setback revealed what he could summon when the going got rough. Going twelve rounds at elite level gave him reference points he plans to use if Hutchinson turns their second meeting into another grueling scrap.

Ring logic backs him up. A tough defeat often teaches a fighter more than a string of easy stoppage wins. Buatsi discovered he can stay in the pocket when an opponent matches his physical strength.

Belief and physical durability are entirely different matters. A boxer can feel mentally bulletproof while his physical reserves are running low, so pure self-belief offers no clue about the version stepping through the ropes.

It also discounts just how punishing their initial collision was. Buatsi got his hand raised, but Hutchinson made him fight for every inch. The Smith clash was hardly the first time Buatsi absorbed heavy damage to stay on course. Surviving a war never wipes away the wear on the odometer.

Hutchinson arrives fresh off an impressive win over Ezra Taylor, an effort that drew heavy praise on talkSPORT. Replicating that success against Buatsi presents a steeper hurdle. Buatsi’s inside work and committed body assault gave Hutchinson fits the first time around, problems the Scotsman must solve.

Hutchinson might not need a massive tactical overhaul. If he took another step forward while Buatsi lost a half-step, the gap between them narrows instantly.

Buatsi laughed off suggestions that anyone forced his hand for the return bout.

“I definitely wasn’t bullied into it,” Buatsi said on talkSPORT. “What I said was that I wanted something on the line. The minute we got it, everything was accepted on our side.”

The vacant WBC light heavyweight crown gives him that target. It puts a world title on the table against an opponent he already solved once, though identical tactics never guarantee an identical finish.

The previous victory feeds Buatsi’s certainty. The lackluster Parker outing gives Hutchinson every reason to believe the timing favors him. Now, Buatsi has to prove those hard-earned lessons still have the physical engine to back them up.

Sports.title: John Fury Fears Humiliation For Fury-Joshua Loser
Sports.content:
John Fury fears the loser of Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua won’t cope with the abuse afterward. That could happen, but these two have waited so long to fight that a defeat shouldn’t carry the weight it would have five years ago.

“They’ll get that much stick, the loser, they won’t be able to cope with it,” Fury said in the BBC documentary Rivals: Fury v Joshua, as reported by talkSPORT.

You can understand a father worrying about that. The losing fighter will have clips of the defeat thrown at him whenever he opens his phone, especially if he gets knocked out. Years of accomplishments can get buried beneath one ugly night when fans want to rub it in.

Still, John is giving that reaction too much power. Neither fighter should have to beat the other at this stage to protect everything he achieved earlier in his career.

The trouble is that Fury and Joshua spent years being compared without getting into the ring together. That allowed their supporters to keep arguing that their man would win. Once they fight, one side will have a result to wave around, and the other will have to live with it.

But it won’t tell us who would have won when both were younger. It will tell us who has more left in December. Those are two different arguments, even if the winning side treats them as the same thing.

John himself accepts that both have declined. That makes his fear of humiliation harder to buy as a reason for the fight never to happen. If neither man is at his best, there should be room to accept a loss without treating the beaten fighter like a fraud.

A bad beating could make retirement the sensible choice for the loser. But where is the winner really going? Beating another aging heavyweight doesn’t suddenly make either man better equipped to face the younger punchers in the division.

My expectation is that the winner looks for another lucrative Usyk fight, if it can be made, or an opponent he believes he can beat. It is difficult to picture either volunteering to face Daniel Dubois. That would mean taking a dangerous fight when a more carefully selected opponent could keep the paydays coming.

That limits what this contest actually settles. The loser could be pushed toward retirement, while the winner carries on choosing his opportunities carefully. Neither outcome makes this the start of a fresh run through the heavyweight division.

John’s fear of the ridicule is understandable. But the winner gets bragging rights over another faded name, and the loser shouldn’t have his whole career dismissed because he came off second best.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Predicts A Mayweather vs Garcia Fight Won’t Happen
Sports.content:
Rumors of a high-profile fight between Ryan Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) and Floyd “Money” Mayweather (50-0, 27 KOs) have been circulating, but Garcia’s promoter Oscar De La Hoya believes that on February 6, 2027, Garcia will not be sharing the ring with Mayweather.

The Golden Boy Promotions CEO, Oscar De La Hoya, thinks Mayweather is capable of giving Garcia a good fight. However, he believes that instead of Mayweather, Ryan Garcia will face Teofimo Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) on February 6th.

Back on October 21st, Ryan Garcia posted breaking news on all of his social media platforms. Garcia claimed a Hall of Fame boxer reached out to him to discuss a potential title fight.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia said. “But it’s real Floyd, and I agreed to a fight at 147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world, 50-0 vs. the current champ.”

Garcia doubled down on the claim when he posted a second message on his Instagram account, and this message included a photo of Garcia and Mayweather in what appears to be a FaceTime call.

As time went on, fight fans were becoming skeptical about the Mayweather vs. Garcia matchup actually happening because Garcia was doing all the talking while Mayweather remained silent.

Then, finally, on November 1st, Floyd Mayweather posted the  for his upcoming exhibition bout. Included in the , Mayweather confirmed the Garcia fight when he stated, “This is a lil tune-up before me and Ryan Garcia lock up Feb. 2027.”

At this point, it seemed like the bout was official, but during a recent interview with Sean Zittel, Garcia’s promoter Oscar De La Hoya made a statement that puts the fight in doubt.

“I do love that Teofimo fight, uh, sometime in February on DAZN. And you know the Floyd Mayweather thing, yes, there are a lot of rumors, a lot of speculation.Who knows? I don’t think it will happen, but look if it does, I’ve always said yeah, it’s a 50/50 fight,” De La Hoya stated.

Ryan Garcia has one more fight on his Golden Boy contract. Garcia keeps talking about Floyd, but if his promoter is leaning toward Teofimo, then there’s a good chance we will see a Garcia vs Lopez title bout in February.

Fighting the WBA welterweight world champion Teofimo Lopez makes a lot of sense. If Ryan wins, he will have a victory over a high-level opponent, and the win would equate to Garcia becoming a unified champion.

If he decides to fight Floyd Mayweather he has everything to lose and nothing to gain. If Garcia loses to Mayweather, it’s an embarrassment, and if he defeats Mayweather, nobody is going to give him credit for beating a 50-year-old man.

Sports.title: Is Diego Pacheco Built For World Titles Or Permanent Contender Status?
Sports.content:
Diego Pacheco needs his November 14 clash with Darius Fulghum to deliver a clear direction. Padding his record with another win over a contender helps, but the undefeated super middleweight has reached a stage where championship talk requires a targeted belt and a credible route to get there.

Facing Fulghum, 30, is not necessarily a bad fight on paper, but when you look at what has been bypassed over the last two years, the frustration for fans makes complete sense. Pacheco walked away from Christian Mbilli twice. The IBF ordered a final eliminator in late 2024, but Pacheco backed out to fight Steven Nelson instead.

A few months later, the WBC ordered a purse bid between them for an interim title, and Matchroom withdrew him again. While traveling to Quebec on an away promoter’s budget is a legitimate business concern, walking away from two separate sanctioning body routes against the same contender gave fans the impression he wanted no part of Mbilli’s pressure.

Then came the Hamzah Sheeraz situation in January 2026. The WBO ordered a purse bid for the vacant super middleweight belt. Pacheco was the No. 2 contender with a clear path to an actual world championship, yet he pulled out right before the bid. Even with Eddie Hearn presenting it as a matter of timing and readiness, walking away from a vacant title shot against another young, tall puncher did not sit well with the public.

Most recently, when the WBO super middleweight opening emerged against Janibek Alimkhanuly around September 2026, Pacheco was bypassed completely in favor of the Fulghum date. While Jacob Bank took the call to face Janibek, Pacheco opted for an in-house Matchroom card in Carson. Fulghum is an accomplished amateur and a solid puncher, but he does not carry the status of a title fight or an elite final eliminator.

At 25 years old, Pacheco has reached the point where building fights no longer cut it. Taking on Fulghum while Mbilli, Sheeraz, and Janibek were all realistic possibilities makes this look like matchmakers protecting an asset rather than letting him fight for the hardware.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Says Jaime Munguia Looks Worn Down
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia looks worn down despite being younger than Canelo Alvarez, according to Tim Bradley. He argued that years of taking heavy punishment have taken a massive toll.

Munguia’s recent outing against Nikita Zon only added to worries that began with his knockout defeat to Bruno Surace, pointing to a fighter who looks uneasy whenever punches head his direction.

“I think even though he’s younger, he is worn down. And I think he’s worn down even more than Canelo Alvarez because when you look at Munguia and his style, all he do is eat shots. He eat punches. His defense is trash,” Bradley said on Boxing King Media.

Munguia settled the score by beating Surace in a rematch and picked up a win over Armando Resendiz, yet neither result dispelled doubts surrounding his punch resistance. Getting hurt by Zon, a fighter without a reputation for big power, made those questions impossible to ignore.

The initial knockout against Surace looks like a clear dividing line. Since that stoppage, Munguia has appeared rattled by incoming fire, even during rounds he controls. An offensive fighter who relies on exchanging blows loses a critical edge the moment hesitation creeps into the equation.

Struggling with Zon does not prove his chin is completely shot, but it does suggest a real psychological change. The willingness to scrap remains intact. The automatic confidence required to withstand flush shots seems diminished.

Bradley pointed out that extra bulk might be hurting Munguia inside the ring.

“You got all these new muscles and six-pack and all of that stuff, and you running out of gas like that, bro. Like, you need to rethink whatever the hell you doing, man,” Bradley noted.

Cardio issues only make defensive flaws worse. Once the punch volume declines, opponents can exploit holes in his guard without fearing immediate retaliation. When doubt about taking a punch enters the mix, an offensive dynamo quickly gets stuck in hesitation.

Paulie Malignaggi agreed with that bleak view, declaring that Munguia is slipping fast. Malignaggi suggested a rematch with Canelo could materialize precisely because Alvarez would view him as an easy target.

That perspective reveals how the industry currently rates Munguia. Wins are keeping him in line for marquee bouts, but shaky moments in the ring are making elite competition eager to sign the contract. Avenging the Surace loss closed a chapter on paper, but regaining absolute trust in his punch resistance is proving to be a much tougher fight.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Took Zuffa Cash Over Cuban Nightmare
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley owes nobody an apology for taking Zuffa’s money. When Eddie Hearn brushed off the financial gap as merely “a couple hundred grand,” Bentley gave the only reasonable answer a 31-year-old prizefighter could give.

He makes his promotional debut this Saturday at the Copper Box Arena against Shane Mosley Jr. While losing his WBO middleweight belt clouded the move, Bentley views the extra cash as life-changing security.

“Couple hundred grand more is a lot of money. That’s a deposit on a house at least, or more than a deposit on a house,” Bentley told Pro Boxing Fans. “A couple hundred grand more might be change to him. But to me, that’s a lot of money. Him and his family are secured and they’re good for life. What about me? Why can’t I have that opportunity?”

It is hard to argue with that logic. Promoters can lecture fighters about championship legacy because they do not have to absorb punches to keep the hardware. For Bentley, the pay bump provides real stability for his family.

Matchroom had floated an idea for him to headline in Ghana, honoring his family roots. Bentley admits he would have loved defending his title there, but his Zuffa deal was already locked in. In the end, he took what made practical sense.

“I’m 31. I ain’t got another 10 years,” Bentley explained. “So, I got to be really selfish and get what I can from this sport before leaving it.”

Now comes the tough part, because the boxing side must justify the decision. Bentley hopes Zuffa can secure matchups with rival middleweight champions, yet those bouts remain unmade. A massive first purse is great, but regular dates against quality opposition will determine the true value of the contract.

Bentley remains frustrated over how the WBO handled his mandatory commitment against Yoenli Hernandez. He believed he had clearance for a voluntary defense before facing Hernandez next year, but claims the sanctioning body shifted its stance once his new promotional pact leaked.

“As soon as everyone caught wind I was moving promotional stables, that’s when everything changed,” Bentley said.

He noted that neither he nor his management ever laid eyes on the petition Hernandez supposedly filed. While that represents Bentley’s side of the fallout rather than concrete evidence against the sanctioning body, it explains his bitterness.

All of that takes a backseat to Mosley. The American is durable, hungry, and dangerous. A loss on Saturday would completely derail Bentley’s timeline for regaining world honors.

Bentley made his financial case. Saturday night is about showing what Zuffa paid for.

Taking on Yoenli was widely viewed as a disaster waiting to happen. The Cuban amateur standout is an absolute nightmare style matchup, and getting taken apart by him for short money would have left Bentley empty-handed, battered, and right back at square one. Cashing in on the front end makes total sense when the alternative is getting wrecked for peanuts.

The trap, though, is thinking Zuffa is a safe harbor. They operate with cold, corporate efficiency. If Bentley slips up and Mosley beats him on Saturday, that multi-fight deal suddenly might not be worth the paper it is printed on. Promotions love you when you give them leverage, but once an older fighter loses his title and drops his debut, the interest dries up fast.

Without a belt to force anyone’s hand, Bentley’s situation is limited. He got his payday, but if Mosley outworks him, Zuffa could easily shelve him or cut bait entirely, leaving him right where he feared he would end up, just with one nice check in the bank.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia Announced For Fury-Joshua
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder faces Jai Opetaia on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, serving as the co-feature to Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua on Netflix, Ring Magazine announced today. On paper, it sounds massive.

In reality, the matchup leans heavily on Wilder’s legacy rather than any guarantee of a thrilling contest. The real question is whether the former champion has anything left to offer, or if he is simply being set up as a marquee name on Opetaia’s resume.

Opetaia makes the jump from cruiserweight to take on a veteran whose present-day form is a massive question mark. Wilder once captivated audiences because someone was practically guaranteed to hit the canvas. Yet recent setbacks have drained that aura. Bouncing back against Tyrrell Herndon and Derek Chisora did little to prove he can still run with top-tier heavyweights. Herndon brought virtually zero profile, while outpointing Chisora hardly signals a career renaissance.

Because of that decline, Wilder becomes an ideal target for Opetaia. He delivers elite name value, championship pedigree, and the lingering threat of a highlight-reel finish. At the same time, his age and physical mileage make him a vastly safer proposition than young, dangerous contenders like Daniel Dubois, Agit Kabayel, Filip Hrgovic, or Moses Itauma.

Opetaia’s camp likely would not jump at those fights with anywhere near the same eagerness. Even someone like Bakhodir Jalolov would represent a much rougher initiation into the heavyweight division. Those challenges would force Opetaia to prove his mobility, punching power, and chin hold up against heavyweights who are in their prime.

Targeting Wilder lets Opetaia chase the spotlight without taking on that degree of risk. Even an explosive stoppage victory would leave plenty of doubts about how he matches up with the division’s elite.

Wilder still holds one classic trump card. If that trademark right hand lands cleanly with full power, Opetaia could be out cold before his slick boxing fundamentals take control. Opetaia showed vulnerability against Huseyin Cinkara, raising genuine concerns about how he handles elite heavyweight firepower.

That equalizer only matters if Wilder actually pulls the trigger. With his history of shoulder trouble, the real capability of that weapon remains unclear until fight night. If he looks tentative, sluggish, and unable to establish respect, Opetaia could roll over him early.

That is the major gamble with putting this bout in the chief-support slot. A faded Wilder getting dominated may generate flashy clips for social media, but it makes for a lopsided, disappointing viewing experience. His name dresses up the marquee, yet it remains to be seen how many fans still view him as must-watch TV.

Opetaia would gain far more credibility by testing himself against a top heavyweight contender or booking a cruiserweight collision with David Benavidez. Wilder offers a different prize entirely, letting Opetaia look devastating against an opponent fans remember as terrifying.

Whether Wilder still has any of that venom left will determine if this co-main event actually delivers on its billing. Wilder has looked completely faded, uncoordinated, and gun-shy for a long time. His legs are gone, his punch resistance has evaporated, and the explosive athleticism that once compensated for his lack of basic boxing fundamentals is nowhere to be found.

Putting him in with someone as sharp, fast, and aggressive as Opetaia feels cynical. For the organizers and Opetaia’s handlers, it checks cynical commercial boxes: It is built to lure casual and older viewers. Those fans remember the destructive knockout artist who ruled the WBC division and had the trilogy with Fury. They see the name, assume it is an explosive heavyweight collision, and either tune into Netflix or buy into the buzz.

The result offers almost no real sporting substance. Hardcore fans see right through it. If Opetaia blasts out a 41-year-old, fragile shell of Wilder, what does it prove? It tells us nothing about how Opetaia handles a legitimate, prime heavyweight contender who can absorb shots and fire back.

Yet, the highlight reel will be circulated everywhere, marketed as Opetaia making a devastating statement in the heavyweight division. The casual viewers will dismiss it regardless. If Wilder looks dreadful, clumsy, and gets wiped out in a round or two, casuals will simply view the whole thing as a sad mismatch featuring a washed fighter rather than crediting Opetaia as an elite heavyweight force.

It ends up in that weird circus middle ground: too lopsided and artificial to earn respect from hardcore purists, and too sad of a spectacle to leave casual viewers satisfied once the opening bell actually rings.

Ghana News.title: PIAC elects Peter Quartey as new Chair for one-year term
Ghana News.content:
Economist and Development Finance Expert, Professor Peter Quartey

Economist and development finance expert Professor Peter Quartey has been elected Chair of the Public Interest and Accountability Committee (PIAC) to serve a one-year term, effective 3rd November, 2026. Members of the Committee elected

Professor Quartey, a Member representing the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences (GAAS), at a meeting held on Tuesday, 3rd November 2026, to serve a one-year term. He succeeds Mr Richard Ellimah, whose tenure as Chair ended in October 2026. The elections follow the swearing-in of five new members of PIAC by the Ministry of Finance.

The five members were nominated by their respective institutions to serve on the Committee in accordance with the established nomination process. Professor Quartey was also sworn in following his renomination by the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences to serve another two-year term as a PIAC Member. At the same meeting, Mr Samuel Bekoe, Member representing Think Tanks, was elected Vice Chair to serve a one-year term.

Mr Samuel Bekoe, Vice Chair, PIAC

Professor Peter Quartey is an accomplished Professor of Economics with over 22 years of experience in development finance, private sector development, monetary and financial sector development, and digital finance.

He holds a PhD in Development Economics from the University of Manchester and an MSc in Quantitative Development Economics from the University of Warwick, both in the United Kingdom.

He also holds an MPhil and a BA in Economics from the University of Ghana. He has extensive experience in strategic

leadership, institutional governance, research and policy development, having held several senior academic and board positions.

Reconstitution of Membership. The Committee's membership has been reconstituted following the expiration of some members' tenure.

The newly sworn-in Members of the Committee.

Mama Agumekosua V from the Queen Mothers Association of Ghana, Dr Edmund Adinkra-Darko of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), Alhaji Abdul Majeed Saeed from the Muslim Groups, Rev Johoiada Godwin Amuzu from the Christian Groups, Mr Daniel Kissi from the Association of Ghana Industries/ Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industries, and Mr Kyei Yamoah from Civil Society and Community-Based Organisations were subsequently sworn into office on Tuesday, 3rd November, 2026 by the Director Legal at the Ministry of Finance, Ms Evelyn Amerley Nuno-Amarteifio.

PIAC congratulates Professor Peter Quartey and Mr Samuel Bekoe on their election and wishes them success in their respective leadership roles. The Committee also welcomes its newly sworn-in Members and looks forward to their contributions towards strengthening its mandate.

Ghana News.title: Ghana remains exposed to volatility in gold, cocoa and oil prices; domestic risks also persist – IMF
Ghana News.content:
Ghana remains exposed to volatility in gold, cocoa, and oil prices, as well as to geopolitical tensions and tighter global financial conditions, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Mission that reviewed Ghana’s first Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI).

The Mission also warned of domestic risks, including significant domestic debt rollover needs, fiscal pressures from the energy, cocoa, and gold sectors, and remaining financial sector weaknesses.

It, however, pointed out that prudent monetary policy, greater exchange rate flexibility, stronger reserve buffers, and buildup of a sinking fund to pay for maturing debt remain key to safeguarding stability.

“Strengthening governance remains a priority. Adoption of the Conduct of Public Officers Bill, publication of the second National Ethics and Anti-Corruption Action Plan, and improved oversight of state-owned enterprises will help build public trust and support private investment”, it stated.

On the performance of the PCI, it said “Performance under the PCI has been broadly satisfactory. Most quantitative targets under this review are met. In response to the decline in foreign exchange reserves in recent months, the authorities [Ministry of Finance & Bank of Ghana] have taken corrective actions, including moving foreign exchange intermediation from the Bank of Ghana to GoldBod, and implementing the higher gold sale requirement for large-scale miners”.

“Steadfast implementation of these measures, alongside greater exchange rate flexibility, will be essential to rebuild reserves in line with program objective”, it added.

The Mission also mentioned that “Structural reforms remain on track. The authorities published the Fiscal Strategy Document, obtained parliamentary approval of the new Cocoa Board Act to strengthen sector governance and financial discipline, and continued quarterly electricity tariff adjustments. They also completed, ahead of schedule, a comprehensive review of customs and excise legislation”.

It added that work is advancing on reforming the Bank of Ghana’s liquidity management framework, rolling out the Integrated Tax Administration System, operationalizing the Fiscal Council, and preparing the Fiscal Risk Statement. “Completing the remaining reforms on time, including the delayed publication of the audit of the ECG’s collection accounts, will be important”.

The Mission thanked the government and other stakeholders for their warm hospitality and constructive discussions, concluding that the IMF remains a committed partner in Ghana’s efforts to preserve stability and achieve stronger, more inclusive, and job-rich growth.

Ghana News.title: Delays in alternative petroleum discharge facility adding up to GH¢0.60 per litre in costs – CEMSE
Ghana News.content:
The Centre for Media, Society and Economic Studies (CEMSE) says delays in developing alternative facilities for discharging petroleum products are contributing to higher costs in Ghana's downstream petroleum sector, with demurrage charges estimated to add between GH¢0.47 and GH¢0.60 to the cost of each litre of fuel.

In a statement issued on Thursday, November 5, 2026, the think tank called for urgent investment in alternative petroleum discharge infrastructure, warning that Ghana's continued dependence on the major facility at Tema is exposing the sector to congestion, delays and additional costs.

CEMSE said the sector recorded cumulative demurrage costs of approximately US$61.6 million in 2025, compared with a historical annual estimate of about US$35 million.

It added that approximately US$46.73 million had reportedly been incurred in demurrage costs in 2026 as of the date of its statement.

According to the organisation, the associated costs translate into an additional burden of between GH¢0.47 and GH¢0.60 per litre of petroleum products, equivalent to approximately 2.63% to 3.35% of the retail pump price.

CEMSE argued that reducing discharge delays through additional infrastructure and improved operational efficiency could lower the cost burden on petroleum users.

“The implication is that petroleum users would have been paying less and saving at least GH¢0.47 on a litre of petroleum products if the cost of discharging is reduced through additional infrastructure and improved operational efficiency,” the statement said.

CEMSE said Ghana's reliance on the major petroleum discharge facility at Tema, which it estimates handles about 75% of petroleum discharges, creates operational and supply-chain vulnerabilities.

It warned that the absence of alternative mooring systems increases the risk of vessel congestion, prolonged waiting times and delays in discharging petroleum products, potentially disrupting timely supplies.

The think tank also pointed to the growth in petroleum product imports over the past decade, arguing that infrastructure development has not kept pace with demand.

It said product supply increased from 3,528,583 metric tonnes in 2015 to 6,089,046 metric tonnes in 2025, representing an increase of about 73%.

Over the same period, the number of Bulk Oil Distribution and Export Companies (BIDECs) rose from 37 in 2015 to 53 in 2026, an increase of approximately 43%.

CEMSE said the growth in product volumes and the number of operators had not been matched by an expansion of mooring infrastructure.

The organisation has also called for a review of the existing exclusivity arrangement governing petroleum discharge infrastructure, including its scope and implications for future investment.

It wants government to assess the regulatory and institutional barriers that may be preventing the development of alternative facilities and establish a framework to encourage credible private-sector investment.

“Alternative petroleum discharge infrastructure should be incorporated into the country's long-term downstream petroleum infrastructure and energy security planning, with defined investment priorities, implementation timelines and appropriate regulatory oversight,” it said.

CEMSE's statement follows an arrangement reportedly granted in 2015 to a South African entity, giving it exclusive rights to operate without a competing facility for 15 years.

The organisation says the arrangement has left Ghana with limited room for competing infrastructure investment.

CEMSE has urged government to provide clear policy direction and take steps to address the infrastructure gap.

As of November 5, 2026, government had not publicly responded to the organisation's call for a review of the arrangement.

Ghana News.title: Queen Máxima applauds PharmAccess’ NkwaPlus for saving patients time and livelihoods
Ghana News.content:
Queen Máxima of the Netherlands has expressed admiration for a digital remote system that allows patients living with hypertension and diabetes to monitor their conditions from home without making frequent visits to the hospital.

During a visit to Manna Mission Hospital in Accra on Tuesday, November 3, the Queen witnessed a live demonstration of the NkwaPlus digital platform, which enables patients to record their blood pressure readings and receive medical advice remotely.

The Queen, who is in Ghana as the United Nations Secretary-General's Special Advocate for Financial Health, interacted with nurses, doctors and patients to understand how the technology is improving healthcare delivery while reducing the financial burden on patients.

One of the patients who caught her attention was 57-year-old Georgina Amedome, a widow and mother of three who has lived with hypertension for 18 years.

Georgina explained that the digital monitoring system has reduced her hospital visits, allowing her to spend more time running her business and caring for her children.

"I have been living with high blood pressure for 18 good years now. Because of NkwaPlus, I have not been coming to the hospital as often as before. I check my blood pressure twice at home. I send the readings to the doctor. If the reading is high, the doctor will ask me to come to the hospital immediately. But if it is normal, I can go about my business and work," she told the Queen.

The Queen appeared particularly interested in how the technology was helping Georgina maintain her livelihood.

"As a businesswoman, I go to the market early in the morning to sell my goods, earn some money and take care of my children at home. It saves me money and time," Georgina explained.

When Queen Máxima asked about the cost of travelling to the hospital, Georgina indicated that she spent approximately GH¢20 on transportation for each visit.

She explained that previously, she had to endure long queues at the hospital, but the digital platform now allows her to check her blood pressure at home and share the readings with healthcare professionals.

The Queen welcomed the development, describing the ability of patients to receive medical attention without frequently travelling to the hospital as a significant improvement.

Queen witnesses live blood pressure monitoring

During the interaction, Nurse Esther Nyadzorgbe demonstrated how patients are registered on the NkwaPlus platform and trained to monitor their blood pressure independently.

She explained that the system has helped reduce treatment defaults and enabled healthcare professionals to monitor patients who might otherwise develop complications without timely medical attention.

"Some time ago, we used to have a lot of emergencies. Some patients defaulted on treatment, while others did not take their medications regularly. But with the NkwaPlus app, we are able to monitor them even from the comfort of their homes. It has reduced the long queues at the hospital and helped our patients save money to take care of their other needs and businesses," she added.

As part of the demonstration, Georgina entered her blood pressure reading of 140 over 100, with a pulse of 80, into the application. The system immediately generated an alert warning that her blood pressure was high and advising her to seek medical attention.

"We suggest that your blood pressure is too high. Please go to a hospital or the nearest health facility immediately," the message stated.

Nurse Esther then asked Georgina to explain what the alert meant.

"The message tells me that my blood pressure is too high. I have to rush to the hospital immediately," she responded.

The Queen subsequently observed how the hospital's medical team received the alert through the platform. A doctor demonstrated how the system could be used to review a patient's readings, assess medication and initiate a video consultation.

During the live consultation, the doctor contacted Georgina to enquire whether she had taken her medication.

"I have received your blood pressure reading. It is high. Have you taken your medication today?" the doctor asked.

After Georgina confirmed taking her medication, the doctor advised her to rest and check her blood pressure again after 30 minutes. The Queen expressed excitement about the system's ability to connect patients and doctors without requiring physical visits for every consultation.

"How wonderful," she remarked after learning that patients could sometimes receive medical advice and have their medication reviewed remotely.

Queen questions cost savings for patients and hospitals

Queen Máxima also sought to understand the financial implications of the technology, particularly the savings patients and healthcare facilities could make through early detection and treatment.

When informed that a home blood pressure monitoring device cost 600 cedis, she described the technology as a significant change in healthcare delivery.

"But that is a big change. You wouldn't be able to do that before, right?" she asked.

She also questioned whether the remote monitoring service was covered by Ghana's National Health Insurance Scheme.

Healthcare professionals explained that the initiative was still being piloted and had not yet been incorporated into the scheme's coverage.

"I want to see how much it saves both the patient and the hospital at the end of the day. Because when somebody comes too late, the hospital has to do a lot more. So you're avoiding problems, right?" the Queen asked.

Healthcare professionals explained that the system was helping to reduce long queues and allowing patients to alert doctors when they experience medical emergencies.

They also highlighted the importance of identifying complications early, noting that conditions such as stroke could require substantially more expensive treatment.

The Queen stressed the importance of digitalisation in making such healthcare innovations possible.

"And you can only do it if you have everything digitised. So you need to have the digitisation process in order to be able to come up with things like this," she observed.

Queen Máxima invited to join digital health platform

The interaction took an interesting turn when one of thedoctors invited Queen Máxima to register on the NkwaPlus platform.

"May I have the pleasure of onboarding you onto the app?" the doctor asked.

The Queen responded with a smile, explaining that she did not have hypertension or diabetes.

"Oh, but I have no hypertension. And no diabetes. I hardly take any salt, and I do my exercises every day," she said.

The doctor explained that the platform was not limited to patients with chronic diseases but could also support general wellbeing.

The healthcare workers then introduced the Queen to the Ghanaian title "Ohemaa", meaning queen, and offered her the name "Adwoa", traditionally given to females born on Monday.

The exchange formed part of the Queen's engagement with healthcare workers and patients at the facility, where she observed how digital technology could make healthcare more accessible while helping patients save time and money.

The hospital visit was part of Queen Máxima's four-day working visit to Ghana, which focuses on improving the financial wellbeing of Ghanaians through accessible financial services and initiatives that protect households against unexpected expenses.

Ghana News.title: Multiple European flights face bomb threats for second time this week
Ghana News.content:
Several flights across Europe have faced bomb threats, officials have said.

An Aer Lingus Airbus A320 plane which departed Dublin on Thursday morning issued an emergency alert, diverted and landed at Evreux air base in northern France.

Meanwhile, Finnish airline Finnair said there was a bomb threat against one of its planes travelling from Helsinki to the Italian capital on Thursday. It was escorted by air force jets and landed as scheduled.

It comes just days after eight European flights, including two departing from the UK, were targeted by suspected bomb threats. No explosives were found on any of the planes after searches.

A statement from Aer Lingus confirmed that flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome "diverted to Normandy this morning as a security precaution."

It added: "The flight landed safely and Aer Lingus will work to re-accommodate customers to their final destination as soon as possible."

Meanwhile, a Wizz Air flight travelling from Milan to Warsaw also issued an emergency alert before diverting to Vienna, Austria - though there has been no report of a bomb threat and the reason is unclear.

On Tuesday, seven planes were searched after bomb threats were made.

Two were from the UK - one travelling from Manchester which landed in Murcia, Spain, the other from London Heathrow to Warsaw, Poland.

Two Ryanair flights - one leaving Dublin and the other from Lisbon - were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC.

The sources added that police bomb disposal experts carried out standard security protocols to ensure the safety of all passengers and crew, and the alert was then cleared.

The UK government described the incidents as "malicious hoax threats".

Ghana News.title: Italian chef fired after refusing to put pineapple on pizza
Ghana News.content:
An Italian chef sacked from a Brisbane restaurant had refused to put pineapple on a pizza because it was an "insult to his culture".

Davide Tamburella was fired from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in May, a fortnight after a meeting with management who had a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour.

Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function. At the time, the chef had stated that any direction from management "need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture".

The details came to light after the chef went to Australia's Fair Work Commission claiming he had been unfairly dismissed.

In its ruling released on Tuesday, the commission noted that Tamburella's refusal to put pineapple on the pizzas was because "he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture".

It also noted that it was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years.

He had previously requested his boss to "check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza".

The state of Queensland, where the restaurant is located, is considered Australia's pineapple heartland and produces all of the country's commercially-grown pineapples.

On the Sunshine Coast, visitors regularly stop to take photos next to The Big Pineapple, a heritage-listed 16m-tall fibreglass model of the fruit, which has become a local landmark.

Other concerns were raised about Tamburella using foul language, his communication style and "escalation of frustration in the workplace".

The ruling also detailed an incident at work in April this year where Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand when he struck a metal hand rail.

Tamburella had been hoping the restaurant would sponsor a visa for him that allows skilled workers to be permanent residents.

However after his sacking, the restaurant ended that process, the tribunal heard.

He lost his unfair dismissal claim on the grounds that the application had been filed too late, according to the ruling.

The restaurant's managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was "more to this story than a pizza topping".

The BBC has approached Tamburella for comment.

On the chef's LinkedIn profile, he describes himself as someone who, throughout his career, has focused on "delivering exceptional food" and "improving business performance".

Three months ago he posted a "letter for chefs" with the theme "respecting the ingredients".

The LinkedIn profile states he now works at another Brisbane restaurant. A BBC check has found that pineapple is not on its menu.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaians look back on Christmas memories that have stayed with them
Ghana News.content:
From childhood surprises and a first trip abroad to simple family gatherings, some Ghanaians have Christmas memories that have remained special to them over the years.

As part of our Christmas series, we spoke to people about the celebrations and experiences from their past that they still remember fondly.

For Kate Quayeson, Christmas as a child was a time to look forward to new shoes, dresses and other treats from her mother.

She recalled how her mother would use a broom to measure her legs before buying her Christmas shoes, often choosing a bigger size so she could wear them the following year.

“My mother will use broom to measure my leg. Then she'll go and buy a shoe that is bigger than my size, maybe like for the next year or something,” she said.

Her dresses were also usually bigger than her actual size, with her mother confident that she would eventually grow into them.

“She will buy a dress that is bigger and the longer that will be bigger than me, all in the name of ‘wobɛnyini abɛto’,” she recalled.

The excitement extended beyond clothes. Kate also looked forward to floral socks, hair products, cream and colourful clips for her hair.

“It was a very nice experience,” she said.

For Kwame Otchere, one Christmas stands out for a different reason.

Two years ago, he travelled to the United States to spend the festive season. It was his first trip outside Ghana and his first experience of flying.

“It was very, very, very enjoyable because it was my first time travelling and my first time being in the plane. So the fun was extra,” he said.

Christopher Richardson, meanwhile, remembers a Christmas when his parents and siblings came together to organise a celebration at home.

The family cooked, listened to music and played games, creating an atmosphere he still looks back on fondly.

“We cooked, we listened to music, played some games and we're just having fun,” he recalled.

It was not an elaborate celebration, but for Christopher, the presence of his family made it special.

“It wasn't a big celebration, but it means a lot to me because everyone was happy and together.”

Ghana News.title: Over 60,000 teachers complete GES promotion exercise as new policy expands career opportunities
Ghana News.content:
Examination

More than 60,000 teachers across the country have successfully completed the three-day Ghana Education Service (GES) promotion exercise, which is expected to significantly expand opportunities for career advancement under a policy that separates professional ranks from administrative positions.

The exercise ended on Wednesday, November 5, with monitoring officers reporting a generally smooth and incident-free process at all centres nationwide.

In a Facebook post on Wednesday, the GES, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Daniel Fenyi, said this year's exercise was particularly significant because it marked a major step in implementing the policy to decouple professional ranks from office positions.

The policy is intended to broaden career progression opportunities and ensure that deserving teachers are not disadvantaged by the limited availability of positions within the Service's administrative structure.

Under the new arrangement, the number of teachers attaining the rank of Director II is expected to increase by 1,500 per cent, while those attaining Director I will increase by 340 per cent.

The Service is also expected to record substantial increases in the number of teachers advancing through other professional ranks, including Principal Superintendent (PS), Assistant Director II (ADII), Assistant Director I (ADI) and Deputy Director (DD).

The GES described the changes as a significant shift in the career progression framework, which places greater emphasis on professional competence, experience and continued service.

It stressed that, as was the case last year, deliberate measures had been taken to ensure that all deserving staff could progress to higher ranks without being constrained by the availability of vacancies.

The policy is expected to have far-reaching implications for teacher morale and professional motivation by creating a more inclusive system that recognises the contributions and professional development of teachers.

The Service wished all teachers who participated in the exercise success and acknowledged the dedication of the officers, invigilators, administrators and other stakeholders whose efforts contributed to its smooth conduct.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
