John Barrett, a professor of political science at Texas-based LeTourneau University, told CBC News that had Talerico been the state's only winner, he may have chalked it up to a political "fluke," that Talerico was just a good candidate with a weak opponent.

But Abbott's concession, along with the Senate and governorship victories, indicated to Barrett that a "political earthquake" had indeed occurred.

"I like that term because every generation or so, the political plates, you know, realign."

Texas 'will continue to evolve'

Barrett listed off a number of areas in Texas, including Denton County, Tarrant County, Collin County, that Democrats have almost never carried.

"They all turned blue," he said. "The suburbs all around the cities turned blue."

Barrett says much of this can be attributed to Latino voters and so-called soccer moms switching their votes from Republican to Democrat.

Those demographics may have initially been drawn to Trump two years earlier over his promises to fix the economy and lower inflation, but he says they've since soured on the president because they believe he hasn't lived up to his promises. He believes that in the future, those voters will still be up for grabs.

"That's not to say that the Democrats are going to win from here on out," he said. "But I do think it's going to be more feasible for them to win."

"Texas is going to be in play in a way that it hasn't been to date."

Cal Jillson, a political science professor at Texas-based Southern Methodist University, says it's too soon to write off Republicans in Texas.

He noted that years ago, the state was a Democratic stronghold and it took decades for the Republicans to become the natural governing party.

Jillson says he believes the midterm results were due, in part, to an electorate that was negative on Trump, saw top Republicans as tied to him and regarded the Republican Party in general as arrogant and entitled.

"I think Texas is still a red state, but not as deeply red as it once was, and it will continue to evolve toward two-party competitive politics," Jillson told CBC News.

Democrats 'zero in' on populist values

Political science professor Robert Alexander at Ohio-based Bowling Green State University, said Democrats all over the U.S., but particularly in Ohio and Texas, featured the same kind of candidates hitting the same kind of populist messages.

Trump has won Ohio three times, and carried the state by 11 points in 2024. But Alexander, who is also the founding director of the Democracy and Public Policy Network, says the same voters who chose Trump then, turned around and voted Brown into the Senate this year.

"So I think the Democrats really did zero in on those populist values," he said.

Democrats also made huge inroads in Ohio's state legislature, breaking the Republican supermajority there.

Alexander says that despite Republican losses at the Senate and governor level, the party was still competitive in races at the state and local level.

"They still lost in most cases, but those races were razor thin," he told CBC News. "I think that speaks to, there is a pull toward the Republican Party in the state, even in a wave year."

Alexander says that rather than being distinctly red or blue, he sees Ohio as "more populist and purplish."

He also notes that 2028 will still be a fight, despite the defeat the Republicans suffered this year. "I mean, it's going to be hyper competitive."

World.title: What to watch for as Carney introduces his 2nd federal budget
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Prime Minister Mark Carney will deliver his second federal budget on Thursday as the Liberal government reveals next steps in its plan to support the country through an affordability crunch and the trade war.

Carney has spent much of the first 20 months of his prime ministership retooling the Canadian economy with an eye toward growth. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is promising more details on what's to come next to further boost economic expansion.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday while helping make his own shoes — continuing the budget tradition of finance ministers getting a new pair before delivering an economic update — Champagne said this document will reveal how Canada will become "masters of our destiny."

"You need to invest in growth, you need to invest alongside businesses. You also need to invest in sovereignty," he said.

Champagne holds up a boot during a tour of the Pajar shoe factory in Montreal on the eve of the budget. (Graham Hughes/The Canadian Press)

Some indicators suggest those investments are paying off: the Bank of Canada and the International Monetary Fund are projecting roughly two per cent GDP growth next year. The OECD expects growth to be lower than that, but still higher than all other G7 countries except the U.S.

The unemployment rate, which has seen some relatively wild swings amid the trade uncertainty, is lower than it was a year ago.

Foreign direct investment into Canada is high and the government's recently announced "productivity mega-deduction," a big ticket item that lets companies write off investments in a tax-advantaged way, is designed to spur things along even more.

Canadians will also get a chance to take some ownership in the projected growth: the budget may include details on how individual investors could eventually buy into the Canada Growth Fund, a new Crown-controlled sovereign wealth fund that will take ownership stakes in some major projects and businesses.

Affordability measures

Still, Champagne suggested more work is needed on the issue many voters tell pollsters they care about most: the rising cost of living, which worsened late last month when the Bank of Canada raised interest rates to tame inflation.

"Mark Carney remains one of the most popular prime ministers we've ever had. And all of that is happening in the context of people still saying that affordability is the top issue," Abacus Data pollster David Coletto said in an interview.

"But it doesn't mean that that immunity lasts forever. People still need to feel that this government cares about those day-to-day issues."

The most recent Statistics Canada jobs data also shows that while average hourly wages rose about 2.3 per cent year-over-year as of September, that fell short of the three per cent climb in consumer prices reported over the same period.

Canadian food bank usage hit record highs this year as some people struggle to buy the groceries they need.

Food bank usage continues to grow in Canada. (Sammy Kogan/The Canadian Press)

The government has kept a lid on immigration since coming into office, dramatically dialling back the number of temporary migrants to tamp down housing prices.

That may have worked to some extent: national average home sale prices are 22 per cent lower than they were at the March 2022 peak while rent has dropped about nine per cent from its all-time high in May 2024, according to the latest industry figures.

The budget will reveal immigration targets for the coming two years.

The Conservatives have hammered the government for rising prices, demanding Carney do more to help consumers shoulder energy price increases largely driven by the U.S. and Israel-Iran war.

They also want Ottawa to cut immigration levels further, framing it as part of the affordability agenda.

"Save you money — that's our mission as Conservatives, and it's our demand for the budget," Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre told reporters on Wednesday, reiterating his call for further tax relief on energy products.

"After a year and a half of Mark Carney, everything's worse."

WATCH | Poilievre on U.S. trade talks: After Democrats retake Congress, Poilievre says Canada must pressure for tariff-free trade | Duration closed caption 1:12 Asked about the U.S. midterm election results, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said 'Americans hate tariffs.' Suggesting Canada is the most popular country with the American people, Poilievre offered to work with Prime Minister Mark Carney to 'leverage' that goodwill to get a trade deal.

NDP Leader Avi Lewis, meanwhile, wants Ottawa to create a wealth tax, build 50 government-run grocery stores and make "a nation-building investment in health care."

The government is sensitive to the charge that it hasn't done enough to address affordability concerns, routinely pointing to last year's income tax cut, the move to scrap the consumer carbon tax and temporarily lifting federal levies on gas as ways it has helped.

WATCH | NDP proposes wealth tax: NDP's Lewis proposes tax on wealth over $10M before Carney tables federal budget | Duration closed caption 0:52 NDP Leader Avi Lewis proposed on Wednesday a 'wealth tax' starting at one per cent on those with assets worth $10 million or more in a plan he suggests could generate $40 billion in annual government revenue. 'It is time to tax wealth in Canada, not merely income,' Lewis said.

But after U.S. voters handed Trump's Republican Party a shellacking in this week's midterms, partly due to higher prices, politicians in this country are clearly attuned to demands that more needs to be done to avoid a voter backlash.

"We need to take care of Canadians, make life more affordable," Champagne said.

"We've already taken a number of measures to support Canadians, but at the same time we understand we need to support them now."

Deficit management

While Ottawa rolls out new initiatives it's also mindful of the deficit, which could be smaller than expected thanks to higher oil prices that have been a huge boon to government coffers.

Even if smaller than planned, the figure is still expected to be higher than the historical norm before the 2020s — and the parliamentary budget officer expects those figures to remain elevated for years.

The spring economic update pegged the deficit at $75 billion for the 2026-27 fiscal year.

This number will almost certainly change after accounting for energy-related revenue spikes and increased spending on initiatives like propping up tariff-hit industries like autos and steel.

The PBO projects the deficit will be about $63 billion this year before rising to $70 billion in the next, further adding to the federal debt, which is increasingly costly as interest rates rise.

Carney has rejigged how the government reports its spending, dividing federal outlays into two buckets: day-to-day operational spending and capital infrastructure. The government is expected to lay out its plan to balance the operational budget by 2027-28.

Canadians will also learn more details in this budget about the government's plan to privatize some of Canada's major airport operations. Those sales would result in a cash windfall, which could then be used to spend more on other planned capital-intensive infrastructure projects or pay down debt.

Whatever comes about, Poilievre isn't buying it: "Mark Carney is out of touch. His spending is out of control. Canadians are out of money."

Defence spending

Canadians will likely get a better sense in the budget of how much the Carney government's defence buildup is costing, where the money is going and where it will be coming from.

Tens of billions of dollars have been poured into national defence over the last year and a half to meet the old NATO benchmark of two per cent of the gross domestic product.

The Western military alliance is now asking members to increase spending further to five per cent of GDP (3.5 per cent direct military expenditures and 1.5 per cent on defence infrastructure) by 2035.

At the conclusion of the recent NATO summit in Turkey, Carney pledged his government would offer a full accounting for taxpayers.

"We will lay out in the budget an update with the decisions we're taking, where the fiscal track is, where the defence spending is, how we're spending the one-and-a-half per cent on defence-related expenditures, resilience expenditures, and that's the right time to do it," Carney said.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the budget would provide an update on how it's meeting NATO defence spending targets. (Nicole Osborne/The Canadian Press)

Defence analyst Dave Perry of the Canadian Global Affairs Institute said details on how Canada met the two per cent target and what the pathway is to five per cent are long overdue.

He said there were 215 words devoted to defence spending in last year's budget, which was a disappointment in terms of explanation and justification.

The government, he said, needs to be more specific about what equipment it intends to buy and how it will pay for it.

World.title: Judge rejects grandparent scammer's bid to back out of guilty plea, sends her to jail instead
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A Calgary woman who admitted to stealing thousands of dollars from elderly victims was handed a 12-month jail sentence plus a year of probation after the judge refused to allow her to back out of her guilty plea.

Alana Love Duncan, 48, pleaded guilty last year to seven counts of fraud over $5,000 after she and several accomplices stole about $70,000 from seven women, who were mostly in their eighties and nineties, over a four-week period in the summer of 2023.

The “sophisticated and predatory” grandparent scam involved Duncan acting as an “in-person courier,” noted prosecutor Don Couturier at a sentencing hearing earlier this year. In each case, the victim received a call with news that her grandson, great-grandson or nephew was in trouble and needed money.

Duncan is the only one who has been charged.

Following her plea, the Crown and defence jointly proposed a conditional sentence for Duncan, meaning she would serve her sentence at home under conditions including house arrest and then curfew.

'She stood face to face with these people'

Defence lawyer Mary Stephensen had told the judge that Duncan had been addicted to crack cocaine but was sober and focused on “trying to right this wrong.”

But in her June decision to reject the conditional sentence, Court of King’s Bench Justice Michele Hollins noted that Duncan is currently unemployed and living at home, receiving government assistance.

The proposed sentence, said Hollins, “would look very similar to the life she is living pre-conviction” and wouldn't “be at all acceptable to a reasonably informed member of the public.”

“She stood face to face with these people and took their money, knowing they believed they had to give it to her to help a family member in trouble,” wrote Hollins.

"Approving this conditional sentence would not sufficiently denounce these crimes."

Attempt to back out of plea

When she learned she would be facing a jail term, Duncan then applied to vacate her guilty plea.

On Wednesday, Hollins rejected that application, finding the proper avenue is an appeal.

Hollins then handed Duncan a one-year sentence, followed by a year of probation and ordered her to pay $12,000 in restitution.

Coin collection handed over

“The vulnerability that was exploited here was familial,” wrote Hollins in her earlier decision.

The victims were instructed to keep the matter private.

They then went to their bank and withdrew between $6,500 and $10,000 in cash, handing it over to Duncan when she arrived to collect.

In one case, a 94-year-old victim did not have the $8,000 she believed was needed for her great-grandson’s bail, so she gave away her coin collection worth $22,000.

Duncan was the one who took the coins.

“These fraudsters impersonated the grandchildren and great grandchildren of these victims, even in one case saying 'I love you lots,'" wrote Hollins.

“They also impersonated the police or other law enforcement persons, again taking extreme advantage of the trust people generally put in law enforcement.”

World.title: ‘Everybody’s pissed’: Sand blowing into homes next to rural N.S. subdivision development
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

When Jill Alcoe-Holland lifted the cover off her backyard pool in Coldbrook, N.S., earlier this year, she discovered so much muck that she immediately sent down her robotic pool cleaner.

It had its work cut out.

“For 15 days, every few hours, I was pulling up a robot full of sand,” she said.

The sand came from a 14-hectare sandpit in the middle of the quiet Annapolis Valley neighbourhood that will eventually be the site of a 30-home subdivision. The sand was dug up and is being shipped out in large dump trucks at all hours of the day, according to residents.

Sand blowing from the pit is going through their windows, covering their parked vehicles and front steps and, when it’s very windy, forcing them to leave their backyards and go inside, they say.

A robotic pool cleaner is filled with mud after operating in a pool in the backyard of a home in Coldbrook, N.S. (Submitted by Jill Alcoe-Holland)

Alcoe-Holland said her family made the mistake of opening all their windows and doors on one of the first warm days of the year.

“We came in for supper and we could write our name on our kitchen table because it was covered with sand,” Alcoe-Holland said.

'Basically a sandstorm'

More than 60 residents in the neighbourhood have signed a petition calling on government officials to do something to mitigate the blowing sand and ensure the subdivision is built sooner than later.

The residents say they aren’t opposed to the new subdivision, but they cannot tolerate having sand everywhere anymore.

“Everybody’s kind of pissed off,” said Rick Young, whose home is directly next to the sandpit.

WATCH | Why did a developer build a huge sandpit in their backyard?: Why this massive sandpit has neighbours 'pissed off' | Duration closed caption 2:02 A large sandpit has formed in a quiet Nova Scotia neighbourhood while a subdivision is being built. But as the CBC's Josh Hoffman reports, neighbours say sand is blowing everywhere, including into their pools, porches and kitchens.

Young said he and his wife can’t open the upstairs windows in their house without sand getting in.

He said he’s found sand built up on the windshields of their vehicles parked in the driveway.

“You didn't dare turn your windshield wipers on. You're scared you’ll scratch your windshield. There was that much sand,” Young said.

The front steps of Rick Young's home, which is right next to the sandpit, are covered in sand that's blown over from the subdivision development. (Rick Young)

David Grant also has to keep his windows closed at times because of the piles of sand that tower over the trees in his backyard.

He was doing yardwork this summer when the wind picked up and made him run for cover, he said.

“There was basically a sandstorm,” he said. “It was bad enough that it was bothering my breathing and I had to go inside.”

Grant said he and his wife have been considering selling their home, but they don’t know how long the sandpit will be here and believe it could reduce their property’s value.

No rules being broken

Subdivision development permits are the responsibility of municipal governments and open pits are regulated by the province.

But pits made as a result of subdivision development don’t need permits, according to a spokesperson for the Department of Environment and Climate Change.

Department staff have visited the site several times and the work is compliant with provincial regulations, the spokesperson said in an email.

Residents are also upset about large dump trucks carrying sand out of the neighbourhood at all hours of the day. (Jeorge Sadi/CBC)

A site development manager with Lutz Trucking Ltd., which is the company doing the work, declined an interview request but said they’re taking all precautions and have met with residents to try to address their concerns.

“It is enormous. There's no question. That was my first impression,” said Dave Corkum, mayor of the Municipality of Kings County.

Corkum said he has heard from several residents about the pit and understands their frustrations.



Despite its size, he said the municipality can’t do anything about it, but he believes the province can do more.

Large piles of sand can be seen through the trees in David Grant's backyard. (Jeorge Sadi/CBC)

“There certainly should be regulations and rules involved when you're right in the middle of a large-scale subdivision,” Corkum said.

There is a two-year time limit for developing a subdivision in Kings County but there can be delays, according to the mayor.

The sandpit has already been there for a year. Residents are afraid they’ll be living next to it for many more months before a subdivision is finished.

“It certainly doesn't look like it's going to happen in the near future,” said Grant, as he waits to sell his home.

MORE TOP STORIES

World.title: Colombia’s government presents “Economic Rescue Bill”
World.content:
Colombia’s Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo on Thursday presented an Economic Rescue Bill that seeks to reduce government spending and increase its revenue.

The bill grants extraordinary powers to President Abelardo de la Espriella to slash government spending by decree and includes a tax reform that includes higher sales tax rates on gasoline, coffee, cigarettes and vegetables.

The bill also includes tax breaks for corporations in an attempt to increase investment.

Abelardo’s extraordinary powers

While on campaign, De la Espriella powers vowed a 40% reduction of the State, which the bill falls short of doing.

Article 7 of the bill does grant the president extraordinary powers to “abolish, merge, and split ministries and administrative departments, as well as to determine or modify their names, objectives, and organizational structure,” and allows De la Espriella to “abolish, merge, split, and change the legal status” of other State bodies like the superintendencies, agencies, special administrative units, and public institutions.

Article 96 allows the government to change the personnel hiring of tax agency DIAN, which “would allow for the elimination of annual competitive exams for entry into the DIAN and a return to the practice of appointing thousands of officials,” according to former DIAN director Luis Carlos Reyes.

Last but not least, the bill mandates a 20% reduction in salaries of State employees, excluding the security forces, and cut half of the costs in temporary contracts.

VAT reforms and squeezing the middle class

The bill seeks to remove popular products like cocoa, coffee, sugar and fruits from a VAT exemption list and introduce a 19% sales tac on them.

An increase in taxes on gasoline will inflate its price.

The bill additionally seeks to charge VAT on vice products like liquor and cigarettes, which would make them up to 53% more expensive.

The bulk of these tax increases wouldn’t take fore until after the November 2027 local and regional elections in an apparent compromise to Congress and Colombia’s political forces.

In an attempt to not impoverish the poor, the bill seeks a mechanism that would refund up to 100% of IVA payments to some 19 million of the country’s poorest citizens.

The increased pressure on the middle class has already resulted in opposition from within De la Espriella’s congressional coalition.

Tax benefits for the capitalists

The government seeks to gradually lower the corporate income tax from 35% to 31% and offer a reduced tax rate for large companies that decide to invest in new enterprises.

According to the Inter-American Development Bank, a similar scheme introduced by former President Alvaro Uribe “was ineffective in promoting investment.”

World.title: Accusations over De la Espriella’s narco ties “lack conclusive or solid evidence,” says Colombia’s justice minister
World.content:
Colombia’s Justice Minister, Ivan Cancino, downplayed the evidence of ties between President Abelardo de la Espriella and drug traffickers that was displayed in Congress by opposition Senator Ivan Cepeda.

In a video, Cancino said that “political oversight is a fundamental tool of our democracy. However, it cannot become an arena for launching accusations without proving and substantiating them.”

The justice minister admitted that the pieces of evidence provided to Congress “may seem serious,” but “lack conclusive or solid evidence, as well as any support that could jeopardize the innocence and the presumption of innocence of our president.”

It is not just about displaying organizational charts, deeds from over a decade ago, and business transactions to construct a narrative that supports neither judicial decisions nor the documentary, testimonial, circumstantial, or expert backing required for these types of accusations. Ivan Cancino

Cancino accused the opposition of remaining “silent regarding the grave scandals involving corruption, drug trafficking, and even alleged sexual abuse, as well as fiscal irresponsibility and possible links to criminal organizations that surrounded the previous government. ”

The justice minister was forced to come out after Cepeda showed Congress evidence of De la Espriella’s business ties with multiple convicted drug traffickers and announced criminal complaints against the president.

De la Espriella’s law firm rose to prominence during the demobilization of paramilitary organization AUC with whom he created a foundation that sought to justify the paramilitary violence that terrorized much of Colombia in the 1990’s and 2000s.

Once the ties between the AUC and elected politicians became known, the president ended up defending many of the “parapoliticians” in court.

According to Cepeda, De la Espriella plays a key role in a “revolving door” system that could end up benefiting the very drug traffickers and corrupt politicians that have paid the president for his legal defense in the past.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: “Brazil and Colombia need each other,” says De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella recognized the election victory of his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Ignacio Lula, who defeated far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Colombian President said that “in the Colombian presidential campaign, President Lula openly supported Ivan Cepeda, and I won. In the Brazilian campaign, I supported Bolsonaro, and Lula won.”

“Neither does Lula decide for Colombians, nor do I decide for Brazilians. THE PEOPLE DECIDE! And when the people speak at the polls, their will is respected because it is sacred,” the president added.

Lula and I have major and profound political and ideological differences, but we agree on one fundamental point: Brazil and Colombia need each other. No other consideration can take precedence over the interests of our nations. Colombia and Brazil are sister nations, facing enormous shared challenges and opportunities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella stressed that “we have much to do and much work to carry out for the benefit of our peoples” an ought to “fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining, the protection of the Amazon, and the well-being of our citizens.”

Lula was the first leftist candidate and critic of US President Donald Trump to win an election, triggering celebrations among leftists throughout the continent.

De la Espriella, a US citizen, has been among the most fanatic among Trump supporter in trying to align his domestic policies to US foreign policy.

World.title: De la Espriella sacks interior minister after Congress bungles Colombia’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella sacked Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara hours after Congress found a procedural flaw in the passed 2027 budget, which makes the law invalid.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella briefly thanked Lara and announced he would be replaced by the ambassador to the Organization of American States, Alejandro Ordoñez.

The news surprised the interior minister, who suddenly left a congressional debate on a law to facilitate the demobilization of illegal armed groups after receiving a message on his phone.

Lara was apparently held responsible for the blunder of Congress, whose two houses approved the 2027 budget but with conflicting versions of an article on financial risk-coverage mechanisms for the Ministry of Finance.

By the time the error was detected, the budget debate had passed its October 20 deadline, forcing De la Espriella to issue a decree that would convert an older version of the budget bill into law.

The interior minister was the administration’s primary political liaison responsible for managing legislative procedure and whip operations in Congress.

Lara’s job was already under pressure after he failed to convince Congress to cede its presidency to the president’s candidate.

While Ordoñez returns from Washington, Justice Minister Ivan Cancino will assume the role of interior minister.

The incoming interior minister is an ultra conservative Catholic with ties to the Society of St. Pius X, which considers the modernizing reforms of the Catholic Church heresies and errors, and was declared in a schism with the church in June.

In Colombian politics and particularly among the opposition, Ordoñez is mainly remembered as the inspector general who illegally removed former President Gustavo Petro from his post as mayor of Bogota in 2013.

Petro was ultimately reinstated and would become president of the country in 2022.

World.title: Colombia’s Congress approves De la Espriella’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress agreed to increase the government’s 2027 budget despite promises by President Abelardo de la Espriella to reduce public spending.

Next year’s budget will be COP634.9 trillion, almost $204 billion, which is 16% more than last year’s budget and 10% higher than the proposal made by former President Gustavo Petro.

According to Finance Minister Miguel Gomez, the budget seeks to bring the State’s finances in line with reality.

The budget was approved in both the Senate and the House of Representatives with the support of De la Espriella’s government coalition.

The Historic Pact, the only leftist opposition party, rejected the budget and boycotted the vote.

On behalf of the national government, I would like to thank you all for your work over the past few months in passing the budget. I would also like to thank the opposition for the strength with which they defended their views. The message that Congress has sent today regarding the government’s economic policy is very important. It is the first step toward putting the country’s economy back on track toward growth, fiscal responsibility, and addressing the nation’s needs. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez

The budget seeks to reimpose the neoliberal model that had been abandoned by Petro and reduce public debt.

According to Green Party representative Jaime Raul Salamanca, who opposed the budget, funding for free higher education was cut in half from COP800 billion ($254 million) to COP400 billion (127 million).

“This cut raises concerns about its potential impact on the continuity and scope of this policy, which has enabled thousands of young people to enroll in public institutions of higher education,” said Salamanca.

The budget also cut the budget for the war crimes tribunal JEP, which could endanger the future of the peace process with the FARC and is opposed by the government.

World.title: De la Espriella announces “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism” as part of his “cultural counterrevolution.”

During a visit to the Culture Ministry, De la Espriella described wokeism as “an ideological paradigm that aims to transform moral, cultural, and social foundations in the West, perverting values, family tradition, and national identity.”

According to the president, Culture Minister Paola Holguin was a general in the “cultural counterrevolution.”

Culture has an enormous capacity to shape society, and that is why the State has a moral, inescapable, and political duty to prevent cultural spaces from being taken over by social communism, which is atheist and an enemy to the fundamental values upon which the nation of Colombia is built. This is where that cultural counterrevolution will begin. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that Holguin, the daughter of a reported money launderer, would lead the “Culture War” against the “extreme left,” which has “permeated all parts of society, particularly the cultural and academic spheres.”

I want to be clear about this: we are going to wage an open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism, which is nothing more than an ideological movement that aims to transform the moral, cultural, and social foundations of the West, corrupting values, family tradition, and national identity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Earlier in the day, the National Museum removed all references to members of the exterminated Patriotic Union party, slain guerrilla leader and presidential candidate Carlos Pizarro, and the struggle for the rights of Colombia’s LGBT+ community.

References to Colombia’s former guerrilla movements was “terrorism apology, which is “exactly what we have come to confront” in an attempt to “recover pride for Colombian culture.”

Atheists, the Pizarro family and gay rights activists rejected the president’s attempts to remove them from mainstream culture.

World.title: Ibero-American foreign ministers unanimously back Argentina’s Falklands claim
World.content:
Ibero-American foreign ministers unanimously back Argentina’s Falklands claim

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:21 UTC Full article

“The Ibero-American community reaffirms, once again, its support for the Argentine Republic,” said Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno

Ibero-American foreign ministers meeting in Madrid unanimously approved a special communiqué backing Argentina’s sovereignty claim over the Falklands and calling on Argentina and the United Kingdom to resume negotiations, on the eve of the Hamburg hearing on the Sea Lion oil project.

The document, approved at the foreign ministers’ meeting held during the 30th Ibero-American Summit of Heads of State and Government, urges both governments to resume talks on the dispute “as soon as possible” and acknowledges Argentina’s “constructive attitude”. The Ibero-American Conference, which brings together the countries of Latin America with Spain, Portugal and Andorra, routinely adopts such a statement at its summits.

“The Ibero-American community reaffirms, once again, its support for the Argentine Republic,” said Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, who called the issue “a sacred cause for Argentines” and defended the diplomatic route to end what he considers an anachronistic colonial situation.

The backing comes five days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea holds hearings in Hamburg on November 10 and 11 on the four provisional measures Argentina requested on October 13 to halt Sea Lion, which is being developed by Israel’s Navitas Petroleum and Britain’s Rockhopper Exploration. According to the tribunal’s schedule, Argentina will present on the first day from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. and the United Kingdom from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m.; on the second day, Argentina will speak from 10.30 a.m. to noon and the UK will close from 5.30 p.m. to 7 p.m. Argentina’s agent is Ambassador Mario Oyarzábal. The tribunal’s 21 permanent judges include Argentina’s Frida María Armas Pfirter, its vice-president, while the United Kingdom, which has no judge of its nationality, has chosen British professor Vaughan Lowe as judge ad hoc.

Argentina is not asking the tribunal to rule on sovereignty, but on rights to maritime resources and the environmental obligations set out in the Law of the Sea Convention. Sea Lion is expected to begin development drilling in 2027 and commercial production in 2028.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has called Argentine attempts to interfere with commercial activity in the area “unacceptable”. According to Infobae, the British government will activate legislation before the end of the year to protect Navitas and Rockhopper from possible Argentine sanctions. London maintains that it will not negotiate sovereignty unless the islanders wish it.

World.title: One dead and more than 2,000 affected by El Niño flooding in the Galápagos
World.content:
One dead and more than 2,000 affected by El Niño flooding in the Galápagos

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:14 UTC Full article

Authorities announced repairs to the road linking the airport with the island and the removal of debris

Heavy rains linked to the El Niño phenomenon triggered a flash flood on Santa Cruz island in Ecuador’s Galápagos archipelago overnight from Friday to Saturday, leaving one person dead and more than 2,000 affected, according to local mayor Fanny Uribe. Water reached up to three metres deep in some neighbourhoods of Puerto Ayora, the island’s main town.

After some ten hours of heavy rain in the highlands of Santa Cruz, water rushed down a ravine towards the inhabited coastal areas. “Rescues were carried out using kayaks and Zodiacs, and most people were brought to safety,” said fire chief Freddy López, who estimated the water reached three metres in the La Cascada and La Unión neighbourhoods. There were no alarms: firefighters, Red Cross volunteers and young residents went door to door to wake people, some of whom had to swim out of their homes. Most took refuge in the Puerto Ayora Coliseum. A local foundation says it has identified at least 500 more people affected who are not on the official register because they are staying with relatives.

Authorities announced repairs to the road linking the airport with the island and the removal of debris. Uribe said she was negotiating housing vouchers with the government for families who lost their homes, was preparing to distribute 1,000 food kits and that the relocation of the La Cascada neighbourhood was being studied. Residents have organised community kitchens and aid networks; a fishermen’s foundation is serving three meals a day to some 1,200 people. According to El País, President Daniel Noboa had not commented publicly on the emergency.

The Environment Ministry said no deaths of giant tortoises or wild birds have been reported as a result of the rains. Farmers in the island’s highlands, whose produce largely feeds the local population, fear for their crops.

Santa Cruz, with about 15,000 inhabitants, is the most populated island in the Galápagos, some 1,000 kilometres from the mainland. Ecuador’s National Risk Management Secretariat declared a nationwide red alert for El Niño on September 29, and its effects are expected to peak in December.

World.title: Paraguay seeks to return part of the savings frozen at Ueno Bank within 24 hours
World.content:
Paraguay seeks to return part of the savings frozen at Ueno Bank within 24 hours

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:08 UTC Full article

Paraguay’s Senate on Wednesday approved a reform of the deposit guarantee law that would allow customers of Ueno Bank, taken over by the Central Bank on Tuesday, to receive an advance of up to 40 minimum wages, about 121 million guaraníes, within 24 hours of the bank’s resolution. The bill now goes to the Chamber of Deputies, which was due to consider it on Thursday.

The current law set a deadline of 15 days, extendable by a further 15, for the Deposit Guarantee Fund to pay savers at a failed bank. The approved text specifies that customers with loans from the bank will have only overdue instalments deducted, not their entire debt, and that the advance is a payment on account that does not change the total coverage of up to 75 minimum wages, about 228 million guaraníes per depositor. According to the Central Bank, that limit covers 97% of customers. Above that figure, the Social Security Institute, the pension fund, will be paid before large savers. The Senate rejected a proposal to extend the guarantee to all public funds deposited in the bank.

The Central Bank’s interim president, Liana Caballero, who took over after Carlos Carvallo’s resignation, said a first payment would be up to 10 million guaraníes and that depositors would be divided into three tranches, although there are still no dates, locations or requirements. “The operational side is the problem in paying out,” she acknowledged. The Association of Banks of Paraguay backed the advance but urged caution over using the fund to return money from pension funds.

“The priority of the government of Paraguay is and will be to protect with all our strength the fruit of that effort and to provide concrete, rapid and responsible answers,” President Santiago Peña said in a televised address. Peña cancelled his attendance at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid. The opposition has said it will push for impeachment proceedings against him and Vice President Pedro Alliana.

The Central Bank took over Ueno after its solvency ratio fell to 5.56%, against a minimum of 12%, and it detected irregular loans to companies owned by the bank’s owners, the Vázquez Group. Eight executives were detained, according to the press. The crisis also affects South American football’s governing body, Conmebol, which has US$14 million deposited in the bank, although it says payment of prize money for the Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana finals is not at risk. The Vázquez Group’s media outlets closed, leaving about 300 employees without pay. Groups of savers gathered outside the Central Bank on Wednesday night to demand their deposits.

World.title: Republicans look for culprits after defeat: Speaker of Congress steps aside and Vance points to Iran
World.content:
Republicans look for culprits after defeat: Speaker of Congress steps aside and Vance points to Iran

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:05 UTC Full article

Johnson, 54, a congressman from Louisiana, has been Speaker since October 2023, when his colleagues chose him as a consensus candidate after the ousting of his predecessor

Speaker of the US House of Representatives Mike Johnson, a Republican, said he will not seek to continue leading his party in the new Congress, while Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican defeat in Tuesday’s midterm elections, an explanation President Donald Trump called “largely true” even as he defended the conflict.

Johnson, 54, a congressman from Louisiana, has been Speaker since October 2023, when his colleagues chose him as a consensus candidate after the ousting of his predecessor, Kevin McCarthy. The Speaker is third in the presidential line of succession, after the vice president, and has been one of Trump’s most loyal allies in Congress. With the Democratic victory, he will lose the post when the new House convenes on January 3, and Republicans will become the minority.

Johnson told his staff on Wednesday that he will not run to lead Republicans in that new phase. In a letter to colleagues he cited the toll three years in the job have taken on his family. “While the outcome of this midterm is not what we’d hoped and fought for, a new battle is just beginning,” he wrote. Congressmen Jim Jordan, chairman of the Judiciary Committee, and Steve Scalise, the majority leader, have already announced bids to succeed him, in a vote expected next week. Trump called Johnson “fantastic” and said he had not asked him to step aside.

Vance, seen as a contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, blamed the defeat on the Iran war and rising gasoline prices. “If you want to argue it was worth it — that losing the Senate for the next six years was worth it — go ahead. But everyone knows why we lost,” he wrote on X. Asked about the post, Trump replied: “I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit, short term.” But he defended the war, now more than eight months old: “The Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.”

Republicans have lost at least seven Senate seats and could lose nine if results in Mississippi and Alaska, still being counted, are confirmed, according to El País. In the House, dozens of seats remain to be called, although Democrats have already passed the majority. The result also opens the race within the Republican Party to succeed Trump, who cannot run again in 2028.

World.title: Peru declares an El Niño emergency in nearly three-quarters of the country ahead of the Pope’s visit
World.content:
Peru declares an El Niño emergency in nearly three-quarters of the country ahead of the Pope’s visit

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 07:00 UTC Full article

Peru’s scientific commission on the phenomenon expects the episode to last until June 2027

Peru’s government has declared a two-month state of emergency over the risk of heavy rains linked to the El Niño phenomenon in 1,380 of the country’s 1,891 districts, about 73%, including all the places Pope Leo XIV will visit in northern Peru from November 13. The measure covers districts in all 24 departments and the province of Callao.

Rains in recent days flooded homes and streets, leaving 324 people affected in Tumbes, on the border with Ecuador, and caused flooding in Chulucanas, in the Piura region, where the pontiff lived in 1985 during his first years as a missionary. President Keiko Fujimori cancelled her trip to the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Sunday to oversee the response and warned of further rain in Tumbes and Piura on November 7 and 8. In October she had already acknowledged that prevention works might prove insufficient for “an El Niño we have not seen in recent decades”. The declaration allows regional and municipal governments to carry out prevention, response and rehabilitation measures with the National Civil Defence Institute.

The emergency includes all 38 districts of Lambayeque, on the northern coast. The Pope, who holds Peruvian nationality and was bishop of Chiclayo, the regional capital, from 2015 to 2023, will celebrate Mass on Friday 13 at the Pampas de Pimentel, by the Pacific, which organisers expect nearly a million faithful to attend. On Saturday 14 he will celebrate another Mass in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, in the Andean region of Cajamarca, and visit Zaña to close the jubilee year marking 300 years since the canonisation of Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo. The security operation will involve some 2,500 police, 1,000 soldiers and 6,500 volunteers.

“We expect the Pope’s visit to Chiclayo may coincide with episodes of rain. They will not be heavy rains,” said Grinia Ávalos, director of meteorology at the National Meteorology and Hydrology Service, who forecast temperatures of up to 32 degrees Celsius in Chiclayo, four to five degrees above normal. The regional coordinator for the visit, Jorge Chávez Cresta, said that according to the forecast scenarios, heavy rains would reach Lambayeque after the Pope has left the country, although he said contingency plans were in place. The region suffered severe flooding during the El Niño episodes of 1982-1983 and 1997-1998, and Chiclayo lacks a comprehensive drainage system.

Peru’s scientific commission on the phenomenon expects the episode to last until June 2027. In Ecuador, El Niño rains left one dead and more than 2,000 affected on Santa Cruz island in the Galápagos last week. Leo XIV will visit Uruguay and Argentina before arriving in Peru.

World.title: Milei skips the opening of the Ibero-American Summit and meets Abascal in Madrid
World.content:
Milei skips the opening of the Ibero-American Summit and meets Abascal in Madrid

5th Thursday, November 2026 - 06:49 UTC Full article

It is Milei’s second visit to Madrid in two weeks. On October 21, at a breakfast event, he called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator” and “corrupt”, and did not meet Abascal on that occasion

Argentine President Javier Milei did not attend the opening of the 30th Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday or the dinner hosted by the King and Queen of Spain for the delegations, and that evening met Santiago Abascal, leader of the Vox party, in the middle of the campaign for Spain’s November 29 general election.

Milei arrived in the Spanish capital from Buenos Aires on Wednesday afternoon but did not attend the opening ceremony at the Teatro Real or the gala dinner at the Royal Palace for the heads of the 22 delegations. According to diplomatic sources quoted by El País, the Argentine president had requested, through Spain’s Foreign Ministry, a private audience with King Felipe VI, as other leaders had, but the ministry did not process the request, considering it inappropriate for him to meet the monarch before meeting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. The Argentine government has not explained his absence.

“President Javier Milei met in Madrid with the deputy and presidential candidate Santiago Abascal,” the Argentine Presidential Office said, sharing a photograph of the meeting. Abascal wrote: “Tonight I met my friend and ally Javier Milei, President of the Argentine Republic, whom I thanked for attending the Ibero-American Summit.”

It is Milei’s second visit to Madrid in two weeks. On October 21, at a breakfast event, he called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator” and “corrupt”, and did not meet Abascal on that occasion. At the time, the Royal Household said a meeting with Felipe VI must necessarily be accompanied by one with the prime minister. Chilean President José Antonio Kast, also attending the summit, met Abascal this week and received an award from Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso.

Milei is expected to coincide with Felipe VI and Sánchez on Thursday at the summit’s plenary session, which brings together the countries of Latin America with Spain, Portugal and Andorra.

World.title: Democrats retake control of the US Congress in a heavy blow to Trump
World.content:
Democrats retake control of the US Congress in a heavy blow to Trump

4th Wednesday, November 2026 - 09:09 UTC Full article

CBS News projected a Democratic majority in the House shortly after 10 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday; with dozens of seats still to be decided, Democrats had passed the 218 needed

The Democratic Party on Tuesday regained control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections, winning in Republican strongholds such as Texas, Ohio and Kansas in a heavy blow to President Donald Trump, who will govern for the remaining two years of his term with Congress in opposition hands.

CBS News projected a Democratic majority in the House shortly after 10 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday; with dozens of seats still to be decided, Democrats had passed the 218 needed. In the Senate, they secured a majority with victory in Iowa and hold at least 53 of the 100 seats, with results in Alaska and Mississippi still pending. According to El País, it is only the seventh time the party in power has lost both chambers in a midterm election.

Democrats won Senate seats in states where they had not done so for decades. In Texas, James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton; in Ohio, Sherrod Brown regained the seat from Jon Husted; in Kansas, Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton became the state’s first Democratic senator in almost a century. They also won in Iowa, with Josh Turek; in Maine, where Troy Jackson defeated Republican Susan Collins, a senator since 1997; in North Carolina, with Roy Cooper; and in South Carolina, with Annie Andrews. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, will be the first Muslim senator in US history. Republicans held seats in Florida, Idaho and Montana.

In governor’s races, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in Texas and will be the first Hispanic woman to lead the state; Xavier Becerra will be California’s first Hispanic governor since 1875; and Deb Haaland, in New Mexico, the first Native American woman to govern a state. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds will be the state’s first Black governor.

Trump told Fox News he was “a little surprised” and that the Democrats “did a good job”, attributing part of the defeat to the Iran war and higher fuel prices. He told The New York Times he would accept the results and hoped to reach agreements with the opposition. On his social network, however, he wrote: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!”, and posted an image of his cap bearing the word “VETO”, a reference to his threat to veto the new Congress’s laws.

With majorities in both chambers, Democrats will be able to block the White House’s legislative agenda and open investigations into the first half of the term. Former president Barack Obama said voters had sent “a clear message” in favour of “a politics that brings people together rather than divides them”. China said it was ready to “keep working” with Washington, and the Kremlin said it expected Trump to maintain his foreign policy. Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said “Americans have said no to war”.

Polls had identified the cost of living, corruption and the Iran war as voters’ main concerns, and turnout was at record levels for a midterm election.

World.title: Paraguay takes over Ueno Bank, with 3 million customers, and freezes its deposits
World.content:
Paraguay takes over Ueno Bank, with 3 million customers, and freezes its deposits

4th Wednesday, November 2026 - 08:27 UTC Full article

“We proceeded to close the entity; therefore, neither the app, nor the cards, nor any service of the entity is active,” said a member of the Central Bank’s board. Photo: EFE/ Juan Pablo Pino

Paraguay’s Central Bank on Tuesday took over Ueno Bank, one of the country’s largest banks, after its solvency ratio fell below 50% of the legal minimum, and froze all its assets and liabilities, including the savings of some 3 million customers and more than US$800 million in public funds. The bank immediately suspended all its services.

“We proceeded to close the entity; therefore, neither the app, nor the cards, nor any service of the entity is active from today,” said Liana Caballero, a member of the Central Bank’s board, which took the decision unanimously. According to its own figures, Ueno’s customers are equivalent to 60% of the country’s adult population, and it manages public funds including about US$380 million from the Social Security Institute, which runs pensions and public healthcare.

The Deposit Guarantee Fund covers savings of up to 75 minimum wages, about 228 million guaraníes or roughly US$38,200 per person. Those with larger balances will have to wait for the Superintendency of Banks’ final accounting. “The priority will always be small savers,” said Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo, who described the situation as “an isolated, one-off event” and said the financial system “remains sound and healthy”.

According to Carvallo, the takeover followed months of investigation that revealed loans to companies linked to the bank’s owners. On October 18, the Association of Banks of Paraguay had asked the Central Bank to report on the solvency of institutions that benefited from facilities in merger processes and warned about a bank’s credit exposure, which it did not identify, to companies in its own group. Days earlier, senators from the ruling party and the opposition had called on President Santiago Peña to dismiss the Central Bank’s leadership, which Peña backed.

Carvallo, who ran Ueno Bank before Peña appointed him to head the Central Bank in 2023, said he had signed his resignation, although he will remain in office until the bank’s resolution is complete. According to the Paraguayan press, several of the bank’s executives were detained, including its president, Miguel Vázquez.

The crisis had immediate political fallout. Vice President Pedro Alliana “paused” his bid for the ruling Colorado Party’s presidential nomination in order to “put the house in order”. The opposition Authentic Radical Liberal Party said it would push for impeachment proceedings against Peña and Alliana. “They plundered the pensioners’ money and this cannot be left like this,” said its presidential hopeful Ricardo Estigarribia, according to the newspaper ABC Color. In 2024, the Social Security Institute’s purchase of about US$32 million in Ueno bonds caused controversy; Peña, who called the reports a “media campaign”, was a shareholder in Ueno Holding, not the bank, and sold those shares in April 2025.

World.title: US $40M Pilgrim’s Pride plant will open Thursday in Gómez Palacio, Durango
World.content:
Pilgrim’s Pride Corporation, the multinational chicken producer, will launch on Thursday its US $40 million El Porvenir plant in Gómez Palacio, Durango, which is expected to create over 300 jobs.

The project is part of Pilgrim’s broader plans to invest $1.3 billion in Mexico between 2026 and 2030 under the Sheinbaum government’s Plan México economic strategy, which is expected to increase production by more than 373,000 metric tonnes and generate over 4,000 direct and 16,000 indirect jobs.

The investment will be divided among several states, with $200 million allocated to Durango and Coahuila in the northern border zone, $150 million to Querétaro, San Luis Potosí and Hidalgo in El Bajío and the center, and $950 million to the southeastern states of Veracruz, Campeche and Yucatán.

Durango’s Foreign Investment Attraction Unit head, Arturo Ortiz Galán, said that the new production line will support local suppliers and the region’s poultry businesses, helping to reinforce Durango’s position as an industrial and agri-food hub. The plant will also expand Pilgrim’s value-added product range by producing cooked chicken.

Ortiz Galán said the expansion was made possible through collaboration with the federal government, which has provided investment incentives.

“Thanks to the good relationship that [Durango] Governor [Esteban] Villegas has with President Sheinbaum, I have been able to easily initiate discussions and secure support from all the relevant ministries,” Galán said. “It’s very positive that there’s a plan to digitalize all processes and create a one-stop shop for investments.”

It delivers food to approximately 30 million Mexicans, employs around 12,600 people across Mexico, and provides 50,000 indirect jobs through its partner farmers, logistics providers and supply chain.

In January, President Sheinbaum praised the Mexican business environment for attracting high investment from Pilgrim’s.

“This investment they are making… is because they have been successful and because they know that investing in Mexico is safe and allows them to continue growing,” Sheinbaum said during a morning press conference.

With reports from Milenio and Mexico Industry

World.title: As Ibero-American Summit gets underway in Madrid, foreign ministers cite ‘excellent’ Spain-Mexico relations
World.content:
Mexico-Spain relations are in “excellent” shape, Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco said Wednesday after a meeting with his Spanish counterpart in Madrid.

In a social media post, Velasco said that he and Spanish Foreign Affairs Minister José Manuel Albares spoke with “our usual closeness and trust” about the “excellent” state of relations between Mexico and Spain, a leading source of foreign investment in Mexico.

“We highlighted the good rapport between President [Claudia] Sheinbaum and Prime Minister [Pedro] Sánchez, which drives a constructive, results-oriented agenda,” he wrote.

“Mexico and Spain will continue to strengthen this fraternal friendship and the dialogue that unites us,” Velasco said.

His meeting with Albares took place on the first day of the Ibero-American Summit, a gathering of leaders and officials from Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries. Velasco is representing Sheinbaum at the event.

After meeting with the Mexican foreign minister, Albares also described Mexico-Spain relations in positive terms.

“Spain and Mexico have strengthened our political, economic and cultural relations over the past year year for the benefit of our sister nations,” he wrote on social media.

There is no doubt that Mexico-Spain relations have improved during Sheinbaum’s presidency after they deteriorated considerably during Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s six-year term in office.

In 2019, López Obrador requested an apology from Spain for human rights violations during the Conquest of Mexico, while in 2022 he advocated a “pause” in bilateral relations while asserting that Mexico had been “looted” for years due to “economic-political promiscuity in the leadership of the governments of Mexico and Spain.”

AMLO’s 2019 request for an apology was “vigorously” rejected by the Spanish government, but in March of this year, King Felipe VI of Spain acknowledged that during the Spanish conquest and colonization of the Americas, “there were significant abuses” and “moral and ethical controversies.” As Mexico News Daily reported at the time, his remarks constituted an unprecedented statement on the matter for a king of Spain.

In April, Sheinbaum met with Prime Minister Sánchez at the “In Defense of Democracy” summit in Barcelona.

Sheinbaum had also called for an apology for abuses committed by Spain during the Conquest and the fall of Tenochtitlán, but in Barcelona, she acknowledged that there had been “a rapprochement from both the Spanish … [prime minister] and the king himself.”

The Ibero-American Summit

In a statement released on Tuesday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE) noted that Sheinbaum had designated Velasco to lead the Mexican delegation at the 30th Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Nov. 4 and 5.

“The Mexican delegation’s presence will be key to continuing to advance cooperation in areas of interest to Mexico, such as the environment and climate change, human mobility, disaster risk reduction, education, gender equality, and science and technology,” the SRE said.

“At the meeting, the host country will report on its results over the past two years in charge of the Pro Tempore Secretariat of the Summit and will hand the presidency over to Honduras for the 2026-2028 period,” the ministry said.

“The first Summit was held in Mexico, in Guadalajara, in 1991. Since then, it has been an important forum for dialogue and cooperation between the two regions,” the SRE said, referring to Latin America and Europe.

World.title: Mexican-Americans among historic winners in Tuesday’s US elections
World.content:
Mexican American candidates captured the governorships of Texas and California, and at least three Latino Democrats flipped Republican congressional seats in Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who defeated Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, will become the state’s first Latina governor ever, and Texas’ first Democratic governor since Ann Richards from 1991 to 1995.

Her victory helped end a Democratic drought in Texas statewide elections dating to 1994.

In the California governor’s race, Democrat Xavier Becerra — whose mother was born in Jalisco and whose father was born in Sacramento but raised in Mexico — had a 64% to 36% lead over Republican Steve Hilton, a former Fox News host, in preliminary returns.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum welcomed their victories Wednesday morning.

“We are very pleased that Mexican Americans have this recognition,” she said in her daily press conference.

Becerra, who previously served as California attorney general and U.S. health and human services secretary under President Joe Biden, became the first Latino elected governor of California.

A previous Latino governor of California, Romualdo Pacheco, was not elected to the post but served nine months in 1875 after the seated governor left to join the Senate. Pacheco was the lieutenant governor at the time.

Hinojosa grew up in the border city of Brownsville, Texas, where her parents began their careers as legal aid lawyers representing farmworkers. Her mother, Crisanta Guerra Lozano, was born in the city of San Luis Potosí, and her father, Gilberto Hinojosa, chaired the Texas Democratic Party from 2012 to 2025.

She recalled crossing into Mexico regularly with her family for breakfast and shopping as a girl.

In South Texas, Tejano singer Bobby Pulido — winner of Latin Grammys for best Tejano album in 2022 and 2025 — defeated incumbent Republican Rep. Mónica De La Cruz in the 15th Congressional District, flipping a seat in a district President Donald Trump carried by 18 percentage points in 2024.

Pulido said last month he lacked U.S. health insurance and had traveled to Mexico for medical care.

The conservative Democrat campaigned on border security and support for government-funded health care and safety net programs, according to the New York Times. His outreach included free performances at quinceañeras and other local celebrations.

His victory marked a reversal in a district viewed as a test of Latino voters’ political loyalties after Trump’s gains two years earlier.

“Hispanics, they’re not so partisan,” Pulido said by way of an explanation. “It’s very much, ‘Are you gonna go fight for me?’ That’s what matters.”

Added Javier Palomarez, president and CEO of the United States Hispanic Business Council: “We are a community that doesn’t vote party. It votes person.”

Democrat Katy Padilla Stout was projected to win Texas’ 23rd Congressional District against Brandon Herrera, a gun-focused YouTube personality, according to CBS News, flipping another Republican seat.

The sprawling border district stretches from San Antonio to El Paso. Its previous Republican representative, Tony Gonzales, resigned in April. Trump carried the current district by 14 points.

In Nebraska, Democrat Denise Powell defeated Republican Brinker Harding to become the state’s first Latina elected to federal office and the first woman to represent its 2nd Congressional District.

Powell, who co-founded a group helping local women run for office, also became the district’s first Democratic winner in a decade. She flipped the seat held by retiring Republican Rep. Don Bacon.

In another notable Texas victory, Democrat and longtime sheriff’s deputy Johnny Garcia defeated Trump-backed Republican Carlos de La Cruz in a San Antonio-area district redrawn by Republicans to favor their party. As redrawn, the majority-Hispanic district would have backed Trump by more than 10 percentage points in 2024.

With reports from El Financiero, Quadratín San Luis Potosí, CBC, Hindustan Times, Fast Company and Nebraska Examiner

World.title: El Jalapeño: Chipotle mystified after Mexican diners treat fast-casual burrito bowl as lunch instead of cultural offense
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

SAN PEDRO GARZA GARCÍA, Nuevo León — Executive leadership at Chipotle Mexican Grill confirmed Tuesday that they are currently re-evaluating their entire global strategy after local diners surprisingly failed to fiercely oppose their version of Mexican-inspired cuisine.

After the U.S. fast-casual chain opened its first Mexican location in the affluent municipality of San Pedro Garza García earlier this year, corporate analysts fully expected a wave of diplomatic friction, or at least a sternly worded statement from local culinary boards. Instead, customer volume has remained consistently high, forcing corporate strategists to confront the unsettling possibility that people simply enjoy a large, convenient bowl of rice, beans and meat without converting their meal break into a cultural referendum.

“We prepared extensive crisis-management protocols for the inevitable national backlash against charging 180 pesos for a scoop of guacamole,” said Chipotle Director of Global Brand Strategy Mark Henderson, speaking via video conference from the packed dining area of the company’s Nuevo León restaurant. “Our market research explicitly warned us that bringing an Americanized version of Mexican food into actual Mexico was the culinary equivalent of selling canned air to a mountain town. We were braced for total outrage, but people keep coming back and asking for extra salsa.”

According to company officials, early performance metrics far exceeded initial corporate expectations, which had originally budgeted for three weeks of novelty-driven foot traffic followed by a swift, dignified retreat from the market. Company leadership now plans to open four additional locations in Nuevo León before expanding into Mexico City, where executives are reportedly preparing an entirely new set of contingency plans in case diners there also treat lunch as just lunch.

Internal memos revealed that brand researchers initially attributed the sustained high sales to a clerical error, suspecting that local patrons were under the mistaken impression that Chipotle was an upscale American salad bar.

At press time, Chipotle board members were reportedly holding an emergency summit to discuss whether the chain could safely introduce hard-shell tacos without triggering a public outcry.
