World.title: Mexico’s economy nearing ‘strong’ according to the latest MND Economy Index™
World.content:
Listen to this article

THE MND ECONOMY INDEX™

Providing broad insight into the Mexican economy

MND Intelligence · Sixth edition

Welcome to the sixth edition of the MND Economy Index™, part of the MND Intelligence™ suite of data products from Mexico News Daily.

The MND Economy Index™ is a 10-pillar, 19-indicator composite index that compiles a broad range of economic data into a single score between 0 and 100, giving Mexico News Daily readers a clear, accessible picture of how the Mexican economy is performing across multiple dimensions.

In the inaugural MND Economy Index™ article, published in late May, we not only analyzed the index score — 63.4 out of 100 — but also explained what the index is, why we developed it and how it works. Click here to read (or re-read) those explanations.

In this edition of the MND Economy Index™ — which uses economic data primarily from the month of August — the index score is 74.5, an increase of 1.4 points compared to the previous score.

The score for August is the highest since we began publishing the MND Economy Index™, reflecting improvements in various parts of Mexico’s economy.

Before we look more closely at the latest index result, here is a short guide to what the overall index score means.

85–100: Exceptional — the economy performing at a high level across nearly all indicators.

— the economy performing at a high level across nearly all indicators. 75–84: Strong — strong broad-based performance with only minor areas of concern.

— strong broad-based performance with only minor areas of concern. 60–74: Above neutral — meaningful strengths, but with notable room for improvement.

— meaningful strengths, but with notable room for improvement. 50–59: Mixed — passing marks overall, more indicators above benchmark than below.

— passing marks overall, more indicators above benchmark than below. Below 50: Broad underperformance — more indicators below benchmark than above.

Mexico’s economy on the verge of a ‘strong’ assessment

As noted above, the latest MND Economy Index™ score is 74.5, an increase of 1.4 percentage points compared to the previous score. The latest score is just 0.5 percentage points below the score required for a “strong” assessment for Mexico’s economy.

Below you will see the score for each of the ten pillars that make up the index, expressed out of 10 to reflect each pillar’s exact contribution to the final composite score.

Pillars are color-coded using a traffic light system: green (a score above 7.5) indicates strong performance; yellow (5.0–7.5) signals decent performance but with room for improvement; and red (below 5.0) flags a pillar that is falling short of its benchmark. Where a pillar score has improved compared to the previous month, an upward arrow appears alongside its corresponding traffic light; a downward arrow indicates a deterioration; and a pause symbol denotes no change.

As you’ll see below, scores for four of the ten MND Economy Index™ pillars increased in August compared to the previous month. Scores for five pillars declined, while the score for one was unchanged.

Collectively, the increases were more significant than the decreases, allowing the index score to rise.

🟢 ⬇️ INFLATION (9.54)

The score for this pillar fell to 9.54 in August from 9.68 in July. Despite the decline, the inflation pillar retained its position as the top contributor to the overall MND Economy Index™ score.

Mexico’s annual headline inflation rate increased to 3.26% in August, ending a four-month streak of declines. The increase caused a slight decrease in the score for the current inflation component of the pillar as the headline rate moved away from the Bank of Mexico’s 3% target.

The score for the pillar component that considers the 12-month forward inflation forecast was unchanged as the Bank of Mexico’s outlook for the third quarter of 2027 is applicable to both July and August. The central bank is predicting a headline inflation rate of 3.2% in the third quarter of next year.

🟢 ⬆️ MONETARY POLICY (9.46)

The score for this pillar increased to 9.46 from 9.32 in July.

The Bank of Mexico’s benchmark interest rate remained at 6.50% in August after the central bank’s board voted to keep it at that level at a monetary policy meeting on Aug. 6. Therefore, there was no change in the interest rate component of the pillar score.

The increase in the pillar score was due to a decline in Mexico’s real interest rate in August — i.e., the Bank of Mexico’s benchmark interest rate minus the annual headline inflation rate.

The real interest rate in August was 3.24%, a reading 0.54 points above the 2.7% neutral midpoint.

The real interest rate in July, at 3.38%, was further away from the neutral midpoint than the reading in August.

🟢 ⬆️ MANUFACTURING SECTOR HEALTH (8.53)

The score for this pillar increased in August, rising to 8.53 from 7.9 in July.

The exports component of the pillar remained at the maximum score due to a 40.4% annual increase in export revenue in August, well above the 16.7% threshold needed for a perfect ten. Official data shows that over 94% of Mexico’s export revenue in August came from the shipment abroad of manufactured goods.

The increase in the overall pillar score was due to 4.1% year-over-year growth in manufacturing output in August. The year-over-year gain represented a significant improvement from the 1.6% increase in July.

🟢 ⬆️ ECONOMIC GROWTH (8)

The score for this pillar increased to 8 in August from 7.6 in July.

The increase was due to a higher annual economic growth rate in August. The annual growth rate in August was 3.5%, according to final data published by INEGI on Oct. 23. Year-over-year growth in July was slightly lower at 3.3%.

At her morning press conference on Oct. 26, President Sheinbaum said that growth of 3.5% in August was “very good news.”

She noted that construction, including housing and public infrastructure projects, was helping to drive growth. Sheinbaum also noted that the production of electronics in Mexico was providing momentum to the economy.

🟢 ⬆️ SOVEREIGN RISK (7.72)

The score for this pillar increased to 7.72 in August from 7.41 in July.

The score for the sovereign credit ratings component of the pillar remained unchanged in August, as there were no month-over-month changes to the Mexico ratings of Moody’s (Baa3/stable); S&P (BBB/negative); and Fitch (BBB-/stable).

The increase in the overall pillar score was due to a narrowing in Mexico’s 5-year credit default swap spread. The credit default swap spread was 77.89 basis points at the end of August, down from 87.19 basis points at the end of July. The narrower spread reflected a decrease in the market-implied cost of insuring against a Mexican sovereign default.

🟡 ⬇️ CURRENCY STABILITY (6.73)

The score for this pillar declined slightly to 6.73 in August from 6.79 in July.

The standard deviation of daily exchange rate movements decreased to 0.25% in August from 0.40% in July, leading to an increase in the score for that component of the pillar.

The decrease in the pillar score in July was due to a lower spot rate score. The score for that component declined because the peso strengthened against the US dollar in August to trade at 16.99 to the greenback at the end of the month, an appreciation of 1.9% compared to the end of July.

The exchange rate was thus more distant from the index’s 19.00 USD:MXN baseline, which is based on the 2025 average rate. This pillar penalizes significant deviation from the 19.00 USD:MXN baseline in either direction, recognizing that a peso that has strengthened too far from this benchmark can erode export competitiveness and reduce the purchasing power of remittances, just as a weakening peso raises import costs.

The spot rate component of the currency stability score will increase in the next MND Economy Index™ as the peso depreciated 6% in September to trade at 18.08 to the dollar at the end of that month.

🟡 ⬇️ INVESTMENT CLIMATE (6.46)

The score for this pillar decreased to 6.46 in August from 6.58 in July.

The decrease was due to lower annual growth on the S&P/BMV FIBRAS Total Return Index, which tracks the performance of Mexico’s listed real estate investment trusts. The index grew 24.9% annually to the end of August, down from a 27.4% year-over-year increase at the end of July.

The score for the foreign direct investment component of the pillar remained steady as the latest available data is still that published by the Economy Ministry in late August. That data shows that foreign direct investment in Mexico increased 2.1% annually in the first six months of 2026 to reach a record-high $34.96 billion. Annual FDI growth of 25% is required for a perfect score in that component of the investment climate pillar.

🟡 ⏸️ PRODUCTIVITY (6.4)

The score for this pillar remained steady at 6.4 in August after increasing to that level in July from 3.8 in June.

Data published by the national statistics agency INEGI on Sept. 10 showed that the IGPLE — INEGI’s quarterly productivity measure — increased 1.7% annually in the second quarter of 2026. That level of productivity growth was significantly stronger than the +0.1% reading in the first quarter of 2026.

INEGI will publish productivity data for the third quarter of 2026 in early December.

🟡 ⬇️ LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT (6.11)

The score for this pillar decreased to 6.11 in August from 6.18 in July. Scores for two of the pillar’s three components stayed the same while one declined.

The number of people in formal sector jobs rose 1.5% in the 12 months to the end of August, on par with the annual growth rate at the end of July.

Nominal wages were up 6.7% year-on-year at the end of August, the same increase recorded at the end of July.

Year-over-year growth in Mexico’s informality rate was 0.2 points at the end of August, up from an annual increase of 0.1 points at the end of July. In August, 55% of all Mexican workers worked in the informal economy. Lowering the informality rate is a major challenge for the Mexican government.

🟡 ⬇️ EXTERNAL INCOME (5.51)

The score for this pillar increased in August, rising to 5.51 from 5.26 in July. A year-over-year reduction in remittances in August — just the second decline this year — was a drag on the pillar score, but a strong increase in international tourism revenue more than offset it.

Incoming remittances declined 3.6% year-on-year to US $5.45 billion in August, the first decline of any month since January.

Thus, the score for the remittances component of the pillar fell sharply, although not so far as to warrant a score of zero, as that would require a year-over-year decline of 16.67%.

The pillar score increased in August as international tourism revenue grew compared to the same month of last year, whereas it declined in July. International tourist spending increased 7% year over year in August to reach $2.4 billion.

The MND Economy Index™ trend

In the graph below you can see how the MND Economy Index™ score has changed over time.

We have now calculated a total of ten index scores in the period between March 2025 and August 2026. The difference between the lowest score (56.9 in March 2025 — predating the publication of the first MND Economy Index™ article) and the highest (74.5 in August 2026) is 17.6 points.

The much higher score in this edition of the MND Economy Index™ indicates that Mexico’s economy is performing much better now than it was early in President Sheinbaum’s six-year term.

The improvement in the index score this year has been significant, increasing more than 10 points between March and August.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice is ‘67% complete,’ Sheinbaum reports: Wednesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🕊️ Government presents progress under Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice: The mañanera focused on advances made over the past year under the plan, which the government devised after the assassination of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo on Nov. 1, 2025. President Sheinbaum said the presentation would cover areas other than security.

The mañanera focused on advances made over the past year under the plan, which the government devised after the assassination of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo on Nov. 1, 2025. President Sheinbaum said the presentation would cover areas other than security. 📊 Sheinbaum says Plan Michoacán is 67% complete: The president said 1,680 of more than 2,500 “actions” under the plan have been completed.

The president said 1,680 of more than 2,500 “actions” under the plan have been completed. 💰 Planned investment more than doubles to 118 billion pesos: Sheinbaum said 118 billion pesos (US $6.3 billion) is slated for Plan Michoacán between 2025 and 2030, up from the 57 billion pesos originally announced. She said 72.43 billion pesos, or 61% of the total, has already been spent.

Sheinbaum said 118 billion pesos (US $6.3 billion) is slated for Plan Michoacán between 2025 and 2030, up from the 57 billion pesos originally announced. She said 72.43 billion pesos, or 61% of the total, has already been spent. 🎪 115 “Well-being Fairs” held across all 113 Michoacán municipalities: Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez said residents completed more than 1.1 million administrative procedures at the fairs over the past year, including ones that facilitated access to welfare programs.

Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez said residents completed more than 1.1 million administrative procedures at the fairs over the past year, including ones that facilitated access to welfare programs. 🛣️ 41 billion pesos invested in Michoacán highways: Infrastructure Minister Jesús Esteva said the government is upgrading 411 kilometers of highway, with the government and private sector investing more than 41 billion pesos (US $2.2 billion) in six projects.

Infrastructure Minister Jesús Esteva said the government is upgrading 411 kilometers of highway, with the government and private sector investing more than 41 billion pesos (US $2.2 billion) in six projects. 🏭 Work on Bajío Industrial Park to start this month: Deputy Economy Minister Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez said 9.3 billion pesos (US $498.5 million) will be invested in the park in Zinapécuaro, which will primarily cater to the agroindustrial and automotive sectors.

Deputy Economy Minister Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez said 9.3 billion pesos (US $498.5 million) will be invested in the park in Zinapécuaro, which will primarily cater to the agroindustrial and automotive sectors. 🎓 795,000 Michoacán students receive government scholarships: Education Minister Mario Delgado said primary, middle school, high school and university students all receive monetary assistance, funded with an investment of 5.7 billion pesos (around US $306 million).

Why today’s mañanera matters

A presentation on the progress made under “Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice” over the past year was the central focus of President Sheinbaum’s Wednesday morning press conference.

The government devised the plan in response to the assassination of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo on Nov. 1, 2025, and general insecurity in Michoacán.

At the start of her Wednesday mañanera, the president noted that today’s presentation would focus on progress in areas other than security. She said that an update on the security situation in Michoacán would be presented at her press conference next Tuesday.

Data presented at Sheinbaum’s Oct. 13 mañanera showed that homicides in Michoacán declined 40.3% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period of last year.

The president was accompanied on Wednesday by various high-ranking officials, each of whom spoke briefly about Plan Michoacán initiatives.

Today’s mañanera allowed the government to both highlight progress on the plan and explain how funds have been spent. Sheinbaum characterizes her weekday press conferences as exercises in transparency, a principle she says is central to her administration.

115 ‘Well-being Fairs’ held in Michoacán

Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez reported that 115 “Ferías del Bienestar,” or “Well-being Fairs,” were held across all 113 municipalities of Michoacán over the past year.

She said that officials helped Michoacán residents complete more than 1.1 million trámites (administrative procedures) at the fairs, including ones that facilitated their access to government welfare programs.

Rodríguez also noted that Michoacán residents exchanged 673 firearms for cash over the past year under the Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz (Yes to Disarmament, Yes to Peace) program. Those exchanges, she said, will save lives.

Key advances under Plan Michoacán

Officials presented key advances under Plan Michoacán across a range of areas. Not all of the investment they outlined is directly linked to Plan Michoacán funding. Summarized below are the presentations made by 10 officials.

Deputy Economy Minister Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez reported that work will start this month on the Bajío Industrial Park in the municipality of Zinapécuaro. He said 9.3 billion pesos (US $498.5 million) will be invested in the project. The industrial park will primarily cater to the agroindustrial and automotive sectors.

Agriculture Minister Columba López reported that more than 177,000 residents of Michoacán are working in the government’s reforestation/employment program called Sembrando Vida (Sowing Life). She said the government is investing almost 2.2 billion pesos (US $117.9 million) in the program in Michoacán this year.

María Luisa Albores, director of the Mexican Food Security agency (Segalmex), reported that the government has purchased more than 63,000 tonnes of corn directly from some 2,400 small-scale farmers in Michoacán.

Environment Minister Alicia Bárcena reported that the government is investing 168.2 million pesos (US $9 million) in “sustainable forestry” projects in Michoacán.

Energy Minister Luz Elena González reported that more than 1,200 electricity projects have been completed in Michoacán, increasing electricity coverage to 99.99% of homes in the state. She said that 508 million pesos (US $27.2 million) were invested in the projects.

Tourism Minister Josefina Rodríguez reported that more than 2.46 million tourists visited Michoacán between January and August. She said tourist numbers increased 10.1% compared to the same period of last year. She said that tourism-related spending injected more than US $186 million into the Michoacán economy between January and August.

Infrastructure, Communications and Transport Minister Jesús Esteva reported that the government is upgrading 411 kilometers of highway in Michoacán. He said that the government and the private sector are investing more than 41 billion pesos (US $2.2 billion) in six highway projects in the state.

Welfare Minister Leticia Ramírez reported that the government is spending more than 30.4 billion pesos (US $1.6 billion) on welfare and social programs in Michoacán in 2026. She said that more than 1 million Michoacán residents benefit from the programs, which include pension schemes, educational scholarships and the distribution of fertilizer to farmers.

Education Minister Mario Delgado reported that over 795,000 students in Michoacán receive government scholarships. He said that primary school, middle school, high school and university students all receive monetary assistance. He said that the scholarships are funded with an investment of 5.7 billion pesos (around US $306 million).

IMSS Bienestar director Alejandro Svarch reported that a new hospital focused on the treatment of addictions had opened in Apatzingán. He also reported that a mental health center had opened in Huetamo. The combined investment in the two projects was 76.1 million pesos (US $3.6 million).

118 billion pesos in investment planned for Plan Michoacán by 2030

Presenting Plan Michoacán on Nov. 9, 2025, Sheinbaum described it as a “comprehensive strategy” and told reporters that it was based on 12 central tenets and included “more than 100 actions.”

Her presentation on Wednesday showed that there are, in fact, more than 2,500 Plan Michoacán “actions,” 1,680 of which have been “completed.” Sheinbaum said that represented progress of 67%.

She also said that 118 billion pesos (US $6.3 billion) is slated to be invested in Plan Michoacán between 2025 and 2030, the final year of her six-year term. That amount is more than double the 57-billion-peso investment that was originally announced.

Sheinbaum said that 72.43 billion pesos has already been spent on the plan. That amount represents 61% of the projected total.

Sheinbaum said that Plan Michoacán involves “very intense work” that is coordinated by the Interior Ministry. She also said that all of the federal government ministries have a “permanent presence” in Michoacán, one of 23 Mexican states governed by the Morena party.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: MND Local Puerto Vallarta: Tourists, traffic and turtles, oh my!
World.content:
Let me be the first to officially welcome you to tourist season in Puerto Vallarta! It’s the time of year when local entertainment ramps up, traffic jams up, and the checkout lines at Costco pile up.

But we may get a little help with traffic this season with the opening of the new Amado Nervo Bridge. It’s not just car traffic, but sea turtle traffic, too. Puerto Vallarta is in the thick of hatching season, when the newborn tortuguitas stumble their way from their nests to the sea by the hundreds, and you can help them on their journey.

And everyone is hoping for a more tranquil winter than last, when, on Feb. 22, members of the Jalisco New Generation cartel blocked traffic and burned cars and OXXO stores in the downtown area. The aftereffects of which have changed perceptions of safety here and abroad.

Read on to learn about how the city is working to restore tourist confidence and attract new visitors, the opening of a new commuter bridge, and sea turtle season.

Vallarta works to restore tourist confidence

Puerto Vallarta is working to revive tourism and attract new visitors amidst a backdrop of increased public perception of insecurity. According to the National Urban Public Safety survey, Vallartenses’ perception of insecurity has more than doubled since last year, rising from 24.7% in September 2025 to 53.6% in September 2026. While significantly up since this time last year, locals’ perception of insecurity has actually decreased since June, when it peaked at 65.4%.

The survey measures public perception of insecurity and doesn’t reflect actual crime rates. Puerto Vallarta remains one of the safer places to travel compared to other tourist destinations, and experiences less theft and violent crime than most U.S. cities of the same size. Also, the U.S. State Department, known for being expeditious about issuing travel warnings, has no current restrictions on travel to Vallarta.

But perception is everything, so the Vallarta tourism industry is working hard to win back traveler confidence and attract new visitors. This fall, representatives from the Puerto Vallarta Tourism Trust toured western states, hosting seminars for high-performing travel advisors in Arizona, Colorado and Utah, and welcomed tourism representatives from the U.S., Canada and other parts of Mexico to Vallarta. They even traveled to Poland, which will have direct weekly flights to Vallarta starting in December.

Despite February’s unrest, Puerto Vallarta remains one of the top destinations for vacationers in the world and is among the Top 10 global destinations for the Thanksgiving holiday, according to a recent survey by Allianz Partners. And if the traffic and Costco lines are any indication, we’ll have a healthy tourist season this year.

Amado Nervo Bridge opening

Here’s hoping a new commuter bridge between Banderas Bay and Puerto Vallarta will ease traffic on the busy Highway 200. The new Amado Nervo Bridge officially opened to cars on Oct. 28th. The bridge is located east of the main tourist corridor, connecting the towns of San Vicente and Ixtapa and surrounding communities, all of which previously had to use the 200 to get from one municipality to the next.

Local transportation officials estimate the bridge will cut as much as 40 minutes from the commute and ease congestion on Highway 200, especially between Mezcales and the Puerto Vallarta airport. The bridge is two kilometers long with three lanes in each direction and a bike lane. It’s a bit out of the way of the normal tourist route, but will hopefully direct more local traffic eastward and make traveling along the 200 smoother.

Turtles take to the sea

Hundreds of thousands of baby sea turtles are making their journey to the sea along Puerto Vallarta’s beaches. November is one of the best months to see them during the height of hatching season.

In Vallarta, a collaborative network of local community groups, grassroots non-profits, university researchers, government agencies, and beachfront resorts runs sea turtle camps along the coast. These camps protect eggs and ensure as many hatchlings as possible reach the sea. When mother turtles come ashore at night to dig nests and lay their eggs, the next morning conservationists remove them and place the eggs into manmade nests at the camps. This helps protect the eggs from predators and poachers. Not all nests are moved; camps only have capacity to protect so many. But still, they manage to save and release more than 150,000 baby turtles each year.

Turtle camps can be found at various spots along the coast of Banderas Bay, including the south end of Varadero beach in front of the Vidanta resort, Playa Holi in front of La Isla Mall, and Boca de Tomates turtle camp north of Bocanegra in the Marina. (Boca de Tomates took a beating with recent storms and could use support to rebuild.)

Camps often invite the public to witness and help with baby turtle releases. There are few things more precious and inspiring in nature than watching a baby sea turtle stumble its way into the surf. Crowds cheer and gasp as the little guys earnestly follow their instincts into the water, only to be washed back onto the sand time and time again until they finally make it out. I highly recommend you try to see a release when you visit.

Debbie Slobe is a writer and communications strategist based in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco. She blogs at Mexpatmama.com and is a senior program director at Resource Media. Find her on Instagram and Facebook.

World.title: 38th Morelia Music Festival kicks off next week, highlighting artists from Asia
World.content:
The historic city of Morelia, Michoacán, is gearing up to host the 38th edition of the “Miguel Bernal Jiménez” Music Festival, which will take place from Nov. 13 to 22.

Featuring Asia as a guest region, the festival will feature representatives from China, Japan, India, Thailand, South Korea and Indonesia, in addition to the participation of artists and musical groups from 13 countries.

“It’s a must-see show,” head of the event Verónica Bernal told news outlet Crónica in an interview.

The festival will take place in different locations across the city, including cultural and religious landmarks like the Morelia Cultural Center, the Clavijero Cultural Center, the Roses Conservatory, the Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe and more.

The opening concert will feature the National Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Ludwig Carrasco, with violinist Yesong Sophie Lee as soloist. The performance will take place on Nov. 13 at 8 p.m. at the Teatro Morelos, one of the event’s primary venues.

The inaugural program includes music by Tan Dun, winner of an Academy Award and a Grammy for the soundtrack to the 2000 film “Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon”, in addition to the performance of El Chueco, a famous 20th-century ballet composed by the Mexican composer Miguel Bernal Jiménez, whose legacy gives this festival its name.

#musitecamx #ballet #guillermokeysarenas #miguelbernaljimenez #compositormexicano ♬ original sound – Fonoteca Nacional de México @fonotecanacional 𝙀𝙡 𝙘𝙝𝙪𝙚𝙘𝙤 es un ballet que utiliza elementos populares y religiosos para contar la historia de un niño paralítico que le teme al mundo exterior y que, tras soñar que supera sus miedos, despierta para disfrutar las procesiones que desfilan frente a la puerta de su casa. El argumento es del bailarín y coreógrafo Guillermo Keys-Arenas, que encargó la música al compositor Miguel Bernal Jiménez, y la obra se estrenó en el Teatro de Bellas Artes en 1951. Sin embargo, con el tiempo la música se independizó de la puesta en escena y es considerada por algunos la mejor partitura del compositor. Bernal Jiménez falleció el 26 de julio de 1956 pero su legado sigue vivo a través de su música, que la Fonoteca Nacional difunde a través de Musiteca.mx. Encuentra la grabación competa en el link denuestra biografía. Fotografía: Caracterización de el Chueco. Guillermo Keys-Arenas, Heterofonía, núm. 114-115, enero-diciembre de 1996, p. 87. México, INBA, Cenidim #FonotecaNacional

Miguel Bernal Jiménez (1910–1956) was an organist, researcher and teacher, originally from Morelia. He was a prominent figure in 20th-century Mexican sacred music and a pioneer in the research of music from the era of New Spain.

According to Festival Director Bernal, other events will also feature works by the composer.

Among the most anticipated performances is Carnaval Barroco by the French ensemble Le Poème Harmonique, which combines music, theater, dance and acrobatics. The show will be part of the celebrations marking 200 years of diplomatic relations between Mexico and France.

Additionally, violinist Lidia Baich and pianist Donka Angatscheva will commemorate the 125th anniversary of the resumption of diplomatic relations between Mexico and Austria.

Bernal said that nearly half of the activities will be free of charge, with a program that includes masterclasses, children’s performances and the traditional floral carpets of Patamban. Tickets can be purchased at a discount (through Nov. 6) here.

With reports from Excélsior and Mi Morelia

World.content:

UGANDA · ECONOMY

Key Facts The survey Uganda’s central bank asks firms every month how confident they feel about orders, jobs and credit.

Business Confidence October 53.5; an economic calendar listed forecasts averaging 57, previous 55.8; bank revised it to 56.7.

The meaning A reading above 50 means more firms are optimistic than pessimistic about business.

The trend It is the weakest reading since February 2023, after a 2026 range of 55.4 to 59.1.

Next release Bank of Uganda lists 3 December 2026 for trade data; confidence reading date unconfirmed.

Uganda’s Business Confidence index fell to 53.5 in October 2026, according to data that the Bank of Uganda, the country’s central bank, published on Wednesday 4 November 2026. That is below the consensus estimate of 57 on an economic calendar, a public schedule of data releases that shows the average analyst forecast, and it is the weakest reading since February 2023, although it is still above the 50 line that separates optimism from pessimism.

For US readers, the drop matters because, in our reading, it follows a rate rise, a weak currency and dearer fuel in Uganda, an East African economy. The central bank raised its main interest rate from 9.75% to 12.0% on Wednesday 14 October 2026, in the same month.

What Happened

The Bank of Uganda’s Business Tendency Indicator is a monthly survey of firms in construction, manufacturing, wholesale trade, agriculture and services. The overall index stood at 53.5 in October, down from 56.7 in September and 57.8 in August.

When the bank first published September, the index read 55.8, and that is the figure an economic calendar listed as the previous reading. The bank has since revised September up to 56.7, which makes the October fall 3.2 points, from 56.7 to 53.5.

Where the Weakness Shows

Firms rated their present business situation at 50.3, down from 53.7, and current employment fell to 47.9, below the 50 line. Their view of their own finances dropped to 47.1 from 52.6.

Access to credit scored 38.9, the weakest of the economy-wide indicators, and orders from suppliers eased to 53.9 from 57.7. The selling-price index, where a reading above 50 means more firms are raising prices, rose to 66.4 from 61.5, which may reflect firms passing on higher costs.

Which Sectors Fell

Construction sank to 39.8 from 46.0, with its order books at 30.3, and wholesale trade slipped to 46.7 from 49.2. Both are now below 50, which means more firms in those sectors are pessimistic than optimistic.

Other services fell to 53.4 from 59.7 and financial services to 77.7 from 85.0, though financial firms remain the most upbeat group. Agriculture rose to 57.5 from 56.4, and manufacturing edged down to 52.6 from 53.1.

What May Be Weighing on Confidence

The bank has said the Middle East conflict has raised oil prices and shipping costs and added to pressure on the shilling, the local currency. It cut its growth forecast for the year to June 2027 to 6.0% to 6.5%, from 7.0% to 7.5%.

The survey itself does not give reasons for the drop, so the link to the rate rise is our reading rather than a finding of the bank. Our earlier report on September confidence showed the first signs of the slowdown.

What It Means for You

If you invest in Ugandan banks or bonds, the survey shows weak scores for access to credit and for current hiring, which can slow profits across the economy. Higher interest rates make local bonds pay more, but they also raise the risk that weaker firms fall behind on loans.

US companies that sell to or buy from Uganda could face cautious customers and slower orders in the weeks ahead. Travelers should note that the bank says pump prices have risen and that tourism receipts fell during temporary travel restrictions.

What Would Turn It Around

Confidence would recover if the shilling steadies, if fuel prices ease and if firms find the higher rates manageable. The survey's separate three-month outlook question, which scored 59.2, shows that more firms expect conditions to improve than expect them to worsen.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether October marks a low or the start of a longer slide, because the date of the next confidence reading is not confirmed, although the Bank of Uganda lists 3 December 2026 for its next monthly trade data. We found no statement of how many firms answered the survey.

The 50 line is a dividing mark, not a forecast of growth. A reading of 53.5 still means optimists outnumber pessimists, but by a thinner margin than at any time since February 2023.

The bank also revises past readings, so October itself may change. We could not confirm what basis the economic-calendar consensus of 57 used.

More: Uganda news in English, every day from The Rio Times. The page collects our reports on the country's economy and its central bank.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Is Uganda's Business Confidence Index?

It is a monthly survey by the Bank of Uganda that scores how optimistic firms are about orders, jobs, prices and credit. Readings above 50 mean optimism and readings below 50 mean pessimism.

What Was the October 2026 Reading?

The index fell to 53.5 in October 2026, below the economic-calendar consensus (the average analyst forecast) of 57. On the same calendar, September was first published at 55.8 and the bank later revised it to 56.7.

When Is the Next Reading Due?

The Bank of Uganda lists 3 December 2026 as the next release date for its monthly trade data. The date of the next confidence reading, which would cover November, is not confirmed.

Which Sectors Are Below 50?

Construction at 39.8 and wholesale trade at 46.7 are below 50, so more firms there are pessimistic than optimistic. Financial services is the strongest at 77.7.

Why Did the Central Bank Raise Rates in October?

At a special meeting on 14 October 2026 it raised its main rate from 9.75% to 12.0%, citing the Middle East conflict, exchange-rate volatility and inflation risks. The increase was 225 basis points, or 2.25 percentage points.

Sources: Bank of Uganda, Business Tendency Indicators (October 2026 data), released 4 November 2026; Bank of Uganda, Monetary Policy Statement for October 2026, 14 October 2026.

UGANDA · ECONOMY

Key Facts The country Uganda, a landlocked East African nation, sells gold and coffee and buys fuel and manufactured goods.

Balance of Trade September deficit of US$980.1 million; estimate US$280 million; previous US$1,143.7 million.

Trade flows Exports fell 4.7% to US$1,422.0 million, while imports fell 8.9% to US$2,402.1 million.

Gold Gold made up 59% of exports, at US$840.0 million from 6,170.9 kilograms.

Next release Uganda’s central bank lists Thursday 3 December 2026 for the October trade data.

Uganda’s goods trade deficit stood at US$980.1 million in September 2026, according to data that the Bank of Uganda, the country’s central bank, published on Wednesday 4 November 2026. That is narrower than the record US$1,143.7 million of August but far wider than the US$280 million that an economic-calendar consensus estimate had expected.

For US readers, in our reading the gap shows how costly freight and a weak currency press on a growing East African economy that sells coffee and gold to world markets. The central bank raised its main interest rate to 12.0% on Wednesday 14 October 2026, so the trade numbers matter for anyone who holds Ugandan assets or does business there.

What Happened

The Bank of Uganda’s tables show exports of US$1,422.0 million and imports of US$2,402.1 million for September, with freight and insurance counted in the import bill. The difference is a deficit of US$980.1 million, about US$163.7 million smaller than in August.

Exports fell 4.7% from August’s US$1,492.1 million, while imports dropped 8.9% from US$2,635.8 million. Against September 2025, exports are up 47.7% and imports are up 38.0%, so the deficit is about 26% wider than the US$778.3 million of a year ago.

How the Estimate Compares

An economic-calendar consensus estimate had pointed to a deficit of US$280 million, but the bank’s lower free-on-board measure, which leaves out freight and insurance, shows US$694.3 million. Either way the gap is wider than forecast, and we could not establish what basis the estimate used.

Freight and insurance added about US$285.8 million to the import bill in September. The central bank has said that Middle East tensions have raised oil prices and shipping costs.

Gold and Coffee

Gold exports were US$840.0 million, or 59% of all exports, and coffee earned US$186.9 million on 735,435 bags of 60 kilograms. Gold earnings slipped from US$889.0 million in August, while coffee rose from US$181.7 million.

Cotton, maize and flowers all earned less than in August, and maize fell from US$13.3 million to US$4.6 million. Informal cross-border trade with neighbours added US$86.2 million to exports, down from US$99.8 million.

What Uganda Imported

Formal private-sector imports were US$2,087.0 million, of which fuel was US$196.9 million and all other goods US$1,890.1 million. Fuel imports fell from US$244.6 million in August, so non-fuel goods now make up about nine of every ten dollars of that bill.

Our report on the record August deficit showed how a jump in imports drove the gap. September shows the first step back, but imports remain 38.0% above a year ago.

What It Means for You

If you hold Ugandan bonds or trade with Ugandan firms, a deficit near US$1 billion a month points, in our reading, to steady demand for dollars. That is a pressure on the shilling, the local currency, which the central bank also cites in its October rate rise to 12.0%.

Coffee shipments held near 735,000 bags in September, so supply to buyers looks steady. Companies that sell goods into Uganda should watch the shilling, which the central bank says is under depreciation pressure.

What Would Narrow the Gap

The gap would narrow if bullion and coffee prices rise, if fuel and freight costs ease, or if a weaker shilling slows import demand. The central bank's higher rate is aimed at inflation and the shilling, so any effect on trade would show only in later releases.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether October will bring a smaller deficit, because that release is due on Thursday 3 December 2026. We also could not confirm what basis the calendar estimate of US$280 million used.

Trade tables are often revised, so the bank may restate September later. We found no commentary from the bank on the September figures.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Was Uganda's Trade Deficit in September 2026?

The Bank of Uganda reported a goods deficit of US$980.1 million for September 2026. That is down from the record US$1,143.7 million in August.

Why Is Uganda's Trade Gap So Wide?

Imports of US$2,402.1 million are far larger than exports of US$1,422.0 million. Bullion and coffee make up most exports, while about nine of every ten dollars of formal private imports are goods other than fuel.

When Is the Next Uganda Trade Release?

The Bank of Uganda lists Thursday 3 December 2026 as its next release date. It will cover October.

ECUADOR · SECURITY

Key Facts The country Ecuador, a South American country that uses the US dollar, has been fighting violent drug gangs.

What happened Police detained five Ecuadorians on Wednesday 4 November 2026, three in Guayaquil and two in Panama.

Who Among them is Jacobo Bucaram, son of former president Abdalá Bucaram.

The US link All five are wanted by US authorities on alleged drug-trafficking crimes and face extradition.

Power Index Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 in Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 37.2 points (November 2026 edition).

Ecuador’s police detained a former president’s son and four other men on Wednesday 4 November 2026, in a joint operation with Panama and the United States. The Interior Minister, John Reimberg, said all five are wanted by US authorities for alleged drug-trafficking crimes and will go through extradition procedures.

For US readers, this is a case in which a Latin American government moves to hand suspects to American courts on drug charges. Our guide to who holds power in Ecuador explains the political families involved.

What Happened

Minister Reimberg announced the operation on Wednesday 4 November 2026. He said the five men carry Red Notices from Interpol, the police cooperation body that circulates international arrest requests, and are required by the United States.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 with 37.2 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (14). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B); 51 homicides per 100,000. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Three men were detained in Guayaquil, Ecuador’s largest city and main port: Jacobo Abdalá Bucaram Pulley, Geovanny Antonio Fernández Menéndez and William José Briones López. Two others, Jaime Estrada Bonilla and his son Jaime Estrada Medranda, were detained in Panama.

Reimberg said the Ecuadorian police worked with the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the American federal anti-narcotics agency, and with Interpol. He said the five were placed at the orders of the competent authorities, in the framework of extradition processes to the United States.

Download the PDF checklist

Who the Men Are

Jacobo Bucaram is the son of Abdalá Bucaram, the populist who served as Ecuador’s president in 1996 and 1997 before Congress removed him. The family name is one of the best known in Ecuadorian politics.

Jaime Estrada Bonilla, 71, is a businessman who served as mayor of the coastal city of Manta from 2009 to 2014. His son Jaime Estrada Medranda, 41, is a former member of Ecuador’s National Assembly and a former vice president of the Ecuadorian Football Federation.

Reimberg said there would be no privileges and no one untouchable in the case. The ministry has not published the US court papers behind the requests.

Why the United States Wants Them

The Ecuadorian government says the US requests concern alleged drug-trafficking crimes. It has not named the US court, the file number or the specific charges against any of the five.

Ecuador has shown it is willing to send suspects north: it has sent a leader of the Choneros gang to US authorities, as we reported in our earlier story. The new case differs because it reaches into politics and football, not only street gangs.

What It Means for You

If you invest in Ecuador through US funds, the case matters little for prices today, but it shows that Washington and Quito are working closely on drug enforcement. That cooperation shapes US aid, security deals and how Ecuador is viewed by foreign lenders.

Travellers need not change plans, since the arrests concern named individuals and no new rules for visitors have been announced. Anyone doing business with Ecuadorian firms or football clubs should watch for further announcements from the ministry.

What Is Not Known

It is not known what the US charges are, which court issued them, or how long the extradition process will take. The ministry has not said whether the three men held in Ecuador will be sent together or one by one.

It is also unclear how the Panama part of the process will proceed, and no lawyer for the five has made a public statement that we could confirm. We will update this story only when an official source confirms new facts.

More: Ecuador news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who Is Jacobo Bucaram?

He is the son of Abdalá Bucaram, who was Ecuador’s president in 1996 and 1997. Police detained him in Guayaquil on Wednesday 4 November 2026.

Why Are the Five Men Wanted by the United States?

Ecuador’s Interior Minister says US authorities require them for alleged drug-trafficking crimes. The specific charges have not been made public.

What Is an Interpol Red Notice?

It is a request to police worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition. It is not an international arrest warrant, and each country applies its own law.

Will the Five Be Sent to the United States?

The minister says extradition processes are under way. No date has been given, and the courts must still decide.

By 10 a.m. Paris time (4 a.m. ET) on Thursday, Nov. 5, France’s Education Ministry said 81 of its roughly 3,700 high schools were blocked, about 2.2%. The Union syndicale lycéenne (USL), a student union that helps lead the movement, said more than 1,000 were “at a standstill.”

The clash opens a national strike day. Our France protests hub tracks every step, and why France is in crisis explains the anger over prices and the 2027 budget.

Key Facts What happened. France counts 81 high schools blocked at 10 a.m. Paris time; students say over 1,000.

The numbers. 81 of about 3,700 schools, or 2.2%. Students count shut schools, not just blockades.

What happens next. Paris march, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. ET (2 p.m. to 7 p.m. Paris), République to Nation.

Prediction markets. Polymarket puts a French state of emergency by Dec. 31 at 6.5% (5:20 a.m. ET, Nov. 5).

In plain English For about six weeks, French teenagers have blocked school gates to protest the government’s budget and school policy. Unions of adult workers now join them for a one-day national strike over pay and prices.

Why the Two Counts Are So Far Apart

The USL counts schools blocked by students, schools closed by the authorities and schools sealed off by police. The ministry counts blockades only, and it said no blockade was reported in 84% of France’s departments, its regional units.

Both numbers can be true at once because they measure different things. Neither side has published how it counted, and the ministry’s figure covers only the first hours of the school day.

Monday Looked Calmer Than This Thursday

The ministry counted 41 blocked schools on the morning of Monday, Nov. 2, the first day back from the autumn holiday. Édouard Geffray, the education minister, told France Inter radio the situation was “fairly residual,” then warned that “the school year is now at risk for several hundred thousand pupils.”

“Everyone is free to protest,” he said, “but nobody must stop others from going to class.” The government has offered 500 extra secondary-school posts in the 2027 budget and a cap of 28 pupils per class, phased in from autumn 2027, yet the blockades continue. The ministry’s own count has roughly doubled in three days, from 41 on Monday to 81 on Thursday.

Unions Bring the Strike to Trains and Classrooms

Thursday’s strike is wider than the student movement. Sophie Binet, general secretary of the CGT (Confédération générale du travail, one of France’s biggest union confederations), wants higher wages everywhere and changes to the government’s draft 2027 budget.

The ministry put the strike rate in public primary schools at 17.54%. At SNCF, the state rail operator, four unions called a strike, and the company expects slightly disrupted high-speed TGV service and disrupted regional trains.

The RATP, which runs Paris public transport, expects normal metro, bus and tram service. The exception is the RER B suburban line, which runs a reduced service.

The Paris march runs from Place de la République to Place de la Nation between 2 p.m. and 7 p.m. Paris time (8 a.m. to 1 p.m. ET), on the route police set after a court upheld the ban on the unions’ preferred one. We covered the route fight and the 70,000-officer police deployment on Wednesday.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, prices a French state of emergency by Dec. 31 at 6.5%, with about US$2.7 million traded. A separate contract puts the chance France passes a national budget by Dec. 31 at 63.5%, with about US$26,000 traded (5:20 a.m. ET, Nov. 5).

Prices are bets, not polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Americans travelling in France today should expect rail delays and a disrupted RER B, the line many visitors use between Paris and its airports. Investors tracking French politics get an early read on whether the strike merges with the student revolt before the budget vote.

What Is Not Known

No turnout, arrest or injury figures for Nov. 5 were available at the time of writing. It is also unclear how the ministry’s count will move through the day, or how many of the USL’s 1,000 schools were in fact open. The next checkpoint is the Paris march, which ends at 1 p.m. ET (7 p.m. Paris), and any second school count would show whether the blockades are growing.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many French high schools were blocked on Nov. 5?

The Education Ministry counted 81 of about 3,700 at 10 a.m. Paris time (4 a.m. ET). The student union USL says more than 1,000 are at a standstill.

Why is France on strike?

Unions want higher wages and changes to the 2027 budget. Students joined them, protesting school policy and the cost of living.

Sources: French Education Ministry; Union syndicale lycéenne; SNCF; RATP; Polymarket.

NIGERIA · POLITICS

Key Facts The candidate Peter Obi, a former state governor, is the opposition candidate for president.

What happened His convoy was attacked in Calabar on Wednesday 4 November 2026, and police arrested one man.

The suspect Police named Victor Edet Yellow Duke, 27; he is presumed innocent.

The vote Nigeria elects its next president on Saturday 16 January 2027, about ten weeks away.

Prediction markets Polymarket, a market where users bet real money, gives Obi a 22.5% chance (5 November, 5:20 a.m. ET).

An attack on a leading opposition candidate has put Nigeria’s campaign for the 16 January 2027 election on edge. Thugs hit the convoy of Peter Obi in the southern city of Calabar on Wednesday 4 November 2026, and police arrested one suspect.

For US readers, Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country and a major oil producer, so a violent campaign matters for investors and for security planning. Our explainer on the election date sets out how the vote works.

What Happened in Calabar

The attack came at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout in Calabar, the capital of Cross River State in south-eastern Nigeria. Obi was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar, a senior traditional ruler, to the Metropolitan Hotel, where his party was holding a presidential town hall.

The Cross River State police command says a group of suspected hoodlums armed with machetes and sticks came from streets near the roundabout and attacked vehicles in the convoy. Windshields were smashed.

Police moved in and arrested one man, while the other attackers ran away. Obi’s party and the governing All Progressives Congress (APC) are rivals in the race.

The Arrest and the Investigation

Police named the suspect as Victor Edet Yellow Duke, aged 27. State police spokesperson Sunday Eitokpah said officers had made an arrest.

The Cross River police commissioner, Ajo Ordue, ordered a thorough investigation to identify other participants. He cautioned that an arrest does not amount to a finding of guilt and that the suspect is entitled to the presumption of innocence.

What Obi Did Next

Obi said he was told that supporters of the APC were throwing stones and that the attackers carried machetes and other dangerous weapons. The police have not said who sent the attackers.

He went on to the town hall at the hotel as planned. His party, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), is an opposition group that backs him for president.

Who Is Peter Obi

Peter Obi is the presidential candidate of the NDC, an opposition party. He ran for president in 2023 for the Labour Party and is a former governor of Anambra State in the south-east.

In September, police in Benue State, in central Nigeria, arrested 46 people over a blockade of his convoy. Calabar is the second such incident in about two months.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a prediction market where users bet real money, shows Nigeria’s presidential race at 5:20 a.m. ET on 5 November 2026 with about US$145,600 traded. It prices President Bola Tinubu, the APC’s candidate, at 68.0%, Obi at 22.5%, Atiku Abubakar, a former vice president, at 5.9% and Rabiu Kwankwaso, a former Kano State governor, at 6.3%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you hold Nigerian bonds or oil-linked stocks through US funds, campaign violence is a risk worth watching before the January vote. Travellers to Calabar and other cities should follow US State Department advice and avoid rallies and crowded political events.

Nigeria’s large diaspora in the United States has a direct stake, because the next government sets rules on trade, remittances and visas. The attack also tests whether police can protect all candidates during a short campaign.

What Is Not Known

Police have given no figure for damaged vehicles, and reports differ on whether anyone was hurt. It is also unclear who sent the attackers.

No charge has been announced against the suspect. Whether the incident changes security around other candidates has not been stated.

More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Related: the Atiku and Tinubu rivalry.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Happened to Peter Obi’s Convoy in Calabar?

A group armed with machetes and sticks attacked vehicles in his convoy on Wednesday 4 November 2026, police say. Windshields were smashed, and one man was arrested.

Who Is Peter Obi?

Obi is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, an opposition party, and was the Labour Party candidate in 2023. He is a former governor of Anambra State.

Who Has Police Arrested?

Cross River State police arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke. Police say the arrest is not a finding of guilt.

When Is Nigeria’s Presidential Election?

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), which runs elections, lists Saturday 16 January 2027 for the presidential and National Assembly votes. Governorship votes follow on Saturday 6 February 2027.

World.title: How Publishers Can Protect Content From AI
World.content:
TECHNOLOGY · LAW

Key Facts The basic tool robots.txt is a public file that asks crawlers to stay out, not a lock.

AI controls Google, ChatGPT maker OpenAI, Apple and Facebook owner Meta each document an AI rule in robots.txt.

Search Blocking Google’s and Apple’s AI training rules does not remove a site from search.

Brazil and Norway Oslo and São Paulo courts issued provisional orders against Meta’s new commercial terms.

The limit robots.txt is not access control, so server-side blocks add protection.

Publishers can tell artificial intelligence (AI) companies not to use their pages through a public text file called robots.txt, which is a request and not a lock. This guide explains the controls the companies document and the licensing routes.

Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

It also covers what the Brazilian and Norwegian court orders against Meta, the owner of Facebook and Instagram, change, as the plaintiffs describe them. Both orders concern Meta’s new commercial terms.

It is general information drawn from the operators’ own documentation and from court filings, not legal advice and not a recommendation of any product. It follows our explainer on the Brazilian ruling and our reading of Meta’s new terms.

What Robots.txt Can and Cannot Do

The Robots Exclusion Protocol, published as RFC 9309 by the Internet Engineering Task Force (the body that writes internet standards), sets out the format. The file must be named robots.txt, sit at the top level of a site and use UTF-8, the standard text encoding.

The standard states plainly that these rules are not a form of access authorisation, so they ask crawlers to behave but cannot force them. Because anyone can read the file, it also reveals the folders a publisher wants kept out of view.

Crawlers match rules by their user-agent name, the label a crawler gives itself. A crawler with no matching group follows the general rules for all robots.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

AI Controls Operators Document

Google says its Google-Extended token lets a site manage whether content Google crawls is used to train future Gemini AI models, Google’s family of AI systems. Google also says the token does not affect inclusion in Google Search.

OpenAI, the maker of the ChatGPT chatbot, says disallowing GPTBot, its training crawler, signals that content should not be used for training. It adds that the settings for GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot (search) are independent and that user-started ChatGPT-User visits may not follow robots.txt.

Meta documents five crawlers. One, meta-externalagent, is used for purposes such as training AI models or improving products by indexing content.

Another, meta-webindexer, supports search in Meta AI, Meta’s chatbot, while facebookexternalhit builds link previews and may bypass robots.txt for security checks. Meta also says meta-externalfetcher, which fetches links at a user’s request, may bypass robots.txt.

Apple says a Disallow rule for Applebot-Extended opts a site out of training its foundation models, the large AI systems behind Apple Intelligence, its suite of AI features. Common Crawl, a non-profit web archive, says its CCBot crawler can be blocked the same way.

Example robots.txt: blocks three AI training controls User-agent: GPTBot

Disallow: / User-agent: Google-Extended

Disallow: / User-agent: meta-externalagent

Disallow: /

The example blocks three AI training controls from a whole site, and a rule can name a folder instead of the slash. Operators say changes are not instant, since Meta says crawlers may cache the file for up to 24 hours and OpenAI says search systems need about 24 hours to adjust.

These AI rules are documented as separate from search. Google says Google-Extended does not affect inclusion in Search, and Apple says pages blocking Applebot-Extended can still appear in results.

Controls Beyond Robots.txt

Robots.txt cannot stop a crawler that ignores it, so publishers who need a hard block can refuse requests at the server. They can do it by user agent or IP address, a machine’s network address, which is a technical measure and not a request.

Google and Common Crawl document how to verify their crawlers by reverse DNS lookup, a check of which network name an address belongs to. Common Crawl also warns that other crawlers sometimes falsely use the CCBot name.

Apple says a nosnippet meta tag, a line of page code that bars quoting, keeps content out of its broad answers in Siri, its voice assistant, and in Search. This is a different control from the training opt-out.

Google says it intends to support a new AI training-preference signal in early 2027. That is a plan and not yet a feature.

In US court papers filed on Friday 4 September 2026, OpenAI argued that copying by Browse, ChatGPT’s web-reading tool, is impliedly licensed unless a site opts out. That is one party’s argument in a pending case.

We found no ruling on it in the filings we reviewed. The question matters because it ties permission to what a site’s robots.txt file says.

Licensing Routes

The US Copyright Office, the federal agency that registers copyrights, said in May 2025 that AI training licences, both individual and collective, are emerging in some sectors but unevenly. It called government intervention premature and said extended collective licensing, where one group licenses on behalf of many owners, could be considered where gaps remain.

On Tuesday 29 September 2026 the US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit decided a case between Thomson Reuters and ROSS Intelligence, an AI legal-research start-up. Thomson Reuters is the information group that owns the Westlaw legal database.

The court found that the market for licensing headnotes, short summaries of legal rulings, as AI training data is rapidly developing, and it counted harm to that market against ROSS. That makes the licensing market part of the court’s fair use analysis, the legal test of whether copying without permission is allowed.

The case concerned legal headnotes and not news. A California federal court rejected a similar licensing-market argument in Kadrey v. Meta, a suit by authors.

What the Brazil and Norway Orders Change

On Tuesday 3 November 2026 the 44th Civil Court of São Paulo granted a preliminary injunction, a temporary order issued before a full trial, according to three Brazilian media associations. They are ANJ for newspapers, Abert for broadcasters and Aner for magazines.

They say it bars Meta from collecting or using members’ content without authorisation, including to train AI. They add that it requires Meta to keep their accounts active without penalty.

The associations put the fine at R$1 million a day (about US$182,000), capped at R$100 million (about US$18.2 million). Those conversions use 5.4935 reais per US dollar, the central bank rate of 3 November.

On Wednesday 28 October 2026 the Oslo District Court temporarily barred Meta from bringing in the same terms, according to a statement by the Norwegian media trade body. The statement says ten Norwegian media groups asked the court that week.

Both orders are provisional. The Brazilian associations say theirs protects their members, and the Norwegian trade body says Meta may not start the terms until a court rules on their lawfulness.

Nothing in the plaintiffs’ descriptions of the orders changes how robots.txt works. Meta’s own crawler page says robots.txt can block meta-externalagent.

What It Means for You

If you run a site or a publication, start by reading your robots.txt file and deciding which AI crawlers to allow. The operators document separate controls for training and for search.

The choice is yours. Blocking training rules does not remove a page from Google Search or Apple search, according to those companies.

If you have a Facebook or Instagram business account, check any notice about Meta’s new commercial terms and consider legal advice before accepting. Readers will not see these controls, because they work between a site and the crawlers that visit it.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether every AI crawler honours robots.txt, since operators document exceptions such as user-started visits. It is also not known whether US courts will treat a site’s silence, or its robots.txt rules, as consent to AI use.

Meta scheduled its new commercial terms to start on Friday 20 November 2026, and whether they will start then has not been confirmed. The plaintiffs say the terms would let Meta use publishers’ content for AI.

We have not seen either court decision, so how far each order reaches is unconfirmed. The plaintiffs’ statements are our only source for what each order says.

More: Meta, AI and news: our full dossier, with the explainer on Brazil’s court ruling.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Blocking AI Crawlers Remove My Site From Search?

Not for the controls that Google and Apple document: Google says Google-Extended does not impact inclusion in Search, and Apple says such pages can still appear in search results. OpenAI treats its search crawler and its training crawler as separate settings.

Is Robots.txt Legally Binding?

The standard itself says its rules are not a form of access authorisation. In December 2025 a New York federal judge ruled in a suit against OpenAI by Ziff Davis, a US digital publisher. The judge found robots.txt is not a technological measure that effectively controls access.

That means ignoring it is not circumvention under the US anti-circumvention law in the Digital Millennium Copyright Act. We found no US ruling that settles whether ignoring it breaks copyright or contract law.

Do the Brazil and Norway Rulings Cover Every Publisher?

Not necessarily: the Brazilian associations say their order protects their members, while the Norwegian statement describes a ban on bringing in the terms. We have not seen either court file.

Sources: Internet Engineering Task Force, RFC 9309, Robots Exclusion Protocol, 2022; Google Search Central, documentation on Google’s common crawlers (Google-Extended); OpenAI, crawler documentation (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User); Meta for Developers, web crawlers documentation; Apple Support, Applebot documentation; Common Crawl, CCBot documentation; US Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training (pre-publication version), 9 May 2025; US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, Thomson Reuters Enterprise Centre v. ROSS Intelligence, No. 25-2153, 29 September 2026; US District Court, Southern District of New York, In re OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation, No. 25-md-3143, OpenAI defendants’ summary judgment filing in the news cases (public redacted version), 4 September 2026; US District Court, Northern District of California, Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, No. 3:23-cv-03417, order of 25 June 2025; US District Court, Southern District of New York, Ziff Davis v. OpenAI, opinion and order of 15 December 2025; Central Bank of Brazil, PTAX reference exchange rate of 3 November 2026, 5.4935 reais per US dollar; joint statement of ANJ, Abert and Aner on the São Paulo injunction, 3 November 2026; statement of the Norwegian media trade body on the Oslo District Court order, 28 October 2026.

World.title: Where US Courts Stand on AI Training
World.content:
The US Supreme Court building in Washington. On 20 February 2026 the court ruled that the emergency powers law IEEPA does not allow the president to impose tariffs. (Photo: Kjetil Ree, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

TECHNOLOGY · LAW

Key Facts The question Whether artificial intelligence (AI) firms may train on copyrighted work without permission has no clear US answer.

Appeals ruling Training an AI legal tool on case summaries was not fair use, the copying exception, 29 September 2026.

Chatbot cases Two California judges ruled for AI developers on training in June 2025, on different grounds.

Pending ChatGPT maker OpenAI asked a New York court on 4 September 2026 to rule training fair use.

Federal agency The US Copyright Office’s 9 May 2025 report says some training is fair use, some not.

No US court has settled whether artificial intelligence (AI) companies may train their systems on copyrighted work without permission, and the rulings so far point in different directions. This page sets out each decision and pending case that matters, with exact dates, as of Thursday 5 November 2026.

Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Meta AI and News story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

It follows court orders that, according to the Brazilian and Norwegian media groups that sued, suspended new terms from Meta, the owner of Facebook and Instagram. Our explainer on what Brazil’s court ruled covers them.

This page is a news summary, not legal advice. A ruling in one case does not bind every other court.

What Fair Use Means

Fair use is a rule in US copyright law that lets people use protected work without permission in limited cases, such as criticism, research or teaching. Judges weigh four factors: the purpose of the use, the nature of the work, how much was taken, and the effect on the market for the original.

In AI cases the fight is mostly about two points: whether training is transformative, meaning it serves a new purpose, and whether it harms the market for the original work. A summary judgment ruling, which a judge issues before trial when the key facts are not in dispute, can settle fair use for the parties in one case.

What the Courts Have Decided

Westlaw is a legal research service owned by Thomson Reuters, the Canadian news and information group. Headnotes are editors’ short summaries of points of law.

On Tuesday 29 September 2026 the US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, which covers Delaware, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and the US Virgin Islands, decided case No. 25-2153. It held that ROSS Intelligence, a legal-research start-up, used 2,243 Westlaw headnotes without permission to train an AI search tool, and that this was not fair use.

The court found the headnotes original enough for copyright, ROSS’s use only minimally transformative, and harm to a developing market for licensing headnotes as AI training data. It also noted that ROSS’s tool cannot generate new text, which it said sets the case apart from generative AI models, which create new text or images.

On Monday 23 June 2025 Judge William Alsup in San Francisco ruled in Bartz v. Anthropic, a suit against the company behind the Claude chatbot. He found that training a large language model, the AI behind chatbots, on books was fair use, as was scanning bought print books.

He refused to excuse the copies Anthropic downloaded from pirate websites. He ordered a trial on them.

Anthropic then settled the pirated-copies claims with the class, the group of authors the suit represents, for US$1.5 billion. The settlement website puts that at about US$3,000 per work, before court-approved fees and costs.

The court granted final approval on Monday 20 July 2026. According to the settlement website, the release covers only past conduct up to 25 August 2025, not what the AI produces.

On Wednesday 25 June 2025 Judge Vince Chhabria granted Meta partial summary judgment in Kadrey v. Meta, a suit by thirteen authors over Llama, Meta’s AI language models. He wrote that the authors offered no meaningful evidence that the AI would dilute, or flood, the market for their books.

He added that the ruling covers only those thirteen authors and that such copying will often be illegal, so companies will generally need to pay. He rejected the authors’ separate argument that Meta’s training cost them licensing income.

What the Copyright Office Said

The US Copyright Office, the federal agency that registers copyrights and advises Congress, published a pre-publication version of Part 3 of its AI report on Friday 9 May 2025. It concluded that some uses of copyrighted work for AI training will qualify as fair use and some will not.

It said non-commercial research uses that do not reproduce works in outputs are likely fair, but copying pirated works to make competing content is unlikely to be fair. It also found licensing deals for AI training emerging in certain sectors and called government intervention premature.

What Is Still Pending

A major open case is In re OpenAI Copyright Infringement Litigation, No. 25-md-3143 in federal court in Manhattan before Judge Sidney Stein. It combines suits by news publishers and other plaintiffs against OpenAI, the maker of the ChatGPT chatbot, and Microsoft, OpenAI’s largest investor.

On Friday 4 September 2026 OpenAI asked for summary judgment that using news articles for pretraining is fair use. Pretraining is the first stage of training, in which a model learns from huge amounts of text.

It also argued that Browse, ChatGPT’s tool for reading live web pages, made fair use of articles or had an implied licence from sites that did not opt out. We found no ruling as of Thursday 5 November.

The Third Circuit’s opinion says the US Justice Department filed a statement of interest in that case on Tuesday 1 September 2026. A statement of interest is a filing in which the government sets out its view in a case it is not part of.

The opinion says the department relied on the Bartz ruling to argue that training is transformative. We have not read that filing.

What It Means for You

If you publish news or run a website, courts have not yet said whether an AI company may train on your articles without paying. The Third Circuit counted lost licensing income as harm, and one California judge wrote that companies will generally need to pay.

If you invest in US-listed AI companies, the US$1.5 billion settlement over pirated books shows what unlicensed sourcing can cost, though this is not investment advice. The OpenAI case alone combines several suits, so one ruling may not end the question.

What Is Not Known

It is not known when Judge Stein will rule on the summary judgment motions, or whether he will treat news articles differently from books. It is also not known whether the Third Circuit’s decision will be reviewed further, or how other appeals courts will treat generative AI.

The Copyright Office has said a final version of its training report will follow, and it expects no substantive change to its conclusions. We have not seen the court files in the Brazil and Norway cases against Meta, and we found no US court ruling on Meta’s new terms.

More: Meta, AI and news: our full dossier, with the explainer on Brazil’s court ruling and a plain-language reading of Meta’s new terms.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Training AI on Copyrighted Work Legal in the US?

It is not settled. Two California judges found fair use for the AI companies on their records in June 2025. An appeals court held on 29 September 2026 that training a competing AI search tool was not fair use.

What Did the Third Circuit Decide?

It held that 2,243 Westlaw headnotes were copyrightable and that ROSS’s use of them to train an AI legal search tool was not fair use. The court distinguished that tool, which cannot generate new text, from generative AI models.

When Will the OpenAI Case Be Decided?

No date has been announced in the court papers we reviewed. OpenAI filed its summary judgment motion on 4 September 2026, and we found no ruling as of 5 November 2026.

Sources: US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, Thomson Reuters Enterprise Centre v. ROSS Intelligence, No. 25-2153, opinion, 29 September 2026; US District Court, Northern District of California, Bartz v. Anthropic, order on fair use, 23 June 2025; US District Court, Northern District of California, Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, order on summary judgment, 25 June 2025; Bartz v. Anthropic court-authorised settlement website, final approval 20 July 2026; US Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training (pre-publication version), 9 May 2025; US District Court, Southern District of New York, In re OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation, No. 25-md-3143, OpenAI defendants’ summary judgment filing in the news cases, public redacted version, 4 September 2026.

World.content:
