World.title: Una nueva oleada de amenazas de bomba afecta al menos a 13 aviones con destino a ciudades europeas
World.content:
Un Airbus A320 de Aer Lingus con destino Roma aterriza este jueves en la base aérea militar de Évreux, en Francia, después de ser desviado por amenaza de bomba.

Una de las aeronaves ha sido escoltada por aviones militares italianos. La incidencia es similar a la registrada el martes en otros siete vuelos

Al menos 13 vuelos con destino a ciudades europeas han sufrido este jueves amenazas de bomba que les han obligado a realizar aterrizajes de emergencia, sin contratiempos en todos los casos. Dos vuelos han sido desviados. Una de las aeronaves, con destino a Roma, ha sido escoltada por aviones militares italianos. Las incidencias, aún bajo investigación, han afectado a aeropuertos de Francia, Italia, Bélgica, Bulgaria, Chequia, Polonia y Austria.

El avión de la compañía Finnair que volaba de Helsinki a Roma ha sido escoltado a primera hora por aviones de la Fuerza Aérea italiana tras recibir una amenaza de bomba, según la agencia Ansa. Su aterrizaje en el aeropuerto de Fiumicino no ha causado ninguna perturbación en las operaciones, según las auroridades. También en Italia, alertas de bomba han sido dirigidas a dos vuelos con destino al aeropuerto de Malpensa, en Milán; los aviones han aterrizado de forma segura, informa Ansa.

Otro vuelo de la misma compañía, operado por Jettime, que viajaba entre Helsinki y Viena, ha aterrizado con normalidad en la capital austríaca tras registrar también una amenaza de bomba, ha apuntado un portavoz de Finnair.

Poco antes, un Airbus A320 de la compañía Aer Lingus que volaba de Dublín a Roma ha registrado una alerta similar y ha tenido que ser desviado a la base militar de Évreux (Francia), según ha informado el gabinete del primer ministro francés, Sébastien Lecornu. La aeronave ha aterrizado sin contratiempos. Los 151 pasajeros y seis tripulantes han sido evacuados mientras efectivos de la unidad de desactivación de explosivos accedían al interior del avión.

Bulgaria ha informado así mismo de aterrizajes de emergencia de tres aeronaves (procedentes de Copenhague, Madrid y Londres) debido a amenazas de bomba que después se han demostrado falsas, según señalan medios locales citando a las autoridades. Y fuentes oficiales han confirmado a Reuters que un vuelo de la aerolínea polaca LOT procedente de Varsovia ha aterrizado en el aeropuerto de Bruselas tras una alerta sospechosa. A media mañana, la policía checa ha comunicado que cuatro aviones con destino a Praga se preparaban para aterrizar tras registrar amenazas de bomba. Una vez han tomado tierra, los artificieros han entrado en las cuatro aeronaves, sin detectar ningún explosivo a bordo.

Estas incidencias se suman a las que se vivieron el pasado martes en otros siete vuelos con destino a ciudades europeas: Varsovia, Sofía, Roma y Murcia. Todos recibieron amenazas de bomba, uno de los aparatos tuvo que ser desviado y se produjeron perturbaciones en varios aeropuertos, donde fueron movilizados los artificieros, aunque finalmente no fueron hallados explosivos en ninguno de los aviones. La víspera, el lunes, otro avión que volaba de Londres a Sofía había sido desviado a Budapest, escoltado por un caza húngaro, por idéntico motivo.

Por ahora, nadie ha reivindicado esas amenazas y ninguno de los países afectados ha señalado a ningún otro Gobierno o grupo terrorista, aunque expertos consultados por EL PAÍS sostienen que esa concentración de amenazas de bomba en cuestión de horas y un mismo espacio aéreo no puede ser casual.

Esta semana, además, se ha producido un ciberataque contra decenas de supermercados de al menos siete países europeos, que ha echado a perder los alimentos almacenados en las cámaras frigoríficas. Y en los mismos días se ha dado a conocer otro ciberataque, este en Francia, contra varios centros regionales del organismo público que gestiona las donaciones de sangre. El ataque puso en riesgo la conservación de grandes reservas de sangre destinadas a transfusiones y ensayos clínicos.

World.title: Así se prepara la banca para los próximos años
World.content:
El avance de la inteligencia artificial en bancos como CaixaBank convive con iniciativas de inclusión como SVisual, el servicio de videointerpretación en lengua de signos.

Más educación financiera, planes acordes con la mayor longevidad de la población y digitalización inclusiva. En el horizonte, las entidades bancarias quieren pasar de un papel reactivo a otro más proactivo que acompañe, oriente y anticipe las necesidades de los clientes

La banca del futuro se imagina a menudo dominada por los algoritmos. Sin embargo, cuando se escucha a los expertos y a quienes la construyen, brota un cariz más humano: todos coinciden en que será híbrida. La tecnología es eficaz en lo cotidiano, está disponible a cualquier hora, concede una autonomía impensable hace unos años, cuando la relación con el banco tenía el rostro del trabajador y no una interfaz. Sin embargo, hay circunstancias —las decisiones más vitales— en las que se prioriza el trato personal. Son momentos en los que la conversación con alguien que orienta adquiere un valor irremplazable. Por eso, entidades como CaixaBank entienden el mañana como una suma compleja: más tecnología y más innovación sin desdeñar la posibilidad de acceder a especialistas y gestores cuando sean necesarios.

La inteligencia artificial (IA) permitirá que la relación sea más sencilla y personalizada, pronostican desde CaixaBank. Su cambio estructural consistirá en pasar de una banca principalmente reactiva, en la que el cliente busca una solución cuando surge una necesidad, a una banca con mayor capacidad para acompañar, orientar y anticiparse. Imaginan una relación en la que el banco tenga más capacidad de acompañar de forma proactiva.

Las funciones de esos modelos inteligentes ayudarán a traducir información compleja, a facilitar la comparación entre alternativas y a generar recomendaciones más adaptadas a cada perfil, como anuncian desde este banco. Como concreta Alejandro San Nicolás, docente del máster en Formación Permanente en IA para el Sector Financiero de la Universidad Internacional de Valencia (VIU), la banca conocerá mejor al usuario a través de sus hábitos, comportamientos, emociones y tendencias de consumo. Este docente añade que los entornos bancarios evolucionarán hacia una suerte de marketplace, donde el cliente podrá contratar productos, realizar compras o acceder a financiación directamente desde la plataforma digital bancaria pertinente: “El propio banco va a empezar a lanzarte ofertas basadas en tus necesidades y en lo que te gusta”, explica San Nicolás.

Las entidades financieras aspiran a esa hiperpersonalización que, como señalan desde CaixaBank, “da la oportunidad de reducir ruido y proporcionar al cliente sólo la información apropiada para su situación personal”. Por eso, insisten en que la formación en competencias digitales, la educación financiera y la prevención del fraude son también una parte crucial de ese nuevo acompañamiento.

Habla

Cómo construir una banca integradora, según CaixaBank La evolución de la interfaz Habrá una generalización del móvil como canal financiero. Las plataformas digitales seguirán en constante cambio. Evolucionará con los agentes de IA, que podrán interpretar necesidades, mantener conversaciones complejas y simplificar procesos completos. Su actuación reducirá la complejidad de gestiones que hoy requieren múltiples pasos. Una longevidad diversa Llegados a la jubilación, se generan necesidades que van más allá del dinero. Por eso, desde la entidad se trata de fomentar el ahorro desde edades tempranas, complementar ingresos en la jubilación, ayudar a optimizar el patrimonio financiero e inmobiliario o acompañar a las personas durante toda esa etapa posterior a la laboral. Un error común es considerar que todas las personas mayores son iguales, señalan desde CaixaBank. Algunos se sienten cómodos con los entornos digitales, otros prefieren la atención telefónica y algunos exigen presencialidad. El colectivo senior es especialmente diverso en cuanto a autonomía financiera y uso de canales. Atención a las necesidades específicas CaixaBank hace hincapié en la inclusión: el 94% de sus oficinas, el 99% de sus cajeros y su aplicación móvil CaixaBankNow son accesibles. Además, dispone de la Tarjeta Braille para personas con discapacidad visual, el servicio de videointerpretación en lengua de signos SVisual para clientes con discapacidad auditiva, TPV accesibles, comunicaciones en lectura fácil, una guía adaptada para ayudar en la toma de decisiones financieras y el programa Día a Día Apoyo Capacidad Jurídica. z La transformación de las sucursales Las oficinas físicas evolucionarán, aunque seguirán desempeñando un papel importante. CaixaBank tiene más de 4.200, repartidas por España. Además, la entidad tiene presencia en cerca de 3.700 municipios: en 2.234 localidades con el modelo tradicional y en más de 1.420 poblaciones a través de 32 oficinas móviles. Estas permiten a clientes (y no clientes) realizar las operaciones bancarias más habituales en localidades sin oficina bancaria o con restricciones que limitan el acceso a los servicios financieros en poblaciones en las que residen más de 632.000 personas. El 70% de los usuarios tienen más de 65 años.

Mantener la confianza... ‘online’

Dar cierta credibilidad a la IA es fundamental para que su implantación sea efectiva. Pero trabajar en entornos tecnológicos plantea riesgos relacionados con la privacidad, la seguridad de los datos y la posible sensación de vigilancia excesiva, como enumera Juan Carlos López-Robles, profesor de ESIC University que imparte en ámbitos como la Informática Aplicada, las Tecnologías de la Educación y las Tecnologías Móviles e Internet de las Cosas (IoT).

Los ingredientes para que la IA tenga una buena integración, según López-Robles, son tres: que sus respuestas sean útiles, que se comprendan sin necesidad de tener un alto nivel de conocimientos específicos y que sean transparentes. “Los usuarios aceptamos mejor una recomendación cuando entendemos el porqué, el para qué y tenemos la sensación de control sobre la decisión final”. Y añade: “La confianza se construye con explicaciones claras y resultados consistentes “. Hay una necesidad de entender los criterios, de conocer las reglas del juego de algoritmos.

Los usuarios están dispuestos a compartir información cuando perciben un beneficio claro y confían en la entidad. Por eso, para CaixaBank, “la personalización solo tendrá recorrido si va acompañada de seguridad, privacidad, transparencia y capacidad de control por parte del cliente”. Un ejemplo de su compromiso es su nueva Dirección de IA y Datos, que coordina de forma transversal esta área y facilita el desarrollo de soluciones escalables, seguras y responsables. Gestiona todo el ciclo de vida de las iniciativas, desde la identificación de oportunidades hasta su diseño, implantación y supervisión. Además, integra el cumplimiento normativo y la gestión de riesgos desde las fases iniciales; se asegura de que los desarrollos sean responsables.

La IA se emplea con criterio, pero también permite al banco ser más seguro. La han incorporado a sus sistemas de defensa para reforzar las tareas de detección, análisis, actuación y para proteger los nuevos entornos. También vigila los agentes, una función que, más allá de responder a preguntas como un chat tradicional, razona, planifica y ejecuta acciones de forma autónoma para cumplir un propósito. Estos sistemas incorporan herramientas como la identificación y corrección automatizadas de vulnerabilidades, la evolución de su centro de operaciones de seguridad y el empleo de sistemas capaces de detectar indicios de actividad sospechosa, correlacionar señales, evaluar amenazas y activar medidas de protección de manera autónoma.

Sobre todo, inciden en que combinan la capacidad analítica de la IA con la supervisión y responsabilidad humanas. En esa mezcla está la virtud, secunda López-Robles: “Nadie quiere pedir cita para hacer una transferencia o revisar los movimientos de la cuenta, pero casi todo el mundo quiere hablar con una persona antes de firmar una hipoteca o una cartera de inversión”.

La atención presencial no puede desaparecer, reconocen los expertos, pero su transformación es inevitable. “Dará paso a una red mucho más reducida, orientada a un trato más personal, en un espacio con sofás y en los que le ofrecen un café”, describe San Nicolás. De ahí que sean fundamentales las citas previas; serán más puntuales, planificadas y especializadas.

Las entidades financieras se adaptan a los nuevos hábitos y refuerzan sus servicios digitales. CaixaBank aumentó en un 30% las altas digitales en el ejercicio 2025, en gran parte gracias a imagin, el banco digital del grupo dirigido especialmente a clientes jóvenes, que cuenta con alrededor de 4,3 millones de clientes. La penetración en el Grupo CaixaBank de clientes financieros de edad de entre 16 y 34 años alcanza el 42%. La tendencia online también se aprecia en los hábitos de pago. En junio, CaixaBank superó el récord histórico de pago con el móvil en España, con 139,7 millones de operaciones en un mes.

La generación de transición

¿Quiénes son los que se pueden sentir más abrumados por los cambios? San Nicolás, como experto en IA para el sector financiero, señala que los que están “en tierra de nadie”. Por ejemplo: “Los mayores de 50 años, una generación que ha visto llegar toda esta transformación cuando ya tenía gran parte de su vida financiera construida”.

La tecnología puede convertirse en una nueva forma de exclusión, advierte López-Robles, profesor de ESIC. “A medida que aumente el número de personas mayores, la clave no será ofrecer más tecnología, sino hacerla accesible, dinámica, sencilla y fluida”, sostiene. Es uno de los motivos que lleva a CaixaBank a ir más allá de la jubilación, que les mueve a planificar una etapa de la vida cada vez más larga y diversa y apostar por un acompañamiento integral. Para López-Robles, el objetivo que se deben proponer las entidades es construir una banca “no solo más digital, sino más inteligente, más sencilla y, sobre todo, más relevante para cada cliente”.

World.title: En el contrato anual con el inquilino hay una cláusula para que mis hijos recuperen la casa. ¿Aplica la prórroga de dos años?
World.content:
Pregunta. Tengo un piso alquilado que cumple el contrato anual el 31 de diciembre. Cuando renovamos el año pasado, incluimos una cláusula por la que se rescindiría dicho contrato si uno de nuestros dos hijos lo necesitaba. El inquilino aceptó las condiciones. Queremos saber si obligatoriamente tiene que estar dos años más, aunque nuestros hijos lo necesiten, avisando con los plazos legales. C. Sisamon

Respuesta. Entiendo que se está refiriendo a la prórroga extraordinaria de dos años prevista en la disposición final quinta del Real Decreto-ley 29/2026, de 6 de octubre, por el que se adoptan medidas urgentes para la protección de la función social de la vivienda y la ampliación de la oferta de vivienda asequible. Este Real Decreto entró en vigor el 7 de octubre de 2026.

Si el contrato de arrendamiento al que se refiere en la consulta tiene una duración de un año (actualmente denominado contrato temporal o de temporada) y no es de vivienda habitual, no se encontraría dentro de los supuestos en los que puede solicitarse la citada prórroga extraordinaria de dos años. Por tanto, el compromiso de desalojo pactado en favor de los hijos del arrendador debería ser respetado por la parte arrendataria. Además, dicha prórroga extraordinaria no resulta aplicable a los contratos temporales.

No obstante, conviene realizar una precisión importante. Si, tal y como parece desprenderse de la consulta, se vienen formalizando contratos de un año de duración, no prorrogables, sobre la misma vivienda y con los mismos arrendatarios, debe tenerse en cuenta que, si el Real Decreto es finalmente convalidado por la Diputación Permanente, el próximo contrato de temporada que se suscriba (en principio en diciembre de 2026) deberá recoger de forma expresa y obligatoria la causa concreta que motiva el desplazamiento temporal del arrendatario y que justifica la temporalidad del arrendamiento. Asimismo, corresponderá al arrendador acreditar la existencia de dicha causa.

En caso de no poder demostrarse la necesidad temporal que justifica este tipo de contrato, el artículo 7.2 de la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos, en su redacción dada por el Real Decreto, establece que esta circunstancia “lo privará de su naturaleza temporal y comportará su sumisión al presente título en las mismas condiciones que los contratos de arrendamiento de vivienda habitual, con efectos retroactivos a la formalización del contrato”.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Fontevraud, un monasterio milenario convertido en faro del hedonismo contemporáneo
World.content:
El refugio de Ricardo Corazón de León se transforma en una referencia del diseño en el Loira con un museo, un hotel y un restaurante de alta cocina

Dormir bajo los mismos techos que cobijaron a Leonor de Aquitania y Ricardo Corazón de León y, siglos después, a los presos más peligrosos de Francia ya es posible. La abadía de Fontevraud, el mayor complejo monástico de Europa, fundado en el siglo XII, ha culminado una metamorfosis que estira sus hilos desde el románico hasta el diseño industrial más limpio del siglo XXI. Clasificado como monumento histórico en 1840, el monasterio es Patrimonio Mundial de la Unesco desde el año 2000. Este histórico recinto del Valle del Loira, que llegó a ser una pequeña ciudad, se postula como un faro de hedonismo contemporáneo, si entendemos hedonismo por desconexión y por silencio.

Ya no solo alberga el mausoleo real de la dinastía Plantagenet, sino también el Museo de Arte Moderno, constituido por la colección privada de Martine (artista) y Léon Cligman (industrial). Casi mil años de historia y dos patrimonios excepcionales dialogan en un entorno hors du monde. Además, respetando la idea de austeridad, el estudio de arquitectura Jouin Manku ha transformado las antiguas celdas del priorato de San Lázaro (colindante a la abadía) en un hotel donde la ausencia se celebra con música callada (que diría Mompou), soledad sonora (que diría san Juan de la Cruz) y, para quien no pueda resistirlo, con la alta cocina del chef Thibaut Ruggeri, premio Bocuse d’Or.

La imponente nave central de la iglesia de la Abadía Real de Fontevraud. CHRISTOPHE MARTIN

Una clase de historia

Entre la reforma religiosa del siglo XII, el Museo de Arte Moderno y el hotel del siglo XXI debemos tener en cuenta unas cuantas fechas. En 1101, convencido de que mujeres y hombres podían cohabitar castamente, el monje Robert d’Arbrissel fundó una abadía que diera cobijo a monjas contemplativas (Le Grand Moûtier, el monasterio principal, edificio hoy increíblemente intacto) y a las que cuidaban a los leprosos (el priorato de San Lázaro, donde hoy está el hotel). Catorce años después, en 1115, antes de morir, D’Arbrissel cedió el poder a la abadesa Pétronille de Chemillé, algo demasiado moderno para la época. En los vitrales de la iglesia de Notre-Dame-la-Neuve se ve a la abadesa recibiendo la cruz.

En 1190, Enrique II y Leonor de Aquitania confiaron la educación de sus hijos a la abadía. El rey fue enterrado en Fontevraud en 1189. Cuando, diez años después, falleció su hijo Ricardo Corazón de León, Leonor decidió sepultarlo junto a su padre, como era su deseo. En 1200, la reina indomable (esa Leonor tan bien interpretada por Katharine Hepburn en la película El león en invierno), tras respaldar firmemente a su hijo Juan sin Tierra, encontró refugio en Fontevraud, donde murió cuatro años más tarde. Hoy vemos las efigies funerarias de los Plantagenet, una al lado de otra, en la nave de la iglesia abacial. La profesora de Historia Medieval y especialista en historia de las mujeres Almudena Blasco opina: “La visibilidad de la Abadía de Fontevraud responde al espacio monástico que Leonor de Aquitania condujo hacia lo simbólico, a los parajes de la dinastía Plantagenet, hacia el imaginario de un Estado que adopta la forma del Imperio angevino donde ella y los hombres de su familia dotan de razonable gobernanza una historia inmortal”.

Visitantes frente a los restos de Ricardo I de Inglaterra, conocido como Ricardo Corazón de León, ubicado en la Abadía Real de Fontevraud. KAZIM KREAZIM

Para 1491, la guerra de los Cien Años había hundido las rentas de las tierras de la abadía. La abadesa Renée de Bourbon, símbolo de la renovación, emprendió la construcción de un cercado de 1,3 kilómetros de longitud alrededor del Grand Moûtier y de una galería adosada al transepto, nave transversal que cruza perpendicularmente a la nave principal. Con la Revolución, en 1789, los bienes del clero se declararon nacionales. La abadía todavía contaba con 70 religiosas y 22 religiosos. En 1792 se produjo la salida de la última abadesa, Julie d’Antin, y se inició la época de los saqueos. La iglesia de Saint-Jean fue desmantelada y sirvió de cantera de piedra, mientras el resto de edificios quedaron abandonados.

En 1804, Napoleón transformó la abadía en una casa de fuerza y corrección, como la del Mont-Saint-Michel. Tras diez años de obras, abrió como prisión y lo siguió siendo ¡hasta 1985!, cuando salieron los últimos prisioneros tras haber participado en la destrucción de los talleres de la cárcel y en la consiguiente restauración de la abadía. La llamada “prisión de las mil ventanas” se entregó al poder civil.

En todo caso, a pesar de ejercer como cárcel, la abadía fue parcialmente visitada y el escritor, historiador e inspector general de patrimonio Prosper Mérimée —fascinado como nos fascinamos hoy con las cúpulas que elevan las viejas cocinas a cargo del arquitecto Lucien Magne, discípulo de Viollet-le-Duc— la clasificó como monumento histórico. Poco a poco varios edificios fueron liberados de la función penitenciaria, como el claustro y el refectorio. Desde la decisión de cerrar definitivamente la prisión en 1963 hasta finales del siglo XX, las obras de restauración fueron dando a la abadía el aspecto que el viajero descubre hoy.

Gestación de un museo

El nuevo milenio trajo el último gran hito de la abadía. Durante más de seis décadas, el magnate del textil Léon Cligman y su esposa, la artista Martine Martine, reunieron en su residencia de París una considerable colección de arte. Tras un sonado desencuentro con la ciudad de Tours, que rechazó el legado por disputas burocráticas, el matrimonio encontró en Fontevraud el refugio definitivo para su tesoro. Inaugurado en 2021 en las antiguas caballerizas del siglo XVIII (la Fannerie), el Museo de Arte Moderno de Fontevraud alberga hoy ese legado de 800 obras.

En sus salas, la pintura de los siglos XIX y XX brilla a través de joyas ocultas como el íntimo Autoportrait de dos (1884) de Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, los trazos al carboncillo de La Repasseuse de Edgar Degas o las naturalezas muertas expresionistas de Chaïm Soutine y Georges Rouault. Mención especial merece André Derain, una de las grandes debilidades del matrimonio, del que se exhiben piezas tan potentes como Portrait de Gitan o Forêt en Île-de-France, además de la serie de 36 ilustraciones originales que el artista concibió para el Satiricón de Petronio. El recorrido reserva un espacio para Germaine Richier, una de las escultoras de vanguardia más importantes de Francia, de quien se expone un conjunto de 14 piezas de bronce monumentales que se acoplan a la sobriedad del entorno medieval. Las artes decorativas asoman con una colección de 88 piezas de vidrio soplado del maestro vidriero Maurice Marinot, cuyos vasos e incensarios parecen capturar la luz del Loira.

Una sala del Museo de Arte Moderno de Fontevraud que exhibe esculturas de bronce de Germaine Richier en diálogo con una pintura de la ciudad de Nueva York creada por Bernard Buffet al fondo de la pared. MARC DOMAG

El verdadero triunfo del museo radica en una museografía limpia y libre de etiquetas donde el visitante asiste a un diálogo transcultural e histórico. Así, un lienzo vanguardista de Robert Delaunay o Juan Gris comparten mirada de forma natural con un torso de Bodhisattva jemer del siglo XII, estatuillas del Antiguo Egipto, máscaras africanas o ídolos precolombinos. En un número especial que la prestigiosa revista Beaux Arts dedicó a la colección, Martine y Léon Cligman explicaron su modus operandi: “Íbamos a las galerías, observábamos, nos cruzábamos con un cuadro que nos gustaba mucho. Volvíamos a casa y solo pensábamos en ese cuadro. Estábamos obligados a volver al día siguiente para admirarlo de nuevo. Eso es una obra de arte, ella te llama”

El diseño austero y restaurante abundante

El estudio de arquitectura liderado por el diseñador Patrick Jouin y el arquitecto Sanjit Manku asumió el reto de transformar las celdas del antiguo priorato de San Lázaro conservando su aura mística. El resultado es un hotel minimalista donde la sobriedad monacal se entiende con la modernidad y con la moderación (140 euros la noche). No es esta su primera gran obra; de hecho, rediseñar espacios históricos, hoteles y templos de la alta gastronomía parece ser su especialidad.

Se encargaron de renovar el hotel La Mamounia (Marrakech) para su centenario; de los espacios públicos, el bar y los restaurantes (como el emblemático Camélia) del hotel Mandarin Oriental (París); de la renovación integral del Park Hyatt Tokyo —famoso mundialmente por ser el escenario de la película Lost in Translation—, así como de varios restaurantes del estrellado chef Alain Ducasse e incluso de la estación de Montparnasse (París): un proyecto de escala urbana donde transformaron la masiva estación ferroviaria para hacerla más luminosa, fluida y habitable, quizás su obra más ambiciosa hasta la fecha.

Respecto al restaurante Fontevraud Le Restaurant, junto al hotel, conviene constatar que la propuesta cuenta con una estrella Michelin y, además, una estrella verde que premia el compromiso ecológico del chef Thibaut Ruggeri, cuya filosofía culinaria pretende ser un fiel reflejo del entorno. Evita el artificio y se basa en el autoabastecimiento (cuenta con un huerto propio en el recinto) y en los tesoros del Valle del Loira, al que define como “el huerto de Francia”. Su comedor se abre directamente hacia el claustro (en el mismo sitio donde se sirven los desayunos) ligando la experiencia gastronómica con la monumentalidad del lugar. No es obligatorio pagar los 100 euros de su menú degustación para disfrutar del entorno; es más, el visitante puede llevar su propia colección de tuppers y cenar al aire libre.

Uno de los platos con champiñones que pueden degustarse el restaurante ubicado dentro de los terrenos de la Abadía Real de Fontevraud. CHRISTOPHE MARTIN

Haga lo que haga, el paseo nocturno tras la cena es una invitación a sentir el ingrávido peso de una noche obscenamente estrellada, leve y sedosa. Así uno comprende que la austeridad es una de las mayores virtudes. Ni el más mínimo temblor en el aire y con el silencio como cómplice.

Por la noche se ofrece la posibilidad de volver a visitar la abadía a solas, iluminada como una gran obra de arte, para prestar atención a lo que más interese, ya sean las tumbas policromadas de Ricardo Corazón de León y su familia en la iglesia abacial, el imponente claustro, la sala capitular, el Gran Refectorio de la Abadía Real con los tan bien mesurados vitrales del artista contemporáneo François Rouan o las famosas cocinas románicas (a menudo llamadas bizantinas), sin duda uno de los elementos arquitectónicos más raros de Europa: una estructura de planta octogonal con múltiples chimeneas en forma de escamas que recuerdan al diseño oriental, utilizada originalmente para ahumar el pescado.

El refectorio del hotel Fontevraud. Nicolas Matheus

Llegados a este punto, liberado de preocupaciones (o al menos de ruido), el único problema es que hay wifi en la habitación —dentro de poco se pagará por lo contrario—, pero una vez activado el modo avión y apagada la luz, todo se aprecia en su justa medida.

World.title: Half of rental agents willing to exclude foreign tenants: study
World.content:
Almost half of rental agents contacted for a government-commissioned study were willing to discriminate against potential tenants with foreign roots, researchers have found.

The study, conducted by the Verwey-Jonker Institute, used actors posing as landlords to phone rental agents and ask them if they could avoid renting to “foreigners; Moroccans, Turks or Poles”.

They found that 97 out of 200 agreed outright with the request. Another 30% didn’t refuse, mostly saying it was up to the landlord, and only 20% said no.

“Expat” privileges

In 36 of the cases, agents distinguished “expats” as good foreign tenants, describing them as highly educated and well paid, with reliable employers. Some also said they tend to leave after a while, which they presented as a way around the 2024 ban on most temporary leases.

“Let me put your mind at rest, neither do we,” one agent told an actor who said they did not have a good feeling about foreigners. “The foreigners we usually talk about are the expats, who just come here to work for the big companies.”

Another said: “Officially we’re not allowed to discriminate, of course, but if you say you don’t want people from certain types of countries, I don’t need to put them forward to you.”

Moroccan-sounding names

In separate tests on 1,662 listings on the rental site Pararius between December and May, applicants with Moroccan-sounding names were invited to viewings less often than otherwise identical applicants with Dutch-sounding names.

For men, there were 14% of cases where only the Dutch-named applicant got an invitation, and 16% for women. Last year’s monitor found no significant discrimination against any group for the first time. The researchers found none this year against Polish-sounding names or same-sex couples.

Findings of the investigations were sent to MPs on Wednesday.

World.title: Back to class: cabinet seeks to train civil servants as teachers
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A majority of MPs are seeking to have soon-to-be-redundant civil servants at the education, culture and science ministry (OCW) retrained as teachers.

The VVD will bring the proposal, which also has the backing of political parties D66, CDA, JA21 and 50Plus, the to the cabinet Thursday.

VVD MP Arend Kisteman believes the plan will “kill two birds with one stone”.

“The announced cuts are a great opportunity to have these enthusiastic people voluntarily retrained for a job in education at the expense of the government,” Kisteman told broadcaster NOS.

The cabinet plans to eliminate 25,000 civil servants over the next nine years, a cut of some 16% by 2035. The OCW will not be spared.

Supporters say retraining already enthusiastic education workers as teachers will help alleviate chronic teacher shortages nationwide, especially in the country’s big cities.

But similar past initiatives have gotten low marks over schools’ reluctance to hire people with little to no classroom experience and civil servants’ reluctance to take salary cuts.

World.title: Disgruntled estate agents plan rival to property site Funda
World.content:
A group of disgruntled real estate brokers is starting a rival online real estate marketplace to the dominant Funda, saying it is “building a platform in which the broker is no longer a cash cow but is at the helm.”

The new platform, called Homek, is expected to launch in March 2027. For now, it’s appealing to brokers to join the platform, with RTL Z reporting that it won’t launch until at least 1,000 agents have bought in or the foundation has raised €1 million.

The increasing price of placing a property on Funda is one of the irritants that led the brokers to start the rival site.

“Homek is the fair, transparent alternative to Funda, without expensive packages or paid priority,” says Homek’s website, which currently doesn’t list any properties for sale or rent.

Only certified brokers affiliated with industry associations can use Homek, unlike Funda, where unaffiliated real estate agents who meet the site’s conditions can place properties.

Brokers on Homek will also share in the profits.

“The high placement costs and priority paid at Funda require an alternative: a housing platform where real estate agents themselves are in charge,” says Homek’s website. It promises “fair rates, equal opportunities and control for the affiliated brokers and offices.”

Supply problems

Funda was established in 2001 by the brokers’ association NVM.

“As brokers, we came up with Funda ourselves,” says Toine Naber, former chairman of the NVM branch in West-Brabant and a past member of Funda’s advisory board. “With Homek, we get the chance to do it again, but this time without giving away control of our own future.”

Sven Heinen, who is slated to be chairman of the Homek Foundation, told RTL Z he recognises that to become successful, Homek must have the goods to offer home buyers or renters.

“In the past, there have been plenty of competitors of Funda who wanted to take a piece of this market, but they all stalled because the supply was too limited,” Heinen says. “Only when many real estate agents join us and share their housing supply…can we become a serious competitor of Funda.”

Heinen says that within 48 hours, they’ve already raised €200,000.

Funda says it’s not worried about the competition for now. “In a healthy market, there is competition, and sometimes new players join,” spokesperson Claire Verhagen told RTL Z. “We look forward to that with confidence.”

World.title: Coalition parties ready to vote against each other on tax plans
World.content:
The ruling coalition parties have signalled they could vote against one another on amendments to the 2027 tax plan before parliament votes on it next week, after a debate that went ran late into Wednesday night.

Prime minister Rob Jetten’s centrist social-liberal D66 and the centrist Christian Democrat CDA said they could back opposition amendments even if their coalition partner, the right-wing liberal VVD, voted against them, broadcaster NOS reported.

“It is not an unthinkable situation,” D66 finance spokesman Henk-Jan Oosterhuis said after repeated questions from MPs. “The coalition is not a merger party.” CDA MP Inge van Dijk said split voting was “certainly not the intention” but did not rule it out.

Senate hurdle

The tax plan sets income tax rates and other levies for next year, and must be passed in time for the tax office to bring in the changes. If it fails, the cabinet will almost certainly fall, NRC reported.

Earlier this week the cabinet offered about €350 million in concessions to opposition parties on the left and right, which have formed rival blocs and demanded that the coalition choose between them.

The coalition holds 66 of the 150 seats in parliament. It now looks likely to win next week’s vote with the help of the ChristenUnie, 50PLUS and the group led by former PVV MP Gidi Markuszower. But that is not enough in the senate, where it needs the support of either Pro and Volt or the BBB.

Left-wing parties attacked the coalition for relying on Markuszower, after MPs, including the coalition parties, voted earlier this year against deals with politicians who call for violence against refugees. Markuszower had said Palestinian refugees should be stopped “with maximum violence”, the Volkskrant reported. Pro, Denk and the PvdD said extra police funding credited to him amounted to buying his support.

Oosterhuis said there was “no agreement” with Markuszower, but added: “If Mr Markuszower wants to support the tax plan, I am not going to ask him to vote against it.”

Wealth tax offer

The Pro and Volt alliance used the debate to table an amendment that would shift €1.5 billion of tax from workers to the wealthiest. Income tax would be lowered, paid for by a higher tax rate on the largest fortunes, higher tax on business owners’ income from their companies and an end to tax breaks on passing on family businesses.

The VVD’s Wendy van Eijk said it was “unthinkable” that any coalition party would back the proposal “in this form”, and that her party would not support higher taxes on wealth.

Parliament votes on each amendment before voting on the plan as a whole. That means the VVD could vote against a wealth tax rise but still back the final plan, if D66 and the CDA help the amendment through.

MPs vote on the tax plan on November 12, and the senate in the week before Christmas.

World.title: Sunny end to week, but near-freezing nights ahead
World.content:
Thursday and Friday will be sunny and dry across the Netherlands, but temperatures won’t rise past 10° and could drop close to freezing overnight, according to the KNMI forecast issued at 6am on Thursday.

The national weather institute KNMI said Thursday afternoon would bring plenty of sunshine, with a high of around 10°. Wind from the east will make it feel colder.

Thursday night will stay dry. Temperatures will fall to near freezing in the east, and stay at about 6° on the Wadden islands. Fog is possible in the far southwest.

Friday will be sunny and dry again. Highs will range from 8° in the far north to 12° in the southeast. Clouds will build in the southwest late in the afternoon.

Saturday may start with fog, mainly in the south and southwest, and some frost is possible inland, the KNMI said.

World.title: PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat
World.content:
PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

World.title: Police arrest “underground banker” in €60m money laundering case
World.content:
Police have arrested a 55-year-old man from Rotterdam on suspicion of handling around €60 million in cash for a Turkish-German crime gang that smuggled gold to Turkey.

The man, who was detained in Eindhoven, was one of five people arrested in raids on October 7, police said on Wednesday. The other four were held in Germany. Police describe him as a suspected “underground banker”, an illegal financial intermediary.

Around 500 Dutch and German police and German customs officers took part in the operation, which was carried out with the support of Europol. The investigation began in October 2023, when German traffic police found several kilos of gold and almost €500,000 in cash hidden in a car on a motorway.

Rotterdam seaport police raided two properties in Rotterdam and Eindhoven, seizing data storage devices, around €10,000 in cash, a vehicle and real estate.

German police seized property worth at least €2 million, along with 19 vehicles, around €100,000 in cash and a “large quantity” of scrap gold and silver bars.

Police say the group funnelled tens of millions of euros a year to Turkey, probably the proceeds of drug dealing. The money was used to buy old gold through friendly jewellers, which was melted into bars and then smuggled to Turkey. An estimated 1 to 4 tonnes of gold, worth €55 million to €210 million, was smuggled over six years.

World.title: Singles and young professionals embrace urban courtyard living
World.content:
With half of Dutch people reporting feelings of loneliness, developments like ZAAM in Zaandam are highlighting the many advantages of living in a lively, green urban courtyard, where residents can enjoy more contact with their neighbours.



Loneliness is rising worldwide, and is also prevalent in the Netherlands, where authorities say social isolation carries health risks. “Those who experience it are more prone to illness and depression and generally report lower levels of happiness,” says the government.

Such loneliness, combined with high home prices and rents in large cities, has led to different forms of living that increasingly appeal to digital nomads and home workers, singles and single-parent families looking for more social contact.

“There’s a lot of loneliness and fear in today’s world,” says the real estate team at ZAAM. “People are looking for more contact.”

For singles, young professionals and anyone looking for a home that combines city convenience with a pleasant living environment, ZAAM offers an alternative to city-centre apartment living in Amsterdam.

ZAAM: green city living with room to connect

ZAAM is a new residential development in the heart of Zaandam, featuring apartments across two distinctive buildings, De Werf and De Zagerij. At its centre is a large, green inner courtyard, creating a welcoming outdoor space where residents can relax, enjoy nature and meet their neighbours.

“ZAAM combines the privacy and comfort of your own apartment with the benefits of living in a green, lively courtyard. It offers a sense of space and community that can be hard to find in a city apartment,” says the ZAAM Real Estate Team.

The apartments range from 39 to 72 square metres and are designed with modern living in mind. Each has at least one bedroom, a bright living area, a modern bathroom and a private balcony or terrace. All apartments are single-level and accessible by lift, making everyday living comfortable and convenient.

The ground-floor apartments, which feature impressive 4.15-metre-high ceilings and direct access to the lush green courtyard, are designed to create an exceptional sense of space and a unique connection with the outdoors.

The development also places an emphasis on sustainability and energy efficiency. Homes are gas-free and feature underfloor heating and cooling through a modern thermal energy system. High energy efficiency also means potentially lower energy bills, the team says.

Two city centres within easy reach

One of ZAAM’s biggest advantages is its location. Situated directly next to Zaandam railway station, the development puts Amsterdam Central Station just 10 minutes away by train. Zaandam’s own lively town centre, with its shops, restaurants and cafés, is also within easy walking distance.

“You really get the best of both worlds: the character and convenience of Zaandam, with Amsterdam practically on your doorstep. You can enjoy a quieter, greener living environment without giving up the advantages of the capital,” says the ZAAM Real Estate Team.

For international residents and young professionals, the location is particularly convenient, with excellent public transport connections and easy access to Amsterdam and the surrounding region.

And while the city is close, ZAAM is meant to offer a welcome change of pace. The green courtyard, private outdoor spaces and thoughtful apartment layouts create a comfortable home environment away from the bustle of the city.

Your new home before the end of the year

With construction nearing completion, the vast majority of ZAAM’s apartments have already been sold. Just a handful of homes remain available, including some ground-floor apartments.

Buyers benefit from the advantages of new-build living: modern materials and appliances, energy-efficient installations, well-designed layouts and the reassurance of a brand-new home. Selected larger apartments also offer extra flexibility, with space for a home office, walk-in wardrobe or additional storage.

Parking spaces are also available for purchase with most apartments – a valuable extra in an area where parking can be a challenge.

You also won’t have to wait years to move in. Completion is planned for late 2026, meaning buyers can look forward to moving into their new home before the end of this year.

Only a limited number of apartments remain available, so anyone interested in securing a home at ZAAM is encouraged to get in touch soon.

Discover the remaining apartments at ZAAM and book your viewing today.

World.title: Polish far-right leader Braun to face second trial
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun will again stand trial, after prosecutors filed an indictment against him for a series of anti-Ukrainian, anti-Jewish, anti-LGBT and anti-EU acts committed during his presidential election campaign last year. Braun is already separately on trial for a number of other alleged crimes, including an attack on a Jewish religious ceremony in parliament. He is also facing further charges for a range of other alleged offences. Grzegorz Braun stanie przed sądem. Prokuratura Okręgowa w Warszawie skierowała dziś akt oskarżenia za zuchwałą kradzież flag Ukrainy w Białej Podlaskiej i Unii Europejskiej w Katowicach, zniszczenie wystawy LGBT w Sejmie oraz zniesławienie organizatorów akcji Żonkile i Muzeum… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 4, 2026 On Wednesday, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw announced that it had indicted Braun for four alleged crimes. It was able to do so after the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, stripped him of immunity earlier this year. One of the charges, for criminal defamation, stems from Braun’s claim, during a televised presidential debate in April last year, that the yellow paper daffodils distributed each year in Warsaw to mark the anniversary of the 1943 Jewish Ghetto Uprising against German Nazi rule are “symbols of shame”. Prosecutors say that Braun’s words were “extremely xenophobic, manipulative and aggressive”, and that they defamed the organisers of the daffodil campaign, in particular the POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews in Warsaw. During the same debate, Braun also warned about the “Judaisation” of Poland, saying that “Jews have far too much say in Polish affairs”. That prompted protests by some of his opponents, one of whom filed a notification to prosecutors. Two other charges relate to thefts of flags. In one incident, Braun and his supporters removed a Ukrainian flag hanging outside city hall in the town of Biała Podlaska during a campaign event. In another, he removed a European Union flag from the industry ministry in the city of Katowice and set it on fire. Braun regularly rails against what he calls the “Ukrainisation” of Poland, warning of the supposed dangers of having so many Ukrainian refugees and migrants in the country. He is also a vocal critic of the EU. On those and other issues, Braun’s rhetoric often echoes Russian propaganda. The final charge, of destruction of property, relates to an incident in June 2025, when Braun vandalised an exhibition about the LGBT+ community in the Polish parliament. He regularly condemns what he calls the “perversions” of LGBT+ people, and has called for homosexuality to be criminalised. The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes. The decision marks the sixth time it has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial https://t.co/O9FN1YbchE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 The charges Braun faces carry prison sentences of up to five years in the case of destruction of property, and up to one year in the case of criminal defamation and theft. Additionally, the deputy leader of Braun’s Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party, Roman Fritz, was indicted for assisting in the theft of the EU flag, while four other men (who have not waived their right to anonymity under Polish law) were indicted for their alleged roles in stealing both the EU and Ukrainian flags. All four incidents for which Braun has been indicted took place when he was campaigning for the May 2025 presidential elections, in which he finished a surprise fourth, with 6.3% of the vote. Since then, KKP has continued to perform strongly in polls, with its support currently standing at around 9%. If it obtained that kind of result at next year’s parliamentary elections, it would be likely to play a major role in deciding what kind of government could be formed. Our essential guide to Poland's parliamentary elections, which will take place one year from now. How does voting work? What do polls suggest the outcome will be? Which issues may animate the campaign? And what role will President Nawrocki play? https://t.co/fmdoFpBaxz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2026 Much of Braun’s political brand has been built around provocative statements and actions. The politician is already on trial for his attack on a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony taking place in parliament, at which he put out the candles with a fire extinguisher. In their statement on Wednesday, the Warsaw prosecutor’s office noted that the latest hearings in that trial had been cancelled after Braun presented a medical certificate justifying his absence. However, the prosecutors pointed out that, last Friday, the day that the hearings had been due to begin, Braun attended a protest by opposition supporters outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw, which that evening had been taken over by government-backed judges. Braun was pictured “jostling with police riot police, addressing the crowd and giving interviews”, showing “no signs of health problems that would prevent him from attending the hearing”, wrote the prosecutors. They have therefore asked the court to investigate the doctor who issued the medical certificate. World.title: “Democracy won in America”: Polish leaders react to US midterm election results

Polish political leaders have reacted to the results of Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which the Democrats won control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans. The outcome was welcomed by Poland’s ruling coalition, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk declaring that “democracy won”. The response was more muted from the right-wing opposition and the office of conservative President Karol Nawrocki, who is a Trump ally. 🚨 🇺🇸 Tusk gives Trump some great advice. But will the US president listen? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged the US president to seek compromises after the Republicans' defeat and not to rely on vetoes as his main way of governing. Trump had earlier threatened to become… pic.twitter.com/s3E6G5zIQT — NEXTA (@nexta_tv) November 4, 2026 Tusk addressed the election results on Wednesday afternoon local time at a press conference alongside his Czech counterpart, Andrej Babiš. “Today, democracy won in America,” said a smiling Tusk. “I love democracy; it is a beautiful thing.” “As President Donald Trump himself said just after the election, the Democrats did a good job, and I really could not agree more with him this time,” added Tusk. “I hope that the result will stabilise the situation also in our region.” Although the United States remains Poland’s most important security partner, Tusk’s government – a broad, pro-EU coalition that ranges from left to centre right – has at times had uneasy relations with the Trump administration. It has been critical of Trump’s conciliatory approach towards Russia, his often tough stance on Ukraine, as well as his pursuit of US control over Greenland. Meanwhile, the head of the parliamentary caucus of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, Zbigniew Konwiński, told broadcaster Polsat News that “personally, I was happy with the Democrats’ victory”. “We know how Donald Trump behaves, how volatile he is in his political declarations, how he can sometimes put Ukraine in a more difficult position than Russia, so I would rather look for the positives in what happened,” said Konwiński. “If we look at recent years, the more Democrats, the stronger the Democrats, the better for Poland,” he added. .@Konwinski_PO: Cieszę się z wygranej Demokratów w USA, bo to lepszy scenariusz dla Polski. @marcinfijolek pic.twitter.com/gJ3TnlMn0l — Graffiti_PN (@Graffiti_PN) November 4, 2026 The speaker of Poland’s parliament, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is also the leader of one of KO’s junior coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), has clashed with the US ambassador to Poland twice this year over Czarzasty’s criticism of Trump. Today, Czarzasty shared and commented on a social media post by Trump, published in the wake of the Democrats’ victory, in which the US president showed an image of his signature red cap with the word “VETO” on it. “Where have I heard this before?” wrote Czarzasty, referring to the fact that Nawrocki has vetoed a record number of bills passed by parliament, where Tusk’s coalition has a majority. Czarzasty then went on to list a series of characteristics that he suggested both Trump and Nawrocki share, including “arrogance”, “lack of respect for women”, a “suspicious past”, “transactional exploitation of their position”, and “admiration for politicians with fascist tendencies”. Skąd ja to znam? Arogancja. Buta. Nieuzasadniona pewność siebie. Brak szacunku dla kobiet ( a to popchnę jakąś dwojga nazwisk, a to zakpię prymitywnie). Dziwna przeszłość. Instrumentalne traktowanie dziennikarzy. Pieniądze za spotkania. Transakcyjne wykorzystywanie funkcji.… pic.twitter.com/ryT2BMOZb2 — Włodzimierz Czarzasty 📚📖 (@wlodekczarzasty) November 4, 2026 Nawrocki has closely aligned himself with Trump. During last year’s Polish presidential election campaign, Trump invited Nawrocki for a private meeting at the White House. His then-homeland security secretary, Kristi Noem, visited Poland to endorse Nawrocki. Nawrocki himself has not thus far commented on Tuesday’s midterm election results. However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the president’s International Policy Bureau, did address the issue in a social media post. “As predicted, in the US midterm elections voters decided on change,” wrote Przydacz. “Poland will continue its good cooperation with the US, because it is our ally, and collaboration is in our mutual interest.” Przydacz also added that the results were “a reminder for Tusk” that “no government lasts forever”. In Poland, too, “the moment will come when voters will decide on change – and it might be quite soon”, added Przydacz, in a nod to next year’s Polish parliamentary elections. Zgodnie z przewidywaniami w wyborach połówkowych w USA wyborcy zdecydowali o zmianie. Wcześniej wygrywali Republikanie, dziś Demokraci. Polska będzie kontynuować dobrą współpracę z USA, bo jest to nasz sojusznik, a kooperacja jest w naszym wspólnym interesie. O tym, kto sprawuje… — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) November 4, 2026 Tusk’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, meanwhile, used the US election results to revive his long-running feud with Elon Musk, who is no longer part of the Trump administration but donated enormous amounts of money to support the Republicans ahead of the midterms. Last year, Musk and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticised Sikorski after he suggested that Musk had threatened Ukraine. In a post on his social media platform, X, Musk told Sikorski to “be quiet, small man”. On Wednesday, Tusk shared a screenshot of a tweet he had published last year, after Musk left the Trump administration, in which Sikorski wrote: “See, big man, politics is harder than you thought.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: International Commission of Jurists criticises takeover of Polish constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) has criticised the takeover of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) by a group of government-backed judges. It says that the move “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary”. However, the ICJ, a Swiss-based NGO led by judges, lawyers and academics from around the world, also chastised Poland’s opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, for his role in the crisis surrounding the TK, in particular his refusal to swear in judges elected by parliament. 🚨#Poland’s constitutional crisis must be resolved through the rule of law. The ICJ urges all authorities to respect judicial independence, follow lawful procedures, and comply with European court rulings. 🔗More information: https://t.co/NWmca9mpUx — ICJ (@ICJ_org) November 3, 2026 On Friday, eight judges who were elected to the TK this year by the government’s parliamentary majority effectively took over the tribunal. They announced that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been suspended for failing to properly fulfil their duties. Meanwhile, large numbers of riot police were deployed outside the court, holding back protesters, including opposition politicians, and preventing Święczkowski and Sochański from entering the grounds. Święczkowski denounced the takeover of the court as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the tribunal’s remaining six judges, who, like him, were appointed under the rule of the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which brought the TK under its political influence. Nawrocki has likewise denounced the actions of the government-backed judges. In the early hours of Saturday, he dramatically forced his way into the court, where he clashed physically and verbally with the judges who had taken over the TK. During a visit to the Constitutional Tribunal last night, President Nawrocki clashed physically and verbally with judges involved in an attempt to take control of the court. The president is today seeking talks with political leaders to discuss the crisis https://t.co/7HmBnuIaDG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 31, 2026 In a statement on Tuesday, the ICJ expressed regret that the latest developments have “deepened the crisis over the tribunal”. It called on Polish “state institutions to seek solutions…that comply fully with the rule of law, including the principle of the independence of the judiciary”. The ICJ’s secretary-general, Santiago Canton, noted that Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of the eight TK judges elected by parliament this year. That “violates international standards and is contrary to the interim measures indicated by the European Court of Human Rights”, said Canton. In May, the ECHR issued an interim order for all judges elected by parliament to be allowed to serve on the court. However, that has been ignored by Nawrocki and Święczkowski, who argued that the ECHR does not have the authority to make such a decision. The ICJ also noted that the roots of the crisis at the TK date back a decade, to the time when the PiS government took actions – including unlawfully appointing judges to the tribunal – that rendered the court illegitimate. “At the same time,” continued Canton, “the suspension of the president and vice-president of the tribunal without a fair and appropriate procedure established by law, carried out with the involvement of the police, contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary.” In its statement, the ICJ added that “criminal and disciplinary proceedings must respect all the guarantees of a fair trial and must never be used as a means to change [a court’s] composition”. Later on Tuesday, after the ICJ had issued its statement, the eight government-backed judges held their first general assembly, at which they moved forward with disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski and Sochański. The justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, has also submitted six requests to the TK to lift Święczkowski’s immunity from prosecution so that he can face charges for a range of alleged crimes relating to both his time as chief justice and his previous role as a senior prosecutor under the PiS government. Skierowałem do Trybunału Konstytucyjnego kolejny, szósty już wniosek o uchylenie immunitetu Bogdanowi Święczkowskiemu, dołączając go do pięciu wniosków przekazanych w piątek. Dzisiejsza sprawa dotyczy zakupu systemu szpiegowskiego Hermes w czasie, gdy pełnił funkcję Prokuratora… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 3, 2026 The takeover of the TK has also stirred controversy among Polish legal experts. The issue has even caused an unprecedented split at the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights (HFPC), a well-respected NGO. On Saturday, the HFPC’s management board issued a statement, signed by its president, Maciej Nowicki, saying that it “sees no clear legal basis” for the actions taken on Friday by the government-backed judges to suspend Święczkowski and take control of the tribunal. It warned that the situation “set a dangerous precedent” and “does not contribute to fixing the tribunal”. However, HFPC also made it clear that the crisis at the court dates back a decade and reiterated its view that Nawrocki “has no right to block or invalidate the election [of judges] by parliament”. That statement prompted six of the eight members of HFPC’s council – a separate body from the management board – to resign. Those to depart included a former chief justice of the TK, Andrzej Rzepliński, and a former deputy human rights commissioner, Hanna Machińska. Machińska announced their resignation in a social media post. She said that the reason for her decision had been the management board’s statement, “with which I disagree”. Speaking later to broadcaster TVN, Machińska said that “we believe that the legal basis [for the TK takeover] was clearly defined”. Poland’s government, including Prime Minister Donald Tusk, has also argued that the takeover of the tribunal was necessary to ensure that legally appointed judges can take up their seats and that the court’s legitimacy can be restored. However, on Tuesday evening, Tusk shifted to a more conciliatory tone, offering to hold a one-on-one meeting with Nawrocki to discuss the crisis around the Constitutional Tribunal and “try to find solutions that will protect Poland from any political upheaval”. The group of eight government-backed judges who last week took control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have held a meeting at which they made a number of key decisions, including moving forward with disciplinary proceedings against the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski. However, the situation is mired in controversy and uncertainty. Święczkowski and the opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, do not recognise the judges who are now claiming control of the court, describing their actions as a “coup d’état”. Meanwhile, there are doubts as to whether today’s general assembly even had a valid quorum, given that the chief justice and six other judges appointed under the former government did not attend. PILNE: Zgromadzenie Ogólne Sędziów TK przyjęło, że kworum to osiem osóbhttps://t.co/SYEf9Ead3L — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 3, 2026 The meeting was called by Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who on Friday declared that Święczkowski and the deputy chief justice, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been suspended for failing to fulfil their duties. Korwin-Piotrowska said that she herself, as the longest-serving judge on the court, was taking control. Large numbers of riot police were deployed outside the court, holding back protesters, including opposition politicians, and preventing Święczkowski and Sochański from entering the court. However, Nawrocki himself did enter the premises, where he clashed physically and verbally with Korwin-Piotrowska. For a general assembly of the TK to be valid, two thirds of the court’s judges need to be present. Normally, given that the tribunal has 15 positions, that would mean at least 10 judges being present. However, only eight judges attended today’s meeting. They were all appointed to the TK by the government’s parliamentary majority this year. But Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of them, meaning that their legal status has become disputed. The TK’s seven other judges, including Święczkowski and Sochański, were all appointed to the court under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under its political control, including by unlawfully appointing three judges. None of them attended Tuesday’s general assembly. Nevertheless, the eight judges present at the meeting, which was broadcast live for the first time in the TK’s history, decided that a quorum had been reached. They did so on the basis that three of the TK’s judges were not authorised to attend: Święczkowski and Sochański, because they are suspended, and Jarosław Wyrembak, because he inherited his position from one of PiS’s unlawfully appointed judges. That meant only 12 judges were authorised to attend, and two thirds of that number is eight, meaning that a quorum had been reached. Zgromadzenie Ogólne TK: JEST KWORUM! 👏 Według przedstawionej interpretacji liczy się je od 12 uprawnionych osób. 2/3 × 12 = 8. Prawo i matematyka.👏 pic.twitter.com/77v2ep9HbT — Pani Prezes 👠 (@PaniNaSzpilkach) November 3, 2026 Once that issue was agreed, the eight judges present proceeded to decide upon a number of key issues. First, they adopted a draft budget for the TK for 2027, something that Święczkowski had been unable to achieve, which was used as an argument for his ousting. Second, they drew lots to decide which of the TK’s judges would sit on disciplinary panels for Święczkowski and Sochański in relation to their suspension from the court. However, some legal experts have expressed doubt as to whether a legal quorum was established at today’s meeting. Ryszard Piotrowski, a prominent constitutional scholar, called the meeting “illegal”, reports news website Onet. Przemysław Rosati, the president of the Supreme Bar Council, also expressed his doubts. Obniżenie progu kworum na skutek zawieszenia prezesa i wiceprezesa otwiera puszkę Pandory. To jest mechanizm, który pozwala dowolnie obniżać kworum na Zgromadzeniu Ogólnym TK – wystarczy, że prezes zawiesi 10 sędziów i będzie mógł na Zgromadzeniu podejmować decyzję w trzy osoby.… — Marcin Matczak (@wsamraz) November 3, 2026 Święczkowski himself rejected the legitimacy of what he called a “social gathering”, saying that Korwin-Piotrowska is a “usurper” who has no right to call a general assembly at all, reported Polsat News. Shortly before the meeting at the TK, Nawrocki also met with the prime minister, Donald Tusk, for the first time since the crisis at the court broke out last Friday. They had convened at the presidential palace for a meeting of the National Security Council that Nawrocki had called before the TK crisis. During public remarks broadcast before the confidential meeting got underway, Nawrocki accused the government of “illegally taking over the Constitutional Tribunal”. He added that Tusk “bears full responsibility for…all these illegal actions”. Grubo! Karol Nawrocki do Tuska: „Pełną odpowiedzialność za wszystkie nielegalne działa w Trybunale Konstytucyjnym ponosi jeden człowiek, który jest obecny – premier Donald Tusk” pic.twitter.com/WMPnWTZIKt — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) November 3, 2026 Tusk and his government have argued that the source of the crisis is, in fact, Nawrocki’s refusal to swear in judges appointed by parliament, as he is required to do, and then Święczkowski’s resultant refusal to accept those judges onto the court. They also note that the TK has not been legitimate for a decade, since PiS unlawfully appointed judges and brought the court under its political influence. Speaking to broadcaster TVN on Tuesday before the general assembly, justice minister Waldemar Żurek said that the actions being undertaken by Korwin-Piotrowska are the only way “to rebuild the independence of the tribunal”. World.title: Poland has EU’s second-highest electricity prices accounting for cost of living
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland had the second-highest household electricity prices in the European Union in the first half of 2026 after adjusting for differences in the cost of living, new Eurostat data show. Prices in Poland were also among the fastest-rising in the bloc. Poland’s relatively high electricity costs reflect the country’s continued reliance on coal, which results in EU charges for carbon emissions, and its taxes and levies, which make up the largest share of household electricity bills anywhere in the EU. In nominal terms, Polish households paid €29.99 per 100 kilowatt-hours (kWh) for electricity in the first half of 2026. This was the seventh-highest price among the EU’s 27 member states and above the bloc-wide average of €28.32. Ireland (€38.71 per 100 kWh) had the highest prices, followed by Germany (€36.18) and Belgium (€35.75). The lowest costs were recorded in Hungary (€11.39), Malta (€12.68) and Bulgaria (€13.41). However, when adjusted for purchasing power standards (PPS), which account for differences in the cost of living, Poland ranked second in the EU, at 41.12 PPS per 100 kWh. Only Romania had higher prices, at 46.89 PPS. The lowest prices when measured in PPS were recorded in Malta (13.75), Hungary (14.7) and Luxembourg (15.47). Poland’s electricity prices, in PPS terms, rose by 10.7% compared with the second half of 2025, which was the second-biggest increase in the EU after Finland. They were also up 17.6% compared to the first half of 2025, the fourth-largest rise in the bloc. One reason why electricity prices in Poland remain high is the country’s continued reliance on coal, which last year generated just over half of power, by far the highest proportion in the EU. Almost all coal used in Polish power plants is mined domestically and is among the most expensive in the world to extract. Additionally, burning it also produces high carbon emissions, which power generators must pay for under the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS). These costs contribute to the high taxes and levies included in household electricity bills, which accounted for 39% of the final price in Poland in the first half of 2026. This was the highest share in the EU, ahead of Germany (23.6%) and well above the bloc-wide average of 18.6%. “In Poland, only one-third of our electricity generation is carbon-free. We have to pay for the rest – often dearly,” noted Polish energy journalist Jakub Wiech, commenting on the data. Without taxes and levies, the nominal price of electricity in Poland would have been just under €16 per 100 kWh, below the EU average of €20.27. However, Bartłomiej Orzeł of the Project Tempo think tank notes that electricity prices in Poland would, in fact, be even higher were it not for the huge state subsidies paid to support the unprofitable coal mining sector, which amount to billions of zloty a year but also shield end consumers from the full cost of extracting coal. He told news website Interia that mines actually sell coal to power stations at a price below the cost of extraction. Poland will from next month be the last remaining EU country still mining hard coal, after the Czech Republic – the only other producer – announced the closure of its last mine https://t.co/0sfMDQb19N — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 30, 2026 According to Wiech, the high tax burden also reflects the costs of transforming Poland’s energy sector while continuing to support coal-fired power stations and the state budget. He says Poland needs “on the one hand, to fund the accelerated but delayed transformation and modernisation of the electricity sector; on the other hand, to maintain the fleet of coal-fired power stations; and thirdly, to contribute to the state budget”, which is struggling with persistently high deficits. Wiech expects, however, that politicians will come under pressure to reduce electricity bills ahead of next year’s parliamentary election. He says they may be tempted to “interfere with electricity bills” and that “it is therefore quite likely that certain charges (e.g. the distribution charge) will be reduced in 2027”. Komisja Europejska wrzuciła dane o cenach prądu za I półrocze 2026 roku i – boy, oh, boy – niesamowita jest to lektura. Na początek mocne uderzenie: w ujęciu standardu siły nabywczej polskie gospodarstwa domowe mają drugie najwyższe ceny prądu w całej Unii Europejskiej.… pic.twitter.com/yKvt5251i7 — Jakub Wiech (@jakubwiech) November 1, 2026 Energy prices and the wider energy transition have already become increasingly politicised this year, with the right-wing opposition criticising EU climate policies. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), the largest opposition party, recently called for Poland to unilaterally withdraw from ETS, claiming that it treats “Poles as a cash machine for the absurd leftist climate policy of the EU”. Opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has twice attempted to call national referendums on rejecting EU climate policy, but in both cases his proposals were rejected by the more pro-EU government’s majority in parliament. Poland's right-wing opposition wants to withdraw from the EU Emissions Trading System, saying it makes Poles "a cash machine for absurd leftist climate policies"@PStrzalkowski explains what costs ETS really brings, and what prospects there are for reform https://t.co/UxpMWpG1pE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 4, 2026 However, when PiS was in power from 2015 to 2023, it recognised the need to move Poland away from coal and towards a mix of renewables and nuclear. Solar energy installations boomed under the PiS government, and the overall share of renewables in the energy mix rose from around 9% in 2015 to a record 29% in 2024. The current government has continued with PiS’s plans to shift towards nuclear and renwables. This year, Poland’s first offshore wind farm in the Baltic Sea began generating electricity, with a number of other offshore projects set to follow. Poland’s national energy and climate plan, approved in June, envisages coal accounting for 0-5% of the energy mix by 2040. Around 15-16% will come from nuclear, 7-8% from gas, with most of the rest from renewables: onshore wind (22-27%), offshore wind (18-21%) and solar (14-18%).
