World.title: Czech Foreign Policy Under Babis: A Shift in Tone But in What Direction?
World.content:
Expectations vs reality

Before and immediately after the 2025 general election, concerns were raised that a government including the far right (or far left, which ultimately didn’t win enough votes to make it into the Chamber of Deputies) means the country would move further away from the unequivocally pro-Western foreign policy of the previous government of Petr Fiala.

While the idea of an outright Viktor Orban-style turn towards Russia was never seriously entertained, major disruption to how Czech foreign policy is carried out and what its priorities are had been a clear ambition of both the SPD and Motorists during the election campaign.

This scenario has, to a large extent, played out. The Motorists, whose chairman Petr Macinka has taken the reins at the Foreign Ministry, indulge in culture-war politics, including personnel reorganisations and effectively defunding human rights and democratisation support programs – a key pillar of the post-1993 Czech foreign policy, alongside development aid and humanitarian policies in general. The party has also escalated its conflict with the more liberal President Petr Pavel.

Meanwhile, the SPD’s influence on the substance of actual policies has been limited, though this has not prevented them from spreading anti-Ukrainian vitriol through public channels and trying to prevent any assistance from getting to Ukraine.

Babis’s catch-all ANO caters to a lukewarm centrism, keeping the voter base happy by avoiding costly international commitments, passively enabling some of the radical ideological excesses of its junior partners as the necessary price of keeping the coalition alive.

These dynamics – the different foreign policy preferences of the coalition partners, except for the shared Euroscepticism; the shared low priority attached to external affairs; and the catch-all ANO at the steering wheel – is resulting in what could be best described as a “Euro-Atlanticism by inertia”. Czechia is aligned with the West by following the current momentum, without active strategy or particular enthusiasm. The government embraces zero-cost postures while hesitating or outright refusing to expend real resources or political capital.

Membership of the EU and NATO is considered non-negotiable and questioning it is verboten (despite the SPD’s preferences). At the same time, the percentage of GDP spent by Czechia on defence is among the lowest among the alliance members, with no ambition for a substantive increase. The prime minister’s financial conflicts of interest have the potential to sour relations between Prague and EU institutions, together with potential rule-of-law breaches (an anti-NGO law, the independence of the public service media, and autonomy of civil servants).

The government’s attitude to Ukraine is not outright frosty, rather lukewarm. Despite the SPD’s rhetoric, the government as a whole does not challenge the designation of Russia as the aggressor in the war. A return to buying Russian energy sources is not, at the moment, on the table. Ukraine’s defence and its importance for Czechia has not been actively emphasised as a key issue, however. Aid has been reduced as part of the general cuts mentioned above. The ammunition initiative of the previous government has remained, though Czechia does not contribute any funds. It also refused to participate in the EU-wide loan to Ukraine at the end of 2025, and is likely to do so again for another 45-billion-euro support package currently being negotiated for the end of this year. This ambivalent approach is likely to stay for the rest of the coalition’s term in office.

The announced paradigmatic shift of Czech foreign policy from a focus on promoting values towards one of pragmatism, embodied by “economic diplomacy”, is a general idea rather than a thought-through strategy, plan or clear goal. Furthermore, pure economic diplomacy makes little sense in an era of geopolitical fragmentation and trade securitisation. Thinking about one’s own security without considering values is, in turn, preposterous.

An issue where the coalition’s stance is, on the other hand, very clear – and remarkably similar to that of its predecessor – is the strong bilateral relationship with Israel, which is rather a non-issue in the Czech political sphere and, again, bears no significant political cost.

Similarly, cooperation between the Visegrad Group (V4) of countries has been portrayed as a priority, but so far remains stuck at the rhetorical level, without any real successes (except for a broad agreement on the EU’s next multi-year budget or on migration). The future success of a revived V4 is by no means guaranteed, given the differences in threat perceptions and strategic outlooks among the four countries (Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia), as well as the impact of domestic election cycles.

World.title: French Election Could Stymie EU Enlargement into Balkans
World.content:
Over a decade on from the Brexit referendum, the EU appears to be on the verge of adding a new member. Montenegro has raced to the front of the pack, provisionally closing a number of negotiating chapters. “28 by 28” is Podgorica’s motto.

Yet for all the talk in Brussels of renewed enlargement momentum, it is the EU member states that hold the keys to the door, and France has long been sceptical about an expanded union. This is not least because any ratification process would inevitably involve going to the people, the fragmentation of its politics making a three-fifths supermajority highly unlikely.

Whilst Montenegro is a relatively easy country to absorb, making fewer demands on the EU’s budget, such a referendum would inevitably become a debate not about the issue at hand – i.e. the accession of one country – but the imminent membership of other candidate countries, such as Ukraine or Turkey, the latter having been misused by Brexit campaigners despite its accession process being essentially dead. There is little appetite for such a vote, especially given France’s polarised political environment.

World.title: Albanian Prosecution Urged to Probe PM’s Alleged Blackmail of Jailed Mayor
World.content:
The abrupt transfer of jailed Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj to Fier prison last week brought to the surface a conflict between him and Prime Minister Edi Rama that extends beyond the fate of Tirana Municipality.

Through his lawyer, Plarent Ndreca, and letters sent from prison, Veliaj alleges that Rama personally orchestrated his punishment by ordering his transfer to Fier and is now blackmailing him into resigning as mayor through an alleged message delivered to the prison by Justice Minister Toni Gogu.

Veliaj says he met Gogu in prison late on Friday evening when the minister allegedly conveyed a demand from Rama that he both resign and admit to having been involved in the so-called “Flamingo” protests against the government – and drop his lawyer, Plarent Ndreca, a former Socialist MP who has sided with the jailed mayor.

Otherwise, Veliaj claims, he would face additional criminal charges.

“I reject the Bolshevik hallucinations that I organised or financed the protests… I challenge the Prime Minister to produce a single piece of evidence to support the allegations about the protests. Otherwise, get lost!” Veliaj wrote, referring to the students’ protests that have rocked Tirana and prompted a heavy police response with arrests, tear gas and rubber bullets.

World.title: EU Hails Montenegro’s Progress – Regrets Stagnation in Much of Balkans
World.content:
The European Commission’s annual Enlargement Package, its report on the progress of EU candidate countries, on Wednesday introduced accession roadmaps for Montenegro and Albania, while criticising a lack of progress towards EU integration in other Western Balkan countries.

“Membership is moving closer for countries that deliver. For the first time, we introduce roadmaps for accession negotiations with Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine,” Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, said during the launch in Brussels.

“Montenegro is the closest to the finish line with a clear path to signing the accession treaty by next summer,” Kallas added.

Marta Kos, European Commissioner for Enlargement, highlighted that, “for the first time since 2011, when the EU closed accession negotiations with Croatia, we are in a position to close accession negotiations with another candidate country”, referring to Montenegro, adding: “The country has already closed 21 negotiating chapters; 14 to go.”

Albania’s Prime Minister, Edi Rama, praised the report, describing it as “another step forward toward the historic goal of uniting with Europe.

“This assessment does not diminish the significance or the urgency of the challenges in the country’s daily life – issues that have received, continue to receive, and will continue to receive the full attention of myself, the government, and the parliamentary majority. On the contrary, the high praise in today’s report motivates us to do even more and to perform even better,” he said.

Serbia was described as having a high level of alignment with EU laws but Kos warned that, “in Serbia, we have seen backsliding across the fundamentals. The new government will have the chance to reverse the course”, referencing recent elections that ousted the long-ruling Serbian Progressive Party.

The country had “made further steps backwards on fundamental rights, in particular in the freedom of expression, public administration, and academic freedom” she noted.

Bosnia and Herzegovina made no progress in key areas of EU integration, including the judiciary, the fight against corruption, media freedom and the economy, while its visa policy has regressed, the Commission said.

The report, covering September 2025 to September 2026, described Bosnia’s growing political instability, weak institutions and state capture, noting that most of the recommendations from last year remain unimplemented.

The Commission also urged Bosnia to align its visa policy with the EU, warning that visa-free arrangements with seven countries could increase irregular migration risks.

North Macedonia was also criticised for failure on EU-related reforms, singling out the lack of progress in fighting corruption, media freedom and judicial independence, while noting that constitutional changes required to advance accession negotiations remain untouched.

Bulgaria has blocked North Macedonia’s EU accession path over disputes concerning history, language and national identity. Although Sofia formally lifted its veto in 2022 following a French-brokered compromise, North Macedonia’s commitment to include Bulgarians among its constitutive peoples in its Constitution remains unfulfilled, leaving the country’s accession process effectively stalled.

In Kosovo, an almost two-year institutional blockade halted the implementation of EU-related reforms, and the country has made only limited progress in key areas, with political instability, a lack of judicial independence, and shortcomings in the fight against corruption.

Kos noted that “Kosovo has recently intensified the implementation of the reform agenda. The EU has welcomed the election of the new president and we hope that the renewed institutional stability will enable Kosovo to progress”. Because of the two-year political crisis, Kosovo risks losing more than 40 million euros in EU growth plan funds after missing the June 2026 implementation deadline.

The Commission’s 2026 Turkey Report painted a bleak picture. It said that “democratic backsliding continued, particularly in the areas of political pluralism, integrity of electoral process, the rule of law and local governance”, amid intensified judicial pressure on opposition politicians and parties.

The report highlighted the continued detention and prosecution of opposition politicians in Turkey, including Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, the annulment of the opposition Republican People’s Party’s 2023 congress, and government pressure on independent media and critics.

Turkey started EU accession negotiations in 2005, but its membership bid has been practically frozen amid international deadlocks and democratic backsliding.

World.title: Greek American Becomes First Openly Gay US Senator
World.content:
Chris Pappas. Photo: Chris Pappas/Facebook

Greek-American Chris Pappas, a Democratic Party candidate, made history as the first openly gay man elected to the US Senate, representing New Hampshire. “Tonight is a victory for everyone,” he wrote on X on November 4.

“For the last 579 days, we’ve taken this campaign to every corner of New Hampshire. Every one of those days has brought me closer to the people who make this state so special,” he added in another post.

Pappas, 46, was elected in the US midterms on November 3 with 56.20 per cent of votes cast, defeating Republican rival John Sununu in the New England state.

The US midterms have turned into a rout for President Donald Trump’s Republicans who lost control of both houses of Congress amid massive swings to the Democrats triggered partly by discontent over rising prices and the Iran war.

Pappas has served in the House of Representatives as a Democrat since 2019.

Born and raised in Manchester, he is of Greek descent, with roots in Livadi, a village in Thessaly. His paternal great-grandfather arrived in New Hampshire in the early 20th century.

“I stand on the shoulders of my ancestors who came to this country to build a life. They started a small business over 100 years ago and I am the recipient of their journey, their struggle, and their hard work,” he said in an interview on Greek TV on November 2.

“I am also blessed that they have bequeathed to me their traditions, their faith, and their involvement in the local community here. And so I think about their example every day. And I try to show the best of what Hellenism represents and the best of what my ancestors reflected throughout their lives and their journey,” he added.

Papas attended Manchester Central High School, and, after graduation in 1998, studied at Harvard College. He then worked in his family’s 106-year-old restaurant in New Hampshire.

Before serving in Congress, he represented District 4 on the New Hampshire Executive Council. When he was elected to the US House in 2018, he became New Hampshire’s first openly gay member of Congress.

His page for his candidacy reported that in Congress he fought for tax cuts for working families and small businesses, and for “cracking down on predatory companies that target veterans and pollute our water, and standing up to Big Pharma to lower drug costs”.

Pappas is married to his husband, Vann.

World.title: Kosovo Identifies Three More Wartime Missing Persons
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Excavations in the village of Kalluder in Zubin Potok of a mass grave, July 30, 2026. Photo: BIRN

Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti confirmed on Tuesday that three more victims of enforced disappearance during the Kosovo 1998-99 war were identified following DNA analysis carried out in the Hague.Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti confirmed on Tuesday that three more victims of enforced disappearance during the Kosovo 1998-99 war were identified following DNA analysis carried out in the Hague.

“Following initial identifications from remains exhumed in Kalluder and Jabuke (villages near Zubin Potok in north Kosovo), the Government Commission on Missing Persons has received new DNA reports confirming the identities of Adem (Fazli) Ademi, Fatmir (Bajram) Fazlija and Ali (Islam) Haliti,” Kurti wrote on Facebook.

Kurti said the families had been notified. The three men were amongst missing Kosovo Albanian intellectuals “who were abducted by Serbian armed forces in April 1999 and subsequently subjected to enforced disappearance”, Kurti explained.

He added that the effort to find missing persons “goes hand-in-hand with the ongoing pursuit of accountability for war crimes – crimes that continue to be denied and concealed, while relevant documents and archives remain classified or sealed, and the perpetrators of genocide are glorified”.

Excavations conducted by Kosovo authorities in August 2026 in the villages of Kalluder and Jabuke in Zubin Potok, discovered human remains believed to belong to at least 23 people. The excavation process in these two villages began on July 28, 2026, and lasted for four weeks.

Three suspects are currently under investigation and in custody in connection with this case, suspected of committing war crimes against the civilian population.

Around 1,600 people remain missing from the Kosovo war.

According to a report by the Institute for Crimes Committed During the War in Kosovo, IKKL, at least 13,227 people were killed, subjected to enforced disappearance or died as a result of the war between January 1, 1998, and December 31, 2000.

The publication of this list marks the first phase of the IKKL’s institutional database, which was developed to document the human toll of the war and serve as a reliable resource for institutions and researchers.

World.title: Crackdown on Serbian Alta Bank Plunges Russians into Financial Uncertainty
World.content:
Alta Bank thrived during the rule of SNS and former President Aleksandar Vucic.

In 2025, for example, Serbia’s state-owned electricity company, Elektroprivreda Srbije, EPS, changed its payment arrangements, directing Belgrade residents to pay their electricity bills into Alta Bank accounts. And shortly before last month’s election, Vucic launched a podcast on his YouTube channel featuring Alta Bank as a sponsor.

On Monday, the bank’s owner, Davor Macura, was detained on suspicion of illegally withdrawing nearly 385 million euros.

The bank’s clients, many of them Russians, have been locked out of their accounts.

Olga, who opened her Alta Bank account in November 2024, said that she and her partner could no longer access their money and had received no information directly from the bank.

“The worst thing is the bank didn’t give us any information, no email, no message about the situation,” she said.

Serbia’s Deposit Insurance Agency said it would begin reimbursing insured deposits of up to 50,000 euros per depositor within seven working days, after the Commercial Court in Belgrade on Tuesday opened bankruptcy proceedings against Alta Bank. The agency appointed state-owned Banka Postanksa stedionica to handle the payments.

In the meantime, the lives and livelihoods of many in Serbia’s Russian community have been turned upside down.

“We used it for everything – salary and savings,” said Olga’s partner, Eugene, who described Alta Bank as the default banking option for Russians who moved to Serbia.

Like Ekaterina, Ivan had also sold his Moscow apartment last month. He transferred some 180,000 euros to his Alta Bank account, which he had opened in December 2023, with the intention of buying a property in Serbia.

“Insurance will give me back 50,000 euros, but it’s less than a third,” he said.

Ivan said the bank had provided no information since its closure, while its branches were closed and its mobile application and website were inaccessible, leaving him unable even to obtain an account statement.

“I’m very happy I took some money out on Thursday to pay my rent and food, but before the end of the year my wallet will be empty,” he told BIRN.

According to Popovic, the Deposit Insurance Agency will pay out compensation for deposits up to 50,000 euros. For deposits above that amount, the creditor will “join the queue” for the bank’s bankruptcy or liquidation estate.

“This procedure can take a long time, measured in years, and payouts are usually made in installments, following successful sales of bank assets.”

‘Cash Only’

World.title: Scapegoats? Accused Shooters in 1992 Sarajevo Execution Protest Innocence
World.content:
BIRN cannot corroborate either man’s account of what happened in Veliki Park on April 22, 1992.

It is a fact, however, that the witnesses in the trial of Vikic and his three co-accused offered contradictory accounts.

One protected witness, a member of Matic’s unit identified only as Witness A, told the court he watched Herenda shoot all eight prisoners from a range of just two metres, though he did not initially tell this to investigators.

Amir Medjic, a reservist in Vikic’s unit guarding Police House, also said Herenda was the sole shooter.

But they differ on how the shootings unfolded.

Witness A put Herenda forcing the prisoners out of a van and shooting them as they climbed a wall; Medjic had them arriving on foot with escorts, whom Herenda sent away after a word from a State Security official.

Other witnesses placed Herenda nearby, but did not say he fired. Two members of Vikic’s unit and its secretary said they had heard that the killers were either Matic’s men or those of Jusuf ‘Juka’ Prazina, another wartime commander; a Novi Grad shift chief said he heard Matic pulled the trigger. None of them actually saw it happen

Jusic, Herenda and a witness from Prazina’s unit each describe four or more shooters, in stark contrast to those who say Herenda acted alone. The appeals panel wrote that many witnesses identified Herenda and Jusic as the killers, yet none of the testimony cited identified Jusic as opening fire.

Individual testimonies have also shifted.

Witness F made several statements to prosecutors between 2006 and 2016, then told the court they were untrue and that he signed them under pressure. The trial chamber itself noted that for many prosecution witnesses it could not tell what they had seen from what they had heard.

A claim that Herenda confessed to the executions rests on two former officers of the intelligence service AID: Edin Garaplija, sentenced to 13 years for abducting Herenda in June 1996, months after the war had ended, and trying to kill him; and a convicted colleague identified in the trial as Witness L.

The abduction came amid a power struggle inside the AID, the successor to the wartime Bosnian State Security Service, as a new leadership moved against alleged rivals.

Interrogated and tortured by the AID officers for four days, Herenda said he never confessed. Yet the trial chamber cited both accounts, by Garaplija and Witness L, when it concluded that the evidence pointed to Herenda as the killer.

Oleg Cavka, a former war crimes prosecutor at the Bosnian Prosecutor’s Office, also said Herenda admitted being “involved”, when Cavka interviewed him in the Netherlands in May 2015. Herenda disputed this, saying he told Cavka only that he had been present, not that he took part. The court judgement cited no record of the interview and Cavka declined to comment for this story.

World.title: British Arrivals in Croatia Set to Increase in 2027 Following WTM London
World.content:
November the 5th, 2026 – British arrivals in Croatia are looking very likely to increase throughout 2027 as the country wows at the WTM in London.

The World Travel Market (WTM) is traditionally held in London at the beginning of November, and it’s one of the largest and most important tourism fairs in the world. Naturally, the Croatian National Tourist Board presented the overall Croatian tourism offer, and Slobodna Dalmacija reports that the delegation was led by the Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina and HTZ director Kristjan Staničić. The Croatian stand’s offer was presented by 32 co-exhibitors.

the uk is one of croatia’s most important source markets

“The signals from the British market are extremely positive for Croatia; the UK is one of the country’s most important source markets, from which we continuously achieve very good results, and British guests are among those with the highest average daily spending in Croatia.

Precisely for that reason, we’re using this appearance at the WTM also for a series of meetings with leading British tour operators, airlines and other partners, with special emphasis on strengthening air connectivity, further growth of tourist traffic and development of cooperation in 2027. Research of the British market shows that guests are paying more and more attention to the quality of the offer and value for money, and are looking for trips outside the main summer months, shorter city breaks and authentic experiences.

It’s exactly these trends that are fully in line with the direction in which we’re developing Croatian tourism – towards higher quality and competitiveness, a more diverse offer and more even tourist activity throughout the whole year. Our goal is to additionally strengthen Croatia’s position on the British market, but also to ensure that the further development of tourism brings greater value to our destinations, the economy and local communities,” Minister Glavina stated.

from huge airlines to travel agencies

During the first day of the fair meetings were held with representatives of partners and organisations such as Jet2.com & Jet2Holidays, EasyJet Holidays, British Airways, TravelZoo, Love Holidays, the British Association of Travel Agents (ABTA), CBS travel, Travel Weekly and others. Key topics were previous activities and results, and certain partners are also announcing additional expansions in their programmes towards Croatian destinations. The above is best confirmed by the latest ABTA trends research, according to which demand for travel on the British market is still strong despite the rise in the cost of living, geopolitical uncertainties, disruptions in air traffic and climate change.

As many as 88 percent of respondents went on at least one holiday during the previous 12 months, which is one percentage point more than the year before and equal to the result from 2019. An important indicator of the research is the position of Croatia, which is in 13th place on the list of world destinations that British travellers plan to visit in the next 12 months, which confirms the competitive position of our country on the important UK market.

research conducted by tomas

“The British market is extremely important for Croatian tourism given that it is a country that enters the top 10 markets from which Croatia achieves the highest tourist traffic, and the recently published results of the TOMAS research show that Brits are the second guests by spending.

On the UK market, we’re also observing an interesting change, which opens additional potentials for Croatia as well, and that is city break tourism, which has become the most popular form of holiday for British guests. Croatia is an interesting destination for them in that context due to its proximity, so we will carry out investments and activities with the aim of further strengthening air traffic towards Croatian destinations also during 2027, and the priority remains the further strengthening of the quality of the overall tourism offer,” director Staničić stated, adding that Croatia has a stable position on the market, which was also confirmed by numerous partners during the talks.

top destinations

Positive trends from the UK market are also indicated by the results of tourist traffic, that is, data from the eVisitor system, according to which from this market in our country during the first 10 months 841 thousand arrivals (+2%) and 4.1 million overnight stays (+1%) were achieved. In this, Britons achieved the most overnight stays in Dubrovnik-Neretva and Split-Dalmatia counties, and looking by destinations, in Dubrovnik, Split, Konavle, Župa Dubrovačka, Rovinj and Zadar.

“Our partners on the British market recognise Croatia not only as a summer destination, but as somewhere that carries high value, authenticity and exceptional diversity. We’re particularly pleased by the fact that British travel organisers are actively expanding their programmes, which directly affects the extension of the main part of the tourist year. British travellers today more than ever are looking for authentic experiences, top gastronomy, preserved nature and rich cultural heritage. Our focus on the promotion of sustainable tourism and the offer outside the summer season perfectly resonates with the trends on the UK market, where younger generations and experienced travellers are paying more and more attention to the ecological and social responsibility of the destination,” believes Bisera Fabrio, director of the HTZ Representative Office in London.

croatia’s incredible food and wine scene

The complete presentation of Croatian eno-gastronomy was complemented by a presentation and tasting of Croatian wines, held as part of the Croatian stand in cooperation between the Croatian National Tourist Board and the Croatian Chamber of Economy. Croatia presented itself within the exhibition stand with a recognisable visual identity, whose panels and video walls will be decorated with multimedia content connected with the new promotional video “Croatia – I hear it’s beautiful” with the one and only John Malkovich taking the main role.

World.title: Croatian-Made Circular Ice Rink Earns Popularity in London
World.content:
November the 5th, 2026 – A Croatian-made circular ice rink made by Wonderland Factory has earned enormous popularity in Leicester Square in the heart of London.

Interest in the new festive winter attraction exceeded expectations, and more than 90 percent of tickets for the season were sold out in the first 24 hours from the start of sales. Ana Roksandic reports for Poslovni that the Croatian company Wonderland Factory, owner of the Ice Wonderland brand, realised the project of a circular ice rink with an area of 400 square metres on London’s Leicester Square, one of the most famous tourist locations in the British capital.

Interest in the new winter attraction exceeded expectations, and more than 90 percent of tickets for the season were sold out in the first 24 hours from the start of sales. It is expected that Leicester Square will be visited by more than 3.5 million tourists during the winter. “In recent years, we’ve realised a large number of projects in the UK, which is one of our main export markets. Leicester Square is a particularly interesting project, not only because of the unique and extremely popular location in the very centre of London, but also because of the complexity of the execution,” said Rahela Bošnjak, director of Wonderland Factory which stands behind the Ice Wonderland brand.

When it comes to the value of the projects, in Croatia it ranges up to 100,000 euros per location, for ice rinks with an area of 400 to 600 square metres.

On the British market, the amounts can reach even 300,000 euros, depending on the scope of the work and additional services, they said from the company. “We are currently also assembling an ice rink in Liverpool, and in Great Britain we have a series of other locations. Nevertheless, we most look forward to Croatia and the beautiful Advents of which Ice Wonderland will be a part. Since we started precisely in Croatia, so we’re always particularly happy to work in Croatia,” Bošnjak stated.

In order to maximally utilise the available space, the Ice Wonderland team designed the concept of a kind of “ice rink on a floor”. The entire construction and the ice rink surface are raised almost two metres above ground level, whereby space under the ice rink is ensured for the placement of the cooling system, technical equipment and all operational installations.

World.title: Mate Rimac Claims State Owes Him 40,000 Euros After Appearing on List of Tax Debtors
World.content:
November the 5th, 2026 – Croatian entrepreneur Mate Rimac has claimed that the state actually owes him 40,000 euros after he appeared on the country’s list of tax debtors.

Mate Rimac reacted after it was published that his name is on the official list of tax debtors, with a recorded debt of 39,261.64 euros. Poslovni reports that he claimed that the situation is actually the opposite and that the state should return almost 40,000 euros in tax to him after he sold a car abroad. In order to support his claims, Rimac published on Facebook the decision of the Customs Administration by which a tax refund was approved to him, as well as a screenshot of the mPorezna application, on which a debt of almost 40,000 euros is not shown. “When the state needs to return tax TO YOU, and you end up on the list of tax debtors. Well, f*** this life…”, Rimac wrote.

He explained that he sold the car abroad and that because of that he is entitled to a refund of part of the special tax on motor vehicles (PPMV). Mate Rimac is currently located in Singapore, and he found out about the publication of the information about the tax debt, as he stated, only after waking up. He didn’t hide his dissatisfaction and irritation with the way the Croatian media reported on the case.

“I’m currently in Singapore so this unfolded while I was sleeping. And our amazing portals can hardly wait to publish anything without checking anything or sending an inquiry for a comment,” he wrote. Along with his post, Rimac attached the decision of the Ministry of Finance, that is, the Customs Administration in Zagreb, issued on the 24th of September 2026.

According to that document, a refund of the special tax on motor vehicles in the amount of 39,262.91 euros was approved to him. The refund relates to a Ferrari 812 GTS car, first registered on the 22nd of September 2020, which Rimac in the meantime sold abroad. “The request of Mate Rimac (…) is accepted and a refund of the special tax on motor vehicles in the amount of 39,262.91 EUR is approved,” it states in the decision that he published. According to the mentioned document, the money should be paid to him from the state budget after delivery of the original of the enforceable decision.

Rimac also published a screenshot of the mPorezna application which on 3 November shows a debt of only 4.83 euros. To briefly recap, the Tax Administration published on the 31st of October the list of tax debtors on which Mate Rimac, founder of Rimac Automobili and head of the company Bugatti Rimac, is also found. On the list for Zagreb County he is listed in 125th place, with a total debt of 39,261.64 euros. For the final clarification of the case an official statement from the Tax Administration is needed. It should also be emphasised that the debt is recorded in the name of Mate Rimac as a natural person and does not relate to the operations of the Rimac Group, Bugatti Rimac or other companies with which he is connected.

the customs administration admits its mistake and apologises to rimac

Mate Rimac has since received an apology from the customs authorities, publishing their response on Facebook. In it, it is confirmed that his name ended up on the list of tax debtors by mistake. They stated that he actually has no overdue debts on the basis of the special tax on motor vehicles and they apologised to him for the inconvenience caused.

In the response, that he published it is stated that by verification an error was established during the publication of the list of tax debtors. “By the conducted checks it was established that during the publication of the list of debtors an error occurred and that Mate Rimac has no overdue debts on the basis of the special tax on motor vehicles,” it states in the response of the Customs Administration.

They explain that the error occurred in the algorithm for updating the list of tax obligors. Because of that the amount of 39,262.91 euros, which the state budget was supposed to return to Rimac, was incorrectly shown as his debt. “It is, therefore, an error, and Mate Rimac’s statements in relation to this issue are completely founded,” they state from the Customs Administration. At the end of the response, they apologised for the error.

“Therefore, we apologise to the entire public and especially to Mate Rimac for the inconvenience caused,” they concluded.

World.title: Croatia Spent €39.5 Million on Ukrainian Refugees in 2025
World.content:
November the 5th, 2026 – Croatia spent 39.5 million euros on Ukrainian refugees in 2025, with the costs having risen considerably compared to 2024.

The costs of reception and accommodation of displaced persons from Ukraine continued to rise last year as well. The state recorded almost five million euros more in expenses than back in 2024. Poslovni reports that for the reception and care of displaced persons from Ukraine in private and collective accommodation during 2025, 39.54 million euros in expenses were recorded, which is approximately 4.7 million euros or 13.5 percent more than the year before. The data are stated in the report on the state and management of commodity reserves for 2025, which the Government considered at its session on the 29th of October and then forwarded to the Croatian Parliament.

According to the report of the Ministry of Economy, the costs of caring for displaced persons from Ukraine increased due to a larger number of accommodation users. Back in 2024, 34.83 million euros in expenses were recorded for these needs, while last year the amount rose to 39.54 million euros. In the budget, 37.71 million euros were planned for compensations related to the reception and care of displaced persons, which means that the realised expenses were about 1.83 million euros higher than the planned amount.

almost 7.8 million euros in bills was paid at the beginning of 2026

The report also reveals that the Directorate for Commodity Reserves at the end of 2025 had 7.77 million euros in outstanding obligations for the accommodation of displaced persons from Ukraine during November and December. These are the costs of individual and collective accommodation that were paid in January and February 2026, in accordance with the contracted deadlines of 30 to 60 days from the receipt of electronic invoices. These expenses relate to 2025 and are not an additional cost that should be added to the total annual amount of 39.54 million euros.

The total obligations of the Directorate for Commodity Reserves at the end of last year amounted to 8.24 million euros, or 30.4 percent more than at the end of 2024. Of that, almost 94 percent related precisely to the accommodation of displaced persons from Ukraine. The Directorate ended last year with a shortfall of revenue in relation to expenses of 3.89 million euros, which was partially covered by the transferred surplus of revenue from previous years of 2.97 million euros. The report states that the shortfall is related to the costs of accommodation and food for displaced persons from Ukraine, whose bills for the end of the year were settled during the first two months of 2026.

eu cash involvement

In addition to funds from the state budget, European Union funds were also used to finance the reception and care of displaced persons. From the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF), 2.84 million euros were allocated during 2025 for the costs of reception and care of displaced persons from Ukraine in individual accommodation. This amount, according to the report, was recorded as revenue from the competent budget for financing operating expenses, in accordance with the instruction of the Ministry of Finance.

In addition to financing accommodation, the state also provided food products for displaced persons from Ukraine during last year. The value of goods delivered from strategic commodity reserves amounted to 510,981 euros. Among the delivered products there were almost 50 tonnes of flour, more than 21 tonnes of rice, 21 tonnes of canned meat, almost 14 tonnes of canned fish and more than 23,500 litres of oil. Larger quantities of pasta, sugar, salt, jam and packet soups were also delivered.

The goods were, at the request of the Directorate of Civil Protection, delivered to the Croatian Red Cross for further distribution to displaced persons from Ukraine accommodated in Croatia. The report also shows the costs of procurement of goods and related services of 29,138.64 euros. Of that, 17,762.17 euros related to the procurement of flour, which is included in the value of the delivered goods, and the remaining 11,376.47 euros to transport and other related costs. The data shows that the reception of displaced persons from Ukraine during 2025 also represented a significant expense in the operations of the Directorate for Commodity Reserves, with accommodation costs rising, and part of the obligations from the last months of the year transferred for payment at the beginning of 2026.

World.title: Women in Croatia Will Now Need to Wait Longer to Retire
World.content:
November the 4th, 2026 – Women in Croatia will now need to wait longer to retire, with new rules coming into force as of January the 1st, 2027.

As of January the 1st 2027, the conditions for women to take regular and early pensions are changing. Index reports that women in Croatia will have to be three months older than this year, and for early retirement, the required pensionable service is also increasing, according to data from the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (HZMO). For a regular pension next year, women in Croatia will have to be at least 64 years and three months old and have 15 years of pensionable service. In 2026, the requirement is 64 years of age and at least 15 years of service.

stricter rules for early retirement

The changes also apply to those hoping to begin drawing their pensions earlier. Women will have to be three months older than they did this year in order to retire. This year, for early retirement, at least 59 years of age and 34 years of service are required. This means that from the beginning of next year both conditions increase by three months.

when will men and women be equalised?

The age limit for women is gradually increasing every year. In 2028, women will need to be 64 years and six months of age in order to claim their regular pension, and in 2029, they’ll need to be 64 years and nine months of age. From the 1st of January 2030, the conditions are completely equalised. Both women and men will then need 65 years of age and at least 15 years of pensionable service for a regular old-age pension. For early retirement from 2030 the requirement of at least 60 years of age and 35 years of pensionable service will apply to both genders.

Taking an early pension also means a lower initial pension amount. Under the current law, the pension is reduced by 0.2 percent for each month of earlier departure in relation to the prescribed age for a regular old-age pension. This means that the reduction amounts to 2.4 percent for one year of earlier retirement, or a maximum of 12 percent for five years. However, from the beginning of 2026 the reduction is abolished after the recipient of the early pension reaches the age of 70.

who can retire early?

Special conditions apply to long-term insured persons. They can acquire the right to their regular pension at the age of 60 and with 41 years of insurance service in actual duration. This possibility applies to women and men who meet the prescribed conditions, and it differs from an earlier pension. Women who have already fulfilled the conditions for a pension under earlier regulations do not automatically lose the acquired right because the age limit additionally increases at the beginning of next year.

World.title: Croatian Tourist Board – London and Advent Launch Winter Campaign
World.content:
November the 4th, 2026 – The Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ) has officially kicked off its winter campaign, showcasing Advent up and down the country in London.

This very influential London fair brings together more than 4,000 exhibitors from 180 countries, and Croatia is presenting its offer with the participation of more than 30 domestic co-exhibitors. Zrinka Gabelica Toplek reports for Poslovni that the Croatian National Tourist Board is currently showcasing a very intensive winter promotion campaign and preparations for the next tourist year. Key activities include appearance at one of the world’s largest tourism fairs, WTM London, which is currently going on, as well as the launch of the first national campaign for Advent events.

The Croatian delegation is led by the Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina and HTZ director Kristjan Staničić, who will hold meetings with leading British and global partners, including airlines and tour operators such as EasyJet Holidays, British Airways, Jet2Holidays and the ABTA association. “WTM London as one of the world’s leading tourism business gatherings enables us to have direct contacts with key partners. It’s also an opportunity to open new possibilities for Croatian destinations, and in that context it is important to further encourage interest in travel in the pre-season and post-season, with a quality offer and an appropriate price-quality ratio,” revealed HTZ director Kristjan Staničić, emphasising the strategic importance of this appearance for positioning Croatia as a year-round destination.

The promotional appearance in London relies on a new visual identity of the stand and multimedia content with John Malkovich, along with the presentation of domestic wines in cooperation with the Croatian Chamber of Economy (HGK). At the beginning of November, the first national Advent campaign for Croatia is also starting across 11 European markets, with the aim of promoting festive and overall winter programmes in Zagreb, Varaždin, Osijek, Opatija and other cities.

World.title: Pula Among the Top 10 Most Affordable Global Air Destinations
World.content:
November the 4th, 2026 – Gorgeous Pula has been ranked among the top 10 most affordable global air destinations.

When planning their trips, people are increasingly guided by expected changes in transport costs, and not only by accommodation and other services. Marin Penavic reports for Poslovni that the Istrian coastal city of Pula has found itself among the ten most affordable world tourist destinations for 2027, according to the ranking published by the wildly popular flight search engine Skyscanner.

pula took seventh place

The Croatian city took seventh place, and one of the key reasons highlighted is the expected drop in air ticket prices. According to Skyscanner’s estimates, the average price of flights to Pula should be around 20 percent lower than this year. In first place on the list is Bilbao in Spain, where the largest drop in air ticket prices is expected – as much as 66 percent compared to 2026. It is followed by Polish Wroclaw with an estimated cheapening of 47 percent, while French Bordeaux is in third place, with flight prices that should be 34 percent lower.

In addition to Pula, among the ten destinations that could be particularly interesting to travellers in 2027 due to more affordable air tickets are also Zurich, Ancona, Rhodes, Carcassonne, Fez and Krabi. Skyscanner’s list thus suggests that the price of transport could play an important role in the choice of destinations during the coming year. Lower flight prices could boost demand for cities that have so far been less accessible or more expensive to visit, and among them is Pula.

pula’s competitiveness

The inclusion of Pula among the ten most affordable destinations is particularly interesting for Croatian tourism, since accessibility by air directly affects the international competitiveness of the destination. At the same time, Skyscanner’s findings show how travellers, when planning their trips, can increasingly be guided by expected changes in transport costs, and not only by the prices of accommodation and other services at the destination.

World.title: Pantheon Data Centre Will Consume as Much Electricity as a Third of Croatia
World.content:
November the 4th, 2026 – The deeply contested Pantheon data centre in Topusko is edging closer to the start of construction despite most being against the facility that will use as much electricity as a third of Croatia.

Representatives of the Croatian Transmission System Operator (HOPS) and the investor in the Pantheon AI data centre in Topusko announced at a panel of the Green Energy Fair that they expect the contract for connection to the electricity transmission network to be signed in November. Poslovni reports that at the panel dedicated to data centres as new challenges for the electricity system, Pantheon project manager Mario Gudelj recalled that HOPS had previously accepted Pantheon’s study for connection to the network back in July this year, and that the signing of the contract is expected in November.

many are against pantheon’s construction

The contract with HOPS will enable the future controversial data centre in Topusko to receive a stable power supply of 1 GW (gigawatt) or 1,000 MW (megawatts). HOPS connection manager Igor Šumonja said that the current system load for all of Croatia stands at around 2,000 to 3,000 MW, and that connecting such a consumer will increase the load by an entire third. This is deeply concerning to the vast majority who are against the construction of harmful and environmentally catastrophic data centres.

“HOPS has approached this seriously and we know that it requires the construction of four new powerful 400-kilovolt transmission lines approximately 300 kilometres long, and the investor will build and pay all the costs of connecting to the network and nothing will be borne by HOPS and the system. In addition to them, we have another 1,600 to 1,700 requests for data centres, but of much lower power than Pantheon,” Šumonja claimed.

As the start of construction of this largest data centre campus in Croatia and the region is planned for 2027, and the start of operations in 2029, Gudelj believes that the contract with HOPS will be signed soon, as well as that the spatial plan in Sisak-Moslavina County will be adopted and the environmental impact study accepted, because without that they cannot start working. “The spatial plan is a more complex story than HOPS because there have been amendments and additions to that plan, for which a public discussion is now underway, but we believe that all those processes in the county will be completed by February or the beginning of March,” Gudelj said.

claims that “pantheon is so different” fall on the deaf ears of an increasingly concerned public

When asked whether he fears that something could ‘get stuck’ at that discussion and because of the citizens regarding this project, he replied that they are not afraid because Pantheon is “so different and brings so many benefits to society, the state and the local community that there is no reason for it to get stuck”, and that in all public appearances he emphasises that they cannot take a single step without satisfying both the residents and the requirements binding from the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

Collaborator on the project Antonio Gužvinec from the company Parsec Lab explained that this future AI campus will also be powered by energy from a solar power plant and battery systems, because the power density of the ‘cabinets’ with servers in them is significantly higher than in ordinary data centres, which is why they also need stronger cooling systems since the processors work practically constantly.

Luka Majić, product manager of the Croatian representative office of the American company Vertiv Croatia, which deals with data centre infrastructure and is also a collaborator on the project, highlighted the growing interest in investments in data centres due to the growth in demand for AI. He announced that in Croatia the company will increase the number of employees by 200, from the current 650, because they have become Vertiv’s global centre of expertise. Gudelj further emphasised that Pantheon will allegedly not buy energy that is currently consumed on the Croatian market.

Regarding the question of whether all this will lead to an increase in the price of electricity in Croatia, Šumonja from HOPS said that they do not set prices, so he cannot say anything about that either. On the question of cooling the centre, Majić from Vertiv said that in data centres a water cooling system is completely standard and that there are several models that are applied for this.

“pantheon won’t expect the topusko spa water” – residents don’t believe it

Gudelj repeated his earlier claims that Pantheon will not affect the waters in the Topusko spas, nor the water supply system. He also repeated the announcement that there will be “around 3,500 jobs” in Pantheon, of which 1,500 will be from the beginning due to construction and other jobs, including three shifts of firefighters that they will pay for, and their goal is for at least around 500 employees to also live in Topusko, which is why they plan to build apartments as well.

“All in all, Pantheon’s footprint on the local community in the county area and beyond, economically, sociologically and democratically, is much greater than the damage to the environment will be. Care will be taken to improve the roads, noise, so that we do not burden the water chemically and so on,” Gudelj claimed, but many aren’t buying his words. He also emphasised that Pantheon will apparently pay HOPS around 80 million euros annually for network fees, which is practically HOPS’s annual investment cycle, to which Šumonja from HOPS said that before Pantheon enters the network, they will test them for at least two years, as well as other customers.

World.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
World.content:
Washington – President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028.

The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss.

But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama.

– Republicans in turmoil –

The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb.

Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states.

The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday.

But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump.

It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden.

“The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said.

Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about.

Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war.

The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal.

He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off.

Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state.

– Democrats on a high –

The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost.

Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer.

The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party.

Before the midterms Kamala Harris, 62, had been the favorite for the nomination, but there are many in the party who would prefer to have someone without a losing track record.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, 53, who was interviewed by Harris to be her running mate in 2024, had a good night on Tuesday as he stormed back to reelection in the key battleground state.

Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom, 59, is another big name who has repeatedly taken on Trump. He predicted in an interview with AFP in September Trump’s presidency “as we know it would be over after the midterms.

But Newsom, like Harris, may be seen as more of an old guard figure in a party that is looking to its rising stars.

A prominent but potentially divisive choice would be left-wing New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who said in September that she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024.

Other possible contenders include former Chicago mayor Rahm Emmanuel, JB Pritzker, the billionaire Illinois governor who set out a lengthy national agenda after winning a third term on Tuesday, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, and Arizona senator and former astronaut Mark Kelly.

World.title: Sixers roll on to down Pistons, Knicks gore Bulls
World.content:
Los Angeles – Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid combined for 56 points as the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in their heavyweight top-of-the-table NBA Eastern Conference clash on Wednesday.

Brown finished with 30 points and Embiid added 26 to give the Sixers another impressive road win that moved them to 8-1 at the top of the standings, with Detroit (6-2) in second.

Brown and Embiid led another balanced offensive performance from Philadelphia, who saw all five starters reach double figures.

LeBron James added a double-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists while Tyrese Maxey drained three three-pointers on his way to a 19-point haul.

Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics in the offseason, said he was “still adjusting” to his new team-mates.

“I’m still figuring it out,” Brown said, before paying tribute to the performance of 41-year-old team-mate James.

“LeBron has been great,” Brown said. “To see what he’s doing at his age makes sense for LeBron James, but for nobody else would it make sense.”

The Sixers moved into the lead towards the end of the first quarter and kept their noses in front for the remainder of the game, stretching the lead to 18 points before a late rally from Detroit.

Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points while Cade Cunningham added 26.

The reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season with a 135-105 blowout over the Chicago Bulls at Madison Square Garden.

The Knicks, who have made a slow start to the new campaign, improved to 4-4 after a dazzling 33-point performance from Jalen Brunson, who drained five three-pointers while making 10-of-17 from the field.

O.G. Anunoby scored 18 points while Karl-Anthony Towns added 17 for a Knicks team who led by as many as 44 points midway through the third quarter.

In Boston, the Milwaukee Bucks threatened to pull off a huge comeback before finally succumbing 109-102 to the Celtics.

Paul George (25 points) and Derrick White (24) led the scoring for Boston, who appeared to be cruising after leading by 20 early in the third quarter.

But a 38-point third quarter from Milwaukee flipped the script and the Bucks edged into a 96-95 lead with five minutes remaining.

Boston regained control down the stretch with George and White closing out the win.

World.title: Gaza turns rubble into power with homemade wind turbines
World.content:
Khan Yunis – Above a maze of tents in a crowded displacement camp in Gaza, homemade wind turbines made from scrap metal and salvaged debris spin in the sea breeze, bringing electricity to struggling Palestinians.

In the southern Khan Yunis camp, Kamal Al-Dabary, a former engineering student, has put his skills to work for families who, like most Gazans, live in displacement with no direct access to the tiny territory’s shattered power grid.

According to the World Bank, more than 90 percent of Gaza’s power generation and distribution capacity was destroyed in April 2026, much of it in Israeli strikes that devastated homes and infrastructure.

Sitting on the ground, Dabary tinkered with electrical wires, metal parts and basic tools on a plastic table.

After carefully twisting cables together and testing them with a multimeter, a small bulb flickered on, then another, signalling that the current was flowing.

“When solar panels were still relatively affordable, we bought one and kept moving it around to follow the sun,” the 60-year-old, displaced by the fighting between Israel and Hamas, told AFP.

The war was triggered by the Palestinian Islamist movement’s deadly October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

But after three years of war, prices have soared as aid and commercial supplies trickled into Gaza through crossings tightly controlled by Israel.

A single solar panel now costs at least 15,000 shekels (nearly $5,000), putting it out of reach for most Gazans, Dabary said.

– ‘Changed everything’ –

“We haven’t had work or income for three years,” he added.

“That’s when the idea of a wind turbine came to mind. Why not harness the wind? So we salvaged parts from the rubble.”

The turbines are built from scooter motors and old water tanks cut into blades.

As the wind turns the blades, they drive a motor that generates electricity. The power then passes through circuits assembled from parts recovered from destroyed homes before being stored in batteries.

This provides enough electricity to charge phones and run lights, fans and even electric razors, small comforts that have become a luxury for families still living in tents and shelters.

Nearly all of Gaza’s residents were displaced at least once during the war, and most now live in a small area still under Hamas rule, while Israel controls more than 60 percent of the territory along its perimeter.

“They help us hold on… until God delivers us from this ordeal and we can return home,” said Dabary, known locally as Abu Ayman.

The output remains modest. But in a camp where shortages are constant, every watt counts.

The system “has changed everything,” said 50-year-old Saleh ben Hasan.

With healthcare and medication hard to access in Gaza, the power can also help keep medical equipment running.

“If a child needs a nebuliser (a device used to inhale medicine) in the middle of the night, who else can we turn to?” he said.

“Electricity is needed… So we turn to our brother Abu Ayman.”

World.title: Tech hit by new AI worries on positive day for most markets
World.content:
Hong Kong – Tech firms tumbled Thursday as investors contemplated the outlook for the AI boom after Democrats swept the US midterms, partly on the back of growing anger over the rapid building of data centres across the country.

However, broader markets mostly rallied and oil plunged after Donald Trump’s Republicans were dealt a historic defeat that was blamed on high prices, tariffs and the Iran war.

The result stoked hopes he will look to wind down the Middle East conflict, which would help temper inflation, and even soften his stance on trade.

But AI-linked firms came under the cosh amid fears for planned data centre construction projects as well as renewed scrutiny from newly installed Democrats on Capitol Hill.

The sector had already been in the crosshairs of investors owing to questions about the vast sums pumped into new facilities, R&D and chip development, and when any companies would see a profit.

Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets said the vote was accelerating a reassessment of AI that was already under way.

“A Democratic Congress introduces another layer of uncertainty: regulatory scrutiny,” she wrote, adding that the three main risks were more oversight, data centre restrictions and capital spending uncertainty.

“The congressional scrutiny could accelerate demands for AI safety standards, independent model evaluations and greater accountability for data centre developers,” she added.

However, she also said: “This is not the same as an outright anti-AI policy agenda. AI is strategically important for US competitiveness, particularly against China, and there remains considerable bipartisan interest in maintaining American leadership.”

Chip firms were hammered in Asia, with South Korea’s SK hynix off more than seven percent and Samsung 5.5 percent down.

Tokyo-listed Kioxia and Advantest shed nine percent, Tokyo Electron more than seven percent and SoftBank five percent.

US Nasdaq futures fell more than one percent.

Broader markets performed better as investors rotated into other sectors including finance and manufacturing names.

Seoul, the poster child of the AI-led surge in the first half of the year, shed around four percent, while Taipei lost almost two percent. Tokyo also fell.

But there were healthy gains in Hong Kong and Shanghai, helped by hopes for an easing of trade tensions between the US and China, with tech titans including Alibaba, JD.com and Tencent.

Sydney, Singapore, Wellington and Manila also advanced.

Oil continued to fall after diving more than eight percent Wednesday on the US result amid optimism Trump will seek a deal to end the Iran war, which has been a key driver of the inflation spike that has hammered US consumers.

Hopes were given a boost when Vice President JD Vance said in a social media post that the Republican defeat was due to the unpopularity of the eight-month-old conflict.

The drop in crude prices — both main contracts are now below $100 for the first time since the start of October — has also tempered inflation worries and in turn Treasury yields, which dipped again Thursday.

The lower cost of borrowing has also been helped by the prospect that gridlock on Capitol Hill would lead to less spending.

That also weighed on the dollar, which held losses against its peers in Asian trade.
