World.title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
World.content:
Beijing – A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say.

Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing:

– Will tariffs be limited? –

Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say.

That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January.

If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai.

However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses.

Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said.

Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington.

– Taiwan a ‘game changer’? –

The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics.

Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack.

But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons.

China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note.

Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package.

But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said.

“If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.”

Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute.

Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”.

– Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? –

From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say.

“Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim.

“Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added.

Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”.

But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

World.title: Arsenal edge stubborn Slavia in Champions League
World.content:
Prague – Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings.

“We have to value the fact that it’s very difficult to win away from home. We’ve done it against a really tough opponent, as we expected,” said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

“Two very different halves. The first one where we played at a really high level in terms of tempo, intensity, quality and clarity in what we had to do,” he added.

The Premier League champions were quick to take control of the game in chilly conditions in the Czech capital.

Madueke reaped the rewards on nine minutes.

Gyokeres controlled David Raya’s long clearance with his chest and passed the ball instinctively to Madueke sprinting behind him down the right flank.

Madueke left the Slavia back four behind him with ease and beat diving Ukrainian teenager Nazar Domchak in the Slavia goal with a low shot.

Gyokeres, one of six changes in Mikel Arteta’s starting line-up from Sunday’s 1-0 win at Liverpool, made it 2-0 on 38 minutes.

He beat Domchak with a neat shot off the far post after a one-two with Mikel Merino on the edge of the Slavia box.

– ‘Far from our standards’ –

Czech champions Slavia were sluggish throughout the first half, producing a single chance when skipper Tomas Holes fired wide from inside the box.

But they stepped up their pace considerably in the second half to stave off a repeat of a 3-0 home loss to the Gunners in the competition exactly a year ago.

Slavia’s Polish midfielder Oskar Kubiak forced a diving save from Raya seconds into the second half.

Gabriel Magalhaes and Raya cleared two headers off the goalline in quick succession with 15 minutes to go, while David Zima fired over the bar.

Raya then forced a Kubiak header onto the post.

Slavia scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute when David Jurasek’s cross bounced through the Arsenal defence and Wiktor Nowak blasted the ball into the net from close range.

“(We) scored two goals. It should have been three, four or five. We didn’t make that gap,” said Arteta.

“Right from the beginning, we were extremely far from our standards and everything that we have to do… in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half.”

It was the 23rd straight game without a win for the hosts in the Champions League, taking them within one of equalling AEK Athens’ all-time record from 1992-2006.

World.title: Haaland breaks City out of mini-rut at Leipzig
World.content:
Leipzig – Erling Haaland’s 78th-minute strike helped Manchester City shake off a mini-slump with a 3-2 Champions League win at RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

After an excellent start to the season, City had lost two Premier League games in a row either side of beating Brighton on penalties in the League Cup.

The visitors twice went ahead — through a Castello Lukeba own goal and an Enzo Fernandez header — only to be pegged back by goals from Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa.

Despite having scored more against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, Haaland had few chances but was right on the spot to turn in an Elliot Anderson cross for the winner.

“For me I think it’s easy. It’s around 100 minutes a game to just stay fully focused,” Haaland told reporters.

“In this period it was about trying to wait for the right moment and attack it in the right way and put it in the back of the net and that’s exactly what I did.”

Haaland has now scored 13 times in nine matches against Leipzig, including a memorable five-goal performance in a 7-0 rout in March 2023.

Despite the victory, City were well below their usual best against a Leipzig side in a rebuilding process under new coach Martin Demichelis.

City coach Enzo Maresca, who arrived in the summer, conceded his side were still a “work in progress” but praised Haaland.

“It’s important that he’s on his game. We know that at any moment he can help us, he can score goals,” Maresca said.

Maresca backed under-fire goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was out of position for Baku’s equaliser.

“It’s not a concern… We are talking about a mistake. A few minutes before he made a save that no keeper in the world could make.”

Nusa’s performance was a highlight for the hosts, with Haaland’s Norway teammate now on six goals and seven assists in 14 matches this season as Leipzig look to replace Yan Diomande, who left for Real Madrid in the summer.

“It’s a pity, to be honest,” Nusa told TNT Sports. “I feel like we deserved more today and you end up with zero points. It’s not a good feeling.”

– City’s mini-slide –

City travelled to Germany having lost two Premier League games in a row for the first time since August 2025.

Leipzig had won just one from three in the Champions League before Wednesday but had been excellent at home, winning five from five while scoring 19 goals without conceding once.

Haaland was handed the captain’s armband for the first time this season but it was another Norwegian, Leipzig’s Nusa, who impressed early.

Nusa forced Donnarumma to tip a shot over the crossbar with 14 minutes gone.

Leipzig looked more comfortable but then conceded in embarrassing fashion with 37 minutes gone when Lukeba bungled a Nico O’Reilly cut-back into his own goal.

Christoph Baumgartner forced an excellent save from Donnarumma just after the break but Leipzig were soon level when Baku threaded a low shot in from an acute angle with the Italian out of position off his line.

Haaland’s first dangerous moment came shortly after Baku’s equaliser, when he forced a close-range save from Maarten Vandevoordt.

Fernandez had City back in front just before the hour mark when he headed in a lovely Iliman Ndiaye cross, but Leipzig restored parity just three minutes later.

Christopher Nkunku linked up with Nusa just four minutes after coming off the bench, allowing the Norwegian to cut a low shot across the face of goal and in.

When Anderson broke down the right flank with 12 minutes left, Haaland immediately adjusted his run towards the far post, where he waited to tap in the England midfielder’s pinpoint cross.

World.title: LIV Golf relaunch collapses as key investor withdraws: reports
World.content:
Los Angeles – The rebel LIV Golf tour’s bid to relaunch itself after filing for bankruptcy has collapsed following the withdrawal of new lead investor BC Partners, multiple outlets reported Wednesday.

The private capital firm made the decision to walk away after struggling to convince several star players to fully commit to the league going forward, the Financial Times and the Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources.

The once free-spending Saudi-backed league that turned the golf world upside-down by luring superstars away from the traditional PGA Tour is now expected to have its remaining assets liquidated.

LIV Golf did not immediately respond to AFP request for comment.

Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) had poured an estimated $5 billion into the tour since 2022, before abruptly pulling the plug earlier this year.

LIV formally filed for bankruptcy protection in September, though officials vowed to relaunch as “LIV 2.0” next season with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money, and equity stakes in the league for players.

New lead investor BC Partners Credit had pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential $300 million.

But several former LIV stars including Jon Rahm publicly announced their decisions to withdraw from the new version of the tour in recent weeks. Several others were believed to be on the fence.

Even Bryson DeChambeau — arguably the breakaway circuit’s biggest name, who continued to back the tour — did not publicly commit to returning.

LIV’s attempt to relaunch was made more complicated after the DP World (European) Tour reversed its policy of allowing golfers to appear in events on both tours, instead forcing the likes of Rahm to choose.

DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings on Tuesday told the Scotsman newspaper he had a duty “to protect the Tour against an entity who spent, so we are told, over $7 billion, with one of their aims being to ‘destroy the DP World Tour’.”

Golf superstar Rory McIlroy, an outspoken critic of LIV, on Wednesday lent his support to Kinnings’ stance and said he also believed LIV had set out to eradicate its rivals.

“I agree with Guy… [LIV] were going around at Augusta this year telling people that that’s what they wanted to do,” McIlroy told reporters ahead of the DP World Tour playoff Abu Dhabi Championship event.

“And then, it’s ironic that a week later, now they are talking about ‘completing and not competing’ and all that. That’s different from what they were saying at the start of the year.”

Documents from bankruptcy filings showed that LIV owes between $500 million and $1 billion in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players.

Rahm, DeChambeau and fellow golfer Dustin Johnson hold the largest unsecured claims against the tour, totaling more than $5 million each in immediate past-due payments.

World.title: Hardeep Singh Puri elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister

was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh on Thursday after the nomination papers of the two other candidates were rejected, leaving him as the sole contender in the by-election.

state president Hemant Khandelwal collected Puri's certificate of election from Returning Officer Umesh Kumar Sharma at the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly. Deputy chief minister Jagdish Devda and BJP MLAs Rameshwar Sharma and Bhagwandas Sabnani were also present, ANI reported.

Puri's nomination was accepted by the Returning Officer on November 3 after objections raised by

leaders and independent candidates were dismissed during scrutiny.



The nomination papers of Rajkumar Lohani and Kante Sayanna were rejected, leaving Puri as the only candidate in the contest.

According to the order, cited by ANI, Sayanna's nomination was rejected because it did not meet the mandatory requirement of signatures from either 10 per cent of the elected members of the state Legislative Assembly or 10 elected members, whichever was fewer.

Lohani's nomination was rejected for failing to submit the mandatory Form 26 affidavit by the November 2 deadline of 3 pm.





The deadline for withdrawal of nominations ended at 3 pm on November 5. With no other candidate left in the race, Puri was declared elected unopposed to the Upper House.

The by-election was necessitated by the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan on October 14. Murugan's Rajya Sabha term was due to end on April 2, 2030.

Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, deputy Chief Ministers Rajendra Shukla and Jagdish Devda, BJP state president Hemant Khandelwal, state cabinet ministers and other party leaders were present at the time.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi gets relief as Allahabad HC rejects plea seeking FIR over remarks on Sikh community
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Allahabad high court on Wednesday declined to interfere with a Varanasi court order

a plea seeking registration of an FIR against

over his remarks on India's

during a visit to the US in 2024.

Justice Vikram D Chauhan dismissed the application filed by the petitioner, Nageshwar Mishra, observing that the allegation against Rahul Gandhi was based solely on newspaper reports about his statements during his US visits, which did not specify the date, time or place of the remarks.

"In such a situation, no order directing registration of a case against a person can be passed," PTI quoted Justice Chauhan as saying.



Mishra approached the high court after the Varanasi Chief Judicial Magistrate's court rejected his application seeking registration of an FIR against the Congress MP on October 17, 2025. On July 9, a sessions court also dismissed Mishra's petition following which he challenged both orders in the high court.

Or he, as a Sikh, is going to be able to go to Gurdwara. That's what the fight is about, and not just for him, but for all religions."

Amid criticism of his remarks by the BJP, Rahul Gandhi

at the ruling party, accusing it of "resorting to lies" over his remarks and claiming that it was "unable to accept the truth."

World.title: ‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday reiterated her commitment to return to Dhaka in December despite a death sentence awaiting her return from India.

âIf death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,â she told The Associated Press in response to questions by email.

âSo, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed,â Hasina said.

The former leader has served as Prime Minister of Bangladesh for one term from 1996 to 2001 and four consecutive terms from 2009 to 2024.

In 2024, Hasina sought asylum in New Delhi after a mass student-led uprising overthrew her government.



In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal ordered her death sentence for crimes against humanity. She was tried for ordering a crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to the United Nations data, cited by AP, nearly 1,400 were killed during the unrest.

The former PM has denied wrongdoing, rejected the tribunal's verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.

Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India to extradite her. However, New Delhi said the request was being legally examined.





âNobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasinaâs return),â Indiaâs high commissioner to Dhaka Dinesh Trivedi remarked during an October discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. reported.

âAgain and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,â Trivedi added.

On Wednesday, Hasina told the AP that she was aware of the risks she could face on returning, but had no intention of changing her decision.

âI know that I may be arrested when I return. I may be imprisoned, tortured or even killed. I am fully aware of those possibilities. But I cannot spend the rest of my life watching my people suffer from a distance,â she told the news agency.

Hasina did not specify how she intended to travel back to Bangladesh from India.

Hasina alleges crackdown on Awami League members

Her proposed return comes as her Awami League party faces an uncertain political future. The party remains banned, while several of its senior leaders have been arrested or forced into exile.

Hasina alleged that at least 20,000 party members had been killed since August 2024. She also claimed that thousands had been arrested, tortured or driven into hiding, while supporters had lost their homes, businesses and livelihoods because of their political affiliations.

âThere is no normal political or democratic environment,â she said, accusing the authorities of systematically targeting the party.

Following Hasina's removal from office, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus headed an interim administration for 18 months.

In February, Tarique Rahman, son of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and a longstanding political rival of Hasina, won a landslide victory in an election held under the interim government. The Awami League was barred from contesting the polls.

Several rights organisations, including Human Rights Watch, have criticised Rahman's government over alleged violations of civil and political rights in recent months.

The government has maintained that arrests have been made in connection with specific charges.

Hasina raises concern over influence of extremist groups

Hasina also expressed concern over the growing influence of hard-line groups in Bangladesh, saying the political climate had allowed extremist elements to gain confidence.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThe present political environment has allowed extremist elements to become more confident,â she said.

Global rights groups and independent observers had earlier raised concerns about radical groups seeking to suppress liberal forces during the Yunus-led interim administration.

Minority communities have also reported facing intimidation.

The interim government denied the allegations. The current administration has continued to face criticism over the deteriorating law and order situation in the country.

Hasina, who took a tough stance against radical groups during her 15 years in power, said she was worried about their growing influence.

Asked whether she expected countries such as the United States and India to press Bangladesh to ensure her safe return, Hasina said she was not seeking protection from foreign governments.

âI value friendship and cooperation with all nations. That has always been our (Bangladesh's) foreign policy. But I do not need the blessing of a foreign power to return to my own country,â she said.

During the hearing, the panel told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant that it had issued notices in 149 newspapers inviting complaints regarding the violence during a march to Parliament on July 20. However, it received very few complaints, either online or in physical form.

It also informed the top court that it had issued another appeal inviting complaints on October 21.

World.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash: court upholds teen’s bail, raps police and prosecution
World.content:
The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, Keralam, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) dismissed the appeals seeking suspension of the bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor crash case that claimed a life, while coming down heavily on the police and prosecution.

Judge Kavitha Gangadharan questioned the very basis for the registration of the FIR against the teenager in conflict with law, pointing out that such registration is warranted only in offences carrying a punishment of seven years’ imprisonment or more. The multiple alterations made to the FIR also came in for criticism. The police were accused of showing scant regard for the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, with the court questioning the absence of the social background report mandated in cases involving juveniles. The court even read out the relevant provisions of the Act to the investigation officer, an Assistant Commissioner with the Crime Branch.

The court observed that the police are not expected to act beyond the law even under pressure. The judge also asked the prosecution to show reason for not imposing fine while dismissing the appeals.

Earlier, the court had directed the investigation officer to submit within an hour details of FIRs registered in the district or elsewhere in the State in connection with accidents involving juvenile drivers in which Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which prescribes punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, had been invoked.

The court sought the data to append it to the order on the appeals filed by the prosecution and the family of the deceased against the bail granted to the teenager by the Juvenile Justice Board. She warned that the investigation officer would be held answerable if no FIRs had been registered elsewhere invoking BNS Section 105 in similar cases and if the provision had been invoked only in the present case. Though the officer submitted details of nine accident cases involving juveniles in the district, Section 105 had not been invoked in any of them.

The court was also critical of the investigating agency for filing the appeal against the bail in the wrong court instead of the court designated to try cases involving juveniles, the only such court in the district. The judge also sought to know from the prosecution whether it had any doubt that the Juvenile Justice Model Rules constituted the sole State government framework governing matters involving children in conflict with law.

Daughter of victim expresses dismay

Bhadrakeerthi R.J., daughter of the victim Jayabalakrishnan, expressed dismay over the verdict, which she said she “could not comprehend.”

“It was dramatic and full of twists. People of Keralam will have no faith in the courts any more. We were expecting a favourable verdict both from this court and the High Court, (which granted anticipatory bail to the judicial officer, the father of the juvenile accused). Issues that had never been raised until today were brought up by the court. However, we will continue our fight,” she said outside the court.

World.title: Karnataka bus fare hike lower than what was recommended by Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee
World.content:
The Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC), chaired by retired IAS officer Atul Kumar Tiwari, had recommended a 28% fare hike for Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), North Western Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC) and Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC), and a 45% increase for Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC). However, the Karnataka government has approved a lower revision of 23% for KSRTC and 33-35% for BMTC.

In its report submitted to the State government and accessed by The Hindu, the committee cited rising expenditure on fuel, personnel, maintenance and capital operations, along with prolonged gaps between fare revisions, as reasons for the financial strain faced by the four State-run transport corporations.

Growing gap

The committee observed that the growing gap between the actual cost of providing services and the revenue generated through passenger fares had affected the corporations’ financial position, increasing their losses and liabilities. It also noted that improvements in operational efficiency alone would not be sufficient to address the structural deficit.

To determine the required fare revision, the committee adopted a Modified Annual Revenue Requirement (ARR) framework, which takes into account the efficient recurring cost of operations, eligible non-fare revenue and assured government support before calculating the amount to be recovered through passenger fares.

Based on this assessment, the committee’s report recommended a 28% increase for the three regional transport corporations under a harmonised fare structure, while suggesting a separate 45% revision for BMTC, considering its metropolitan operating conditions and cost structure.

RTC Fare hike requested by RTCs in memorandum (including outstanding liabilities) Committee-recommended fare hike KSRTC 38.66% 28% BMTC 189.00% 45% KKRTC 39.45% 28% NWKRTC 39.00% 28%

Source: Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC) report

Sought by corporations

The report also highlighted the difference between the fare increases sought by the corporations and the committee’s assessment. KSRTC had sought a 38.66% increase, while the committee identified a technical fare gap of 32.33% and recommended a 28% revision. For BMTC, the corporation had sought a 189% increase against a technical fare gap of 99.21%, with the committee recommending a 45% hike.

Similarly, KKRTC had sought a 39.45% increase, with the committee identifying a technical gap of 40.43% and recommending 28%. NWKRTC had sought a 39% increase, against a technical gap of 37.22%, with the recommended revision fixed at 28%.

The committee further recommended that any difference between the assessed fare requirement and the actual increase approved by the government be treated as a “policy fare gap”. It said the shortfall should be calculated separately for each corporation based on passenger distribution and actual operational data.

Since such a gap would arise from the government’s decision to keep fares below the level required for full revenue recovery, the committee recommended that the State government meet the shortfall through an identified and committed budgetary funding source. It also suggested that the funding amount and payment schedule be incorporated into the fare revision decision.

Annual review

The report proposed an annual review of the ARR framework based on actual operational and financial performance, with periodic adjustments to prevent the accumulation of unrecovered costs.

It also called for transparent, stage-wise and service-wise fare schedules. While KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC were advised to follow a harmonised fare structure for comparable regional services, BMTC was recommended to retain a separately calibrated urban fare structure reflecting shorter journeys and metropolitan travel patterns, according to the report.

The Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee (PTFRC) is a three-member panel chaired by retired IAS officer Atul Kumar Tiwari. It was established to review the financial health of State-run transport corporations and recommend structured bus fare revisions.

World.title: Thaimai app to monitor high-risk pregnancies,  newborns rolled out in Tiruchi district
World.content:
A pilot project to monitor the health of high-risk pregnant women and newborns through a mobile app has been launched in Tiruchi district.

“The app is meant to track the health requirements of high-risk young mothers and newborns who may have missed coming to hospital or seeking medical assistance for several reasons. It will be used by approximately 400 field workers and 150 doctors within the Tiruchi district,” T. Manivannan, District Health Officer, told The Hindu.

Teams of district-level health workers will identify and upload details of high risk cases on the platform. Village health nurses and medical workers will access the data to provide on-ground support. “This app will be monitoring the health of high-risk pregnant women, post-natal women, mothers who skip or do not follow medical advice, and newborns with medical issues, for up to a month,” the official added.

District officials would be able to review monitoring data through the platform.

The ‘Tiruchi Mother-Child Monitoring App’ (that functions under the State’s ‘Thaimai’ app platform) was launched on November 1 by Health and Family Welfare Minister K. G. Arunraj and Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh. District Collector Pratik Tayal and Corporation Commissioner N. Ponmani were present

World.title: Jinson Abraham’s exhibition Kollavarsham 1202: Munnē: Ippōzh: Ini in Thiruvananthapuram, interlinks fabric and time
World.content:
Jinson Abraham’s photography exhibition Kollavarsham 1202: Munnē: Ippōzh: Ini, currently on at the College of Fine Arts (CFA), Thiruvananthapuram, defines time or kalam, as a goddess. An extension of his earlier work on Kollavarsham calendars, this show focuses on the interrelation of body and fabric, and how the latter was used as an identifier and, in some instances, turned into a constraint.

The exhibition is divided into two parts: Udal or The Body and Archives of Uprising.

In Udal, Jinson transforms the body into a living archive for the marginalised, who were denied space in much of Kerala’s history, carrying traces of “dispossession, labour, caste, and resistance”. These people, who were “denied landownership, caste privilege and basic human dignity”, are absent from history books, the photographer notes. This set of 15 sepia-tinted monochrome pictures, shot on a Sinar F2 camera, recreates that historical presence and human values, placing the subjects as “bearers of agency, memory and dignity”.

Jinson begins this series with a set of nude photographs to establish the idea that the body was itself in Nature for years. “Nobody thought about covering the body for years. However, they may have been forced to do so, to protect themselves from the wind, rain, cold or animals. The body can exist without a cloth. People would have depended on it to protect them, but then the clothes would have been the same for men and women.” Says Jinson.

The following portraits show how fabric becomes an identifier in the Keralam context, deciding who deserved rights and who would be oppressed. In one portrait, a woman clad in kasavu doesn’t have the right to wear the fabric she wove, but the photograph reclaims her agency by dressing her up in that attire.

Furthermore, Jinson shows how people were allowed to wear a single piece of cloth that was fashioned to cover their bodies. A pair of photographs explores the moustache tax, or meeshakaram, and breast tax in 17th-century Keralam, posing questions about gender inequality. “While men paid taxes for moustaches, women didn’t have to. But here’s the interesting question. Men could eliminate the tax by shaving their moustache off, but what do you do about breasts?” asks Jinson.

The exhibition further showcases how women ultimately took control of their own bodies, deciding how they want to cover themselves. A photograph of a man wearing a kurta represented social reformers like Sreenarayana Guru, BR Ambedkar and Ayyankali, who rejected notions of how members of their caste should dress.

The last few pictures in this series also trace how fashion, especially women’s fashion, was subjected to an animal gaze, followed by a colonial gaze and ultimately the male gaze. “It was at this juncture, where we see people attributing violence against women to the length of their clothes, holding it responsible for crimes against them,” says Jinson. The series ultimately ends with a couple’s portrait, with a message on how men are taught about women’s empowerment, without understanding how to coexist with them, says the photographer.

Archivals of uprising

The Archivals of Uprising section features photographs, representing the goddess of time, Kalam, and the 12 months of the year. The Kollam Era calendars, or Malayalam calendars, use Malayalam numbers and feature the portraits next to them. The first month in the Kollam Era calendar is Chingam and the last is Karkkadakam.

“It has 13 components, with 12 rashi chakras and one sun,” says Jinson. The photos of the Kollavarsham 1202 calendar explores the evolution of women’s clothing. The portraits are shot on 4 x 5 square inch sheet films and are developed by photographer Alekh Ajay Ghosh. The photos show how women fashioned a single piece of fabric into their attire, with draping depending on weather, livelihood and other factors. The latter photographs also trace the evolution of a blouse, showing how it came to its present form.

The 13 portraits are also arranged into a single image resembling Leonardo da Vinci’s The Last Supper, with Kalam at the centre and each subject related to the central character. The characters wear handmade fabric clothes designed by Dinu Elizabeth Roy. One of the portraits also showcase a woman, clad in just a necklace made of rocks, presented as a predecessor to the other female subjects.

Jinson, who has drawn inspiration from the style of works by photographer Keerthana Kunnath and the Bengali Nayika painting traditions, says, “I wanted to produce something that celebrates the past, identifying what we have missed. The problem with these portraits is that we don’t have actual images from that era. My whole team is going to time travel to learn something and bring it to the calendars. “

Asked about the Kollavarsham 1203 calendar, Jinson says, “We do have some ideas in mind and at the moment we have a structure to work with as well. When we began thinking about this year, we thought about the idea of blouses, and we ended up thinking about clothes this way. If I live 30 more years, there will be 30 last suppers, narrating Keralam’s history, reviving things that were not documented well.”

Kollavarsham 1202: Munnē: Ippōzh: Ini is on till November 10 at College of Fine Arts, Thiruvananthapuram. Time: 10am to 7pm

World.title: Amit Shah at Karnal rally says Rahul Gandhi creating ‘ruckus’ culture in Parliament
World.content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday (November 5, 2026) claimed that Rahul Gandhi has turned creating a ruckus in Parliament and resorting to boycotts into a culture of the Congress.

Terming Parliament the supreme place for debate in a democracy, Mr. Shah said, “Rahul ji, you don’t allow Parliament to run; you don't discuss issues. You have turned creating ruckus and resorting to boycotts into a Congress culture.”

The Home Minister on Thursday led the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) march from Sector 12 to the Dayanand Chowk in Karnal.

‘Fitting reply’

Addressing a rally after the march, Mr. Shah also accused Rahul Gandhi of spreading anarchy in the country.

“Do you think our 80-year-old democracy will fall for your tricks? Rahul ji, we are people of the streets; take note of what I’m saying. The BJP will give you a fitting reply — in Parliament, in Vidhan Sabha, in villages, anywhere,” Mr. Shah said.

Party leaders join Shah

Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, Union Minister and Karnal MP Manohar Lal, State BJP chief Archana Gupta, the party's Haryana in-charge Smriti Irani and several State Ministers joined Mr. Shah for the ‘Loktantra Bachao’ march, along with hundreds of party supporters.

Mr. Shah also reiterated his proposal to convene a special session of Parliament to discuss the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

If you want a responsible discussion, let's debate inside Parliament. It is the BJP's resolve to identify and remove infiltrators from electoral rolls, unlike the INDIA bloc that seeks to protect infiltrators,” Mr. Shah alleged.

The Home Minister also sought details of Rahul Gandhi's foreign visits, saying, “You're the leader of the opposition (in Lok Sabha), people have the right to know.”

On Tuesday, Mr. Shah said the government is willing to convene a special session of Parliament to discuss SIR and dared the opposition to join the debate.

The 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) campaign comes amid an ongoing political confrontation between the BJP and the opposition parties over allegations of electoral irregularities and the functioning of democratic institutions.

On November 1, the INDIA bloc held a 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' protest at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, where opposition leaders accused the Centre of electoral irregularities and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Amit Shah takes part in 'Loktantra bachao, Arajakta hatao' march in Karnal

World.title: Thousands of troops secure Indonesia trial as tensions run high over wiretap scandal
World.content:
Indonesian authorities tasked thousands of police and military personnel to provide security on Thursday (November 5, 2026) for a trial involving former President Joko Widodo, as tensions in the capital remained high over allegations that top officers had been involved in intercepting the current President's telephone conversations.

Three senior generals have already been detained in the wiretapping scandal, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been named chief of staff to President Prabowo Subianto last month.

Gen. Listyo previously served as national police chief under Mr. Widodo, though the former President has not been implicated in the wiretapping investigation. There are allegations that Cabinet officials, politicians, journalists, civil society leaders and business executives were also subjected to unauthorised surveillance.

After losing two Presidential races to Mr. Widodo, Mr. Prabowo aligned himself with the popular leader and campaigned as his successor, choosing Mr. Widodo’s son as his running mate in a move that fuelled concerns about a growing political dynasty in Indonesia’s young democracy.

Mr. Widodo and Mr. Prabowo were once close political allies, with Mr. Widodo backing Mr. Prabowo’s successful 2024 Presidential bid, but their relationship has come under increased scrutiny amid signs of a growing rift since Mr. Prabowo took office.

Neither has commented on the wiretapping case.

Retired police Gen. Oegroseno, a former deputy national police chief, told the Forum Keadilan TV podcast on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that investigators should examine all possible lines of command behind the wiretapping, including whether any directives originated from Mr. Widodo.

“Investigators should not hesitate to question a former President if necessary,” Gen. Oegroseno said. “The motive behind the alleged wiretapping operation must be fully uncovered under the leadership of the current police chief.”

The wiretapping operation could also constitute a serious human rights violation and could be used to intimidate critics and weaken civil liberties, said Usman Hamid, Amnesty International's executive director in Indonesia.

“This is not merely about the alleged wiretapping of the President,” Mr. Hamid said in a statement. “Authorities must disclose who else may have been targeted and investigate the full impact of the operation.”

Police allege the unauthorised wiretapping took place between 2025 and 2026, after Mr. Prabowo had been elected and while Gen. Listyo was still national police chief. National Police Legal Division head Sonta Nasution and Eko Hadi Santoso, a senior instructor at the National Police Education and Training Institute, were also detained.

Authorities have called in more than 20,000 troops to Jakarta, and on Thursday (November 5, 2026) said that 6,770 police and military personnel had been deployed to secure Mr. Widodo's hearing. Mr. Widodo was called to testify in a defamation trial stemming from allegations that he used a fake university diploma. The trial is unrelated to the wiretapping case and Mr. Widodo denied the diploma allegations.

As he arrived on Thursday (November 5, 2026) morning at the East Jakarta District Court, the former President was welcomed by hundreds of his supporters chanting messages of encouragement.

The Presidential palace has said the wiretaps were being considered an “act of treason” that endangered state interests, but has not linked the deployment of troops to Jakarta to the case.

East Jakarta Police chief Alfian Nurrizal said that the deployment for the hearing was a precautionary measure due to potential security risks and large crowds, and that most of the forces were being held on standby.

Indonesian military spokesperson Maj. Gen. Muhammad Nas previously said that the deployment of the 20,000 marines and other personnel to Jakarta was a “normal occurrence”.

Despite the number of troops sent to Jakarta, there has also been no visible military presence on the streets and authorities have said most are being held in reserve in barracks and other facilities.

World.title: ‘Pamani Illam’ is Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s new camp office
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday (November 5, 2026) began discharging his official duties from the newly renovated government bungalow, ‘Pamani Illam’, at the Podhigai Compound on Greenways Road in Chennai.

After assuming office as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vijay had been discharging his official duties from his office in the main block of Fort St. George on weekdays. The Chief Minister had been commuting from his residence at Neelankarai, about 18 kilometres from the Secretariat.

He had also been using his residence at a multi-storeyed building in Pattinapakkam on certain occasions. Meanwhile, steps were underway to shift his office in the Secretariat from the main block to the 10th floor of Namakkal Kavignar Maligai.

On Thursday, Mr. Vijay inspected ‘Pamani Illam’, which had undergone renovation by the Public Works Department (PWD). Official sources said he was present at the camp office for nearly three hours and discharged his official duties from there.

During the course of renovation, Mr. Vijay had inspected the government bungalow on a few occasions. The PWD had recently allotted the bungalow to function as Chief Minister’s camp office after completing the renovation work.

Previous occupant

Spread over about 5,000 sq. ft., the camp office has been provided with various facilities. These include meeting rooms where the Chief Minister can hold discussions with Ministers and officials. The premises will also be used to receive dignitaries and visitors on official visits, sources said. The bungalow was previously occupied by former Chief Secretary V. Irai Anbu.

World.title: FCC bars PHC from hearing cases related to PTI workers' preventive detention
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) on Thursday restrained the Peshawar High Court (PHC) from hearing cases related to the preventive detention of PTI workers and activists under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO) following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The directive was issued by a two-judge bench, headed by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and including Justice Aamer Farooq.

The bench took up a set of petitions challenging interim bail of the detainees, granted by the PHC against surety bonds of Rs100,000 each. The PHC had issued the interim orders in the absence of any report by the provincial government explaining reasons and circumstances that led to the detention of PTI activists and also directed that they should not be arrested pending the cases related to their detentions before the high court.

The PHC will next hear the case on Nov 12.

More than 60 appeals challenging the PHC’s interim orders have been fixed before the FCC. The pleas were moved by the KP Home and Tribal Affairs Department additional chief secretary.

The FCC restrained the high court from proceeding further on the cases and decided to issue notices to the parties with a direction that they may also file their pleas before the superior court.

KP Advocate General Sanaullah Khan, who pleaded the case before the FCC on behalf of the provincial government, told Dawn that the PHC’s orders had been challenged under Article 245 of the Constitution, which provides for calling in armed forces in aid of civil forces.

He cited clause 3 of the provision, arguing that a high court could not “directly entertain a case under Article 199 of the Constitution since it cannot exercise its jurisdiction in relation to any area in which the armed forces are acting in aid of the civil power”.

Clause 3 of Article 245 states: “A high court shall not exercise jurisdiction under Article 199 in relation to any area in which the armed forces of Pakistan are, for the time being, acting in aid of civil power.”

When the KP advocate general presented this argument before the FCC, Justice Farooq observed that a high court received several cases under Article 199 on a daily basis.

“Does this mean the high court should not hear such cases?” he questioned.

The advocate general replied that matters such as tenancy disputes could be taken up as the high court was approached for these cases after the matter was referred to competent forums.

Former additional advocate general Shah Faisal Ilyas, who was representing one of the parties, raised an objection during the proceedings and requested the court to hear the parties before issuing any injunctive order, asserting that the objections raised by the provincial government against the high court’s order were untenable.

CJ Khan then directed the counsel to furnish his formal objections after going through the FCC’s order first and stated that the court was issuing notices to the respondents.

The KP advocate general said while speaking to Dawn that the framers of the Constitution had provided protection to provisions relating to the preventive custody under Article 10 (safeguards as to arrest and detention).

He specifically cited clauses 3 and 4 of the provision and contended that provisions of the MPO were invoked on the basis of “subjective analysis of the government functionary to prevent any action prejudicial to the public safety and law and order”.

The FCC’s directive comes less than a month after the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas.

In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release. Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results.

Scores of PTI workers and leaders had been detained following the Oct 11 move, including lawmakers. Sohail Afridi, who has been rendered non-functional as the chief minister after the imposition of governor’s rule, has also been detained.

The PHC remains seized with petitions against these detentions, including that of Afridi.

World.title: PM directs cancellation of petrol pump licences over failure to facilitate fuel subsidy beneficiaries
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday directed the authorities concerned to cancel the licences of petrol pumps that fail to facilitate registered beneficiaries under the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Programme.

Chairing a meeting to review progress on the programme, the prime minister expressed satisfaction over its implementation and transparency, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

“Simplifying the registration and subsidy disbursement procedures has led to an increase in registrations, enabling more deserving citizens to benefit from the facility,” the prime minister said.

He said the technology-driven and transparent subsidy scheme would prove to be a “game changer” for similar public welfare initiatives in the future.

The prime minister also appreciated Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima, Federal Secretary for Information Technology and Telecommunication Zarar Hashim Khan and their team for developing an effective monitoring and dashboard system for the programme.

The meeting was informed that 15,519,282 citizens had registered under the subsidy scheme so far, including 15.06 million motorcycle owners and 449,000 owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.

A total of 63,153,685 fuel tokens had been issued under the scheme, of which 59,445,347 had been used, the meeting was told.

Payments amounting to Rs28.6 billion had been disbursed under the fuel subsidy scheme as of November 4, 2026, the briefing added.

The meeting was also informed that separate call centres had been established for consumers and petrol pumps to provide information about the programme and address complaints.

PM Shehbaz announced a relief scheme in September for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc. Under the scheme, owners of two- and three-wheeled vehicles are eligible for a subsidy of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc are entitled to the same subsidy on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

World.title: Minister says electoral reforms panel to have 2 members each from PML-N, PPP and PTI
World.content:
The ruling PML-N, its coalition partner PPP and the opposition PTI will each get two seats on the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER), Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday.

In a post on X, Chaudhry said the allocation of seats in the Senate for the committee would give two seats each to the PML-N, PPP and PTI.

The Awami National Party (ANP), Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), National Party and Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) will each be allocated one seat, he added.

“The final decision on the names of the committee members will be made by the leader of the house (the prime minister) and the deputy prime minister after consultations with the opposition, coalition partners and relevant parliamentary leadership,” Chaudhry said.

Earlier this week, the government, taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, formally appr­oached its allies to join the proposed PCER.

It had contacted its key allies, the PPP and the MQM-P, seeking nominations for their representatives on the proposed committee. The PPP had submitted the names of its legislators for the PCER. However, the names have not yet been made public.

On Tuesday, the government formally approached the opposition to seek its representation on the proposed PCER. However, the opposition had termed the formation of the committee a “futile exercise” unless its long-standing demands were met.

Chaudhry had also contacted PTI chief whip in the National Assembly, Aamir Dogar, asking him to submit the names of opposition lawmakers for the committee.

However, Dogar had expressed reservations over the proposed composition of the committee and demanded equal representation for the government and opposition.

Last week, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari urged National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to use the “authority and power” delegated to him by jailed PTI founder Imran Khan to direct opposition members to participate in parliamentary committees.

He said the opposition leader should nominate representatives to the committee on electoral reforms and submit the names to the Speaker’s Office.

Later on, a PPP delegation had also met Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas.

During the meeting, the PPP delegation invited the opposition to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms.

World.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
World.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo announced his intention to retire from the Portugal national team on Thursday in a social media post, bringing to an end one of the most illustrious international careers in the history of football.

The 41-year-old said he would ‘hand back the number 7 shirt’ after the November international break.

Ronaldo captained the team to their first major trophy at Euro 2016 and helped them win the 2019 and 2025 Nations Leagues.

“It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. They are also made with the heart,” said Ronaldo.

“If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.” Ronaldo thanked his family, the Portuguese people and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his 23-year career with national team.

“Portugal will always be a part of me,” he captioned the announcement video.

Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal and scored 146 goals. He holds the all-time record for international appearances and for international goals.

World.title: Lahore’s air pollution a year-round problem, worsened by winter and agricultural burning: report
World.content:
LAHORE: Lahore’s fine particulate matter pollution remained above Pakistan’s prescribed standards for the past 12 months, including the relatively cleaner summer months, indicating that the city’s air pollution remained a year-round problem intensified by winter weather and seasonal agricultural burning, according to an analysis.

The report, titled ‘Lahore’s smog: The year-round baseline, and what changes in October ’, was released by the environmental monitoring project ‘Hamari Hawa’ on November 2 and prepared by its founder, Hammad Tariq.

It drew on ground-monitoring data, satellite observations and atmospheric reanalysis to examine pollution levels and possible sources around Lahore.

On Monday, air pollution in Lahore reached hazardous levels, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 530 and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations climbing to 343 micrograms per cubic metre.

According to the analysis, Lahore’s monthly average PM2.5 concentration remained above 35 micrograms per cubic metre from October 2025 to October 2026. Even in the city’s cleaner months, April to September 2026, monthly averages ranged from 40 to 59 micrograms per cubic metre, against the national annual standard of 15 micrograms per cubic metre.

The report used IQAir’s historical data, which aggregates readings from ground monitors across the city. It recorded a monthly average of 40 micrograms per cubic metre in June 2026, the lowest during the period, while averages from October 2025 to February 2026 ranged between 124 and 183 micrograms per cubic metre. October 2026 recorded 100 micrograms per cubic metre.

The report cautioned that the national limit of 35 micrograms per cubic metre is a 24-hour standard, whereas the monthly figures are monthly averages. The comparison therefore showed the persistence of pollution but does not establish how many individual days exceeded the daily limit.

The analysis identified a sharp seasonal decline in the height of the atmospheric layer into which pollutants can disperse as one of the factors behind the winter increase.

Using ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis data, it estimated that the average mixing height over Lahore falls from around 830 to 860 metres in May and June to about 400 metres in October and 260 metres in November. It declined further to around 190 metres in December.

A shallower mixing layer leaves less air available for pollutants to disperse, allowing concentrations near the ground to rise even without an increase in emissions, the report said.

According to the report, in an idealised comparison where emissions and other conditions remain unchanged, reducing the mixing layer to half or a third of its earlier depth could make smoke roughly two to three times more concentrated.

It also noted that Lahore’s average wind speed remained relatively light throughout the year, ranging from about 1.8 to 2.4 metres per second, and that October is not necessarily windier or calmer than September.

The report also examined satellite-detected heat spots on farmland around Lahore, which it classified as crop-associated detections after excluding locations near known kilns, dumps, industrial sites and towns.

Between October 15 and November 1, 2026, satellites recorded 781 such detections within 40 kilometres of central Lahore. Of these, 322 were in Sheikhupura district, 149 in India’s Tarn Taran district, 106 in Amritsar, 77 in Nankana Sahib, 62 in Lahore district and 50 in Kasur.

The analysis found that between 37 and 63pc of crop-associated satellite detections within 100 kilometres of Lahore on the Pakistani side occurred after November 1 in each of the seven seasons from 2019 to 2025.

It said the timing was significant because agricultural burning around the rice harvest coincided with the period when the atmospheric mixing layer becomes progressively shallower.

However, the report stressed that satellite heat detections do not confirm individual fires. A single field fire may generate several detections, while fires obscured by clouds or occurring between satellite passes may not be recorded. The figures also do not measure the area burnt or the quantity of pollution released.

The report said pollution sources operating throughout the year include vehicle exhaust, factories, brick kilns, power plants, generators, household fuels, open rubbish burning and dust. Some fine particles are also formed in the atmosphere through chemical reactions involving gases released by these sources.

Citing the Urban Unit’s 2023 Lahore emissions inventory, which was based on 2020–21 data, the report said that transport accounted for about 35pc of the city’s PM2.5 emissions, compared with 33pc from crop-residue burning, 29pc from waste burning and three per cent from industry.

It cautioned against interpreting the frequently quoted figure of 83pc for transport as its share of PM2.5. That figure covers all pollutants by weight and is dominated by carbon monoxide, it added.

A separate Punjab-wide Urban Unit inventory for 2020 estimated that heavy-duty vehicles and buses produced 55pc of road vehicles’ exhaust PM2.5, compared with 18pc from motorcycles. The report said the figures are provincial estimates and should not be treated as a direct measurement of Lahore’s current pollution.

It also identified 890 mapped brick kilns within 50 kilometres of central Lahore, including 196 within 25 kilometres.

The analysis further highlighted the difficulty of establishing how much pollution originates from within Pakistan and how much of it crosses the border. It cited estimates of the cross-border contribution to Lahore’s pollution ranging from 13 to 30pc based on figures from different studies and geographical areas.

It concluded that emissions inventories, ground-level monitoring and source-apportionment studies measure different aspects of air pollution and their percentages cannot be directly compared or converted into one another.

The report’s central finding was that the seasonal improvement in air quality does not mean Lahore has clean air during the rest of the year. It argued that persistent emissions form the baseline, while the shrinking atmospheric mixing layer and crop-residue burning add to pollution during the smog season.

Meanwhile, the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD) released a report stating Lahore recorded a 15pc net improvement across six major air pollutants during the first year of the Punjab government’s real-time air quality monitoring programme, while the city’s peak Air Quality Index (AQI) declined by 28pc in October 2026 compared to the corresponding period last year.

The department said the improvement reflected a reduction across six major atmospheric pollutants rather than a change in a single parameter, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Lahore also recorded no days in the hazardous AQI category, defined as an index above 300, during October 2026, against four such days in October 2025.

The findings were based on the first full year of real-time air quality monitoring and publicly available ground-based measurements. The government said the data provided an empirical basis for assessing the impact of its air pollution control measures and developing targeted interventions.

According to the EPCCD, the first reading on Punjab’s real-time air quality portal was published on Oct 1, 2025, with an initial network of 30 regulatory-grade monitoring stations. The network has since expanded to 59 stations, which continuously measure six air pollutants and seven meteorological parameters.

The government plans to increase the number of monitoring stations to 100 during the 2025–26 period to strengthen its capacity for monitoring ambient air quality across the province, it said.

The department maintained that the expanded network had enabled authorities to make more informed decisions through accurate, ground-based measurements, particularly in contrast to assessments relying on low-cost, non-regulatory sensors and satellite-derived models.

The EPCCD also highlighted the role of meteorological conditions in interpreting the improvement.

According to official Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) statistics, Lahore received 50pc less rainfall in October 2026 than in October 2025, indicating that the improvement was recorded despite relatively drier conditions.

Another important factor in assessing air pollution is the atmospheric boundary layer, also known as the mixing height, which determines the volume of air available to dilute and disperse pollutants.

The department said ground-based measurements conducted by the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) using a ceilometer in Lahore showed an increase of only 10 metres in the minimum mixing layer height during the comparison period.

This finding was presented in contrast to a 25-metre increase cited by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI). The EPCCD, in its report, questioned the reliability of the latter assessment, arguing that ground-based instruments provided more appropriate measurements for evaluating local air quality interventions.

The department also referred to peer-reviewed research published in January 2026, which identified systematic biases of between 200 and 500 metres in ERA5 reanalysis data over the monsoon region. It said such model-derived products were useful for regional research but had limitations when used to assess the local impact of air pollution control policies.

Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning.

In the transport sector, the government has introduced 612 electric buses, while also providing electric bikes and improving traffic management to reduce emissions from conventional vehicles. The department said around 500,000 vehicles had undergone emissions testing, while more than 800 legal notices had been issued to heavy transport vehicles over emissions and fitness certification requirements.

The government aimed to expand its electric bus fleet to 3,000 vehicles as part of its clean mobility strategy, the report said.

It further noted that industrial compliance had also been strengthened through the Environment Protection Force — responsible for monitoring emissions, fuel quality and fugitive dust control systems at more than 600 sites across Punjab. The department said industries emitting excessive smoke without adequate emission-control systems, as well as units using unauthorised fuels, were not being allowed to operate.

The government has also imposed a complete ban on the operation of tyre pyrolysis plants and the use of carbon powder as industrial fuel, citing concerns over hazardous emissions, it noted.

Agricultural emissions, particularly those caused by the burning of crop residue, remain another major component of the anti-smog strategy. The EPCCD said field-level stubble-burning incidents had declined by one-third during the first year after the government provided 10,000 super seeders to farmers through targeted subsidies.

The government plans to increase the number of subsidised super seeders to 25,000 and introduce additional mechanised solutions, including Kubota harvesters and stubble balers, to discourage open burning and facilitate the use of crop residue as industrial fuel, it said.

The department also attributed part of the reduction in emissions to changes in the energy and industrial sectors. According to the latest statistics from the Ministry of Energy’s Petroleum Division, the annual compound growth rate of coal consumption declined by 14.2pc.

Meanwhile, more than 95pc of brick kilns in Punjab have adopted the zigzag technology, which the department said had helped reduce coal consumption and emissions from the brick-making sector.

The EPCCD said coordination among government departments and stakeholders, coupled with regulatory enforcement, cleaner transport initiatives and the expansion of ground-based monitoring, had contributed to the progress recorded during the first year.

It maintained that the 2026 findings provided a baseline for measuring future improvements and refining pollution-control interventions, while emphasising that sustained enforcement and a transition towards cleaner fuels and technologies would remain essential to protecting public health and improving air quality in Lahore and other parts of Punjab.

World.title: New wave of bomb threats hits passenger flights across Europe
World.content:
Airlines across Europe received a series of bomb threats on Thursday morning for the second time this week, forcing many to make unplanned or escorted landings, although none of the threats immediately proved to be genuine.

While no country has attributed blame for the threats, they come at a time when European officials have been blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as “hybrid attacks”. Moscow and Tehran both deny any such campaign.

Aer Lingus flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome landed safely on Thursday at Evreux airport, 100 km (62 miles) west of Paris, after being diverted as a security precaution, the Irish airline said in a statement.

Bulgarian officials reported three aircraft making emergency landings in the Balkan country because of bomb threats.

Airplanes flying from Copenhagen and Madrid landed safely in Sofia, the interior minister said, according to broadcaster bTV.

A third aircraft, from London, was diverted and landed in Plovdiv, Bulgaria’s second-largest city, local media said. The government did not respond to requests for comment.

Czech, Italian, Polish authorities also report bomb threats

Czech police said on X that four airplanes heading to Prague had received bomb threats on Thursday and that authorities were making preparations for the landings, although they assessed the credibility of the threats as low.

Italy’s air force safely escorted a Finnair plane from Helsinki to its scheduled landing in Rome, a person close to the matter said. Another Finnair flight from Helsinki, operated by Jettime, landed as normal in Vienna after receiving a bomb threat, the Finnish carrier said.

Polish airline LOT said a flight from Warsaw to Brussels had landed safely at its destination after a security warning, and no suspicious items were found.

It also said a LOT flight to Paris had been stopped as it was taxiing towards take-off and that its passengers had then been transferred to another aircraft as a precaution.

Italian media reported that a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw had to land in Vienna due to a bomb threat.

On Tuesday, at least seven flights and a cruise ship received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports across Europe, although no devices were discovered.

This week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries. Some experts said hoax bomb threats could be part of a similar pattern of cheap, deniable disruption efforts.

Eliran Almog, CEO of aviation cybersecurity firm Cyviation, said the repeated threats could serve both to disrupt operations and to observe how airlines, airports and national authorities respond.

“These aviation threats are also occurring in the same period as cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe,” Almog said.

“Different essential services are experiencing disruption that carries economic costs and can undermine public confidence.”

World.title: Democrats flex congressional majorities as Trump accepts electoral losses
World.content:
Democrats vowed on Wednesday to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Trump ​spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.

A wave of anger over Trump’s policies , particularly the US-Iran war’s role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats ‌in deeply Republican states for a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.

It will be the first time that Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with a Democratic-controlled Congress in both chambers.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said the incoming majority will be focused on affordability and accountability.

Shift shows only states with a 2026 Senate race and in which 95pc or more of expected votes have been counted. —Reuters

“We don’t work for Donald Trump,” Jeffries, a New York lawmaker who is on track to become the first Black speaker of the House , told reporters on Wednesday. “We work for the American people. And the days of the House of Representatives functioning like ​a wholly owned subsidiary of the Trump administration are over.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has emerged as a national Democratic figure since his election a year ago, released a video on social media urging his party to address the concerns ​of voters burdened by rising prices who want schools and roads.

“It is not enough to simply win power. We must use it,” Mamdani said. “Now, it’s time for us in the Democratic Party to deliver.”

Trump, who had devoted his last pre-election public appearance on Monday to talking about his renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, called in reporters on the morning after his party’s sweeping midterm defeat to show off the ballroom he is building at the White ​House.

“When I get criticised, like, ‘Why are you working on the White House?’ I’m doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol of America, and it’s got to be pristine, it’s got to be perfect,” Trump said. “For me it’s relaxing.”

He turned only briefly to the elections ​during his nearly hour-long appearance, telling reporters, “I’ll get along probably with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive, but I have the power of the veto.”

US President Donald Trump looks at the final steel beam as it is lifted on the day it goes into the ballroom, at the White House in Washington, DC, US, November 4, 2026. —Reuters

Trump had cast the midterm elections as a referendum on the first half of his second four-year stint in the White House, repeatedly urging his Republican base to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” a message that Democratic Party leaders were happy to amplify.

The result: voters in conservative strongholds who had propelled the president to his second term in office just two years ago swung dramatically toward Democrats, fueled by deep frustration over the unpopular war with Iran, anxiety over the high ​cost of living and anger at Trump’s stewardship of the country.

In Texas, the biggest Republican-led state before Tuesday, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning their first Senate seat there since 1988 and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott.

Kansas elected its first Democratic senator ​since the Great Depression nearly a century ago, and in South Carolina, a state that Trump carried by nearly 18 points in 2024, Democrats turned aside his hand-picked Senate candidate.

Waiting on Alaska, Mississippi

Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remained uncalled as of Wednesday morning, leaving open the possibility that the ‌Democrats’ majority could grow ⁠by another two seats to 56-44.

Once seated in January, Democrats are expected to use their power to investigate Trump’s administration, family and allies and demand concessions on major legislation. The Democratic Senate can block Trump’s nominees , including any US Supreme Court justices should a vacancy arise.

The Democratic victory is fuelling questions about the longevity of the Supreme Court’s two eldest justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito , and the durability of its conservative majority.

US President Donald Trump looks at the final steel beam as it is lifted on the day it goes into the ballroom, at the White House in Washington, DC, US, November 4, 2026. —Reuters

In the meantime, Republicans hold the reins and will have at least one must-pass piece of legislation ahead – a measure to fund the federal government past December – that they could use to enact conservative priorities during the so-called lame-duck period.

The loss also upended Republicans’ House leadership , with House Speaker Mike Johnson saying he would not continue to lead his caucus next year.

Trump, who is barred by the US Constitution from seeking a third ​term, acknowledged the war with Iran had played a role in his ​party’s losses but stood by his decision.

Vice President JD Vance, ⁠who may run as a Trump successor in the 2028 election, piled blame on his boss’s decision to attack Iran in February.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote in a long social media post. “The president himself said so last night. If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a ​worthwhile cost to pay.”

Democratic wave

Democrats focused their campaign on corruption and affordability, blaming Trump’s expensive tariffs on imports, some of which were ruled to be an illegal tax by the courts, and the ​war with Iran for driving up ⁠costs while highlighting the billions of dollars the Trump family has made since he returned to the White House.

Republicans, led by Trump, attacked Democrats for defending transgender people’s rights and similar social issues, portraying them as radical and extreme. Voters made it clear they were more concerned with pocketbook issues.

“This is close to an extinction-level event for Republicans,” Republican Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said in public remarks analysing the results.

The Democratic wave flooded huge swaths of the country. Republicans lost ground in 99 per cent of the approximately 2,100 counties where most votes had been counted as of Wednesday morning, according to tallies compiled ⁠by Reuters and ​USA Today.

Abdul El-Sayed, a Democrat from the party’s rising left wing, won Michigan’s open Senate seat, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber and defeating Mike Rogers, ​who entered the race with Trump’s backing.

The night included other historic firsts for both parties, including the first Black woman elected governor in US history with Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms’ win in Georgia and New Mexico’s Deb Haaland becoming the country’s first Native American woman to be elected governor.

World.title: ECP sets Feb 7 as polling date for first phase of Punjab local govt elections; KP polls delayed
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday decided to hold the first phase of local government elections in Punjab on Feb 7, 2027, in view of fog and weather conditions, while polls in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were postponed until further orders.

ECP had initially proposed holding the elections on December 14 in Punjab. In KP, the polls were to be held across the province, excluding 12 districts where special emergency measures were in place.
